(b) `parse_pdf_value` (`cid_fonts.py:194`) converts reals to Python `float` (lossy: `1` vs `1.00000000000000000001` collide), drops the generation of references, and folds literal and hex strings to bytes, so `(\101)` and `<5C313031>` collide. It is a capability parser, not an equality oracle.
**Fix:** The harness tokenizes with the bounded `cid_fonts._tokenize` and builds its own tree (`_semantic_value`, `test_text_commit_real_corpus_acceptance.py:273`) that ignores ONLY dictionary key order, keeps name tokens, literal/hex distinction, reference generations and array order, folds only int/real equality through `canonical_pdf_scalar` (`cid_fonts.py:306`), and treats duplicate keys, parse failures and trailing tokens as unequal (`_objects_semantically_equal`, `:335`). Product-side digests use sorted keys (`inspect.py:158`, `_canonical_object_digest`). Sibling entry: "tobytes(encryption=KEEP) reorders dictionary keys..." (same root, product side).
**File:** `test_scripts/test_text_commit_real_corpus_acceptance.py:273`, `:335`, `:352`; `model/text_commit/cid_fonts.py:194`, `:306`; `model/text_commit/inspect.py:158`

## A higher-resolution render or full decode on a document poisons later lower-resolution renders of the same document
**Area:** MuPDF image store; `model/text_commit/verify.py` (`ObservedPage`, `observe_page`), `model/text_commit/engine.py` (`commit`)
**Symptom:** After a Tier 0/1 commit the live document rendered a pixel-different image (8180 px, max channel diff 103 on an HVAC image) than a fresh open of its own saved bytes, and on a pair of `tobytes` snapshots the same image rasterized differently, so the V0d outside-the-target-pixels check reported false changes at an image corner.
**Cause:** Measured on 1.27.1: `get_pixmap(dpi=96)`, `get_text("dict"/"rawdict")` with the default flags (TEXT_PRESERVE_IMAGES), `get_image_rects`, `get_image_info(xrefs=True)` and `get_image_bbox` all decode images at full or higher resolution into MuPDF's store, and a later lower-resolution render of the SAME document reuses that decode (fresh open subsamples). The tile-lookup rule is an inference, not read from MuPDF source. Zero-effect calls: `rawdict(flags=TEXTFLAGS_RAWDICT & ~TEXT_PRESERVE_IMAGES)`, `get_text("text")`, `get_drawings`, `get_texttrace`, `get_image_info()` without hashes.
**Fix:** Every render and extraction of the commit proof runs on an isolated `tobytes(encryption=KEEP)` snapshot (pre and post), never on the live page (`engine.py:310-335`); on the snapshot the 96 dpi render comes FIRST (`observe_page` renders before any extraction, `verify.py:122`) so the pre and post snapshots rasterize alike. Flags and image APIs were left unchanged so gate inputs are identical. No `store_shrink` (global side effect, and it also drops the user's own warm tiles). Any new commit-time probe must read the snapshot and keep render-before-extraction.
**File:** `model/text_commit/verify.py:101-125`, `model/text_commit/engine.py:310-335`, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_live_store_isolation.py`

## An extracted text line is not a content-stream show, and a whitespace-stripped match admits MuPDF-synthesized spaces
**Area:** `model/text_commit/source_run.py` (`group_page_runs` click-time grouping), `model/text_commit/replay.py` (`origin_reliable`)
**Symptom:** Grouping the index runs of one extracted line into "one show" produced an editor text that differs from what the page shows, or bound the wrong show: a mirrored show lists its runs in reverse x order; a show whose pen position is not tracked can paint anywhere on its line; `<Buffer> Tj < Tank> Tj` extracts identically to `(Buffer Tank) Tj`.
**Cause:** (a) Runs are split at every space and kind change by the parser (`text_block_parsing.py`), so line and show identity are not related by extraction. Order is parser order, not `origin.x` (`source_run.py:17`). (b) Replay does not track advances; after an untracked advance a show's `origin_reliable` is False (`replay.py:146`, `:568`) and it lies somewhere on the text line of its last repositioning, so checking only the direct successor is not enough. (c) MuPDF synthesizes page-text spaces from TJ kern gaps and `Tc` gaps (helv 12 pt: kern -100 no space, -150 a space; `Tc` 1.5 none, 2.0 'B u f f e r'); a whitespace-stripped comparison of decoded show text vs member text still passes, but the page text and the show text differ.
**Fix:** Grouping is a proof with eight conditions and any failure leaves the line ungrouped (the single-run hit then refuses at binding, which is safe): exactly one reliable show near the first origin; that show has `array_item_count == 1` and `char_spacing == 0` (`source_run.py:415-418`); decoded text minus whitespace equals member text minus whitespace AND the non-space glyph-code count equals the character count (`:424-426`); the successor's origin must be reliable (`:427-429`); no untracked show may paint into the union, bounded by `_untracked_band` (`:262`, +/-3 em) and failing outright when the band cannot be bounded; a show claimed by two lines groups for neither (rule 8, `:374`).
**File:** `model/text_commit/source_run.py:17-60`, `:262`, `:374`, `:415-429`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_source_run.py:148`, `:379`, `:432`, `:526`

## A Tier 1 splice is a whole operator, a token only names a candidate, and CID text needs a font registry to bind
**Area:** `model/text_commit/patch.py`, `model/text_commit/plan.py` (`_build_tier1`), `model/text_commit/engine.py` (`cached_candidate_identity_failure`), `model/text_commit/inspect.py` (`bind_source_text`)
**Symptom:** Three related misreadings that each produced a wrong or refused edit: (1) a Tier 1 transplant deleted bytes beyond the string (a trailing TJ kern); (2) an Apply with a preview token committed a different show when a "twin" (same text, same replacement) existed; (3) every CJK / Identity-H target bound as `undecodable_target`.
**Cause:** (1) `build_transplant_replacement` splices `stream_bytes[show.op_start:show.op_end]`, the whole operator, not the string range (`patch.py:335-365`). (2) A plan token is content-derived and only names a cached `PreparedEdit`; the show may have moved or a twin may bind first. (3) `bind_source_text` matches latin-1 bytes; a target outside latin-1 returns `UNDECODABLE_TARGET` unless a font registry is passed (`inspect.py:1215-1220`).
**Fix:** (1) Treat every Tier 1 replacement as an operator replacement and fence TJ kerns before building it (`plan.py:2428-2449`). (2) A cache hit must re-bind on the LIVE page before committing: page xref, page fingerprint, then a fresh `bind_source_text` whose stream xref and `op_start/op_end/string_start/string_end` equal the cached binding's (`seq` is only an ordinal) (`engine.py:126-170`, called from `pdf_text_edit.py:1920-1943`). (3) Always pass `registry=engine.registry` when the target may be non-latin-1.
**File:** `model/text_commit/patch.py:335`, `model/text_commit/plan.py:2428`, `model/text_commit/engine.py:126`, `model/text_commit/inspect.py:1215`

## A save-time hook with nothing to save must not touch the live document, and a tobytes snapshot cannot be compared with the original object table
**Area:** `model/tools/watermark_tool.py` (`prepare_doc_for_save`), `ToolManager.prepare_doc_for_save`, acceptance harness baselines
**Symptom:** Every save of an unwatermarked document (14/14 `save_reopen` cells) changed the Catalog: `/Names/EmbeddedFiles` appeared, `/PageMode` became `/UseAttachments` (readers open the attachment pane) and a new EmbeddedFile stream was added, even though the user had never used watermarks. Separately, a baseline taken with `doc.tobytes()` differed from the original file in about 1300 HVAC objects.
**Cause:** (a) `WatermarkTool.prepare_doc_for_save` called `_write_watermarks_embed(doc, [])` unconditionally, and `ToolManager.prepare_doc_for_save` hands hooks the LIVE document by default; `embfile_add` rewrites the Catalog and appends objects. (b) `tobytes` drops object streams and re-serializes the objects they held, so snapshot vs original is not object-for-object comparable.
**Fix:** (a) With no watermarks the hook acts only when the document already carries the attachment (then clear it, fail-closed if `embfile_names()` raises) and otherwise returns without touching the document (`watermark_tool.py:110-120`; the only `embfile_add` is `:303`). Rule: a hook may mutate the live document only when it has something to persist. (b) Compare a live snapshot only with another `tobytes` copy, and the original file only with a save-then-reopen of the result (`test_text_commit_real_corpus_acceptance.py:226`, `_measurement_copy`; umbrella `test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py:407`).
**File:** `model/tools/watermark_tool.py:110`, `:303`; `test_scripts/test_watermark_save_noop.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_real_corpus_acceptance.py:226`

## Redo must dispatch on what the first execute committed, and the after-snapshot must be page-level and strict
**Area:** `model/edit_commands.py` (`EditTextCommand.execute`, `_redo`, `_capture_after_snapshot`)
**Symptom:** A redo re-ran `model.edit_text` against today's page: it could land another tier or silently use the legacy engine, and a consented rebuild's redo either asked again or reproduced different bytes. A page-level restore of a whole-document snapshot mis-applied the document.
**Cause:** "No forward patch recorded" was read as "safe to re-run". But a Tier 0/1 commit whose reversal was not recorded, and a consented rebuild, both have a first outcome that a re-run cannot reproduce. Separately, the non-strict snapshot helper can fall back to a WHOLE-document snapshot, which `_restore_page_from_snapshot` cannot take.
**Fix:** `_redo()` (`edit_commands.py:487`) dispatches by the first outcome: forward PatchSet present -> `_redo_tier0`; tier in HIGH_FIDELITY_TIERS without a reversal -> `_refuse_redo` (zero mutation, `STALE_PLAN`, stays on the redo stack); a real (consented) fallback -> restore its after-snapshot, refusing if none; only the `engine="legacy"` baseline and mocked models (returns `None`) re-run. `_capture_after_snapshot` (`:456`) uses `_capture_page_snapshot_strict` only and backs up/restores annotation parent refs around it (`insert_pdf` rewrites the live annotation dicts). Only a real fallback records an after-snapshot (`:440-449`).
**File:** `model/edit_commands.py:310-337`, `:440-470`, `:487-527`

## A byte-by-byte Python lexer is the whole-page replay bottleneck, and any fast path needs an equality contract and a linear-time guard
**Area:** `model/text_commit/pdf_lexer.py` (`lex_content_stream(coalesce_inert=True)`), `model/text_commit/replay.py`
**Symptom:** A cold replay of an HVAC drawing page (about 1.3 MB of `q 1 0 0 1 x y cm 0 0 m ... l S Q`, about 930k tokens, about 70 shows) held the GUI thread about 1.4 s, so the first click in edit mode and every Apply rebind stalled.
**Cause:** The pure-Python lexer visits every byte; path operators dominate the stream and have no replay effect except clearing the operand stack. (Companion O(n^2) in the same budget: `page.annots()`, see the annot_xrefs entry.)
**Fix:** `coalesce_inert=True` lets C-level regexes claim spans whose entire effect is "clear the operand stack" and yields each as one `INERT_RUN` token (`pdf_lexer.py:118-147`, `:264-282`; replay opts in at `replay.py:593`). Soundness: only whitespace/regular characters (no delimiters), letters that spell only path/colour/clip operators, q-blocks only if every `cm` has six number operands (otherwise coalescing is switched off for the rest of the stream). The contract is "replay with and without coalescing returns EQUAL `PageReplay` objects on every input", pinned by adversarial, fuzzed, and every-fixture-page tests plus a linear-time guard (an ambiguous number regex backtracks exponentially). Never merge a fast path without the equality test and the pathological-input timing test.
**File:** `model/text_commit/pdf_lexer.py:118`, `model/text_commit/replay.py:593`, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_replay_fast_path.py:108`, `:199`, `:241`, `:279`, `:297`

## A page-level "pending maintenance" flag that only save clears turns one legacy rewrite into a refusal of every later true-text edit on that page
**Area:** `model/text_commit/plan.py` (HEAD `:1895`), `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (HEAD `:1813`, `:1963`), `model/text_commit/preview.py` (HEAD `:54`, `:298`), `model/edit_commands.py` (`AddTextboxCommand`)
**Symptom:** After adding a text box or a consented rebuild on a page (reproduced; object operations per ARCHITECTURE, not each measured), every true-text edit on that page was refused `pending_page_maintenance` until save; undoing the rewrite did not lift it; the editor that was already open stayed refused after a save, and the toast said "try again later" although nothing would change that.
**Cause:** A legacy page rewrite queues a `pending_edits` entry (and revokes fidelity protection) for a later `clean_contents`; only save (or `edit_count % 5`) drains it. The planner refused any page with a pending entry, `open_preview_session` froze the flag at session open (`preview.py:54`), and `AddTextboxCommand` undo restored page bytes but not the bookkeeping, so the flag outlived its cause.
**Fix:** Retired in part 5 Stage B (the gate lives on only as an enum value, `dto.py:52`; see the entry "The pending_page_maintenance gate is retired: fidelity protection already stops clean_contents ..." for why that is safe). The bookkeeping now travels with the bytes: `AddTextboxCommand` captures pending entries and protection membership before and after execute and restores them on undo/redo (`edit_commands.py:856-915`, `_page_book` `:888` / `_restore_page_book` `:901`). General rule: queue/flag state a command creates must be owned and reversed by the same command.
**File:** `model/text_commit/dto.py:52`, `model/edit_commands.py:856-915`, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_pending_maintenance_retired.py`

## Consent must be an explicit argument of this call; a missing callback or missing UI must mean "no"
**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`edit_text`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`_confirm_legacy_fallback`, `_fallback_consent_callback`, cross-page move)
**Symptom:** A tiered refusal fell through to the legacy redact-and-reinsert engine with no prompt when `confirm_fallback` was `None`, and a headless confirm answered Yes; consent stored on a manager attribute leaked as "sticky consent" after an exception or re-entry; a replay of an already-granted consent that still passed `None` would now be refused instead of honoured.
**Cause:** The old API read `confirm_fallback=None` as "do not ask, just go legacy". Consent semantics lived in missing-ness and in object state instead of in the request.
**Fix:** `None` is a refusal: `if confirm_fallback is None or not confirm_fallback(chain): return FALLBACK_DECLINED` (`pdf_text_edit.py:2218-2226`). The prompt is reachable only through the per-request `allow_rebuild` flag ("改用重建文字…"), which makes the controller pass the callback (`pdf_controller.py:2742-2757`); no view means False (`:2733-2738`). Replays of an already-decided consent pass a pre-approved callable, never `None` (`_move_consent_already_given`, `:230`, used at `:3074`). Consent must be decided BEFORE the `try`/snapshot of the operation: refusing inside the `try` raised into `replace_active_document_from_snapshot`, which replaces the document handle (itself a mutation) and then a modal.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py:2218`, `controller/pdf_controller.py:230`, `:2726-2757`, `:3074`

## Finalize must emit while the editor still exists, pull the controller's real result, and re-arm the preview after a refusal
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`finalize_text_edit_impl`, `_not_applied`, `_teardown_editor`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`edit_text`), `view/pdf_view.py` (`display_page`, `_detach_text_editor_before_scene_clear`)
**Symptom:** (a) A refused edit lost the typed text because the editor was torn down before the outcome was known. (b) After a refusal the kept editor's Apply stayed disabled forever. (c) After a successful commit the synchronous `show_page` re-entered `display_page` and deleted the editor proxy that finalize still referenced.
**Cause:** (a) The first version emitted after teardown, so the only knowable result was "signal sent". (b) `controller.edit_text` ends the preview session on EVERY attempt (`pdf_controller.py:2817`), so the in-flight preview result is dropped. (c) The success path's synchronous `show_page` re-enters `display_page` -> `scene.clear()`, which deletes the proxy.
**Fix:** (a) Build the request, emit it with the editor alive, pull the real result (`consume_last_edit_result`, `_pull_edit_result` `text_editing.py:2593`) and tear down only on SUCCESS (`:2568-2582`). (b) `_not_applied` calls `invalidate_plan_preview(regenerate=True)` when `emitted` (`:2615-2630`). (c) `_detach_text_editor_before_scene_clear` removes the proxy and its mask/border items from the scene first (`pdf_view.py:4995`), and `_teardown_editor` is deleted-proxy-proof (`text_editing.py:2733-2746`, `_qt_object_alive`). The `_finalizing_text_edit` re-entry guard (`:2173`) must stay set through the whole pull.
**File:** `view/text_editing.py:2166-2200`, `:2568-2635`, `:2733`; `controller/pdf_controller.py:2817`; `view/pdf_view.py:3414-3452`, `:4995`

## Switching the active document session before finalize commits the edit into the wrong document, and a plan token cannot tell byte-identical copies apart
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`finalize_text_edit_before_session_change`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`_refuse_foreign_session`), `view/text_editing.py` (session stamp)
**Symptom:** Opening another document with an inline editor open applied the un-committed edit to the NEW active document (the active session changed before finalize ran); with a byte-identical copy open the token still "verified".
**Cause:** The session-changing code switched the active session before finalize ran; the token is derived from content, so a copy with identical bytes accepts it; reading the session id at finalize time reads the new session.
**Fix:** Finalize against the still-active session first (`SESSION_SWITCH`, `pdf_view.py:5037-5044`, called before the switch at `pdf_controller.py:1366`); stamp `editing_session_id` when the editor OPENS (`text_editing.py:1958-1964`); every request carries it and the controller refuses a mismatch with zero mutation and a notice, never a modal (`pdf_controller.py:2905-2921`); add-textbox carries it as a positional argument (Task B).
**File:** `view/pdf_view.py:5037`, `controller/pdf_controller.py:1366`, `:2905`, `view/text_editing.py:1958`

## An in-flight async result is fresh only if its generation matches, so every input that changes the preview must bump it at a chokepoint
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`PreviewBackedInlineTextEditor`: `configure_render_context`, `_schedule_preview`, `invalidate_plan_preview`, `apply_plan_preview`, `set_plan_preview_state`)
**Symptom:** Changing font or size while a plan preview was in flight let the OLD result arrive with the same generation and set a token for a preview the user no longer saw; a refusal recorded right after a re-arm vanished immediately.
**Cause:** The generation was bumped only in the `textChanged` handler; font/size went through `configure_render_context` -> `_regenerate_preview` and requested a new raster under the SAME generation. Generation-keyed state (`set_plan_preview_state`) is ignored for any generation but the current one, so writing it BEFORE the bump that re-arming performs wipes it.
**Fix:** Bump at the chokepoint, not per handler: `configure_render_context` bumps when any render input actually changed (`text_editing.py:1002-1013`), `_schedule_preview` bumps synchronously per keystroke (`:1062`), `invalidate_plan_preview` covers drags and document mutations (`:1030-1043`); `apply_plan_preview` rejects `generation != self._plan_generation` (`:1371-1376`). Write generation-keyed state AFTER the re-arm (`_not_applied`, `:2625-2640`). Any new preview input (a new style control) must go through `configure_render_context` or call `invalidate_plan_preview`.
**File:** `view/text_editing.py:1002`, `:1030`, `:1062`, `:1371-1397`, `:2615-2640`

## A preview-side `no_change` gate hides style and position overrides, so the view must rewrite the reason the way the commit side does
**Area:** `model/text_commit/plan.py` (gate order), `view/text_edit_reasons.py` (`effective_rejection_reason`), `view/text_editing.py` (`current_rejection_reason`)
**Symptom:** Changing only the font, size or position (text unchanged) showed no refusal reason, or "nothing changed", while the commit side said "style/geometry override needs a rebuild"; paragraph mode showed "text not found" for a multi-line target the commit would call `multi_span_target`.
**Cause:** The plan checks `NO_CHANGE` BEFORE the style/geometry overrides (`plan.py:1874` vs `:1886-1891`; order pinned by structural-gate tests), so a preview of a restyled or dragged editor reports `no_change`. The preview also cannot resolve a multi-line target at all (`target_unresolved`).
**Fix:** One shared view-side rewrite (`text_edit_reasons.py:183-218`): cross-page move -> `cross_page_move_requires_rebuild`; paragraph + `target_unresolved` -> `multi_span_target`; `no_change` + position -> `geometry_override_present`, + style -> `style_override_present`, otherwise None (a true no-op). The editor and the controller toast both go through it (`text_editing.py:2279-2300`). Never reorder the plan gates to "fix" a message.
**File:** `model/text_commit/plan.py:1874-1891`, `view/text_edit_reasons.py:183`, `view/text_editing.py:2279`

## Whether a finalize clears the scene depends on the branch actually taken, not on the caller
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`display_page`, `initialize_continuous_placeholders`, `reset_document_view`), finalize reasons in `view/text_editing.py`
**Symptom:** A search jump or page change in continuous mode finalized (committed or discarded) the open inline editor although the scene was never rebuilt, so the user's input was lost for no reason.
**Cause:** The same `display_page` call clears the scene only in single-page mode; in continuous mode it only calls `update_page_in_scene` + `scroll_to_page`. `change_scale` -> `initialize_continuous_placeholders` always clears. Callers finalized by call site, not by branch.
**Fix:** Finalize with `SCENE_REBUILD` (a close-always reason that commits a verified edit or discards visibly) only where `scene.clear()` really follows: `display_page` computes `keeps_scene = not pix.isNull() and continuous_pages and page_items` and skips the finalize when True (`pdf_view.py:3414-3423`); `initialize_continuous_placeholders` and `reset_document_view` always finalize (`:3346-3362`, `:3087-3095`). A zoom uses the keep policy (`VIEW_RESCALE`, see the release helpers at `pdf_view.py:3565-3600`). An action aimed only at ANOTHER document must not rebuild the active scene; a cancellable action confirms first and finalizes second.
**File:** `view/pdf_view.py:3414`, `:3346`, `:3087`, `:3565`; `view/text_editing.py:236-262` (reason sets)

## A new mode flag must be decided per editor intent, through one intent-aware chokepoint, and the creator must use the argument, not the view state
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`_plan_preview_applies`, `create_text_editor`), `view/pdf_view.py` (`_text_plan_preview_required`)
**Symptom:** The add-text-box editor (`add_new`) was treated as a true-text edit: empty-page previews returned `target_unresolved`, Apply was permanently disabled, plan mode painted no text, the rebuild button bypassed consent and called `add_textbox`; over existing text it was handed a token that belonged to the text underneath.
**Cause:** Plan mode, the preview hook, the Apply token gate, the refusal state and the rebuild offer were all keyed on the mode flag `_text_plan_preview_required`, never on the editor's intent. And `create_text_editor` decided plan mode before `view.editing_intent` was updated, so it read the PREVIOUS editor's intent.
**Fix:** One chokepoint: `_plan_preview_applies(intent)` is True only for `edit_existing` AND the flag (`text_editing.py:2212-2227`). It is the only read of the flag in the module, locked by a test that counts reads (`test_text_commit_add_text_intent.py:411`). `create_text_editor` passes the intent as an ARGUMENT (`:1950-1953`). Any new per-editor mode must be evaluated for `edit_existing`, `add_new` and drag/rebuild in that one function.
**File:** `view/text_editing.py:1950`, `:2212`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_add_text_intent.py:411`

## Shared panel state must be re-synced at teardown, not only while a live editor exists
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`_sync_text_property_panel_state`, `_sync_text_apply_enabled`, `_sync_text_refusal_state`), `view/text_editing.py` (`_teardown_editor`)
**Symptom:** After an editor closed, the previous refusal reason and the "改用重建文字…" button stayed visible and Apply could remain enabled in the shared text card.
**Cause:** The panel sync early-returned or skipped the refusal/Apply refresh when there was no live editor, so the last editor's state outlived it.
**Fix:** `_teardown_editor` ends with `_sync_text_property_panel_state()` (`text_editing.py:2799-2801`), which ALWAYS calls `_sync_text_apply_enabled()` (`pdf_view.py:2394-2398`); with no live editor `_sync_text_refusal_state` hides the label and button and Apply is disabled (`:2314-2345`). Any new shared widget fed by an editor property must be reset on that path.
**File:** `view/pdf_view.py:2314`, `:2385`; `view/text_editing.py:2733`

## Hiding, disabling or clicking a disabled focused button hands focus to a ClickFocus ancestor and triggers a FOCUS_OUTSIDE finalize; an editor in a proxy needs the view focused first
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`text_card`, `_on_text_rebuild_clicked`, focus guard), `view/text_editing.py` (`_not_applied`)
**Symptom:** Pressing Apply while the preview was pending (or after a refusal re-armed the preview and momentarily disabled/hid the focused button) finalized FOCUS_OUTSIDE and committed or discarded the unverified text. Calling `editor.setFocus()` alone did not restore typing.
**Cause:** A press on a disabled child, or hiding a focused child, gives focus to the first ClickFocus ancestor; that was `rightPanel`, outside the edit context, so the app-level focus net finalized (`pdf_view.py:2745-2760`). An editor inside a `QGraphicsProxyWidget` only moves the scene's focus item with `setFocus()`; the keyboard focus stays elsewhere.
**Fix:** `text_card.setFocusPolicy(Qt.ClickFocus)` makes the card itself the edit-context focus target (`pdf_view.py:2117-2126`). After a declined or refused rebuild, hand focus back to the editor (`:2299-2312`). After a refused Apply, call `graphics_view.setFocus()` BEFORE `editor.setFocus()` (`text_editing.py:2655-2670`), before the delayed 40 ms FOCUS_OUTSIDE check (`pdf_view.py:2739-2741`) can overwrite the result.
**File:** `view/pdf_view.py:2117`, `:2299`, `:2706-2760`; `view/text_editing.py:2655-2670`

## Clicking the page-number box during an edit is a focus-outside finalize that commits the CURRENT token before any page change
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`page_number_input`, focus guard), umbrella `test_scripts/test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py`
**Symptom:** A stale-token test that "switched page through the page box" went red for the wrong reason; the real user path shows the edit is committed (with the current verified token) the moment the box takes focus.
**Cause:** The page box is outside the edit context, so the focus change finalizes FOCUS_OUTSIDE before any `sig_page_changed`; focus-outside is a keep-reason that commits a verified edit. Only a canvas-keeping switch (wheel) keeps the editor open. An earlier test drove the box with focus + keys and no event processing, so the finalize ran after the switch (synthetic-timing red).
**Fix:** The test for "a page switch invalidates the token" uses real wheel events (`_wheel_until_page`) and documents that the page box cannot reach that case (`test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py:1436-1442`, `:1475-1481`); the product behavior (commit-before-switch on a verified token) was probed on 2026-09-30 and is documented there, not asserted by a test. Assert delivery order, not token strings (tokens are content-derived).
**File:** `view/pdf_view.py:1602`, `:2745-2760`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py:1436`, `:1475`

## Pressing Apply during an input-method composition used to drop the preedit (measurable only offscreen)
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`InlineTextEditor.inputMethodEvent`, finalize composing branch, `apply_permitted`)
**Symptom:** With an IME composition pending, Apply (or a click away) committed the text WITHOUT the composition, so the composed characters were silently lost; the recorded session showed "專案" replacing the selection only on Enter and "示範" vanishing on click-away.
**Cause:** `toPlainText()` excludes the preedit; the plan token was generated for the committed-only text and stayed valid, so every finalize path committed text that lacked what the user was typing. This was found as a red offscreen test before the product defect was confirmed on video.
**Fix:** Part 5 A1 (see the two IME entries at the end for the display half): the editor tracks the preedit (`text_editing.py:375-389`); `current_plan_token()` returns None while composing (`:1424`); `apply_permitted()` is False while composing, before the add-box exemption (`:2248`); finalize treats a preedit as un-applied input for every intent: keep-reasons keep the editor and the preedit with a notice, close-always reasons discard visibly, never commit the text-without-preedit (`:2420-2436`); `has_unapplied_input` counts a preedit (`:2721`). Escape belongs to the IME while composing (`:344-348`, `pdf_view.py` `_handle_escape`).
**File:** `view/text_editing.py:375`, `:1424`, `:2248`, `:2420`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_finalize_policy.py:802-1043`

## Normalize an injected settings DTO at one chokepoint, and dataclasses.replace carries the already-resolved derived field
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`text_commit_settings` property setter), `model/text_commit/dto.py` (`TextCommitSettings.__post_init__`)
**Symptom:** A model built with `text_commit_settings=None` read as "no engine" and fell through to the legacy path in some readers; `dataclasses.replace(TextCommitSettings(engine="legacy"), ...)` kept `preview="plan"` under the legacy engine (incoherent pair: Apply would commit something other than what was previewed).
**Cause:** (a) Each reader guessed what `None` meant. (b) `preview` defaults to an `"auto"` sentinel resolved in `__post_init__`; `replace()` copies the RESOLVED value, so changing `engine` does not re-derive `preview`.
**Fix:** (a) The property setter is the chokepoint: `None` becomes the shipped tiered defaults (`pdf_model.py:264-270`), fail-closed like the consent gate, never a silent legacy path. (b) Pass `preview=` explicitly in any `replace(settings, engine=...)` (documented at `dto.py:321-322`). Related entries: "The engine default lives in two literals in dto.py", "A consent gate sized for an opt-in becomes a modal ... when the flag ships on".
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py:261-280`, `model/text_commit/dto.py:295-335`

## Flipping a default exposes every side effect that depended on the old default
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`_draw_all_block_outlines`, `text_target_mode_combo`, `_on_current_page_switched`), shipped-default flip (critique step 12)
**Symptom:** After making `run` the shipped target mode and `plan` the shipped preview: (a) the visible pages' text index was no longer built before the first hover, so the first click in run mode paid index build + grouping in one GUI event (HVAC p6 cold click 222/294 ms vs 150 ms target); (b) the mode-dependent controller state was never initialised because the combo already held the target value; (c) page jumps no longer triggered the viewport-debounced work.
**Cause:** (a) Index pre-build was a side effect of the paragraph-outline pass, which returns early in run mode. (b) `setCurrentIndex(findData("run"))` before `connect` emits no `currentIndexChanged`. (c) `show_page` calls `scroll_to_page(emit_viewport_changed=False)`, so a page jump never reaches the debounce.
**Fix:** (a) A `prewarm_only` branch of the outline pass builds the visible pages' index in its own event for run mode (`pdf_view.py:4877-4897`). (b) Call the handler once explicitly after panels are built (`:808-811`; combo created `:2166-2170`). (c) Hook `_on_current_page_switched` to `_schedule_outline_redraw` (`:5015-5027`). Procedure for any default flip: list every behavior that only happened because of the old default (index builds, signals not firing when the value is already the target, debounce triggers) and add a test per item.
**File:** `view/pdf_view.py:808`, `:2166`, `:4877`, `:5015`

## PySide6 Signal(int) silently truncates a float
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`sig_add_textbox`), `model/edit_commands.py` (`AddTextboxCommand`), `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`add_textbox`)
**Symptom:** A 10.5 pt text box was created at 10 pt: the signal declared `int` for the size slot, and emitting 10.5 delivers 10 with no error (measured: `Signal(int).emit(10.5)` -> `[10]`). `AddTextboxCommand` additionally stored `int(size)`.
**Cause:** PySide6 coerces the argument to the declared C++ type at emit time. The font-size rule ("sizes stay float", see the existing font-size entry) was applied in the model but not at the signal boundary.
**Fix:** Declare `float` (`pdf_view.py:487`: `Signal(int, object, str, str, float, tuple, object)`) and store `float(size)` in the command (`edit_commands.py:866-876`). Residual: `PDFModel.add_textbox` (`pdf_model.py:2906`) and `pdf_object_ops.add_textbox` (`:707`) still annotate `size: int = 12`; harmless at runtime, correct when touched. Audit every `Signal(...)` carrying a font size, coordinate or other float.
**File:** `view/pdf_view.py:487`, `model/edit_commands.py:866`, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_small_defects.py:67`, `:84`

## A plan-mode "kept" notice must follow the editor's actual state, not only `emitted` or `already_refused`
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`_kept_notice`, `_not_applied`)
**Symptom:** Ctrl+S with a kept editor said "preview still updating" (promising a token) while the plan preview had already REFUSED the input and no token would ever arrive.
**Cause:** The notice for `SAVE_SHORTCUT` branched on `emitted` and `already_refused` only; in plan mode a refusal can be recorded by the PREVIEW (`plan_rejection_reason()`) without any emit, so neither flag is set.
**Fix:** Choose the wording from the editor's state: `if already_refused or self.current_rejection_reason()` -> name the refusal (`_SAVE_ALREADY_REFUSED_KEPT_NOTICE`), else "preview still updating" (`text_editing.py:2705-2709`). Every notice that says "wait" must first prove a token can still arrive. Save-path notices also must not claim "document unchanged" because the save still happens (`_SAVE_NOT_INCLUDED`, `:278`).
**File:** `view/text_editing.py:2682-2710`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_finalize_policy.py` (`-k "test_save_with or test_save_without"`)

## Fullscreen reaches finalize through set_mode("browse"), a view action that borrows a mode switch and therefore discards
**Area:** `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`enter_fullscreen`), `view/pdf_view.py` (`set_mode`, `release_text_editor_for_fullscreen`)
**Symptom:** Pressing F5 with an unverified or refused inline edit discarded the input with a "mode switch" warning (finalize reason `mode_switch`, not `fullscreen`) and cleared search state and the mode before the user could decide; with a verified token it committed.
**Cause:** `enter_fullscreen` normalized the view by calling `set_mode("browse")`, and `set_mode` finalizes with `MODE_SWITCH` (a close-always reason: commit-if-verified, else discard). A view action that only borrows a mode switch inherited the discard policy, and the search/snapshot clearing ran before the finalize.
**Fix:** Owner decision (2026-10-05): fullscreen mirrors zoom. `enter_fullscreen` settles the editor FIRST via `release_text_editor_for_fullscreen()` (`FULLSCREEN`, a keep reason): a verified edit commits, un-applied input keeps the editor with a warning and F5 enters nothing and clears nothing (`pdf_controller.py:1251-1259`); only then search, snapshot and `set_mode("browse")` run. Any new action that goes through `set_mode` must be assigned a finalize policy explicitly.
**File:** `controller/pdf_controller.py:1251-1272`, `view/pdf_view.py:2506`, `:3565-3600`

## Time-to-token jumps from about 1.3 s to about 16 s when open-time background work has not settled (inferred cause)
**Area:** `controller/pdf_controller.py` (open-time render/thumbnail scheduling), latency harnesses, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py` (`wait_preview`)
**Symptom:** On HVAC p6, entering edit mode and clicking within about 450 ms of opening, with background work still running, gave a 15.0-16.8 s time-to-token (about 1.3 s when quiet) and a 201-253 ms cold click; the first umbrella case's preview phase took 15.6 s (p5) and 16.5 s (p6). A user who edits a big file right after opening sees Apply disabled for over ten seconds.
**Cause:** INFERRED, not proven: after open, background render/thumbnail workers (2-4 still running after the click) appear to hold the GIL against the main-thread/QThread preview work. Measuring after quiescing the background removes the symptom, so a quiet-state latency number hides it.
**Fix:** Not fixed (listed as a latency item out of part 5 scope). Rule for latency measurements: report both the quiet and the not-quiesced case, and never publish only the quiesced number. Related existing entry: "Open-time background work can steal responsiveness from the first visible page".
**File:** `controller/pdf_controller.py` (open-time scheduling), `test_scripts/test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py:480` (`wait_preview`, `PREVIEW_TIMEOUT_S`); evidence in the mother plan, 2026-10-02 VERIFY part 4 (latency table)

## In offscreen Qt a modal never returns, so an unexpected exception in a controller-level test hangs pytest instead of failing it
**Area:** `view/message_boxes.py` (`show_error`, `confirm_degraded_fallback`), test harness `close()` paths, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py`
**Symptom:** The whole pytest run stalls with no failure; `faulthandler` only dumps stacks and does not end the process. Also a teardown `view.close()` hangs when the "unsaved changes" prompt appears.
**Cause:** Any unexpected exception in a controller path reaches `show_error` (`QMessageBox.critical`) and any dirty close reaches the save prompt; under the offscreen platform there is nobody to answer the modal.
**Fix:** The umbrella `_App` records and answers every `QMessageBox` entry point with a safe default ("question" -> No), patches `QMessageBox.exec`, and patches `show_error` / `confirm_degraded_fallback` at the NAMES the using modules hold (`test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py:300-320`); its `close()` ends preview work first (a running QThread aborts on widget destruction) and replaces `controller.handle_app_close` with `event.accept()` before `view.close()` (`:524-540`). Controller/view tests must either stub the modals or assert on a recorded modal list; an orphan editor must not count as unsaved input at teardown.
**File:** `view/message_boxes.py:12-18`, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py:300-320`, `:524-540`, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_finalize_policy.py:552-611`

## Test stubs must accept *args and **kwargs, and monkeypatches must target the name the using module holds
**Area:** `test_scripts/test_text_commit_*.py` (verify/engine stubs, controller-level monkeypatching)
**Symptom:** (a) A verify stub with fixed positional parameters broke the moment production added a keyword (`observed=`). (b) A "force refusal" test passed for the wrong reason because the patch never took effect.
**Cause:** (a) Over-specific stub signatures duplicate the production signature. (b) After `from x import f`, patching `x.f` does not change the already-bound name in the using module.
**Fix:** Write stubs as `def _spy(model, page_num, visual_rect, text, *args, **kwargs)` and delegate (`test_text_commit_small_defects.py:92-94`; `test_text_commit_shadow_mode.py:190`). Patch where the name is used: the umbrella patches `controller_module.confirm_degraded_fallback` and `show_error` on each importing module (`test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py:311-318`). For a "forced X" test also assert that the X path was actually taken (a spy on the legacy engine, the dialog recorder), not just the absence of success.
**File:** `test_scripts/test_text_commit_small_defects.py:92`, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py:311`

## In offscreen tests QTest.keyClicks with CJK terminates the process, and QTest focus plus keys without event processing causes false reds
**Area:** `test_scripts/test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py` (`type_replacing_all`, `pump`), any Qt test that types text
**Symptom:** `QTest.keyClicks(editor, "專案")` under the offscreen platform ends the process at once (exit 127, no traceback, no faulthandler output). Separately, a test that sent focus and key events back to back without processing events failed: the delayed focus-out finalize ran after the later action.
**Cause:** (a) Offscreen has no keymap for CJK key events. (b) `focus_outside` finalize is deferred through `QTimer.singleShot(40, ...)` (`pdf_view.py:2739`, handler `:2741`), which only fires when the event loop runs.
**Fix:** Type Latin/digits with `keyClicks` and CJK with `QInputMethodEvent` carrying a commit string, sent via `QApplication.sendEvent` (`type_replacing_all`, `:457-480`, module docstring `:12`). Drive sequences through `pump(ms)` (`:380`), which processes events, between steps. Do not model preedit input with `keyClicks`; use `QInputMethodEvent` with a preedit string and attributes.
**File:** `test_scripts/test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py:12`, `:457-480`, `:380`; `view/pdf_view.py:2739`

## Flipping a behavior policy makes tests that depended on the old behavior pass vacuously
**Area:** `test_scripts/test_text_commit_characterization.py`, `test_text_commit_no_silent_legacy.py` and similar tests written against the old default
**Symptom:** After "no silent legacy" and the shipped-default flip, tests did not go red: strict-engine xfails and "the text is still there" drag tests kept passing because the edit was now refused, so nothing was ever edited and the assertion held trivially.
**Cause:** A test that asserts on the OLD outcome (text unchanged, no exception, xfail) is satisfied by the NEW refusal. Counting failures is the wrong audit.
**Fix:** After any policy flip, grep for tests whose setup relied on the old branch and make each assert that the intended new branch was taken: characterization xfails were reworded to "xfail because refused", the old `test_legacy_kill_switch_moves_without_asking` was turned into three tests with the new expectations (`test_text_commit_no_silent_legacy.py`, 3 failed / 29 passed in the part 5 red run), and the legacy-engine spy is asserted called/not called (`:150`). Sibling: "Single-item TJ admission moves ordinary PyMuPDF insert_text pages to Tier 0".
**File:** `test_scripts/test_text_commit_no_silent_legacy.py:150`, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_characterization.py`

## subprocess-captured pytest output must be decoded as UTF-8 or a cp950 reader thread crashes
**Area:** test/harness code that runs `pytest` (or any zh-TW-printing tool) through `subprocess` and reads the pipe
**Symptom:** The harness's pipe reader thread died with `UnicodeDecodeError` on this machine (locale cp950) while the child's output was fine, losing the run's output.
**Cause:** `text=True` / default decoding uses `locale.getpreferredencoding()`, not the child's UTF-8.
**Fix:** Same rule as the existing entry "Subprocess text I/O silently depends on the caller's locale, not the child's": read captured output with `encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"` and set `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` / `PYTHONUTF8=1` in the child's `env`. Applies to any driver that captures pytest output from a subprocess, not only to the two tests named there.
**File:** `test_scripts/test_performance_script_runner.py`, `test_scripts/test_security_packaging.py` (the existing entry's files); any stage driver that captures pytest output through `subprocess`

## QImage(Format_RGBA8888).fill(uint) takes raw byte order, not 0xAARRGGBB
**Area:** `test_scripts/test_text_commit_plan_preview_no_css.py` (and any test that fills or reads QImage pixels)
**Symptom:** A raster filled with `0xAARRGGBB` on an `RGBA8888` image shows the wrong colours and `pixel()` returns swapped channels, so a "red CSS frame" or "solid verified frame" marker is not recognisable.
**Cause:** The `uint` passed to `fill` for `Format_RGBA8888` is interpreted as memory byte order (0xAABBGGRR on little-endian), while `Format_ARGB32` uses 0xAARRGGBB.
**Fix:** Use `QImage.Format_ARGB32` for synthetic marker images and compare after `convertToFormat(QImage.Format_ARGB32)` (`test_text_commit_plan_preview_no_css.py:44-50`, `:77`, `:85`). Never mix a hand-written ARGB constant with an RGBA8888 buffer.
**File:** `test_scripts/test_text_commit_plan_preview_no_css.py:44`, `:77`

## Same-batch Qt tests can abort natively depending on order
**Area:** `test_scripts/test_page_render_coordinator.py`, `test_scripts/test_page_reorder.py` (batch ordering in the full suite)
**Symptom:** `Fatal Python error: Aborted` (Qt native abort, reported at `test_page_reorder.py` lines 159/198) twice in the same batch while the same two files run together alone pass (32 passed). It looks like a regression in the change under test.
**Cause:** Order-dependent native teardown between Qt-heavy tests in one process (page_render_coordinator then page_reorder); not caused by the change under review. Not fully root-caused.
**Fix:** Do not "fix" the code under test. Run the two files alone to confirm, and run ONE pytest process at a time (a concurrent pytest also aborts Qt tests, per CLAUDE.md). Treat a native abort that disappears in isolation as an ordering/teardown issue and record it, do not mark the stage red for it.
**File:** `test_scripts/test_page_reorder.py:159`, `:198`; `test_scripts/test_page_render_coordinator.py`

## A harness "shipped defaults" leg must clear TEXT_COMMIT_* before main.run, and a scratch harness that deletes the env afterwards still measures the env configuration
**Area:** `test_scripts/test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py` (`_App.__init__`, `shipped=True`), `model/text_commit/dto.py` (`TextCommitSettings.from_env`, `:340`), any latency/measurement harness
**Symptom:** A latency harness reported "shipped" numbers that were really the env-configured configuration: the variables were removed only after `main.run` had already read them. (Found in an untracked scratch latency harness; the tracked umbrella's positive shipped leg does not have this flaw.)
**Cause:** `TextCommitSettings` reads `TEXT_COMMIT_*` once at composition (`dto.py:367`, `_choice`); deleting the variables later changes nothing for the running app.
**Fix:** Remove the variables BEFORE the app is built: the umbrella `_App` `delenv`s every `ACCEPTANCE_ENV` name (and `_UNSET_ENV`) in the constructor when `shipped=True` (`test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py:290-298`) and asserts the shipped configuration explicitly (`test_shipped_text_commit_defaults_are_the_acceptance_configuration`, `:1677`). Note the negative cases always start from the env (there is no shipped-default negative leg). A "shipped" claim needs a check of the live settings object, not of `os.environ`.
**File:** `test_scripts/test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py:282-298`, `:1677`; `model/text_commit/dto.py:340`, `:367`

## PySide6 has no QRect(QRectF) constructor, so a try/except around the conversion silently made the IME cursor-rect widening dead code
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`InlineTextEditor.inputMethodQuery`)
**Symptom:** The IME candidate window got a zero-width anchor. The caret is hidden (cursor width 0) in plan mode until the first key press, and `inputMethodQuery(Qt.ImCursorRectangle)` returned `rect.width() == 0`; the widening override never took effect and nothing logged an error.
**Cause:** In Qt6 `QTextEdit.inputMethodQuery(ImCursorRectangle)` returns a `QRectF`. PySide6's `QRect` has no `QRectF` constructor (verified here: `TypeError: QRect.__init__(QRectF)`; only `QRect(QRect)`, `QRect(int,int,int,int)`, point/size overloads). The first draft converted with `QRect(value)` inside a try/except, so the TypeError was swallowed and the original zero-width rect was returned.
**Fix:** Keep the value a `QRectF` and widen it directly: `if isinstance(value, QRectF) and value.width() < 1.0: widened = QRectF(value); widened.setWidth(1.0); return widened` (`text_editing.py:391-402`; `QRectF` is imported at `:10`). The test asserts `rect.width() > 0 and rect.height() > 0` (`test_text_commit_finalize_policy.py:1038-1039`) with the precondition `editor.cursorWidth() == 0`. Never wrap a Qt type conversion in a bare try/except whose except branch is the success path of the surrounding feature.
**File:** `view/text_editing.py:391-402`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_finalize_policy.py:1025-1039`

## The plan-mode editor never calls QTextEdit's native paint and toPlainText() excludes the IME preedit, so a composition was invisible and a token for the committed-only text could commit while composing
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`PreviewBackedInlineTextEditor.paintEvent`, `_paint_composing_frame`, `current_plan_token`, finalize composing branch)
**Symptom:** On a real IME recording (`ecc-dwg.pdf`): select all, type "專案" -> the screen did not change until Enter; type "示範" -> not shown either, and clicking outside committed only "專案". The composition was neither visible nor safe.
**Cause:** (1) Plan mode paints the last verified raster (or the frozen original frame) plus UI chrome and deliberately never delegates to `QTextEdit.paintEvent` (`paintEvent` `:1165-1172`, `_paint_plan_mode_frame` `:1286`), so the in-layout preedit never appears; the frozen-frame short-circuit would also hide it. (2) `toPlainText()` contains only committed text, so the verified token (computed for that text) stayed valid during composition and every finalize path (Apply, click-away) committed text without the composition. Hypothesis A "the proxy editor never receives the preedit event" was tested and rejected (events reach the real focus widget, the graphics view); hypothesis B (our paint path) was the cause. Offscreen tests can prove logic and pixels but not the real candidate-window appearance (Stage E).
**Fix:** Track the preedit in `inputMethodEvent` (`:375-389`). Paint it as UI chrome BEFORE the frozen-frame short-circuit: `if self._preedit_text: self._paint_composing_frame(); return` (`:1159-1164`; `_paint_composing_frame` draws the base frame plus the "組字中" badge and a chip with the preedit underlined, `:1245-1284`, `:1252-1264`), keeping the rule that native glyphs never overlay the page. While composing: `current_plan_token()` is None (`:1421-1431`), `plan_preview_pending()` is True (`:1230`), Apply is not permitted (`:2248`), keep-reasons keep editor and preedit, close-always reasons discard with a visible notice (`:2420-2436`). Qt itself bumps the generation at composition start/end (`textChanged`, measured 10 -> 11 -> 12), so cancelling the composition re-previews and Apply returns without a keystroke.
**File:** `view/text_editing.py:375-389`, `:1151-1172`, `:1230`, `:1245-1284`, `:1421-1431`, `:2248`, `:2420-2436`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_finalize_policy.py:1043` (`test_a_preedit_is_visible_in_the_editor_paint`); `test_scripts/test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py` (`test_ui_apply_during_an_ime_preedit_never_commits_the_text_without_it`)

## A secure save (garbage=4) renumbers the LIVE document's xrefs in memory, even for a save to a new path, so xref-keyed patch sets go stale and undo must relocate by content
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`_save_doc`, `_atomic_full_save`, secure save paths), `model/edit_commands.py` (`EditTextCommand._relocated_patchset`, `_apply_retained_patchset`)
**Symptom:** After a secure save (any save while `secure_save_required` is set, even `save_as` to a different file) Ctrl+Z / redo of an earlier Tier 0/1 edit failed `STALE` with zero mutation although the document had not been edited since: the retained PatchSets name page/stream xrefs that now belong to other objects. Measured on 1.27.1 with a synthetic two-page document holding one unreferenced object: `doc.save(path, garbage=4)` to a NEW path reduced `xref_length` from 10 to 9 on the same handle with no reopen; and the persistence test asserts `model.doc[0].xref != page_xref` after the save.
**Cause:** `doc.save(..., garbage=4)` compacts the object table of the open handle in place. `_atomic_full_save` always passes `garbage=max(4, ...)` (`pdf_model.py:3420`), and the secure paths pass the live handle (`:3917-3923`, `:4079-4087`); only non-secure saves use `garbage=0` (`_save_doc` default, `:3381`). History is keyed by PAGE, but each `EditTextCommand` retained xref-keyed forward/inverse PatchSets and stream storage.
**Fix:** Record the page's xref layout at commit (`_tier0_layout`, `edit_commands.py:279-285`, `:576`; `_page_xref_layout`, `:609`). On a stale replay, if the layout really moved, relocate by content: find the one content stream whose decoded bytes EXACTLY equal the expected bytes, require it unique in `/Contents`, and require that no other page shares it (`find_pages_sharing_content_stream`; `garbage=4` merges identical objects, patching a shared one would edit another page), re-key the patch set and fingerprint, and re-key the opposite side (`:628-720`). The splice still re-checks bytes and digest, so the identity gate is unchanged; captured storage dictionaries are dropped because they hold pre-renumbering references (`:710-715`). An unchanged layout with a failing fingerprint is genuine staleness and still refuses. (Part 5 final review: relocation is admitted only when a renumbering-invariant fingerprint also matches, see the entry "A relocation that re-derives the page fingerprint from the current page accepts any change".)
**File:** `model/edit_commands.py:279-285`, `:576`, `:609-720`; `model/pdf_model.py:3381`, `:3420`, `:3917`, `:4079`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_persistence.py:458-640`

## page.annots() iteration is O(n^2) on annotation-heavy pages; use page.annot_xrefs() when only identity is needed
**Area:** `model/edit_commands.py` (`EditTextCommand._page_xref_layout`), `model/text_commit/inspect.py` (`_annotation_entries`, page fingerprint)
**Symptom:** 19-80 ms per call on `hvac-dwg` p6 (367 annotations on p5, about 125 ms of the Apply rebind); the layout capture runs on every Tier 0/1 commit and every relocation, and the fingerprint on every rebind. Measured here on a synthetic page with 300 text annotations: iterating `annots()` about 50 ms vs `annot_xrefs()` about 0.06 ms.
**Cause:** `page.annots()` builds a full Annot object per entry and PyMuPDF finds each by walking the page's annotation list: O(n^2).
**Fix:** Take identity from `page.annot_xrefs()` (one read of /Annots): `_page_xref_layout` (`edit_commands.py:609-626`). Where the rect is needed too, `_annotation_entries` walks the list once (`first_annot`/`next`), keeping the `annots()` order and Link/Popup/Widget filter, and still loads any xref the walk did not reach (`inspect.py:511-540`). A test pins that the layout never calls `page.annots()` (`test_text_commit_persistence.py:610`, `test_page_xref_layout_never_walks_page_annots`).
**File:** `model/edit_commands.py:609`, `model/text_commit/inspect.py:511`, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_persistence.py:610`

## The pending_page_maintenance gate is retired: fidelity protection already stops clean_contents on Tier 0/1 pages, and an editor kept open across a save needs a fresh preview session
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`apply_pending_redactions`), `model/text_commit/dto.py` (`PENDING_MAINTENANCE`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`save`, `save_as`, `_invalidate_inline_editor_preview`)
**Symptom:** (a) Same-page true-text edits after an add-text-box/rebuild were refused (the entry on the flag above). (b) After retiring the gate, an editor opened BEFORE a save and kept open across it was refused "preview is stale" on Apply, because the save had cleaned the page the preview session had snapshotted.
**Cause:** The gate (HEAD `plan.py:1895-1898`, "page has pending legacy cleanup that may run clean_contents", introduced with Tier 0 in `5615d4c`) guarded against a later `clean_contents` destroying byte identity. That fear is already handled: `apply_pending_redactions` skips every page in `fidelity_protected_pages` (`pdf_model.py:3673-3699`) and keeps its pending entries, and a Tier 0/1 commit protects its page. A 14-case spike (`add_textbox`, then bypass the gate and call `_prepare`) produced 14/14 `PreparedEdit`s, so multi-stream `/Contents` after an add does not turn the refusal into another refusal.
**Fix:** Remove the refusal and the `page_has_pending_maintenance` parameter everywhere (planner, engine, preview session input, `pdf_text_edit.py`, controller); keep the enum value `PENDING_MAINTENANCE = "pending_page_maintenance"` (`dto.py:52`, never rename a declared code) with a retirement note. After `save` / `save_as` the controller calls `_invalidate_inline_editor_preview()` (`pdf_controller.py:2030-2052`, defined `:794`), which ends the preview session and has the view drop the token and re-preview against the cleaned page. A guard test asserts the planner no longer has the parameter (`test_text_commit_pending_maintenance_retired.py:206`).
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py:3664-3699`, `model/text_commit/dto.py:52`, `controller/pdf_controller.py:794`, `:2030-2052`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_pending_maintenance_retired.py:96-300`

## Save-hook chokepoint: ToolManager.prepare_doc_for_save refuses and rolls back any hook that rewrites a fidelity-protected page
**Area:** `model/tools/manager.py` (`ToolManager.prepare_doc_for_save`, `_ProtectedPageGuard`, `_check_hook`, `_abandon`)
**Symptom:** A save-time tool hook (`clean_contents`, a watermark rewrite, an OCR pass) that rewrites a page's content streams destroys the byte-for-byte proof a Tier 0/1 commit established, and does so silently, once per extension, on the LIVE document.
**Cause:** `prepare_doc_for_save` hands each extension the live document (or the previous hook's clone); nothing stopped a hook from rewriting protected pages. Appending an overlay (a watermark) is legitimate; rewriting an existing stream is not.
**Fix:** One guard at the single chokepoint, not per extension: snapshot the protected pages' decoded streams, `/Contents` key and stream storage before the hooks run (`manager.py:43-53`, `:229-239`), then after EACH hook check (a) the document it was handed, exactly, rolling a rewrite back (`violations_in_place`, `roll_back`), and (b) any returned clone, where every original stream must survive verbatim and in order but extra streams may be appended (`violations_in_clone`) (`:55-73`, `:258-293`). A violation closes the leftover clones, logs, and raises `ProtectedPageViolation` ("save refused, nothing written"); if the rollback itself fails the message says the live document may differ and advises Save As (`:294-304`). A hook that raises goes through `_abandon`, which also rolls back and logs a failed restore (`:241-256`). The guard only compares decoded bytes (see the stream-dictionary entry).
**File:** `model/tools/manager.py:31-304`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_maintenance.py:246`, `:269`, `:286`, `:302`, `:376`

## A relocation that re-derives the page fingerprint from the current page accepts any change, not only a renumbering
**Area:** `model/edit_commands.py` (`EditTextCommand._relocate`, `_apply_retained_patchset`, `_capture_tier0_reversal`), `model/text_commit/inspect.py` (`renumber_invariant_page_fingerprint`)
**Symptom:** After a Tier 0 edit, a font added to the page resources, an annotation added outside the undo stack, an OCR pass that added a content stream (or, after a renumbering save, a changed `/Rotate`, box or ExtGState) no longer made undo `STALE_UNDO`: the undo patched the stream and went on. Before part 5 the same sequence refused with zero mutation.
**Cause:** The relocation rescue ran on ANY change of the xref layout (page, content streams, fonts, annotation xrefs) and replaced `expected_page_fingerprint` with the CURRENT page's fingerprint. After that only the patched stream's own bytes were checked, so everything else `page_fingerprint` protects was silently waived. `page_fingerprint` itself cannot tell a renumbering from a change: it hashes xref numbers through six helpers (stream xrefs, font entries, `R<n>` in canonical values, annotation xrefs).
**Fix:** Store a renumbering-invariant fingerprint at commit (`renumber_invariant_page_fingerprint`, the patched stream's bytes elided) and relocate only when the current page's equals it; otherwise `STALE` with zero mutation. It re-expresses `page_fingerprint`'s coverage by CONTENT: the page graph is walked with every indirect reference replaced by the referenced object's canonical content (refs are transparent, so renumbering, merging of identical objects and direct-vs-indirect spelling do not move it; `/Parent`, `/P` and references to other pages are cut; streams are folded by decoded bytes, images by dictionary only), content streams in `/Contents` order, the default OCG visibility, and the resolved page geometry. Parameterizing `page_fingerprint` itself was not feasible without threading a mode through every helper and `marked_content`. Also exception-safe: every fingerprint, layout and storage capture the replay needs is computed BEFORE the splice, a MuPDF error anywhere is `STALE` (the stream is restored if the write itself failed), and nothing escapes `undo()`/`redo()`. Measured: 12 ms per page on `hvac-dwg.pdf` (8 pages incl. the 367-annotation page, all equal before and after a real `garbage=4` renumbering).
**File:** `model/edit_commands.py` (`_relocate`, `_apply_retained_patchset`), `model/text_commit/inspect.py` (`renumber_invariant_page_fingerprint`); `test_scripts/test_text_commit_persistence.py` (`test_undo_refuses_when_anything_but_a_renumbering_changed_the_page`, `test_undo_redo_after_a_renumbering_save_on_a_rich_page_still_work`, `test_a_raising_relocation_helper_is_stale_with_zero_mutation`)

## A document SnapshotCommand restores bytes but not the maintenance bookkeeping that travels with them
**Area:** `model/edit_commands.py` (`SnapshotCommand`, `MaintenanceBook`, `DocSnapshot`, `AddTextboxCommand`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`_capture_doc_snapshot`, `mark_page_content_dirty`, `apply_pending_redactions`)
**Symptom:** Tier 0 edit on page P (P is protected); move an image on P (a `SnapshotCommand`); undo; save. P was unprotected and pending, so `apply_pending_redactions` ran `clean_contents` over the verified Tier 0 stream and the Tier 0 undo then went STALE. Redo of the object op left the page protected although its content had been rewritten.
**Cause:** A content rewrite changes `pending_edits` and `fidelity_protected_pages` (through `mark_page_content_dirty`) next to the document. `SnapshotCommand.undo`/`execute` restored the document bytes only. Stage B had fixed the same class for `AddTextboxCommand` alone, with a private page-book.
**Fix:** One mechanism at one chokepoint. `MaintenanceBook.capture(model, pages=None)` records the book (whole document, or given page indices); `_capture_doc_snapshot` returns a `DocSnapshot` (plain `bytes` plus the book taken at the same instant), so every before/after pair of every controller call site carries it; `SnapshotCommand` restores the book on undo and on redo. Plain bytes (mocks) carry none and restore only the document. `AddTextboxCommand` uses the same class scoped to its page. Still open: structural commands do not remap page-indexed bookkeeping (`TODOS.md`). The restore itself lives in `PDFModel._restore_doc_from_snapshot` (the one function every document-snapshot restore calls), not in `SnapshotCommand`: `replace_active_document_from_snapshot` (the cross-page move's failure rollback) used to put the bytes back only, so a failed move left the source page unprotected and pending, and `pdf_object_ops._restore_delete_transaction` (a failed multi-object batch delete, SWEEP-A1: first request rewrites a protected page, a later one fails) restored bytes and `pending_edits` but not `fidelity_protected_pages` -- the next save ran `clean_contents` over the Tier 0 stream and the earlier Tier 0 edit's undo went STALE_UNDO, with no recorded command to repair it. Rule: never restore a `DocSnapshot` by reopening its bytes yourself; go through `_restore_doc_from_snapshot`.
**File:** `model/edit_commands.py` (`MaintenanceBook`, `DocSnapshot`, `SnapshotCommand`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`_capture_doc_snapshot`); `test_scripts/test_text_commit_maintenance.py` (`test_undoing_an_object_op_restores_protection_and_pending_so_save_keeps_tier0`, `test_redoing_an_object_op_reapplies_dirty_and_unprotected`, `test_replace_active_document_from_snapshot_restores_the_book_with_the_bytes`, `test_failed_batch_delete_rollback_restores_protection_with_the_bytes`, `test_failed_batch_delete_then_save_keeps_the_tier0_stream_and_its_undo`, `test_restore_doc_from_snapshot_restores_the_book_carried_by_the_snapshot`)

## The every-5th-edit clean_contents pass rewrote OTHER pages inside one edit's undo unit, so undo and redo did not restore their bytes
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`apply_pending_redactions`, `_maybe_garbage_collect`), `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`edit_text` Phase 6), `model/edit_commands.py` (`EditTextCommand`, `MaintenanceBook`)
**Symptom:** Edit page 1, then edit page 2 four times (consented rebuilds). The 5th edit also compacted page 1's content stream. Ctrl+Z of that edit restored page 2 but left page 1 in the compacted form; undo-all then redo-all ended with page 1 in a different byte state than the edited one (text and pixels equal, so nothing visible).
**Cause:** `edit_text` ends with `_maybe_garbage_collect()`, which on every 5th edit ran `apply_pending_redactions()` over EVERY queued page. `EditTextCommand` snapshots and book-keeps only its own page (`MaintenanceBook.capture(model, [page_idx])`), so bytes and queue entries of the other pages changed inside the unit with nothing to reverse them. The rule "every command that rewrites page bytes owns and reverses the queue/flag state it creates" had a rewriter no command owned.
**Fix:** `apply_pending_redactions(pages=None)` takes an optional page set; `_maybe_garbage_collect(page_idx)` passes the edited page only, so the interactive pass cleans just the page whose undo unit it runs in (that page's bytes and entry are covered by the command's after-snapshot/book). Other pages keep their bytes AND their queue entries until the save-time pass (`pages=None`), which is outside the undo history by design. Save boundary (not a defect): the save-time clean is not an undo unit either; after save, undo, redo the page is back in its edited form with its entry re-queued by the command's post book, content-equal to the saved file, and the next save writes the same compacted stream (`has_unsaved_changes` tracks content, not stream compaction).
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`apply_pending_redactions`, `_maybe_garbage_collect`); `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`edit_text`); `test_scripts/test_text_commit_maintenance.py` (`test_the_fifth_edit_pass_cleans_only_the_edited_page`, `test_undoing_the_fifth_edit_restores_every_page_s_bytes`, `test_undo_all_then_redo_all_returns_to_the_edited_bytes`, `test_undo_redo_across_a_save_requeues_the_compaction_the_save_performed`)


## An undone consented rebuild left its clean_contents entry queued, so the next save rewrote a Tier 0 page and its redo went STALE
**Area:** `model/edit_commands.py` (`EditTextCommand`, `MaintenanceBook`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`mark_page_content_dirty`, `apply_pending_redactions`)
**Symptom:** Grip-move a line with "rebuild text" consent, Ctrl+Z, edit another line of the page (Tier 0), Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Y: the redo was refused `STALE_PLAN` and stayed stuck on the redo stack (text stays "Price 2024"). Same with the order Tier 0 edit, rebuild, undo, undo, save, redo. Control without the rebuild: save leaves the page bytes untouched and the redo succeeds.
**Cause:** The consented rebuild queued `pending_edits[{page_idx}]` and dropped the page's protection (`mark_page_content_dirty`); `EditTextCommand.undo` restored page bytes and the protection membership but not the pending entry, and the after-snapshot / Tier 0 redo did not re-queue it. `AddTextboxCommand` and `SnapshotCommand` already owned this state; `EditTextCommand` was the one command that did not, so the entry survived the undo and the save ran `clean_contents` on the (now protected) Tier 0 page.
**Fix:** `EditTextCommand` captures a page-scoped `MaintenanceBook` before `edit_text` (`_pre_book`) and after the commit and reflow (`_post_book`). Undo restores the pre book through `_restore_protection_membership` (both the patch-replay and the snapshot branch); the Tier 0 forward replay and the rebuild after-snapshot redo restore the post book. A mocked model without the maintenance attributes yields no book and keeps the protection-only behaviour. The legacy `engine="legacy"` re-run redo re-queues by running `edit_text` again. Rule restated: every command that rewrites page bytes owns and reverses the queue/flag state it creates.
**File:** `model/edit_commands.py` (`EditTextCommand._pre_book`, `_post_book`, `_restore_protection_membership`, `_redo_tier0`, `_redo_from_after_snapshot`); `test_scripts/test_text_commit_pending_maintenance_retired.py` (`test_undo_and_redo_of_a_consented_rebuild_own_its_cleanup_entry`, `test_undo_of_a_rebuild_keeps_the_pending_entry_of_an_earlier_command`, `test_tier0_redo_survives_a_save_after_an_undone_rebuild`, `test_tier0_redo_survives_a_save_after_a_rebuild_undone_on_top_of_it`)


## A failed legacy rebuild rolled the page bytes back but not the maintenance book, so the next save rewrote a Tier 0 page
**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`edit_text`, `_apply_redact_insert_body`, `_verify_rebuild_edit`, `_rollback_rebuild_page`), `model/edit_commands.py` (`MaintenanceBook`)
**Symptom:** A page with an earlier verified Tier 0 edit; a consented rebuild or grip move of another line fails to fit or verify ("已回滾" error dialog). The page looks unchanged, but protection is gone and a `clean_contents` entry is queued: the next save rewrites the Tier 0 stream and Ctrl+Z of the earlier Tier 0 edit is refused (`STALE_UNDO` / `STALE_PLAN`).
**Cause:** `_apply_redact_insert_body` calls `mark_page_content_dirty` (drops protection, queues the entry) before the fit and verify steps, and every failure path restored only the page snapshot. `EditTextCommand.execute` keeps its `_pre_book` on success only and a raising command is never recorded, so no undo could repair it. A `RuntimeError` raised from inside the rewrite that no site rolled back (MuPDF, a failed sub-step) restored not even the bytes.
**Fix:** `edit_text` captures `MaintenanceBook.capture(model, [page_idx])` next to the page snapshot and every rollback goes through `_rollback_rebuild_page` (bytes first, then the book, then the block index): strategy A/B/C overflow, the two `_verify_rebuild_edit` failures and the generic `except Exception`. Those sites raise `_RebuildRolledBack` (a `RuntimeError`); any other `RuntimeError` after the rewrite started is rolled back by `edit_text` itself. Fixed at `edit_text`, not in `EditTextCommand`, because `move_text_across_pages` calls `model.edit_text` directly. Rule: any rollback of a transaction that called `mark_page_content_dirty` restores the book with the bytes.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_rollback_rebuild_page`, `_RebuildRolledBack`, `edit_text`); `test_scripts/test_text_commit_pending_maintenance_retired.py` (`test_failed_rebuild_rollback_restores_protection_and_pending[...]`, `test_failed_rebuild_rollback_keeps_an_earlier_pending_entry_once`, `test_failed_rebuild_rollback_leaves_other_pages_bookkeeping_alone`)

## The protected-page save guard decoded every protected stream before and after each extension (about 90 ms per page per save)
**Area:** `model/tools/manager.py` (`_ProtectedPageGuard`, `_StreamRecord`, `ToolManager.prepare_doc_for_save`)
**Symptom:** With all 50 pages of `hvac-dwg.pdf` protected, `ToolManager.prepare_doc_for_save` took about 4440 ms (88.8 ms per page) on every save, even when no hook touched anything.
**Cause:** The guard snapshot decoded each content stream twice (`read_page_streams`, then `capture_stream_storage`), and every post-hook check decoded every protected stream again, for all four extensions, although only the watermark tool overrides `prepare_doc_for_save`.
**Fix:** Snapshot raw bytes plus the dictionary (`_StreamRecord`); a stream whose raw bytes and `/Length`-less dictionary are unchanged is proven unchanged without decoding, and only a changed stream is decoded (the original is re-decoded from the snapshot in a scratch document; a dictionary holding an indirect reference is decoded up front because the text cannot vouch for its target). `ToolManager._cannot_have_rewritten` skips the post-hook check for an extension that does not override the hook and returned nothing. The contract is unchanged: decoded CONTENT, so a hook that only re-encodes a stream is still allowed. Measured after: about 62 ms for the same 50 protected pages (1.2 ms per page).
**File:** `model/tools/manager.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_maintenance.py` (`test_an_extension_using_the_base_no_op_is_not_re_checked`, `test_the_guard_never_decodes_a_protected_stream_that_did_not_change`, `test_a_hook_that_only_re_encodes_a_protected_stream_is_not_a_violation`)

## A refused plan preview was painted as the frozen original, so the typed text vanished (and a state-only change never repainted)
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`InlineTextEditor._paint_plan_mode_frame`, `plan_preview_pending`, `plan_preview_refused`, `set_plan_preview_state`)
**Symptom:** Real-IME field run on `ecc-dwg.pdf`: the owner typed a character that is not in the subset font; after the commit the box showed the original text again (no typed text, no badge) for several seconds, then nothing. "I could not see what I typed." The refusal itself was correct.
**Cause:** `_paint_plan_mode_frame` drew the chip and badge only while `plan_preview_pending()`. A refusal makes `plan_preview_pending()` false (a reason is recorded), so the frame fell back to the frozen first frame. Separately, `set_plan_preview_state` changed the state without changing the frame, so no `update()` followed and the previous `預覽更新中` chip stayed on screen until an unrelated repaint.
**Fix:** A separate predicate `plan_preview_refused()` (plan mode, no preedit, text differs, recorded refusal other than `no_change`, no verified raster) drives the same chip + badge overlay with the `無法套用` badge (`PLAN_REFUSED_BADGE_TEXT`); the CSS preview stays banned. `set_plan_preview_state` calls `viewport().update()` after its generation guard. Rule: any state that decides what `paintEvent` draws must schedule its own repaint at the point it changes, even when the pixels the previous frame holds look unchanged to the caller. Do not fold the refusal into `plan_preview_pending()`: that predicate also gates the "still updating" notice and the Apply logic.
**File:** `view/text_editing.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_plan_preview_no_css.py` (`test_refused_preview_paints_the_typed_text_chip_and_a_refusal_badge`, `test_refusal_state_change_schedules_a_full_repaint`, `test_no_change_refusal_paints_no_refusal_badge`); `test_scripts/test_text_commit_real_ime_round4.py` (`test_a_refused_ime_commit_repaints_the_chip_and_the_refusal_badge`, `test_a_slow_refusal_is_repainted_with_the_refusal_badge`)

## `set_mode(current_mode)` finalized the open editor as MODE_SWITCH and discarded un-applied input
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`PDFView.set_mode`, `_start_text_edit_from_hit`, `_hit_matches_open_editor`)
**Symptom:** In text-edit mode with a refused (or composing) editor, pressing F2 (or F1, or the ribbon button) closed the editor and threw the typed input away with the generic "not applied" toast. The owner pressed F2 precisely because the typed text was not visible. The context-menu "Edit Text" on the editor's own run did the same (discard, then re-open the original text).
**Cause:** `set_mode` treated every call as a mode switch and finalized with `MODE_SWITCH`, a close-always reason that commits only a verified edit and discards everything else. Re-entering the mode you are already in is not a switch. `_start_text_edit_from_hit` always finalized first and re-opened from the hit.
**Fix:** With a live editor and `mode == current_mode`, `set_mode` re-syncs the checked action and the property panel, refocuses the view and the editor widget and returns (no finalize, no body: the body would also reset drag state and redraw the outlines under the live editor). `_hit_matches_open_editor` (page, span id, else bbox within `POSITION_CHANGE_TOLERANCE_PT`) lets the context menu keep the editor on its own run; another run finalizes first and, if the editor survives (un-applied input), opens nothing. Consequence for tests: a fake editor placed while `current_mode == "browse"` is an impossible state and now exercises the early return instead of `MODE_SWITCH` (`test_text_commit_degrade_visibility.py` sets `current_mode = "edit_text"`). Hook any future side effect of "mode entered" on a real switch, not on every `set_mode` call.
**File:** `view/pdf_view.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_finalize_policy.py` (`test_f2_on_the_current_mode_keeps_a_refused_editor`, `test_f2_during_a_composition_keeps_the_preedit`, `test_reentering_add_text_keeps_an_add_box`, `test_context_menu_edit_text_on_the_editors_own_run_keeps_it`, `test_context_menu_edit_text_on_another_run_commits_a_verified_edit_first`)

## Edit actions hosted in a collapsible sidebar are invisible at 0 px, and a focus-taking action button ends the edit it acts on
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (text property card), `view/text_inline_action_bar.py` (`TextInlineActionBar`), `view/text_editing.py` (`_is_focus_within_edit_context`)
**Symptom:** The owner had dragged the right sidebar to 0 px, so `套用`, `取消`, the refusal reason and `改用重建文字…` (all in the text card) were invisible: "I could not find Apply, nothing happened." Clicking a focusable sidebar button also moves focus out of the editor (a `FOCUS_OUTSIDE` finalize and, with a real IME, a composition reset).
**Cause:** Controls that act on the live editor were placed in a panel the user can collapse, away from the editor, with default focus policies.
**Fix:** `TextInlineActionBar` is a child of `graphics_view.viewport()` placed beside the editor (`compute_inline_action_bar_pos`: below, above, right, left, never over the editor rect, so the IME cursor stays free).
