Two attributes are mandatory and pinned by tests: `Qt.WA_NoMousePropagation` (without it a press on the bar background reaches the viewport's `_mouse_press` and finalizes as `CLICK_AWAY`) and `Qt.NoFocus` on the bar (round 7 / KBD-1 amended: the three BUTTONS are `Qt.TabFocus`, see the KBD-1 entry at the end; the grip and strip stay `NoFocus`). A viewport overlay is not a scene item: it does not scale with zoom and does not take part in scene hit testing. Costs: wheel events over the bar are swallowed; the OS IME candidate window can cover the bar (never the editor); `QTest.mouseClick` on a NoFocus button walks up to the viewport (StrongFocus), so a test that first focused a sidebar widget sees the focus move to the graphics view. Rule: UI that acts on an inline editor lives next to it, never in a panel that can be collapsed.
**File:** `view/text_inline_action_bar.py`, `view/pdf_view.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_real_ime_round4.py` (`test_inline_bar_is_a_viewport_child_and_shows_the_refusal`, `test_inline_bar_visible_with_right_sidebar_dragged_to_zero`, `test_bar_clicks_never_finalize_or_move_focus`); `test_scripts/test_text_commit_inline_action_bar.py`

## A viewport overlay placed from the Resize event lands on the old geometry: PDFView's event filter runs before QAbstractScrollArea's
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`eventFilter` viewport `QEvent.Resize` branch, `_position_text_action_bar`)
**Symptom:** After resizing the window (or dragging the sidebar splitter) with a kept editor, the inline action bar sat on top of the editor or tens of pixels away from it, and stayed wrong until a keystroke or a scroll. Only seen when the whole page fits in the viewport.
**Cause:** `PDFView` installs its viewport filter after `QAbstractScrollArea` installed its own, so it sees `Resize` first, before `QGraphicsView` re-centres the scene. When the page fits (scroll range 0) the re-centring changes no scrollbar value, so `valueChanged` never fires either, and nothing repositions the bar. A test that only resizes through a size that changes the scroll range passes.
**Fix:** The `Resize` branch keeps the immediate `_position_text_action_bar()` and also schedules `call_later(self, 0, self._position_text_action_bar)` (F16-VIEW-TIMER); the function wraps its body in `try/except RuntimeError` so the deferred call survives teardown. Rule: position a child of a scroll area's viewport from the editor's final mapped rect, and test it through resizes that only re-centre.
**File:** `view/pdf_view.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_real_ime_round4.py` (`test_bar_follows_a_resize_that_only_recenters_the_scene`)

## Pointer-driven keep notices: de-dup by state, and not for focus that went to a dialog
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`TextEditManager._not_applied`, `_kept_notice`, `_focus_outside_notice_allowed`, `_pointer_notice_stamp`), `view/pdf_view.py` (`_handle_escape`)
**Symptom:** Clicking the page while the input was refused or the preview still updating kept the editor and said nothing, so the editor looked frozen. The opposite risk once a notice exists: a modal opened by Ctrl+S (or alt-tab) takes the focus and would toast "click away" for a click that never happened; repeated clicks would stack toasts.
**Cause:** The keep policy existed but only `VIEW_RESCALE` had a notice and a de-dup key.
**Fix:** `CLICK_AWAY` and `FOCUS_OUTSIDE` on an un-applied input name the reason (or the pending preview) once per `(text, preedit)` stamp stored on the editor. `FOCUS_OUTSIDE` is silent, and records no stamp, while a modal or popup is active or the application is not `ApplicationActive`. The composing notice names the cancelled action. Escape on changed text toasts `ESCAPE_DISCARD_NOTICE`. Known consequence: a click-away after a Ctrl+S, F5 or zoom notice on the same text is silent (the action bar and the `無法套用` badge carry the reason); a right-click on the page with a kept editor shows the new `FOCUS_OUTSIDE` notice because the scene clears its focus item on a right press.
**File:** `view/text_editing.py`, `view/pdf_view.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_finalize_policy.py` (`test_click_away_on_a_plan_refused_input_says_why_once`, `test_click_away_while_the_preview_is_pending_says_so`, `test_focus_leaving_a_refused_editor_says_why_once`, `test_focus_outside_notice_is_suppressed_under_a_modal`, `test_escape_discarding_changed_text_says_so_once`)

## Page snapshot restore via insert_pdf grafts copies: page, OCG and font identity lost
**Area:** `model/page_snapshot.py`, `model/pdf_model.py` (`_capture_page_snapshot_strict`, `_restore_page_from_snapshot`, `xref_epoch`), `model/edit_commands.py` (`EditTextCommand.undo`, `AddTextboxCommand`)
**Symptom:** After a consented rebuild (改用重建文字…) then Ctrl+Z, every later true-text edit on the page was refused `mc_wrapper_not_pure_layer` ("圖層結構不支援原位修改"), even a pure reorder of the run's own characters. The page object got a new xref, `/Properties` pointed at duplicated OCGs that `/OCProperties` does not list (all wrappers classified `props_unresolved`), and `/VP`, `/StructParents`, TOC destinations and Popup annotations were lost. A failed legacy edit's rollback did the same; xref_length grew about 100 objects per undo/redo cycle.
**Cause:** The page snapshot was a one-page PDF (`insert_pdf` of the live page) and the restore was another `insert_pdf` plus `delete_page`. `insert_pdf` grafts COPIES of every indirect object the page references, so shared document-level objects lose their identity. The capture also mutated the live annotations' `/P`.
**Fix:** One chokepoint: a page-object-graph snapshot (`PageSnapshot`) restored in place by xref (`restore_page_graph`), no graft fallback. It is only valid under the xref numbering it was captured in (`PDFModel.xref_epoch`): a live `garbage >= 2` serialization (a save) renumbers the document and bumps the epoch, after which undo/redo of the command refuse with zero mutation (`STALE_UNDO` / `STALE_PLAN`, `PageSnapshotStale`). A print is not a save and must not do this (see the DS-1 entry). Any new code that serializes the LIVE document with garbage >= 2, or installs a new live `fitz.Document` that keeps the numbering, must call `_note_live_doc_serialized` / restore the epoch. Do not add mc_* codes to `_NOT_REBUILDABLE` or soften the marked-content classifier: the classifier was right, the page really was different.
**File:** `model/page_snapshot.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/edit_commands.py`; `test_scripts/test_page_snapshot_identity.py`, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_undo_restore_identity.py`

## A whole-document snapshot undo/redo shortens the xref table and flips the epoch: later page-snapshot redo refused
**Area:** `model/page_snapshot.py` (`restore_page_graph` gate (c)), `model/edit_commands.py` (`SnapshotCommand.__init__`, `_stamp_live_epoch`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`merge_ordered_sources_into_current`)
**Symptom:** Add a highlight or rotate a page (whole-document `SnapshotCommand`), then do a rebuild or add a textbox, then Ctrl+Z twice and Ctrl+Y twice: the second redo is refused ("snapshot objects lie outside the document" or "xref numbering changed since the snapshot"), the command stays stuck on the redo stack. The same after redoing a merge (bare `after_bytes`) with a textbox above it.
**Cause:** Redoing a `SnapshotCommand` reopens the document from `garbage=0` bytes taken BEFORE the later command existed, so `xref_length` is shorter than the xrefs the later rebuild/textbox allocated; a gate that refused records beyond the table rejected a restore that was provably correct (those slots are free in this lineage). Separately, the merge records a plain `bytes` after-state, which the doc setter installs under a FRESH epoch even though the numbering is identical, so every page-snapshot command above it went stale.
**Fix:** `restore_page_graph` grows the table (`get_new_xref` until `xref_length` exceeds the largest record xref; sanity cap `PAGE_SNAPSHOT_MAX_XREF_GROWTH`, a corrupt snapshot still raises `PageSnapshotStale`) after the stale gates (b), (d), (e) pass, and treats out-of-range `prior` entries as null on rollback. The epoch is stamped at one chokepoint, `SnapshotCommand.__init__` (`_stamp_live_epoch`: a bare `after_bytes` with no int `xref_epoch` becomes a `DocSnapshot` carrying `model.xref_epoch`), not per call site. Rule: any command whose undo/redo reinstalls a whole document must carry the epoch of the numbering it reinstalls, and a page-graph gate may only refuse what is actually unsafe, never what merely looks different from the live table.
**File:** `model/page_snapshot.py`, `model/edit_commands.py`; `test_scripts/test_page_snapshot_identity.py` (`test_redo_chain_across_a_doc_snapshot_command_keeps_identity`, `test_restore_grows_the_xref_table_for_records_beyond_it`, `test_merge_style_plain_after_bytes_keep_redo_chain`)

## Keeping the editor on same-mode re-entry (F2) with no word looks like a dead key
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`TextEditManager.notify_same_mode_reentry`, `_MODE_REENTRY_KEPT_NOTICE`, `editor._reentry_notice_stamp`), `view/pdf_view.py` (`set_mode` same-mode branch, `_start_text_edit_from_hit`)
**Symptom:** In text-edit mode with a refused or still-previewing input, F2 (or the ribbon button, or the context menu "Edit Text" on the editor's own run) did nothing visible and showed no toast, while the other actions (click away, F5, Ctrl+wheel, double Escape) each said why the edit could not be applied.
**Cause:** Round 4 made same-mode `set_mode` a silent no-op re-entry so it no longer finalized `MODE_SWITCH` (which discards un-applied input); nothing told the user why the editor stayed. Reusing the click-away stamp (`_pointer_notice_stamp`) would not work either: a click-away on the same text, which the owner did first, would silence the F2 notice.
**Fix:** `notify_same_mode_reentry()` NOTIFIES and never finalizes; it names the reason (or the composition / "preview still updating"), stays silent when the text is unchanged or Apply is permitted, and de-dups on its own `editor._reentry_notice_stamp = (notice, text, preedit)` so key auto-repeat does not stack toasts. Rule: a path that keeps un-applied input without finalizing must say why, and each notice family keeps its own de-dup stamp.
**File:** `view/text_editing.py`, `view/pdf_view.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_finalize_policy.py` (`test_f2_on_a_refused_editor_says_why_once`, `test_f2_after_a_click_away_on_a_refused_editor_says_why_again`, `test_f2_during_a_composition_names_the_cancelled_mode_switch`, `test_context_menu_edit_text_on_the_editors_own_run_says_why`)

## A `garbage=0` full save persists the objects undo and a kept rebuild leave behind (222 KB became 5.9 MB)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`save_as`, `_full_save_to_path`), `model/page_snapshot.py` (`restore_page_graph`), `model/save_compaction.py`
**Symptom:** On a copy of `ecc-dwg.pdf` (222,884 bytes) a legacy rebuild of a line, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+S wrote 6,126,947 bytes (the owner's file: 5,901,966). A KEPT rebuild then Ctrl+S, and rebuild -> undo -> redo -> Ctrl+S, wrote 6,126,935 bytes. 11 unreachable streams (5,747,584 bytes), a raw 5,181,580-byte `FontFile2`, a 272,265-byte `ToUnicode` and a 224,840-byte content stream.
**Cause:** Three independent causes. (1) The rebuild embeds the whole system font raw (see the Story entry). (2) The save is NOT incremental: `apply_redactions` flips `doc.can_save_incrementally()` to 0 (`insert_htmlbox` alone leaves it 1), so `save_as` takes `_full_save_to_path`, which serialized with the default `garbage=0`, keeping every unreferenced object. The first diagnosis assumed Ctrl+S was incremental; the saved file had exactly one `%%EOF`. (3) Undo does not clean up: `restore_page_graph` writes only the snapshot's own records back and never touches live objects absent from the snapshot, so after Ctrl+Z the Redact annotation, its AP, the content stream, the font resources, `FontFile2` and `ToUnicode` (xref 108..120, 5,678,929 stream bytes) stay in the live document. Measured `tobytes` sizes of that live document: `garbage=0` 5,902,003; `garbage=1` 221,600; `garbage=4` 221,340.
**Fix:** Save-time pruning, not undo-time cleanup: every non-secure full save uses `garbage=1` and an incremental save falls back to the pruned full save when the session orphans are large (numbering rule and thresholds in the entry above). `garbage=1` keeps the numbering, so the epoch stays and page-snapshot undo/redo still work after a save; redo of a command whose slots the save freed works because `restore_page_graph` grows the table and `_write_record` resurrects free slots. Pinned by the real-app tests `test_rebuild_undo_save_writes_no_orphans_and_redo_survives` and `test_kept_rebuild_save_has_no_rebuild_leftovers` (`unreachable == []` after a full save; the saved file stays near the original size).
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/save_compaction.py`, `model/page_snapshot.py`; `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py`, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py`

## MuPDF Story (`insert_htmlbox`) embeds a font as a raw, unsubsetted stream and a fresh copy on every call
**Area:** `model/font_stream_compaction.py`, `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (legacy edit_text strategies A/B/C, vertical retry, push-down), `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (textbox insert), `model/pdf_model.py` (`_build_insert_css`, `_font_face_css_for_token`)
**Symptom:** One legacy rebuild with a CJK `@font-face` added a 5,181,580-byte `FontFile2` (`<</Length1 5181580/Length 5181580>>`, no `/Filter`, magic 00010000: exactly the size of `kaiu.ttf` on disk) plus a raw 272,265-byte `/ToUnicode` CMap, even when the rebuild was kept. The built-in Droid fallback adds about 3.5 MB per box.
**Cause:** The Story device embeds the font program verbatim and never subsets or deflates it, and every `insert_htmlbox` call embeds its OWN copy: nothing dedupes across calls. A rebuild with a vertical `scale_low` retry, strategies A/B/C and a push-down of N overlapping blocks therefore inserts up to N+1 copies. A bare `insert_htmlbox` on a blank page gave a 5,455,835-byte file; `tobytes(garbage=4, deflate=True)` gave 2,963,042 (FontFile2 deflates to about 2.86 MB, the CMap to 96 KB); `doc.subset_fonts()` gave 181,002 raw / 22,409 deflated.
**Fix:** `font_compaction_scope(doc)` wraps the operation (watermark at start). On normal exit it re-points duplicate new `FontFile*` / `ToUnicode` streams to the first identical copy (decoded-bytes hash, only objects at or above the watermark) and Flate-compresses each surviving unfiltered stream once; `/Length1-3` are snapshotted and restored verbatim. `insert_htmlbox_tracked` is the single model-side chokepoint (it raises outside a scope unless `scratch=True`), guarded by an AST test over `model/`. The scope must close BEFORE the command's after-snapshot, so redo restores the compacted bytes; the tiered engine never opens one. Compress-only: a kept kaiu rebuild still adds about 2.9 MB compressed per surviving copy (owner-visible). Subsetting needs `fontTools` (not a pinned dependency) and `doc.subset_fonts()` is unsafe on the live doc: it rewrote the original fonts 8 and 67 (40,726 -> 214,442 and 46,798 -> 177,698 bytes), breaking byte-identical streams. The compaction is best-effort: a failure inside it is logged and never fails the edit. Residual: `_ACTIVE_SCOPES` is keyed by `id(doc)`; a document closed inside an open scope whose id is reused would look scoped (no current path does this; the textbox repair retry opens one scope per attempt).
**File:** `model/font_stream_compaction.py`, `model/pdf_text_edit.py`, `model/pdf_object_ops.py`; `test_scripts/test_font_stream_compaction.py`

---

## A press inside the open inline editor was swallowed as a drag: jitter moved the box and refused unchanged text
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`_mouse_press` / `_mouse_move` / `_mouse_release`, `_should_start_editor_drag`, `_editor_cursor_at_scene`, `_begin_editor_drag` / `_finish_editor_drag`), `view/text_inline_action_bar.py` (`EditorMoveGrip`)
**Symptom:** On the owner's recording, a click with a few pixels of jitter inside the open editor moved the box about 14 px, and the unchanged text was then refused with `geometry_override_present` ("移動文字位置需要重建文字"). A drag inside the box could never select text.
**Cause:** Every press inside the editor box was treated as the start of a box move; the move threshold was a fixed 3 px, below the platform drag distance, so ordinary hand jitter crossed it. The same press placed no caret.
**Fix:** In-box mouse means caret and selection (native text-field behaviour, left button only; right click changes nothing; double click selects a word); the hit-test goes through the editor's document layout WITH its scroll offset (scroll-independent) and is clamped to `[0, len]`. Moving is explicit: the `⠿ 移動` grip (`EditorMoveGrip`) on the inline bar, shown for edit_text AND add_text editors, reports GLOBAL positions because the bar follows the box while it is dragged; a grip press without movement touches nothing. The drag-start threshold is `max(3, QApplication.startDragDistance())` in VIEWPORT pixels (`_viewport_delta`), so it does not scale with zoom. An in-box or strip press while an input method composes first commits the composition (`commit_ime_composition`: `inputMethod().commit()`, then `reset()` if the editor is still composing, because `commit()` is a no-op in several platform contexts), then places the caret; presses on the bar buttons and on the page outside the box keep the round-4 behaviour. The view sets the I-beam itself after `QGraphicsView.mouseMoveEvent` on every move with an open editor and resets it on `_teardown_editor` / `set_mode`: offscreen Qt gives an I-beam over a proxy by itself, while the real Windows window kept the drag hand. add_text keeps its own I-beam mode cursor.
**Known limits:** on `/Rotate` pages the grip is the only way to move a box, and two older bugs used to be the only behaviour: `_clamp_editor_pos_to_page` measured the box unrotated (a 90 degree page jumped 52 px), and `_finish_editor_drag` derived `editing_rect` from the proxy origin, which is the box corner, not its top-left, on rotated pages (270 degrees: y0 540 instead of 379). Both were fixed in round 7 (see the Round 7 rotated-move entry below: `_proxy_visual_extent`, `_proxy_corner_offset`). The first-click pending-drag branch (`_pending_text_info` is only ever set to None) is dead code. Whether the real Windows IME honours the commit-before-caret ordering, and whether a Shift-click while composing followed by the next IME keystroke deletes the new selection (`QWidgetTextControl` removes the selection on the next IME input), are owner real-IME acceptance items.
**File:** `view/pdf_view.py`, `view/text_inline_action_bar.py`, `view/text_live_strip.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_editor_mouse_gestures.py`, `test_scripts/test_text_editing_gui_regressions.py`

## Plan-mode editing never paints a caret, a selection or legible typed text: they live in the live text strip
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`PreviewBackedInlineTextEditor.paintEvent`, `inputMethodEvent`), `view/text_live_strip.py`, `view/text_inline_action_bar.py`, `view/pdf_view.py` (`_build_text_editor_stylesheet`, `_sync_text_action_bar`)
**Symptom:** In the shipped plan-preview mode the owner saw no caret, no selection and only a 9-10 px, ellipsised chip of what was typed; long text wrapped on invisible lines (Home went to the start of the visual line, Up/Down moved across lines nobody could see, the last glyph could not be clicked).
**Cause:** (1) In plan mode `paintEvent` never calls `QTextEdit.paintEvent`: it draws the frozen/verified raster plus the pending/refused badge and chip, so Qt's caret and selection can never appear. (2) The caret is also off by design (`setCursorWidth(0)`, revealed on the first key press only) and IME-only input never revealed it. (3) `selection-background-color: rgba(30,120,255,0.0)` in the stylesheet makes any native selection transparent. (4) The hidden layout uses the substituted screen font (1.0 em CJK advances; the PDF font was 0.835 em), so it wraps where the PDF does not and its per-character x never matches the raster (5 px off at char 1, about 18 px at char 4 at 214 % zoom). A caret drawn from that layout inside the box would not line up with the glyphs.
**Fix:** `LiveTextStrip` is the first row of the inline action bar, OUTSIDE the box: the editor's plain text in a screen font (>= 14 px), the caret, the selection band and the IME preedit underline, mirrored synchronously from the editor's signals; click/drag/Shift-click in it moves the editor's caret and selection (a strip press while composing commits first). The strip never takes focus; the editor keeps it. `\n` is laid out as `U+2028` so positions stay 1:1 (write it as the escape, never the raw character). In plan mode AND run target mode the hidden layout is `NoWrap` (paragraph mode keeps `WidgetWidth`, so Up/Down still work). `inputMethodEvent` must reveal the caret (`reveal_caret()`, idempotent, signals once): IME-only users never press a key. The IME cursor rectangle (`ImCursorRectangle`) is the strip caret, falling back to the box when the bar is hidden, and `inputMethod().update()` runs on caret and bar moves. Rule: the box stays PDF-faithful; everything the user must see while typing goes in chrome beside it. Dead end / follow-up: a raster-aligned in-box caret needs per-glyph geometry of the NEW text carried in `PlanPreviewResult` through the controller to the view, and pending or refused text has no raster at all. The two-row bar is taller, so probes placed below the box in older tests now hit the bar (the "outside the box" point moved to the left of the box).
**File:** `view/text_live_strip.py`, `view/text_editing.py`, `view/text_inline_action_bar.py`, `view/pdf_view.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_live_text_strip.py`

## Dead end: nulling the objects a command created at undo time is unsafe (PyMuPDF `InsertedImages` cache)
**Area:** `model/page_snapshot.py` (`restore_page_graph`), `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`insert_image` use), save-time pruning design
**Symptom:** (Considered, never shipped.) After Ctrl+Z of a rebuild the live document keeps 13 unreachable objects (xref 108..120, 5.68 MB). Nulling them at undo (`update_object(x, "null")` for `xref >= the command's pre-operation xref_length`) is attractive: a garbage=0 save of the nulled clone was 221,600 bytes, redo restored every record byte-equal, and `can_save_incrementally` stayed 1.
**Cause:** PyMuPDF keeps `doc.InsertedImages`, a digest-to-xref cache consulted by `insert_image` (used by `model/pdf_object_ops.py`). Insert an image, undo it with its slot nulled, insert the same image again: PyMuPDF returns the nulled xref and the page references null. Other MuPDF-side caches carry the same risk, and the PGSNAP header would need a watermark.
**Fix:** Do not null live objects at undo. Prune at save time (`garbage=1` full saves plus the incremental fallback, see the entries above), which touches only the serialized copy. The same reasoning is why a modified base-file object that became unreachable is still written by a true incremental save (rare, deliberately not nulled).
**File:** `model/save_compaction.py`, `model/page_snapshot.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`

## A grip move uncovered the source text: the single underlay mask followed the moved box
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`TextEditManager.refresh_text_editor_mask_color`, `sync_text_editor_origin_mask`, `_build_background_matched_mask`, `_install_editor_in_scene`, `_teardown_editor`), `view/pdf_view.py` (`_update_editor_drag`, `_maybe_refresh_editor_mask_for_page`, `_detach_text_editor_before_scene_clear`)
**Symptom:** After dragging the `⠿ 移動` grip of an existing text (manual step S17a, copy of `ecc-dwg.pdf`, +30 px at 214 %), the original glyph stayed visible at the old spot beside the moved box: the line read "備備為C標新設。". Pre-existing on the round-6 base.
**Cause:** One opaque mask item (z 11) hid the source glyphs under the proxy. Every drag step `setRect`s it to the proxy rect, so the open rect was uncovered while the moved box painted the frozen original frame: the text was on screen twice. The mask brush is not the page colour: grey text below `_MASK_MIN_CONTRAST_RATIO` tints it (white page -> 202 grey), which is normally hidden under the frozen frame. Copying that brush, or widening the mask to the union of both rects (one ring sample over two spots), paints a visible grey block. An exact-span patch is also not enough: on the CJK corpus glyph ink overhangs the span bbox (measured on a copy of `ecc-dwg.pdf` with no margin: 1 px above and below at 100 %, 1-2 px above at 214 %, deviation up to 55).
**Fix:** A second item `_text_editor_origin_mask_item` (z 10.5: above the hover highlight 10, below the moving mask 11, proxy 12, focus border 13) covers the SOURCE SPAN, `_editing_origin_span_scene_rect` (the origin page's scene origin + `_editing_original_rect` * render scale, snapshotted in `_install_editor_in_scene`; visual-page space, so rotation-agnostic, and it survives several drags and a cross-page move), PLUS a margin of 1 pt (`_ORIGIN_MASK_MARGIN_PT`, at least 1 scene px via `_origin_mask_margin_px`), snapped OUTWARD to whole pixels with `toAlignedRect()` (a fractional edge blends the span's edge pixel and leaves a glyph sliver), while an `edit_existing` box is displaced by more than 0.5 scene px. The displacement test still compares the proxy's `_editing_origin_scene_rect` (the widget rect at open) with its current rect; the cover, the ring sample and the cache signature use the span (see the next entries for why the widget rect is wrong as a cover, and for the uniformity gate that can skip the patch). No span -> no patch. It is filled with the UNTINTED ring-mean colour of the ORIGIN page (`_build_background_matched_mask(..., page_idx=origin, tint=False)`, no `text_rgb` read), created lazily, hidden when the box returns, resampled only when the origin page pixmap changes, skipped when there is no page sample, removed by `_teardown_editor`, detached before `scene.clear()`, and never created for add_new (the page text under an add_text box is real content). Synced from `refresh_text_editor_mask_color`, the one chokepoint for drags, page re-renders and font changes (the fake drag tests stub its view wrapper). The margin is pinned by a failing run with the margin forced to 0 (6/6 red). Known cost: the margin plus the outward snap paints over [max(1, rs), max(1, rs)+1) scene px per side around the span bbox (DOC-1, pinned by `test_origin_patch_overhang_is_one_to_two_scene_pixels_per_side_at_50_percent`: 1-2 pt at 100 %, 2-4 pt at 50 %, 1-1.5 pt at 200 %; an earlier version of this entry and of FEATURES/TODOS/ARCHITECTURE said "up to 1 pt", which no zoom satisfies, the code was measured and kept because the 1 px floor and the outward snap are what hide the glyph ink and the span's edge pixel) of neighbouring content (a table rule, underline, tight-leading neighbour line) while the box is away unless the ring gate skips the patch (it only just does for a word 2.5 pt away at 50 %: 5.07 % against the 5 % limit); it reappears on commit or cancel (TODOS, owner S17a list). The first round-7 version covered the widget rect and a flat colour unconditionally; both were wrong, see "The origin patch covered the editor widget" and "The origin patch is skipped on a non-uniform background" below.
**File:** `view/text_editing.py`, `view/pdf_view.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_editor_mouse_gestures.py`, `test_scripts/test_text_editing_gui_regressions.py`, `test_scripts/test_multi_tab_plan.py`

## Rotated pages: the editor proxy pos is a corner of the box, not its top-left
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`_clamp_editor_pos_to_page`, `_finish_editor_drag`, `_resolve_editor_page_idx_for_drag`), `view/text_editing.py` (`_compute_editor_proxy_layout`, `_quarter_turn_proxy_layout`, `_proxy_corner_offset`, `_proxy_visual_extent`)
**Symptom:** On `/Rotate` 90 and 180 pages the first grip move jumped the box 52 / 89 px; after any move on 90/180/270 `editing_rect` was wrong (270: y0 540 instead of 379), so the apply went to the wrong place.
**Cause:** The open path rotates the proxy about (0, 0) and places `pos` at the box's x1 (90), (x0 + W, y0 + H) (180) or y1 (270). The clamp treated `pos` as the top-left of an unrotated W x H box, and the finish path computed `editing_rect` as `(pos - page origin) / rs`.
**Fix:** `_proxy_corner_offset` (proxy `pos` minus the box's visual top-left) is subtracted by `_finish_editor_drag`; `_proxy_visual_extent` (the rotated box relative to `pos`) drives the clamp and the page-resolve centre; `_quarter_turn_proxy_layout` holds the 90/270 forward placement. The FORWARD (open) expressions stay literal (`x0 + sr.x1` at 90, `y0 + sr.y1` at 270, `_compute_editor_proxy_layout` for 180) so open positions are byte-identical to before; forward and inverse are NOT one shared helper, so they can drift apart. They are pinned by tests instead: the literal pre-refactor formulas hard-coded in `test_text_editor_rotated_move.py`, a real-MVC scene-box check (proxy `sceneBoundingRect().topLeft()` == page origin + `editing_rect` top-left * scale, at open and after a grip move, 0/90/180/270), and a move + rebuild-consent apply + save/reopen run (swapping the 90/270 offset rows fails 12 tests). Read the rotation from `view._editing_rotation`, never `proxy.rotation()` (the fake proxies in the GUI regression tests store `rotation` as a float attribute). `_finish_editor_drag` also snaps back to the exact original rect when the box returns to its open spot (see "An out-and-back grip drag must restore the exact original rect" below). Residual: a cross-page move onto a page with a different `/Rotate` keeps the origin rotation (TODOS). R7-INT-2: the clamp holds the SOURCE SPAN inside the page, not the 80 px minimum-width padding: `create_text_editor` stores `_editing_min_width_pad_px` (edit_existing at 0/180: widget width minus the span's pixel width; the padding is on the visual right at both rotations) and `_clamp_editor_pos_to_page` subtracts it from the right extent. Clamping the padded box made a short run near the right edge (page numbers, last table column) jump left on the first 1 px move and put its open spot out of reach (B1 never restored, Apply disabled). Guards: `test_a_vertical_first_grip_move_near_the_right_edge_never_jumps_x`, `test_out_and_back_to_the_open_spot_near_the_right_edge_restores_the_rect_and_apply`, `test_dragging_to_the_right_edge_keeps_the_source_span_on_the_page`. R3-INT-1: the same on the vertical axis: a PARAGRAPH editor at 0/180 is measured taller than its source span (`_measure_text_content_height_px` wraps at the span width and keeps the default 4 px document margin), and the excess hangs below the span at both rotations, so a paragraph near the page bottom opened hanging past it and the first grip move (even 1 px horizontal) shoved it up by the whole hang. `create_text_editor` stores `_editing_height_pad_px` (edit_existing at 0/180: widget height minus the span's pixel height; run mode is 0) and `_clamp_editor_pos_to_page` subtracts it from the bottom extent. Guards: `test_out_and_back_to_the_open_spot_near_the_bottom_edge_restores_the_rect_and_apply`, `test_dragging_a_paragraph_to_the_bottom_edge_keeps_the_source_span_on_the_page`.
**File:** `view/pdf_view.py`, `view/text_editing.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_editor_rotated_move.py`, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_editor_mouse_gestures.py`

## A span whose own bbox crosses the page edge: the grip-drag clamp must keep the open spot reachable
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`_clamp_editor_pos_to_page`), `view/text_editing.py` (`_install_editor_in_scene`, `_editing_open_proxy_pos`)
**Symptom:** (R7-DEG-1.) Helvetica 14 with its baseline 5 pt below the page top has a span bbox y0 of -5.95 pt, so the editor opens above the page. The first grip move, even a purely horizontal 5 px one, dropped the box 6 px; dragging back could not return above the page top, so `editing_rect != _editing_original_rect`, the B1 / R7-INT-1 restore never fired and the settled reason was `geometry_override_present` (Apply disabled).
**Cause:** `get_text_info_at_point` returns the raw span bbox (font ascender/descender metrics, never clipped to `page.rect`). The clamp bounded the proxy to the page, which excludes the box's own open position.
**Fix:** `_install_editor_in_scene` stores the open proxy position (`_editing_open_proxy_pos`, cleared at teardown); `_clamp_editor_pos_to_page` widens each axis range to include it when dragging on the origin page (allowed region = page UNION open spot). A drag still cannot go further past the edge than where it opened. Same class as R7-INT-2 (min-width pad) and R3-INT-1 (paragraph height pad), different input. Plan-stage follow-up (EDGE-REFUSE-1): `_build_tier1` used to run `_bbox_within_page` on the verify bbox unconditionally, so a zero-growth shrink (`iii` -> `i`) of such a span was refused `growth_outside_page` for overflow that pre-dated the edit (same-advance edits go through Tier 0, which has no containment check, and were never refused). The containment check now runs only when the verify bbox differs from the target bbox (real growth); real growth on a span that already crosses the edge is still refused. Guards: `test_zero_growth_shrink_of_a_span_already_crossing_the_page_edge_is_not_refused[right_edge|top_edge]` (plan + commit) and `test_growth_of_a_span_already_crossing_the_page_edge_is_still_refused` in `test_text_commit_tier1_slice1.py`. The bottom edge and 90 / 270 variants were not reproduced.
**File:** `view/pdf_view.py`, `view/text_editing.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_editor_mouse_gestures.py`

## Plan mode paints no in-box chip; outside plan mode the composing chip is the only preedit echo
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`PreviewBackedInlineTextEditor._paint_editor_overlay`, `_paint_composing_frame`, `_paint_plan_mode_frame`), `view/text_live_strip.py`
**Symptom:** (Owner decision, round 7.) The plan-mode box showed a small elided chip of the typed text or the composition at its bottom-left, duplicating the live text strip above the box.
**Cause:** The chip predates the strip (round 4 R4-1, part 5 A1) and was kept in round 6.
**Fix:** In plan mode the box paints only its base frame plus the badge (組字中 / 預覽更新中 / 無法套用); the plain chip branch and `plan_preview_chip_text` are removed, and `_paint_editor_overlay` returns after the badge when `self._plan_mode or not self._preedit_text`. Gotcha: the COMPOSING chip must stay outside plan mode (every add_text box, legacy edit_text): `_paint_composing_frame` bypasses the native paint and `LiveTextStrip` is hidden for non-plan editors, so removing it there makes the IME preedit invisible. Retiring it needs a new echo, option a1 in TODOS (show the strip for add_text/legacy editors). The badge is now the only in-box signal in plan mode and is clipped in narrow editors (~80 px wide at 100 %); the strip and the bar reason are the readable signals. `_composing_chip_parts`, `elide_composing_parts` and `_fit_edge` stay: they have a live caller.
**File:** `view/text_editing.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_plan_preview_no_css.py`, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_finalize_policy.py`, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_real_ime_round4.py`

## The origin patch covered the editor widget, not the source span
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`TextEditManager.sync_text_editor_origin_mask`, `_install_editor_in_scene`, `_teardown_editor`)
**Symptom:** (Round 1 adversarial review, REG-1 / RPU-1.) With a short run `AB` (18.7 px wide) next to another run `NEIGHBOUR` on the same baseline, a grip move of `AB` erased the neighbour's ink inside the old spot: 115 dark pixels in the overlap before, 0 after, and the patch measured 82 x 16 px against the 18.7 px span. Real runs hit this too (short CJK labels and table numbers narrower than the 80 px editor floor).
**Cause:** The first round-7 version covered `_editing_origin_scene_rect`, the proxy's `sceneBoundingRect()` at open. That is the editor WIDGET, not the text: at rotation 0 and 180 `_compute_editor_proxy_layout` clamps the width to `MIN_EDITOR_WIDTH_PX` (80), and in paragraph mode the height is the Qt-measured content height. On 90/270 the widget happens to equal the span, so the bug is invisible there. The widget rect is the right input for "did the box move" (it is what moves) and the wrong input for "what must be hidden".
**Fix:** Snapshot the span separately: `_editing_origin_span_scene_rect` = page scene origin of `_editing_origin_page_idx` + `_editing_original_rect` * render scale (visual-page space, so no per-rotation code), taken in `_install_editor_in_scene` next to the widget snapshot and deleted in `_teardown_editor`. `sync_text_editor_origin_mask` keeps the displacement test on the widget rect and uses the span for the cover (span + 1 pt margin, `toAlignedRect()` outward), the ring sample and the signature. A missing span means no patch (fail closed). Gotchas: snap outward, not to the nearest pixel (the first run with the exact fractional span failed the two ecc-dwg owner-run tests and the cross-page test with edge-pixel slivers), and the widget-sized patch is not testable on a single-run page (the existing F1 tests missed it): `test_origin_patch_covers_the_source_span_not_the_editor_widget[0|90|180|270]` uses a page with a Courier `NEIGHBOUR` run on the same baseline (red at 0 and 180, guard at 90 and 270). The tests that compared the patch with widget rect + margin now use `_expected_origin_cover(view)`.
**File:** `view/text_editing.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_editor_mouse_gestures.py`, `test_scripts/test_text_editing_gui_regressions.py`

---

## The origin patch is skipped on a non-uniform background (ring uniformity gate)
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`_qimage_ring_nonuniform_ratio`, `_build_background_matched_mask(..., measure_ring=)`, `sync_text_editor_origin_mask`, `_origin_mask_skip_signature`, `_ORIGIN_MASK_MAX_RING_NONUNIFORM_PCT`, `_MASK_RING_OUTLIER_L1`)
**Symptom:** (Round 1 adversarial review, RPU-2.) On a page with 1 pt black/white stripes behind the text, the moved-away spot showed a flat grey block (colour 131, luma std 0.00) while the surrounding pattern had std 79.7. The same happens on hatching, dense rules, images and two-tone fills.
**Cause:** The patch is one flat colour, the mean of a 3 px ring. The only fail-closed rule fired when sampling failed, not when the ring was not one colour. `_mask_leak_ratio(patch, ring_rgb)` runs on the patch just filled with `ring_rgb`, so it is 0 by construction and cannot gate anything (`_MASK_TEXTURE_MAX_LEAK_PCT` is dead and was left alone). Before round 7 the flat brush was hidden under the opaque frozen frame; the patch made it visible for the first time.
**Fix:** `_qimage_ring_nonuniform_ratio(image, inner_rect, ring_px, mean_rgb)` returns the fraction of ring pixels more than `_MASK_RING_OUTLIER_L1` (48, summed r+g+b) from the ring mean (same ring as `_qimage_ring_mean_rgb`; numpy over the four ring bands only, `pixelColor` fallback without numpy; the first version looped over every span pixel with `pixelColor` and blocked the UI thread 0.5-0.9 s on a paragraph at zoom 4 / DPR 2, PERF-1, now < 1 ms; `test_ring_nonuniform_ratio_cost_follows_the_ring_not_the_span_area` and `..._matches_the_per_pixel_definition`). `_build_background_matched_mask(..., measure_ring=True)` reports it as `ring_nonuniform_pct` in the debug dict (None unless asked, None in the fallback result). `sync_text_editor_origin_mask` clears the patch, logs at debug, and remembers the verdict in `_origin_mask_skip_signature` (same signature as the draw cache, reset by `_clear_text_editor_origin_mask_item`) when the ratio is above `_ORIGIN_MASK_MAX_RING_NONUNIFORM_PCT` (0.05), so mouse moves during the drag do not re-measure. The moving (editor) mask is untouched. HDZ-1: the ring is NOT a fixed 3 IMAGE px: `sync_text_editor_origin_mask` passes `reach_scene_px=margin+1` and `_build_background_matched_mask` measures `max(3, ceil(reach*k)+1)` image px (`k` = image px per scene px = the pixmap DPR, from `_resolve_mask_sampling`), so the gate covers everything the cover paints (margin plus the outward snap) at DPR 2 / high zoom; the ratio is then multiplied by `ring_px/3` (a one-sided rule is diluted 1/T by a T px ring: 4.4 % at T=7 vs 10 % at 3), so 0.05 means the same at every DPR and zoom and nothing changes at DPR 1 / 100 % (`test_origin_patch_is_skipped_for_a_rule_inside_the_covered_band_at_any_dpr`, `..._still_painted_when_the_rule_is_outside_the_covered_band`). Threshold from measurements (3 px ring): synthetic white 0.000, ecc-dwg CJK run 0.0033 at 100 % and 0.0040 at 214 %, 1 pt stripes 1.000; 0.05 is more than 12x above the corpus and far below real hatching. Consequence by design: on such pages the source text stays visible beside the moved box until commit or cancel (no worse than before round 7); a real background reconstruction is open (TODOS). Blind spot: a sparse hatch or a lone rule crossing the span interior touches the ring only at its ends and can stay under 0.05, so the flat patch still wipes that rule (TODOS). Red-first disclosure: the gate was written before its test (the threshold needed the measurements); red was shown afterwards by setting the constant to 2.0 (gate off), which makes `test_origin_patch_is_not_painted_over_a_striped_background[0]` fail with the patch present.
**File:** `view/text_editing.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_editor_mouse_gestures.py`

---

## A keep-finalize during a grip drag must complete the drag first
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`finalize_text_edit_impl`), `view/pdf_view.py` (`_on_move_grip_started`, `_on_move_grip_moved`, `_on_move_grip_finished`, `_finish_editor_drag`)
**Symptom:** (Round 1 adversarial review, CS1; the reset predates round 7.) Pressing the grip, dragging 40 px, then a keep-finalize (`SAVE_SHORTCUT`, `VIEW_RESCALE`) left the box displaced with the origin patch visible, the cursor stuck on the closed hand, and `editing_rect` equal to the original: later grip moves and the release were ignored, so Apply committed the text at the OLD spot while the screen showed it at the new one.
**Cause:** `finalize_text_edit_impl` resets the drag state (`view._drag_active = False`) before its keep branch; `_on_move_grip_moved` and `_on_move_grip_finished` return early when `_drag_active` is False, so the pending `_finish_editor_drag` (which derives `editing_rect` from the proxy) never ran. The grip is `NoFocus`, so keyboard shortcuts and view rescales still reach the editor while the mouse holds it; the origin patch decides from the proxy displacement, the commit path from `editing_rect`, which made the mismatch visible.
**Fix:** For non-discard reasons, while `view._drag_active`, `finalize_text_edit_impl` first calls `view._on_move_grip_finished(QPoint())` (moved -> `_finish_editor_drag`, so `editing_rect` follows the proxy and the cursor resets; pressed but unmoved -> state and cursor reset only, no preview invalidation), before the delta is computed. The existing drag-state reset below then makes any later grip moved/finished event a no-op. Discard reasons are unchanged (teardown). Not exercised: a non-grip body drag would also be completed through `_on_move_grip_finished` (the grip is the only mover). Test: `test_a_keep_finalize_mid_grip_drag_completes_the_drag[SAVE_SHORTCUT|VIEW_RESCALE x 0/90/180/270]`. Disclosure: its red run fails on the cursor assertion first (still `ClosedHandCursor`), so the red log itself does not show the `editing_rect` assertion failing; the repro record showed `editing_rect` unchanged before the fix. SEQ-1 (round 7, round 3): the grip keeps its OWN `_dragging` latch, cleared only by a left release it receives, so a finalize that ends the drag while the release is swallowed (Ctrl+Shift+S opens a modal `QFileDialog` with the button still down; Ctrl+O, Ctrl+P, close prompts, Alt+Tab) left it latched: closed-hand cursor, and the next press returned early, so the next whole move gesture did nothing. Fix: `EditorMoveGrip.reset_drag()` (no signal; also run from `hideEvent`), called by `PDFView._reset_move_grip_latch()` from `_on_move_grip_finished` (every branch, even when `_drag_active` is already False) and from the drag-state reset in `finalize_text_edit_impl` (covers discard reasons); a left press on a latched grip now restarts the drag instead of being ignored. Not driven: the real native dialog; the lost release is modelled by omitting it. Tests: `test_a_grip_press_with_a_stale_latch_starts_a_new_drag`, `test_a_finalize_that_swallows_the_grip_release_leaves_the_next_grip_drag_working[SAVE_SHORTCUT|CANCEL_BUTTON x 0/90/180/270]`, `test_an_ended_grip_drag_clears_the_grip_latch_in_every_view_path`.
**File:** `view/text_editing.py`, `view/pdf_view.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_editor_mouse_gestures.py`

## An out-and-back grip drag must restore the exact original rect
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`_finish_editor_drag`), `view/text_editing.py` (`_emit`, `_ORIGIN_MASK_MIN_DISPLACEMENT_PX`)
**Symptom:** (Round 1 adversarial review, B1; reproduces at rotation 0, so it predates round 7.) Drag the box out and back to its exact open pixel position: the proxy matches, the origin patch hides, but `editing_rect` is 0.047 to 0.056 pt off `_editing_original_rect` (109.0 vs 109.0466), the plan preview is refused with `geometry_override_present`, `apply_permitted()` is False and Apply stays disabled.
**Cause:** The proxy is placed at `setPos(round(...))`, so the open rect is exact but `_finish_editor_drag` inverts from the rounded pixel grid. The residual (up to 0.5 / scale pt) is far inside `POSITION_CHANGE_TOLERANCE_PT` (0.5), but `_emit` sends `new_rect` for any edge differing by more than 0.01 pt and the model refuses any `new_rect` as a geometry override. Different layers use different "moved" thresholds.
**Fix:** After the inverse, `_finish_editor_drag` compares the box's `sceneBoundingRect()` with `_editing_origin_scene_rect`; within `_ORIGIN_MASK_MIN_DISPLACEMENT_PX` (0.5, the origin patch's own displacement test, imported from `view.text_editing`) and on `_editing_origin_page_idx`, `editing_rect` becomes an exact copy of `_editing_original_rect`; otherwise the inverse stays (3 px off the open pixel is still a move). Gotchas: compare the scene bounding rect (the visual box), not `proxy.pos()` (the first attempt compared `pos()` and failed at 90/180/270, where `pos` is a corner); the block is guarded with `getattr` so the fake views in the GUI regression tests, which lack `sceneBoundingRect`, keep the old path. Tests: `test_grip_out_and_back_to_the_open_position_restores_the_exact_rect_and_keeps_apply[0|90|180|270]` (red 4/4) and the guards `test_grip_out_and_a_little_back_keeps_the_inverse_rect[0|90|180|270]` (3 px) and `test_grip_one_or_two_px_off_the_open_spot_is_a_move_not_a_snap[1|2 x 0|90|180|270]` (1 and 2 px net off the open spot must stay a move with the origin patch visible; red 8/8 when the tolerance is raised to 2.5). The older round-trip test asserts `abs=1.2/scale` and hid the drift. R7-INT-1 (round 2): the 0.5 px snap alone left a band at zoom >= 200 %, where one grip pixel is <= 0.5 pt (0.467 pt at 214 %): `_editing_position_changed` / finalize / `apply_permitted` say "not moved" but `_emit` sends `new_rect`, so the preview is refused, Apply disabled, and a consented rebuild drops the move (`new_rect_arg` None). The snap now also fires whenever `_editing_position_changed(view)` is False (the one chokepoint, same pt tolerance as finalize) and shifts the proxy back onto the open scene position, so box, preview and commit agree and the origin patch hides; a drop OUTSIDE the point tolerance (1 px at <= 100 %, 0.5 pt+) is still a move. Test: `test_grip_one_px_off_the_open_spot_at_214_percent_is_not_a_move_and_keeps_apply` (red: `editing_rect` 0.43 pt off).
**File:** `view/pdf_view.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_editor_mouse_gestures.py`

## A grip drag whose release was swallowed must be completed by the next gesture
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`_settle_lost_grip_drag`, `_end_editor_grip_drag`, `_on_move_grip_started`, `_on_move_grip_finished`, `_mouse_press`, the ACTIVE branch of `_mouse_move`)
**Symptom:** (Round 3 adversarial review, SEQ-2.) A modal opened mid-drag without a finalize (Ctrl+O's file dialog, the close prompt) swallows the grip release and leaves `_drag_active` True. (a) An in-box click then cleared `_drag_active` in `_begin_editor_selection` without `_finish_editor_drag`: the box and the origin patch showed the move while `editing_rect` stayed at the open spot, and the commit landed there with `position_changed` False. (b) A button-less pointer move kept the ACTIVE branch alive, so the box followed the hovering pointer.
**Cause:** Only the SELECTING branch checked `event.buttons() & LeftButton`; every other path that clears the drag state assumed the release would arrive and finish the drag.
**Fix:** One chokepoint, `_settle_lost_grip_drag()` (= `_on_move_grip_finished`: clear the grip latch, then `_end_editor_grip_drag`, i.e. `_finish_editor_drag` when the box moved). It runs at the top of `_mouse_press` (any viewport press is a new gesture; the grip owns its own press) and in the ACTIVE `_mouse_move` branch when no LeftButton is held. A new grip press finishes the stale drag with `_end_editor_grip_drag` only: the grip set its latch for the new press before emitting `drag_started`, so clearing it would drop the new drag. After the settle the box is in the same state as after a real release (a moved box is `geometry_override_present`, Apply refused until the rebuild consent). Unit tests that model a viewport drag with `_FakeMouseEvent` now pass `Qt.LeftButton`. Tests: `test_an_in_box_click_after_a_lost_grip_release_completes_the_drag_and_commits_the_move`, `test_a_button_less_move_after_a_lost_grip_release_ends_the_drag_instead_of_moving_the_box`, `test_a_left_button_move_still_drives_a_live_viewport_drag`, `test_a_second_grip_press_after_a_lost_release_completes_the_first_drag_and_keeps_its_own_latch` (x4 rotations; red: `editing_rect` shift 0.0 pt, `_drag_active` still True). Not driven: the real native dialog; the right/middle press shares the chokepoint but is not separately tested.
**File:** `view/pdf_view.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_editor_mouse_gestures.py`, `test_scripts/test_text_editing_gui_regressions.py`

## The search-jump highlight was hidden under the origin patch
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`display_page`, both branches), `view/text_editing.py` (`_SEARCH_HIGHLIGHT_Z`, `_ORIGIN_MASK_Z`)
**Symptom:** (Round 3 adversarial review, SCN-1.) With an `edit_existing` box grip-moved away and still open (the SEARCH focus-out finalize keeps an unverified or refused edit), searching for the run's text and clicking the hit centred the view on the source span but showed blank page there: the 2 px red search-hit rectangle had zero red pixels in the span region (697 with the patch hidden).
**Cause:** `display_page`'s continuous branch deliberately keeps the editor open on a search jump and adds the highlight with `scene.addRect` and no `setZValue`, so it sits at z 0 under the origin patch (z 10.5), which covers the source span plus a margin of at least 1 scene px and so swallows the pen (1 px outside the span edge).
**Fix:** The highlight item gets `_SEARCH_HIGHLIGHT_Z` = 10.75 (above the patch, below the moving mask 11, proxy 12 and focus border 13). Z order: page 0 < outlines 6 < hover 10 < origin patch 10.5 < search-hit rect 10.75 < moving mask 11 < proxy 12 < focus border 13. The single-page branch (which clears the scene, so no editor or patch can exist) sets the same z for consistency. Any new transient scene item that must stay visible over the page needs a z chosen against this ladder, not the default 0.
**File:** `view/pdf_view.py`, `view/text_editing.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_editor_mouse_gestures.py` (`test_search_jump_highlight_is_drawn_above_the_origin_patch_while_the_box_is_moved`, red: z 0.0 against 10.5)

## Legacy rebuild `new_rect` width test ran on the unrotated rect (short lines on /Rotate 90/270 pages never moved)
**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_apply_redact_insert_body` `new_rect` clamp, the `clamped_new.width < 5` fallback to `layout_rect`)
**Symptom:** (Round 3 E2E3-1, real `hvac-dwg.pdf` page 4, /Rotate 270.) Moving a line under 5 pt tall (3.75 pt `HVAC System Cover`) and confirming the rebuild-consent apply returned SUCCESS but rebuilt the text at its OLD spot (dx +0.71 pt, wanted +14); the only trace was the log warning `new_rect ... clamped 後為空，退回原位插入`. A 38.5 pt line on the same page moved correctly, so it hid until round 7's rotation-aware grip move made the path reachable.
**Cause:** `new_rect` is in UNROTATED space, where a quarter-turn page's line has width = the VISUAL line height. The `width < 5` "clamped to a sliver" guard therefore fired for every drawing-sheet line (3.3-4.9 pt), unclamped.
**Fix:** The sliver test compares against what the caller asked for: `clamped_new.width < min(5.0, new_rect.width)`. A page clamp that really eats the box (drop past the edge) still falls back in place. Rule: a size threshold on an unrotated rect is a visual-height threshold on /Rotate 90/270 pages.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_geometry_page_rotation.py::test_legacy_move_of_a_short_line_lands_at_the_dropped_place` (red: moved 0.40 pt, wanted 40 at 3.75 and 4.9 pt; the 12 pt control and the off-page fallback pass before and after). The /Rotate 90 upward-text twin of this fixture was fixed afterwards, see "Legacy vertical rebuild anchored the htmlbox at the wrong end for upward text".

## Test harness ended the preview session while a kept editor was alive (every test passed, pytest exited 0xC0000409)
**Area:** `test_scripts/test_text_commit_finalize_by_result.py` (`_App.close`), same close shape in `test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py` and `test_text_commit_shipped_defaults.py`; `controller/text_commit_coordinator.py` (`begin_session` via `on_text_edit_plan_preview_request`)
**Symptom:** `test_text_commit_finalize_policy.py` printed "98 passed" and the process then exited -1073740791 (0xC0000409, fault in `Qt6Core.dll`). One test alone (`test_refused_token_apply_keeps_focus_and_its_result`, which types a key right before it ends) reproduced it deterministically, at HEAD too. CI would fail a green suite.
**Cause:** The harness closed by `_end_text_edit_plan_preview_session()` + `wait_for_done()` while a kept inline editor was still alive. The keystroke had armed the editor's 150 ms preview debounce; it fired after the session ended, `on_text_edit_plan_preview_request` saw no session key and began a NEW session, i.e. a running `QThread` that nothing joined. Qt aborts on "QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running" at interpreter exit. The product close path is not affected: `handle_app_close` finalizes the editor (CLOSE_DISCARD) before the window goes.
**Fix:** The harness tears the editor down first, as the product does: `view.finalize_text_edit_for_close(save=False)` before ending the session. Rule: a close helper must destroy whatever can still enqueue preview work (the editor and its timers) before it ends the session that work feeds.
**File:** `test_scripts/test_text_commit_finalize_by_result.py`, `test_text_commit_ui_real_corpus.py`, `test_text_commit_shipped_defaults.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_finalize_policy.py::test_app_close_tears_the_editor_down_before_ending_the_preview_session` and `::test_kept_editor_with_a_late_keystroke_exits_the_process_cleanly` (subprocess, asserts exit code 0; red: 3221226505 / editor left alive). Other per-file harness closes (`_end_text_edit_plan_preview_session()` without `wait_for_done`) have the same shape but no join; not observed to crash.

## Legacy vertical rebuild anchored the htmlbox at the wrong end for upward text (and took the line height from the text length)
**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_apply_redact_insert_body` vertical branch, `_line_ht`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`_binary_shrink_height`, `_vertical_html_rect`)
**Symptom:** (Round 4 ROT90-UP-1; reproduced at HEAD 1f51010 too.) Synthetic /Rotate 90 page, upward text (`dir (0,-1)`, run rotation 270), legacy engine, one-character same-advance edit: with the unmoved `new_rect` the rebuilt ink jumped from visual (400,291,426,300) to (1,295,12,299), dx -406 (the visual left edge = unrotated page bottom), and with `new_rect=None` to (1,239,27,248). A move by `new_rect` landed ~400 pt away too. After the anchor fix alone, two more offsets showed on both quarter turns: the no-rect rebuild sat 8.56 pt inside its pinned edge, and a tight rect scaled the run to 43 % (92 % once the line height was right).
**Cause:** (1) `insert_htmlbox(rotate=...)` starts the text at the rect's TOP for text reading down the unrotated page (run rotation 90, `insert_rotate` 270, first line at the RIGHT edge) but at the rect's BOTTOM for text reading up (run rotation 270, `insert_rotate` 90, first line at the LEFT edge). The branch always built `Rect(x0, y0, x1, page_rect.y1)` and always fixed the right edge (`vertical_shift_left`), which is only right for downward text. (2) `_line_ht` (the `line-height` the css pins) used the span bbox HEIGHT; for a quarter-turn run the unrotated bbox height is the text LENGTH (26.7 pt), not the line thickness (12 pt), so the line box was ~28 pt: the glyph sat 8.56 pt inside the pinned edge and a rect as wide as the real line (12 pt) forced MuPDF to scale the content down. (3) Even with the right line height, a rect exactly as wide as the line is ~2 pt short of the htmlbox's line box + leading (the same 2 pt as `_MUPDF_HTMLBOX_LEADING_OVERHEAD`), which scales the run to ~92 %.
**Fix:** `reads_up = is_vertical and rotation == 270`. Upward text: `insert_rect` = `(x0, page_rect.y0, x1, run bottom)` (bottom edge pinned, growing up), no-rect path anchors the LEFT edge (`anchor_right=False`; `vertical_shift_left` cannot move a first line), `_binary_shrink_height(grow_up=True, max_y0=base_y0)` mirrors the shrink (y1 fixed, y0 searched). `_line_ht` for vertical runs comes from `origin.x` advances / bbox WIDTH. The `new_rect` vertical path widens the rect to `_line_ht + 2` AWAY from the pinned edge. Rule: for rotated htmlbox inserts, know which end and which edge the content starts at before choosing the rect, and never measure a quarter-turn run's line thickness on the unrotated y axis. Residual: `vertical_shift_left=False` on downward text still pins the wrong (left) edge; nothing passes it. Not reproduced on a real fixture (no local /Rotate 90 page has upward text; hvac-dwg upward text is on /Rotate 270 pages only).
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_geometry_page_rotation.py::test_legacy_rebuild_of_quarter_turn_drawing_text_keeps_its_place[90|270 x unmoved_rect|no_rect]` (red at the start: 90 both modes dx -399..-406 pt, 270 no_rect +8.6 pt; the line-height part is pinned by the width assertion, red when `_vertical` is forced False: 4/4) and `::test_legacy_move_of_a_short_line_lands_at_the_dropped_place[90-...]` (red 4/4, moved -399.6 pt).

## SEQ-2 `_settle_lost_grip_drag` read `_drag_active` before `__init__`-less test views had it (26-32 tests failed, never run after SEQ-2)

**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` -- `_mouse_press` / `_settle_lost_grip_drag`; `PDFView.__new__` fixtures in `test_autopan`, `test_interaction_modes`, `test_object_*`
**Symptom:** `AttributeError: 'PDFView' object has no attribute '_drag_active'` at the first line of `_mouse_press` in every fixture-built view; the round gate reported no regressions because the six files were not rerun after SEQ-2.

Rule: after adding a read to a hot entry point, rerun every file that calls it on a `__new__` stub, not only the feature's own tests.

## GUI-test harness `view.close()` leaked a live PDFView and a visible inline editor per test (mouse_gestures: 161 editors, ~45k widgets, ~2 GB)

**Area:** `test_scripts/qt_teardown.py`, `_gui_session` in `test_text_commit_editor_mouse_gestures.py`, the `gui` fixtures of `test_text_commit_live_text_strip.py` and `test_text_commit_source_show_commit.py`
**Symptom:** Tests passed, but a whole-suite process grew without bound (about 10 GB in a ~4 000-test run) and every later `processEvents()` serviced 160+ leaked visible `PreviewBackedInlineTextEditor` top-levels, their debounce timers and strips.
**Cause:** `view.close()` only hides a `PDFView`. The view stays alive; its action bar -> `live_text_strip` holds the open editor until `unbind()`, which only `TextEditManager._teardown_editor` calls, and the editor is a visible top-level widget. Harnesses never cancelled the editor, never `deleteLater()`-ed the view, and `processEvents()` does not deliver `DeferredDelete`.
**Fix:** `dispose_pdf_view(view, controller, model)` (finalize/discard the editor first, end the preview session, close the model, `view.close()`, `view.deleteLater()`, flush `DeferredDelete`) in the three harness teardowns; test `test_gui_session_teardown_leaves_no_live_view_or_visible_editor`. Rule: any harness that opens a real editor tears down with `dispose_pdf_view`, not `view.close()`. Not converted: the other ~40 files that call `view.close()` on views without an open editor.
**File:** `test_scripts/qt_teardown.py`

## A cross-page move of any line that is not the page's last block always failed: the deletion guard looked the positional span id up again

**Area:** `controller/pdf_controller.py` -- `move_text_across_pages`, `_source_run_text_probe`, `_count_page_runs_with_text`, `_resolve_cross_page_move_source_span_id`
**Symptom:** Grip-dragging a line that has another block after it onto another page ended in the dialog "原始文字刪除未完成，已取消跨頁移動。": no move, no history entry, the source text deleted then rolled back. Only the last block of a page (and the single-line fixture the tests used) moved.
**Cause:** After the source deletion the controller rebuilt the index and treated `find_run_by_id(source_page - 1, resolved_target_span_id) is not None` as "text not deleted". Span ids are positional (`p{page}_b{block}_l{line}_s{span}`), so deleting block b1 renumbers the next block into b1 and the lookup finds that neighbour. A second latent bug sat on the same path: the ambiguous-candidate ranking called `PDFModel._normalize_text_for_compare`, which does not exist.
**Fix:** judge the deletion by content: count the page's runs whose whitespace/case-folded text equals the source run's text before the deletion and require the count to drop afterwards (a duplicate line elsewhere or a renumbered neighbour cannot mask or fake it). The ranking uses the module-level `_normalize_run_text`. Rule: never use a positional id to ask "is that thing still there" after a structural edit; compare content or geometry. Tests in `test_cross_page_text_move.py` (non-last lines, duplicated line, no-op deletion still aborts, overlapping-candidate ranking).
**File:** `controller/pdf_controller.py`, `test_scripts/test_cross_page_text_move.py`

## Save As left the live handle on the old file: another tab that rewrote it corrupted the first tab's unread pages and its next save (PERS-1)

**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` -- `save_as`, `_detach_live_doc_from_source_file`, `_session_reading_path`, `_backing_file`, `save_external_document`, `close_session`
**Symptom:** Open A, edit, Save As B, then File > Open A in a second tab, edit it and Ctrl+S (a full rewrite of A: the default after any kept or undone legacy rebuild, because `can_save_incrementally()` is 0 after a rebuild, and also the round-6 orphan fallback). Back in tab 1 the pages not yet viewed are blank or lose their original text (MuPDF "zlib error: incorrect header check" / "syntax error in content stream"), and Ctrl+S in tab 1 writes those blank pages over a good B. Reproduced on HEAD 1f51010 too (real rebuild flow, rotation 0 and 90); it is older than the round-6 fallback.
**Cause:** `save_as` to a new path writes the copy but keeps `self.doc` on A (deliberately un-pruned, so undo/redo slots survive) and then remaps the session to B in `_path_to_session_id`. The same-path guard in `open_pdf`/`save_as` only reads that map, so A looked free; MuPDF reads stream bytes from the file at stored offsets on demand, so the second tab's in-place rewrite moved the objects under tab 1's handle. A page already loaded still looked right, which hid the damage until scrolling.
**Fix:** invariant: a session's live handle never reads a file the session no longer owns. After every `save_as` the handle is rebound (`_detach_live_doc_from_source_file`) to a private `live_<uuid>.pdf` copy in the model temp dir, written from the LIVE doc with `garbage=0` (same numbering and orphans, so `xref_epoch`, retained page snapshots and the test that the live doc is not pruned stay valid; the epoch is restored after the reopen, encryption is re-authenticated). Skipped for in-memory docs, for a handle already on the saved file and for one already on a private copy (a second Save As does not stack copies); `close_session` deletes the copy. The copy is also deleted when a later whole-document reinstall replaces the handle (round 6 FS-2: SnapshotCommand undo/redo for delete/rotate/reorder pages, metadata, merge; the `delete_pages`/`move_page`/`pdf_object_ops` rollbacks; `_roundtrip_live_doc`; also a `recover_*.pdf` the session was rebound to): `close_session` finds the copy only through `session.doc.name`, and the in-memory replacement reports `"pdf"`, so each Open -> Save As -> page op -> undo -> close tab used to leave one document-size `live_*.pdf` in the temp dir for the model's lifetime. The `doc` setter is the one chokepoint every handle replacement passes through: `_retire_replaced_handle` queues the old handle's temp-dir file (unless the new handle reads the same file) and `_sweep_retired_live_copies` unlinks it once the old handle is closed (the reinstall helpers sweep right after their `close()`; `close_session`/`close` sweep too; Windows refuses to unlink an open file, so a copy still open stays queued). `_backing_file` is the only "is a file behind this doc" test: `fitz.open("pdf", data).name` is `"pdf"`, not empty. Same class, guarded at the write side: `save_as` now also refuses a target another session's live handle reads (`_session_reading_path` checks `doc.name`, not just the path map), and `save_external_document` (export pages, merge-to-new-file) refuses any path an open tab reads, the active one included. Pitfall when testing: a stale-offset read only shows when the rewrite moves the objects (grow page 1's stream in tab 2); a same-layout rewrite passes by luck, and the sign is often page 1 losing its original text rather than blank pages.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`; `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py` (`test_save_as_away_then_rewriting_the_original_in_another_tab_leaves_the_first_tab_intact`, `test_external_exports_refuse_to_overwrite_a_file_an_open_tab_reads`, `test_save_as_refuses_a_target_another_tab_still_reads_even_when_its_path_moved_on`, ...)

## A failed overwrite of the open file closed the live doc first: edits lost, session dead, retry reported "document closed" (PERS-2)

**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` -- `_full_save_to_path`, `save_as` (orphan fallback, prepared-doc branch), `_install_stage_over_open_file`, `_rebind_to_recovery_copy`, `_atomic_full_save` (secure sibling, round-7 FS-1), `_restore_doc_from_snapshot`
**Symptom:** Ctrl+S on a file-backed doc (after a legacy rebuild / a 64 KiB+ session orphan, so the round-6 guard picks the full save) while another app, antivirus or sync client holds the PDF: the dialog said "document closed" instead of Permission denied, every later page read or edit raised, the unsaved edits were gone and (disk full) the target could be left truncated. The close-then-copy window itself is older than the orphan guard (HEAD 1f51010 has it on the plain full-save path); the guard routed ordinary saves into it, and the retry in `save_as` masked the real error.
**Cause:** the non-secure same-path branches did `doc.close()` -> `shutil.copy2(temp, path)` -> reopen with nothing between: a copy failure left `self.doc` closed and the only pruned copy was unlinked in `finally`. `save_as` wrapped the orphan-fallback `_full_save_to_path` in the same `try` as the incremental attempt, so its failure re-ran `_full_save_to_path` on the closed handle.
**Fix:** one helper, `_install_stage_over_open_file`: copy the stage to a hidden sibling first (handle and target untouched), then close and `os.replace` it over the target (atomic; no truncated target), reopen; on a replace failure rebind to a recovery file with the live doc's content (`garbage=1`, numbering and epoch kept, re-authenticated if encrypted) and re-raise the real error. Same-class site: the watermark prepared-doc branch (recovery = a separate `garbage=1` copy of the LIVE doc, because the staged clone carries the watermark overlay; costs one extra serialization on that route only). `save_as` retries only a failed incremental attempt. Rule: never close the only handle to unsaved edits before the step that can fail; if you must, keep a copy to rebind to. Side effect: the target is replaced rather than overwritten in place (a symlinked target is resolved first; file ACLs come from the directory, like the secure path). Owner decision (round-6 FS-4, kept): the atomic replace is preferred over in-place identity, so other hard links to the file keep the old content, NTFS named streams on the target (e.g. `Zone.Identifier`, Mark-of-the-Web) are dropped, and a crash between the sibling copy and `os.replace` leaves a visible `.<12 hex>.<tag>.pdf` next to the document (the dot prefix does not hide it on Windows). Do not "fix" this by writing in place; Windows `ReplaceFileW` is the TODOS follow-up. Secure sibling (FS-1): `_atomic_full_save(replace_live_handle=True)` had the old close -> `os.replace` -> reopen-the-TARGET shape, so a failed replace (or a failed reopen) showed the pre-edit file or a closed handle while the `finally` deleted the stage, the only file holding the edits. It now writes the recovery copy first (a byte copy of the verified stage when `doc` is the live doc; a separate `garbage=4` serialization of the LIVE doc when `doc` is the watermark clone, bumping the epoch) and delegates to `_install_stage_over_open_file`, so the secure and non-secure routes share one rebind path. Also `_restore_doc_from_snapshot` now opens the replacement before closing the live handle. Audit: no other site closes the live handle before a step that can fail (optimizer saves work on snapshot copies). Round-8 LS-2 (same invariant, the branch the staged install skips): `_full_save_to_path` only staged when the target was the file the live handle reads (`doc.name`). After any SnapshotCommand undo/redo the live doc is in memory (`doc.name == "pdf"`, `_backing_file` is None) and stays so for the rest of the session, so every later Ctrl+S, and every Save As over an existing file, fell to `self._save_doc(self.doc, path, garbage=1)`: MuPDF opens the destination truncating, so a disk-full or writer exception left an 18-byte (partial) file that no longer opened, while the file-backed route kept the old bytes. Fix at the write chokepoint: `PDFModel._save_doc_to_user_path` (`utils/path_staging.write_via_staging`: sibling stage, then `os.replace`) now serves every non-secure full save to a user path that is not the open-file install: `_full_save_to_path` else branch, `save_as` prepared-doc else branch, `save_external_document` (export pages, merge to file), the page-image export (`export_pages(as_image=True)`: explicit `output=`/`format=` because the stage name ends in `.pdf`) and `model/headless_merge.py`; a failed write also leaves no partial file at a NEW path. Not changed: the incremental save appends in place by design (the file is the prior revision plus a tail), and the secure/open-file routes already stage. Rule: any write whose destination is a user-chosen path goes through a stage + replace, never `doc.save(path)` straight onto it; do not condition the stage on 'the target is the open file'.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`; `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py` (`test_a_failed_overwrite_of_the_open_file_keeps_the_session_edits_and_the_real_error`, `test_a_failed_overwrite_in_the_prepared_doc_branch_keeps_the_session_edits`, `test_a_failed_install_after_the_close_rebinds_the_live_doc_with_numbering_and_epoch`, `test_a_failed_install_over_an_encrypted_file_keeps_the_live_handle_authenticated`, `test_a_failed_secure_overwrite_of_the_open_file_keeps_the_session_edits`, `test_a_secure_save_whose_reopen_fails_keeps_the_session_alive_on_a_copy`, `test_a_failed_secure_overwrite_in_the_prepared_doc_branch_rebinds_to_the_live_doc`, `test_a_secure_save_that_cannot_make_its_recovery_copy_leaves_everything_untouched`, `test_a_failed_snapshot_restore_keeps_the_current_doc`, LS-2: `test_a_failed_full_save_never_truncates_an_existing_target`, `test_a_failed_prepared_doc_save_never_truncates_an_existing_target`, `test_a_failed_external_export_never_truncates_an_existing_target`, `test_a_failed_save_to_a_new_path_leaves_no_partial_file`, `test_a_failed_image_export_never_truncates_an_existing_image`; `test_scripts/test_headless_merge.py::test_headless_merge_failed_write_keeps_an_existing_output`)

## Moving Apply / Cancel / rebuild consent to a `Qt.NoFocus` bar locked keyboard-only users out (a regression vs the focusable sidebar buttons)
**Area:** `view/text_inline_action_bar.py` (`TextInlineActionBar`), `view/pdf_view.py` (`_chain_text_action_bar_tab_order`, `_sync_text_action_bar`)
**Symptom:** After the R4-2 move, a keyboard-only user whose input was refused (glyph coverage, structural, `geometry_override_present` after a move) could not trigger `改用重建文字…` or `套用`: Tab inserts a tab character in the editor, Ctrl+Alt+R then Tab walked the card and left the edit context (FOCUS_OUTSIDE notice) without ever reaching a button, and the only keyboard exits (Esc, F1, Ctrl+S) discard or keep without consenting. At HEAD the buttons were plain (StrongFocus) buttons in the text card: Ctrl+Alt+R, Tab, Space worked.
**Cause:** Two halves. (1) `setFocusPolicy(Qt.NoFocus)` on the buttons, chosen so a MOUSE click cannot move focus out of the editor, also removes them from the Tab chain: `NoFocus` conflates "no click focus" with "no keyboard focus". (2) The bar is a child of `graphics_view.viewport()`, created before the card, so even a TabFocus button sits nowhere near the card in Qt's default focus chain (probe: card controls, toolbar, tab bars, thumbnails, graphics view; never the buttons). Qt also IGNORES `QWidget.setTabOrder` while the card and the bar are not yet in one window (calling it at card-build time did nothing), and stacking/re-parenting a panel resets its chain.
**Fix:** The three buttons are `Qt.TabFocus` (keyboard only; a mouse press still leaves focus with the editor). `PDFView._chain_text_action_bar_tab_order` links rebuild -> Apply -> Cancel after `text_target_mode_combo` (the order they had at HEAD) and runs from `_sync_text_action_bar` (every editor open), idempotently (re-links only when `nextInFocusChain` is off). The bar, `EditorMoveGrip` and `LiveTextStrip` stay `NoFocus`. Hidden/disabled buttons are skipped by Qt, so a hidden rebuild button or disabled Apply never breaks the walk. Rule: when a control must not take focus from a click, use `TabFocus`, never `NoFocus`, unless it has another keyboard path; and any action that has only a mouse path is a defect. Not done (owner decision, TODOS.md): a one-key Apply/rebuild shortcut and a keyboard way to move the box (the grip is mouse-only). Not proven: the focus hand-back after a declined keyboard consent (`_on_text_rebuild_clicked`) is not what keeps the editor alive in the test (removing it left the test green); the test guards survival and focus placement only.
**File:** `view/text_inline_action_bar.py`, `view/pdf_view.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_rebuild_action.py` (`test_the_bar_buttons_are_tab_reachable_but_never_click_focusable`, `test_a_keyboard_only_user_can_give_rebuild_consent`, `test_a_keyboard_only_user_can_apply_and_cancel`, `test_a_declined_keyboard_consent_keeps_the_editor_and_returns_focus_to_it`, `test_a_mouse_click_on_the_rebuild_button_never_takes_the_keyboard_focus`)

## Saving back to the open file failed for paths that open fine: the hidden staging file embedded the stem plus a uuid and overflowed MAX_PATH / the 255-character name limit (FS-3)

**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`_install_stage_over_open_file`, `_atomic_full_save`), `model/pdf_optimizer.py` (`save_optimized_copy_from_snapshot`), `utils/path_staging.py`
**Symptom:** On default Windows (`LongPathsEnabled=0`) a PDF at a ~218-259 character path (deep OneDrive/SharePoint folders with long CJK names) opened and edited fine, but every full (non-incremental) save back to its own path failed with `FileNotFoundError: [WinError 3]` at the sibling copy. A stem over ~209 characters failed even with long paths enabled. HEAD 1f51010 staged in the temp dir and copied onto the target, so it did not fail; the secure `.tmp.pdf` stage and the optimizer's `_opt` stage had the same limit.
**Cause:** the atomic same-directory stage was named `.{stem}.{uuid32}.<tag>.pdf`, 38-42 characters longer than the target itself, so a target within 40 characters of MAX_PATH (or 40 characters of the component limit) could be read and written but not staged beside.
**Fix:** `utils/path_staging.staging_sibling(target, tag)` returns `.<12 hex>.<tag>.pdf` in the target's directory (stem-independent, about 25 characters) and, when the full path would still exceed 259 characters (short stem in a very deep folder), the `\\?\` extended-length form, which `shutil`, `os.replace` and MuPDF all accept regardless of `LongPathsEnabled`. All three stem-derived staging sites use it. Rule: never derive a staging name from the target's name; stage beside the target (atomic `os.replace` needs the same volume) with a short fixed-size name.
**File:** `utils/path_staging.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/pdf_optimizer.py`; `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py` (`test_save_over_the_open_file_works_for_paths_near_the_windows_limit`, `test_secure_export_to_a_deep_new_path_stages_without_overflowing`, `test_staging_sibling_name_is_independent_of_the_target_stem`, `test_extended_length_path_only_rewrites_what_does_not_fit`), `test_scripts/test_pdf_optimize_workflow.py` (`test_save_optimized_copy_to_a_path_near_the_windows_limit`)
