## A close that was not carried out left the inline editor with a dead plan preview
**Area:** `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`handle_app_close`, `_accept_app_close`, `on_text_edit_plan_preview_request`), `controller/text_commit_coordinator.py` (`wait_for_done`, `end_session`)
**Symptom:** (Round 6 MT-1.) Edit text so a verified token exists, click the window X and answer Cancel (or Save All with input that cannot be applied, or close while a print/optimize job runs), then keep typing: Apply never enables, no refusal and no rebuild offer ever arrives (`current_plan_token()` None, `current_rejection_reason()` None, `rebuild_offered()` False). Only Esc or a session change re-armed the preview. The `wait_for_done(1000)` call is at HEAD too.
**Cause:** `handle_app_close` called `plan_preview_coordinator.wait_for_done()` BEFORE the unsaved-changes prompt and the print/optimize deferrals. `wait_for_done` ends the coordinator's session, but the controller's `_plan_preview_session_key`/`_plan_preview_target` are cleared only by `_end_text_edit_plan_preview_session`. After an ignored close the next keystroke took the same-key branch of `on_text_edit_plan_preview_request`, skipped `begin_session`, and `coordinator.request()` returned None because it had no session. One fact (is there a live preview session) was held twice and the close path updated only one copy. The same early teardown also dropped an in-flight result the open editor was waiting for.
**Fix:** The preview session is ended only once the close is certain, in `_accept_app_close` (used by every `event.accept()` path: nothing dirty, Discard All, Save All): it goes through `_end_text_edit_plan_preview_session` (both copies) and then joins the worker; a failed join ignores the close and leaves the keys consistent. Ignored closes (Cancel, Save All that cannot apply, print/optimize deferral, render/thumbnail join timeout) never touch the preview. Chokepoint guard in `on_text_edit_plan_preview_request`: a cached key with a resolved target but no live coordinator session is reset and re-armed as a new session, so any future code that ends the coordinator directly cannot recreate a silent preview. Rule: a close helper must not destroy per-editor state ahead of the answer; the finalize-before-teardown order (finalize, then end the session) is unchanged. Not checked: the page-render and thumbnail coordinators are still cancelled and joined ahead of the prompt (pinned by `test_thumbnail_coordinator.py`); whether a cancelled close leaves a blank page or stale thumbnails was not driven.
**File:** `controller/pdf_controller.py`; `test_scripts/test_multi_tab_plan.py` (`test_mt1_cancelled_app_close_keeps_the_plan_preview_alive`, `test_mt1a_save_all_that_cannot_apply_the_input_keeps_the_plan_preview_alive`, `test_mt1b_close_deferred_by_a_running_job_keeps_the_plan_preview_alive[print|optimize]`, `test_mt1c_carried_out_app_close_still_joins_the_preview_worker`, `test_mt1d_a_coordinator_session_ended_behind_the_controllers_back_is_reopened`; red 6 of 6 before the fix). The `preview_mvc` fixture there tears the editor down before ending the session (see "Test harness ended the preview session while a kept editor was alive"): without it the file passed 80 tests and exited 0xC0000409.

## A close asked while the grip button was held saw no unapplied input
**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`TextEditManager.has_unapplied_input`), `view/pdf_view.py` (`_settle_lost_grip_drag`, `has_unapplied_text_edit`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`_confirm_close_session`, `handle_app_close`)
**Symptom:** (Round 6 MT-2.) Press the move grip, drag the box and, without releasing, press Ctrl+W: no unsaved prompt, the tab closed and the move was lost with no Cancel offered. Alt+F4 in the same state closed the window with no prompt at all. After a release the same Ctrl+W asked correctly.
**Cause:** `editing_rect` follows the box only in `_finish_editor_drag`, so while `_drag_active` is True `_editing_position_changed` compared the old rect and `has_unapplied_input` answered False. The SEQ-2 chokepoint named the close prompt in its docstring but ran only from a viewport press and a button-less move, never before the close checks.
**Fix:** `has_unapplied_input` (the only source of the close question; `has_unapplied_text_edit` and `_inline_editor_has_unapplied_input` delegate to it) calls `_settle_lost_grip_drag` first, i.e. finishes the drag where the box stands like the release it stands in for. The later real release is a no-op (latch reset, `_drag_active` already False). Display-only readers (`apply_permitted`, `current_rejection_reason`) deliberately do not settle: they run during a drag.
**File:** `view/text_editing.py`; `test_scripts/test_multi_tab_plan.py` (`test_mt2_*`)

## A save that installs over the target failed with a sharing error caused by the app's own thumbnail worker, and left the session on a temp copy (R7-2)

**Area:** `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`_background_file_readers_released`, `save`, `save_as`, `_save_session_with_dialog`, `_save_session_for_close`, `save_ordered_sources_as_new`), `controller/thumbnail_coordinator.py` (file worker), `model/pdf_model.py` (`_install_stage_over_open_file`)
**Symptom:** Open a large image-heavy PDF, edit so the round-6 orphan fallback (or a secure / watermark save) picks the install path, press Ctrl+S while the clean-session thumbnail worker is mid-page: the dialog shows `[WinError 5]` (access denied; `WinError 32` for some sharing modes), `doc.name` is now a temp `save_<uuid>.pdf` / `recover_*.pdf`, `is_save_back_to_original` stays False and every later Ctrl+S is a full rewrite. No data is lost.
**Cause:** `ThumbnailCoordinator`'s file worker opens the user's saved file itself (`fitz.open(path)`). Edits and `save` only `cancel()` it (flags checked between pages), nothing joined it, so the worker's handle outlived the call into the model. Windows refuses `os.replace` over a file another handle holds open; the model's rebind-to-recovery then did what it is designed to do. The model is not at fault: its failure is the safe outcome for a reader it cannot know about, and a retry loop there would only hide the race. Only `handle_app_close` joined the worker.
**Fix:** the controller owns the reader, so it releases it: `_background_file_readers_released(resume_thumbnails=...)` cancels the coordinator and joins it (`SAVE_READER_JOIN_TIMEOUT_MS`) around every controller write to a user path (`save`, `save_as`, the close-time saves, merge-to-new-file). A worker that does not stop in time is logged and the save proceeds (the model's recovery rebind still protects the session). An interrupted job is restarted afterwards, also when the save failed; a closing tab does not restart it. Not changed (owner decision, see TODOS): the optimizer's `ProcessPoolExecutor` initializer holds `source_path` open for the pool's lifetime, but that path is only used for a clean file-backed session and the progress dialog is window-modal, so a save cannot be started from the main window while it runs.
**File:** `controller/pdf_controller.py`; `test_scripts/test_thumbnail_coordinator.py` (`test_save_joins_the_thumbnail_file_worker_before_installing_over_the_target`, `test_save_as_joins_*`, `test_save_releases_readers_first_then_resumes_an_interrupted_job`, `test_closing_*`, `test_merge_export_joins_readers_before_writing_the_output`)

## Printing in a secure session renumbered the live document and stranded page-snapshot undo (DS-1)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`_decrypted_snapshot_bytes`, `_open_numbering_clone`, `write_pruned_live_copy`, `capture_print_snapshot_bytes`), `model/tools/manager.py` (`build_print_snapshot`)
**Symptom:** Rotate a page (or edit the TOC, metadata, delete an object: anything that latches `secure_save_required`), add a text box, File > Print > OK, Ctrl+Z: the undo is refused with zero mutation (`AddTextboxCommand.undo(): refused (xref numbering changed since the snapshot)`) and the box stays; the same for a rebuild/legacy `EditTextCommand`. The annotation xrefs the sidebar listed before the print went stale too (`delete_annotation(16)` -> False after `[16, 19] -> [9, 12]`).
**Cause:** The secure print prune was `tobytes(garbage=4)` / `save(garbage=4)` on the LIVE handle, which renumbers the document in place. At HEAD this was invisible to undo (page snapshots were `insert_pdf` one-page PDFs); once page snapshots became in-place xref graphs valid only under their `xref_epoch`, every snapshot command on the stack went stale after a read-only action.
**Fix:** The live handle is only ever serialized with `garbage=0` (numbering-preserving, `encryption=KEEP`) into a throwaway authenticated clone (`_open_numbering_clone`); the `garbage >= 2` prune and the decrypt run on the clone. `_decrypted_snapshot_bytes` and `write_pruned_live_copy` (used by `ToolManager.build_print_snapshot`) are the two chokepoints; neither bumps the epoch any more. Saves are different: they replace the file and legitimately renumber (still `_note_live_doc_serialized`, TODOS "Remap page-graph snapshots across a renumbering save"). Rule: a read-only export of the live document (print, worker snapshot, preview) must prune on a clone, never on the live handle. Cost: one extra `garbage=0` in-memory serialization per secure print.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/tools/manager.py`; `test_scripts/test_page_snapshot_identity.py` (`test_print_in_secure_session_keeps_textbox_undo_and_redo`, `test_print_in_secure_session_keeps_live_numbering_and_still_prunes`, `test_print_of_encrypted_secure_session_keeps_numbering_and_decrypts`, `test_numbering_preserving_paths_keep_the_xref_epoch[print_*]`), `test_scripts/test_secure_persistence.py`

## Merging into the current document never bumped the render revision, so search/render/OCR kept the pre-merge bytes (DS-2)
**Area:** `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`merge_ordered_sources_into_current`, `_invalidate_active_render_state`, `capture_worker_snapshot_bytes`)
**Symptom:** Merge PDFs > add a file above Current > "merge into current" > Ctrl+F for text from the added file finds nothing, while text of the old page 1 is highlighted on the new page 1; async renders and OCR also used the pre-merge document.
**Cause:** The method swapped the live document (`replace_active_document_from_snapshot`) and called only `_invalidate_thumbnails` / `_rebuild_continuous_scene`; the revision-keyed caches (`_worker_snapshot_cache`, `_render_cache`, page sizes) are only dropped by `_invalidate_active_render_state`, which every sibling structural op and undo/redo call.
**Fix:** `_invalidate_active_render_state(clear_page_sizes=True)` right after the replace. Rule: any controller method that installs snapshot bytes as the live document must bump the render revision; `test_every_live_document_replacement_in_controller_bumps_render_revision` (AST guard over `controller/pdf_controller.py`) enforces it.
**File:** `controller/pdf_controller.py`; `test_scripts/test_pdf_merge_workflow.py` (`test_merge_into_current_bumps_render_revision_and_page_sizes`, `test_merge_into_current_worker_snapshot_matches_live_doc`, `test_search_after_merge_into_current_uses_merged_document`, `test_every_live_document_replacement_in_controller_bumps_render_revision`)

## A save over the open file lost every copy of the edits when the replace and the recovery reopen both failed (ERR-1)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`_install_stage_over_open_file`, `_rebind_to_recovery_copy`, `_open_recovery_in_memory`, `SaveRecoveryError`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`_save_failure_text`)
**Symptom:** (Round 7 ERR-1.) Save over the open file; `os.replace` fails (target locked) and `fitz.open` of the recovery copy fails too: the `PermissionError` is shown as an ordinary "儲存失敗", the session is a closed handle ("document closed" on every render/save) and no `save_*`/`recover_*` copy is left, so the edits exist nowhere. Second shape: the replace succeeded, the target reopen and the recovery reopen both fail: the target holds the edit but the user is told the save failed and the session is dead.
**Cause:** the handle is closed before the replace (Windows). `_rebind_to_recovery_copy` returned False on a failed reopen and the `finally` deleted the recovery file because `rebound` was False - the only file holding the edits (on the secure route `_atomic_full_save` had already deleted the stage).
**Fix:** (1) `_rebind_to_recovery_copy` falls back to `_open_recovery_in_memory` (read the recovery file's bytes, `fitz.open("pdf", data)`, re-authenticate), so a path/lock problem cannot kill the session; the `finally` keeps the recovery file only when the handle still reads it. (2) If even that fails, the recovery file is KEPT and `SaveRecoveryError(recovery_path, target_written)` replaces the plain error (`__cause__` = the real error); its message says whether the file was written and where the edits are. (3) The controller shows that message as written (`_save_failure_text`) instead of "儲存失敗: ..." in all four save sites: `save`, `save_as`, `_save_session_with_dialog` and `_save_session_for_close` (the Save All / close path, R8-ERR1-CLOSE: it used to log the error at WARNING and open a Save dialog for the dead session, so the user saw "儲存失敗: document closed"; it now shows the message, offers no dialog and returns False so the close is ignored; an ordinary error still falls back to the dialog). Rule: a recovery copy is deleted only after the session is proven to live without it. Audit: `_install_stage_over_open_file` is the only close-before-reopen site (all callers share it; `_restore_doc_from_snapshot`, `_roundtrip_live_doc`, `_detach_live_doc_from_source_file` open the replacement first). Side effect: after an in-memory rebind the session has no backing file (`_backing_file` is None) until the next successful save-back; a later save writes a normal full file.
**Round 14 (S14-SAVEREC-DEAD-TAB, owner decision C):** the session that raised `SaveRecoveryError` still sat in the tab bar on a CLOSED handle, and `bool(closed_doc)` raises `ValueError: document closed`, so every `if not model.doc` guard was a crash site: a second Ctrl+S / Save As replaced the recovery-path message with `document closed`, `change_page` / `rotate_pages` / the signal slots raised, and the print command opened a modal. Fix at the chokepoints: (1) `DocumentSession.save_lost_error`, set only by `PDFModel._mark_session_lost` (both raise sites of `_install_stage_over_open_file`; it also drops the session's share locks and releases its path so reopening the file starts a live tab); (2) `PDFModel.doc` returns `None` for a lost session, so the closed handle is never handed out (`session.doc` stays for `close_session`); (3) `save_as` (and so `save_session_as`) re-raises the stored error first; (4) controller: `_render_active_session` is the one tab-switch guard (`_render_lost_session`: empty view + notice + status text, editing is off because `total_pages == 0`), `_live_only` wraps every `_connect_signals` slot except `_LOST_SESSION_SLOTS`, `_present_lost_session` runs from every `SaveRecoveryError` catch (`_report_save_failure`); Save As on a lost tab copies the recovery file (`PDFModel.copy_lost_session_recovery`, staged + replaced) and shows both paths, the close prompt offers only Save As / Discard, and Discard keeps the recovery copy until app exit (the model's temp dir removes it; the old comment “discarding the tab removes it” was wrong). Gotchas found on the way: `QGraphicsScene.addWidget()` returns a proxy PYTHON owns - dropping the reference before `scene.clear()` aborts inside Qt (use `QGraphicsProxyWidget` + `scene.addItem`); touching a proxy after `scene.clear()` is an access violation, not a Python error (`shiboken6.isValid` first). Not guarded: direct programmatic calls of mutators (only view signals are wrapped; the UI has no other route); Save As on a lost tab may overwrite the original path if the user picks it (the dialog confirms the overwrite).
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`; `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py` (`test_replace_failure_*`, `test_written_target_*`), `test_scripts/test_save_recovery_error_message.py` (`test_close_path_*`, S14 dead-tab section)

## A close ignored because a background join timed out must say so
**Area:** `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`handle_app_close`, `_accept_app_close`, `_ignore_close_join_timeout`)
**Symptom:** (Round 7 ERR-2.) After answering the unsaved-changes prompt (Save All / Discard All) the window stayed open with no explanation when the plan-preview worker join exceeded 1 s; the render and thumbnail joins were equally silent.
**Cause:** Each `wait_for_done` timeout only called `event.ignore()`; since the preview join moved after the prompt, the user had already discarded or saved.
**Fix:** All three joins go through `_ignore_close_join_timeout`, which ignores the close, logs, and shows a warning toast asking the user to retry.
**File:** `controller/pdf_controller.py`; `test_scripts/test_multi_tab_plan.py` (`test_close_join_timeout_*`)

## A second incremental save from the same live handle overwrote the previous revision and broke the xref chain (EXT-1)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`save_as` incremental branch, `_renew_handle_after_incremental_save`, `_handle_is_spent_for_incremental`)
**Symptom:** (Round 8 EXT-1.) Ctrl+S, edit, Ctrl+S on a file-backed session (also two Ctrl+S with zero edits on a file carrying the editor's `__pdf_editor_watermarks` attachment, such as `test_files/1.pdf`). The file keeps `%%EOF` x 2 however many saves are made; the newest trailer's `/Prev` points into bytes the newest revision overwrote. qpdf: `xref not found` / `loop detected following xref tables`; when both revisions have the same length `/Prev` equals its own `startxref` and MuPDF itself opens the saved file with 0 pages. `fitz.open` and pypdf repair a merely wrong `/Prev` silently, which is why the multi-save tests never noticed. Reproduces in pure PyMuPDF 1.27.1 and at HEAD.
**Cause:** MuPDF remembers the end-of-file offset it read when the handle was opened; an incremental `save` does not advance it. The second incremental save from the same handle therefore appends at the ORIGINAL end of file again. Every full-save path already reopens the file (`_reopen_doc_after_save`); only the incremental branch kept the handle.
**Fix:** after a successful incremental save `save_as` calls `_renew_handle_after_incremental_save`: it reopens the saved file, swaps the live handle (the `doc` setter resets the tiered engine; the xref epoch is restored because the numbering did not change; the persisted baseline is re-noted) and closes the old handle. If the reopen fails or the page count differs, the old handle is marked spent (`_INCREMENTAL_SPENT_ATTR` on the `fitz.Document`) and `save_as` refuses the incremental route for it, so the next save is a full save. Rule: a `fitz.Document` may append at most one incremental revision; anything that saves incrementally must hand the session a fresh handle. Judge multi-save output with a strict reader (qpdf/pikepdf or the raw `startxref` -> `/Prev` walk in the tests), never with `fitz.open`.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`; `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py` (`test_repeated_incremental_saves_*`, `test_a_same_length_second_revision_does_not_loop_the_xref_chain`, `test_a_failed_reopen_after_an_incremental_save_forces_the_next_save_to_a_full_one`, `test_real_file_saved_repeatedly_passes_a_strict_reader`, `test_signed_doc_repeated_incremental_saves_*`)

---

## Reading `needs_pass` on an authenticated handle blanks it (R9 M9-1)
**Area:** `model/signed_append_save.py` (`_replayable`), `model/pdf_optimizer.py` (`resolve_file_backed_optimize_source`, `_capture_encryption_descriptor`); every `doc.needs_pass` read in `model/` and `controller/`
**Symptom:** (Round 9 M9-1.) Open a signed PDF that also has a user password (AES-256) with the password, add a highlight, Save As (or Ctrl+S after a SnapshotCommand undo, which leaves an in-memory handle). The save reports success and `has_unsaved_changes()` is False, but the live pages extract `''` and the written file authenticates yet every page's text is `''` (annotation strings raise `UnicodeDecodeError`); on the in-memory Ctrl+S the unreadable file replaced the user's ORIGINAL. MuPDF logs `aes padding out of range` / `syntax error in content stream`. The optimizer's file-backed source probe blanked live page 2 the same way.
**Cause:** In PyMuPDF 1.27.1 the `needs_pass` getter re-runs the empty-password check and overwrites the handle's crypt key even after a successful `authenticate()`. Every object not decoded yet then decrypts to garbage on that handle (a fresh `open` + `authenticate` alone reads fine; `open`, `needs_pass`, `authenticate`, `needs_pass`, `get_text()` returns `''`). `_replayable` read `state.needs_pass` on the LIVE document; the append declined (encrypted) and the fallback full save serialized the poisoned handle. `is_encrypted`, `metadata`, `permissions`, `xref_get_key(-1, ...)`, `can_save_incrementally()` and `len()` do not poison; a second `authenticate(pw)` heals the handle.
**Fix:** Never read `needs_pass` on a handle that may already be authenticated. `_replayable` reads the flags only on `base` (a fresh, never-authenticated copy of the source file) and compares `state` to it through the trailer `/Encrypt` entry (same dictionary means the same password requirement; an owner-only signed file still appends). The optimizer probe gates on `doc.is_encrypted or session.auth_level is not None` (`auth_level` is set at open exactly when a user password was needed) and `_capture_encryption_descriptor` uses `is_encrypted` plus `metadata['encryption']`. Reads that remain sit on freshly opened or `tobytes` clone handles right before their `authenticate()` and are listed in the AST guard `test_needs_pass_is_only_read_where_the_handle_is_known_unauthenticated`; a new site fails it until audited.
**File:** `model/signed_append_save.py`, `model/pdf_optimizer.py`; `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py` (`test_encrypted_signed_save_keeps_the_live_session_and_the_file_readable`, `test_append_state_refuses_an_encrypted_state_document`, `test_append_state_refuses_an_encrypted_state_over_a_plain_source`, `test_signed_owner_only_encrypted_doc_still_appends_after_an_undo`, `test_needs_pass_is_only_read_where_the_handle_is_known_unauthenticated`), `test_scripts/test_pdf_optimize_workflow.py` (`test_file_backed_source_probe_*`)

## A watermark save over the open file rebound the live handle to the baked target: text edits on that page became un-undoable (R9 M9-2)

**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`save_as` prepared-doc branch, `_atomic_full_save(replace_live_handle=True)` with a prepared clone, `_install_stage_over_open_file`, `_rebind_to_recovery_copy`)
**Symptom:** (Round 9 M9-2.) Pending watermark on page 1, Tier 0 text edit on page 1, Ctrl+S (or Save All on close; incremental on or off, secure or not) to the same path. Ctrl+Z logs `layout moved but the page also changed beyond a renumbering; relocation refused` and `tier0 inverse patch stale (StalePlanError); undo refused`; undo and redo return False for the rest of the session. A watermark on another page, or no watermark, is fine. Ctrl+S three times also baked the overlay 1, 2, 3 times.
**Cause:** the prepared clone (watermark overlay inserted into the page's /Contents) was staged and `_install_stage_over_open_file` reopened the TARGET as the live handle. The live doc therefore carried `[q, orig, Q, overlay]`, the xref epoch was not restored, and every retained patch compared the page against a stream layout that no longer matched. The pending-watermark list was still set, so the next save added another overlay on top.
**Fix:** `_install_stage_over_open_file(..., keep_live_content=True)`: after the atomic `os.replace` the session is rebound to `recovery` (the `garbage=1` serialization of the UNBAKED live doc, same numbering; `_rebind_to_recovery_copy` restores the epoch and falls back to an in-memory open) instead of reopening the target. Both callers that stage a prepared clone pass it (`save_as`; `_atomic_full_save` when `doc is not live_doc`). The handle then reads a private temp copy like Save As already does, so later saves take the plain user-path write and bake one overlay each. Rule: a stage that is not the live doc's content must never become the live handle.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_persistence.py` (`test_undo_redo_survive_a_watermark_save_over_the_open_file`, `test_watermark_save_over_the_open_file_does_not_stack_copies`, `test_watermark_on_another_page_keeps_undo_and_the_session_off_the_target`, `test_watermark_save_survives_a_failed_private_copy_reopen`)

## Another program rewrote the session's file: Ctrl+S appended onto foreign bytes and reported success, or silently clobbered it (F10-FS-1)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`save_as`, `_refuse_save_over_foreign_rewrite`, `_record_disk_fingerprint`, `_file_fingerprint`, `SourceChangedOnDiskError`, `DocumentSession.disk_fingerprint`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`_save_failure_text`, `_save_session_for_close`)
**Symptom:** (Round 10 F10-FS-1.) Open a.pdf, insert a page, copy another PDF over a.pdf in Explorer (or `copy /y`, `Copy-Item`, `open('wb')` - all succeed while the file is open), Ctrl+S. App path: "儲存完成", dirty False, the file and the live document are the foreign document plus the session's xref update; the user's pages are gone. Bare-edit path: `Can't do incremental writes on a repaired file`, then `PermissionError [WinError 5]` naming the hidden `.<hex>.install.pdf` staging file, session rebound to a copy of the foreign content. After a Save As the new file is not held at all (the live handle reads a private copy), so a foreign rewrite of it was replaced by the session's pages on the next Ctrl+S with no prompt.
**Cause:** MuPDF opens the file with a share mode that allows writers, reads objects lazily at stored offsets, and repairs the xref when the bytes no longer match - after which the in-RAM edits are gone. Nothing recorded what the session's file looked like, so no save could tell its own file from a foreign one.
**Fix:** every session keeps `disk_fingerprint` = `(size, mtime_ns, sha256 of the first and last 4 KB)` of the file it owns (`disk_fingerprint_path`, canonical), recorded at `open_pdf` / `import_session_transfer` and at ONE chokepoint: the end of `save_as` after a successful write (also after a failed save to the same path - that write was ours). `save_as` checks it before anything is touched (before `apply_pending_redactions`): a save back to that path whose current fingerprint differs raises `SourceChangedOnDiskError` (nothing written, session still dirty, the refusal repeats until the user saves elsewhere). The edge digest is needed because Explorer / `copy /y` keep the SOURCE's mtime. A missing or unreadable file is not a conflict. The controller shows the message as written; the close / Save All path shows it and then offers the Save dialog. Rule: anything new that writes the session's own file outside `save_as` must re-record the fingerprint or the next Ctrl+S is refused.
**Residual risk (owner decision, TODOS):** the gate only protects the file. The live document still reads the foreign bytes and can lose its edits in RAM before any save (deny-write share lock for the session vs. loading into memory). RESOLVED on Windows by the deny-write share lock (OD-FS1-LOCK entry below); the gate remains the defence where the lock is degraded or unavailable. Separately, a damaged file that MuPDF repairs lazily DURING a save drops the in-RAM edits too (`is_repaired` False -> True, edits gone even when the raw incremental save returns normally); moving the full-save fallback out of the `except` block made that case report success with the edits missing, so it was reverted. RESOLVED (up to 200,000 xref slots) by reading every object at open (OD-FS1-READALL entry below).
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`; `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py` (`test_save_over_a_file_a_foreign_writer_replaced_is_refused_not_reported_as_success`, `test_save_after_save_as_refuses_to_clobber_a_foreign_rewrite_of_the_new_file`, `test_a_same_size_same_mtime_foreign_rewrite_is_still_detected`, `test_the_sessions_own_saves_never_trip_the_changed_on_disk_gate`, `test_a_save_that_failed_after_writing_the_target_does_not_lock_the_session_out`), `test_scripts/test_save_recovery_error_message.py` (`test_a_save_refused_because_the_file_changed_on_disk_is_shown_as_written`, `test_close_path_explains_a_changed_file_then_offers_save_as`)

## A signed Save As embedded another program's revision of the source as its signed prefix (F11-FS-1)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`_save_signed_by_appending`, `_signed_append_base_bytes`, `_edge_digest_of_bytes`), `model/signed_append_save.py` (`append_state_onto_source(source_bytes=...)`)
**Symptom:** (Round 11 F11-FS-1.) Signed file open, live doc memory-backed (any SnapshotCommand undo or repair), another program appends an incremental revision to the source. Ctrl+S is refused (F10-FS-1), but Save As to a NEW path wrote a file that started with the FOREIGN bytes plus the session's revision (3 xref sections instead of 2); the visible pages were the session's, the foreign revision sat in the history under the signature.
**Cause:** the F10-FS-1 gate only guards the file being WRITTEN. `_save_signed_by_appending` takes `original_path` as the signed prefix and `append_state_onto_source` read its current bytes unconditionally, so the source side had no check at all.
**Fix:** `_signed_append_base_bytes` compares the source's current bytes with the session's `disk_fingerprint` of that path: the first `size` bytes whose edge digest (`_edge_digest_of_bytes`, same function of the content as `_file_fingerprint`, pinned by a test) matches are the prefix, so an untouched, mtime-touched or foreign-APPENDED source gives exactly the bytes the session opened (output = those bytes + one revision, signature kept); a shorter, rewritten or unreadable source gives `None` and the save takes the existing full-rewrite path with the existing "signature will no longer verify" warning, never a copy of the foreign file. (SIG-DIALOG: that rewrite now needs the user's consent, reason `source_changed`.) A session with no fingerprint of that path keeps the unchecked read. The bytes are read once and passed to `append_state_onto_source(source_bytes=...)`, so there is no check-then-read race.
**Residual risk:** the digest covers the first and last 4 KB of the opened bytes, like the F10-FS-1 gate: a foreign edit confined to the middle of a file larger than 8 KB that keeps its length is not seen (small files are digested whole). The live handle can still read foreign bytes (owner decision in TODOS, unchanged).
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/signed_append_save.py`; `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py` (`test_signed_save_as_never_embeds_a_foreign_revision_of_the_source_as_its_prefix`, `test_signed_save_as_after_a_mtime_only_touch_still_appends_onto_the_source`, `test_signed_save_as_after_a_foreign_in_place_rewrite_does_not_embed_the_foreign_file`, `test_signed_save_as_over_a_source_that_vanished_still_degrades_not_crashes`, `test_signed_append_base_is_the_opened_prefix_when_a_large_file_gets_a_foreign_append`, `test_edge_digest_of_bytes_matches_the_file_fingerprint_digest`)

## A stream's `/Length` differs between the live handle and the appended encrypted file, so the signed append declined (H10-1)
**Area:** `model/signed_append_save.py` (`_same_record`, `_same_object_text`, `_differing_xrefs`, `_identical`)
**Symptom:** (Round 10 H10-1.) A signed PDF encrypted with an owner password only (AES-256/AES-128/RC4, empty user password, opens unprompted) was fully rewritten, dropping the signature bytes, by Save As or by Ctrl+S after a SnapshotCommand undo, once the edit had added or changed a stream (a highlight's appearance Form XObject, any text edit's `/Contents`). Only a `signed append save declined` debug line and the "falling back to a full rewrite" warning showed it. A dictionary-only edit (page rotation) appended fine, and the existing owner-only test passed because its post-undo handle was re-opened from encrypted bytes.
**Cause:** The replayed stage was correct (source kept as an exact prefix, decoded and raw streams equal), but the verification compared `xref_object()` text and a stream dictionary printed `/Length 125` in the live, unsaved handle (plaintext) and `/Length 144` once read back from the appended revision (ciphertext = plaintext + IV + padding). `/Length` is derived from the stream bytes, so the difference carried no meaning.
**Fix:** `_same_record` compares everything but the top-level `/Length` when BOTH records are streams with equal raw bytes (`_same_object_text(..., ignore_length=True)`); non-stream objects, unequal bytes and every other entry still compare exactly. The chokepoint is shared by the replay selection and the post-write verification. AES-256, AES-128 and RC4-128 all green. Not changed: `text_commit.inspect` fingerprints already treat `/Length` as encoding noise (`_INVARIANT_STREAM_ENCODING_KEYS`).
**File:** `model/signed_append_save.py`; `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py` (`test_state_level_append_accepts_a_live_new_stream_on_an_owner_only_file`, `test_owner_only_aes_signed_doc_keeps_the_signed_revision_after_a_live_highlight`, `test_same_record_ignores_only_the_derived_stream_length`)

## A 28 KB PDF declaring a 4M-slot xref stream stalled every signed-append save ~70 s (H10-2)
**Area:** `model/signed_append_save.py` (`_in_use_xrefs`, `_differing_xrefs`, `_identical`, `append_state_onto_source`, `xref_slots_are_unbacked`, `MAX_UNBACKED_XREF_SLOTS`, `XREF_SLOTS_PER_SOURCE_BYTE`, `MAX_APPEND_GROWTH_SLOTS`)
**Symptom:** (Round 10 H10-2.) An xref stream with `/Size 4000000 /Index [0 4000000]` whose extra rows are all free Flate-compresses to 28 638 bytes; MuPDF opens it in 0.09 s (2 pages, not repaired; its own cap is 8 388 607). `_differing_xrefs` walked `range(1, xref_length)` in Python with two `xref_object()` + two `xref_is_stream()` reads per slot: 34.4 s per walk, and one signed save walks twice (replay + verify), so Save As or a post-undo Ctrl+S of a signed file froze the UI for ~70 s. Round 10 then declined such tables before the walk, which made it worse in a quieter way: the declined save is the full rewrite, so the signature was lost, and because that rewrite writes a classic table (20 B per slot) the next signed save of the same session passed the guard and walked anyway (4M: 20.6 s).
**Cause:** the walk's cost is proportional to the DECLARED table size, which a file controls for a few KB. The replay only needs the slots that hold an object on either side.
**Fix (round 11, H10-2 Part A):** a census. `_in_use_xrefs(doc)` asks MuPDF which slots hold an object, one C call per slot (`fitz.mupdf.ll_pdf_object_exists` through `itertools.compress`, ~0.19 us per slot, no object loaded): `n`/`o` rows and unsaved new objects are in it; free rows, never-written `get_new_xref()` padding, `/Index` gaps and slot 0 are not; no side effect on the handle. `_differing_xrefs(state, base, state_in_use)` compares only `state_in_use | _in_use_xrefs(base)` below the state's length with the unchanged per-slot body. A slot outside both sets reads `null` on both sides, which the full walk skipped at its null/null shortcut, so the result is the same list (pinned by `test_the_census_diff_equals_the_full_walk` on control / object-stream / owner-only AES files, file-backed and memory states). One state census serves the replay and the verification: three censuses per save. If the state census exists but the base/check census fails, the append declines; it never falls back to an unbounded walk. Fallback: without the primitive (`_in_use_xrefs` returns None and logs which one is missing), the round-10 guard (`xref_slots_are_unbacked`: `MAX_UNBACKED_XREF_SLOTS` = 100 000 always allowed, then one slot per source byte) still declines before the full walk. The `get_new_xref` pad loop (~12 us per call) is bounded on its own by `MAX_APPEND_GROWTH_SLOTS` = 100 000 (state length minus base length; normally a few slots). The full walk keeps skipping the stream probe for slots null on both sides. Measured on a copy of the 4M fixture: `append_state_onto_source` 0.10 s declined -> 2.6 s appended (prefix kept, 29.6 KB); the 8.3M practical maximum ~5.7 s (probe). At MuPDF's cap (8 388 607) MuPDF itself refuses new objects (`FzErrorLimit`), the edit fails and the existing fallback runs.
**Trade-off:** still O(declared slots), at C-call speed on the UI thread (~0.7 s per million slots per census). `fitz._as_pdf_document` and `fitz.mupdf.ll_pdf_object_exists` are private PyMuPDF API, bounded by the `>=1.27,<1.28` pin and the getattr fallback; `test_in_use_census_semantics` asserts both exist so a PyMuPDF bump fails loudly instead of silently taking the guard.
**Gotcha:** `xref_object(x)` RAISES on an `/Index`-gap slot (`code=7: cannot find object in xref`); that is why `_source` catches and why a census must not be built from `xref_object`.
**Residual (owner accepted, round 10, "Part C"):** new objects take numbers at or above the declared `/Size` (MuPDF allocates at `xref_length()` and never reuses free slots). qpdf 12 / pikepdf ignore object ids above `file_size / 3` ("reported number of objects (4000005) is not one plus the highest object number (10075)": the number it reports is the highest id it accepted), so on such a hostile file they show all pages but the new annotations resolve to `null`; MuPDF, pypdf and poppler show the edit. The native incremental Ctrl+S had the same limit before this fix. Relocating new objects into low free slots (Part C) was not taken; padding the file to 3 x the highest object number was rejected. The round-10 residual line "MuPDF's own writer is O(declared slots), not fixable in Python without changing the numbering" was wrong: the slow full serializations were PyMuPDF's Python file-object sink, see the next entry.
**File:** `model/signed_append_save.py`; `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py` (`test_a_tiny_file_declaring_a_huge_xref_table_appends_and_keeps_the_signature`, `test_the_signed_append_reads_only_slots_in_use`, `test_in_use_census_semantics`, `test_the_census_diff_equals_the_full_walk`, `test_without_the_census_the_unbacked_guard_still_declines_before_any_walk`, `test_a_missing_base_census_declines_instead_of_walking_the_whole_table`, `test_the_append_declines_a_state_that_grew_past_the_growth_cap`, `test_a_signed_save_as_of_a_sparse_table_keeps_the_signature`, `test_the_same_declared_table_appends_when_the_floor_or_the_file_backs_it`, `test_xref_slots_are_unbacked_boundaries`, `test_the_xref_walk_skips_the_stream_probe_for_slots_free_on_both_sides`)

## Every whole-document snapshot took ~19 s on a 4M-slot table: PyMuPDF's Python file-object sink, not MuPDF's writer (H10-2 Part B)
**Area:** `model/doc_bytes.py` (`serialize_doc`, `serialize_via_file`, `serialize_in_memory`, `source_is_encrypted`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`serialize_document_bytes`, `_capture_doc_snapshot`, `_encryption_keeping_bytes`, `_decrypted_snapshot_bytes`, `_roundtrip_live_doc`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`merge_ordered_sources_into_current`), `model/pdf_optimizer.py` (`_document_bytes`), `model/tools/watermark_tool.py` (`prepare_doc_for_save`), `model/text_commit/engine.py` (`_build_scratch_copy`), `model/text_commit/preview.py` (`_live_keep_round_trip`, `_session_snapshot_bytes`), `model/text_commit/verify.py` (reopen probe, `_ocg_membership_status`), `model/xref_compaction.py` (`compact_in_memory`)
**Symptom:** (Round 10/11 H10-2.) On the 28 KB / 4M-slot file every annotation or text command took ~40 s (two `_capture_doc_snapshot` calls of ~20 s), and search / OCR / print paid the same for their worker snapshot on the GUI thread. Model scenario "highlight, undo, highlight, Ctrl+S, highlight, Ctrl+S" took 148 s and ended with an 80 MB file without the signature.
**Cause:** `tobytes()` and `save(io.BytesIO)` hand MuPDF a Python file object (`JM_new_output_fileptr`, a SWIG director), so every `fz_write` calls into Python, and MuPDF's classic xref writer makes about one write per row: ~4.5 us per row. MuPDF's native file output writes the same 80 001 834 bytes in 0.35 s instead of 18.6 s, byte-identical (an ordinary 47 MB file: 0.18 s -> 0.056 s).
**Fix:** one chokepoint, `model.doc_bytes.serialize_doc(doc, *, encryption, garbage=0, no_new_id=0, deflate=0, scratch_dir=None, in_memory=False)`, returns what `tobytes` would (pinned): by default `doc.save(<snap_*.pdf in scratch_dir>)`, read back and deleted at once; a DECRYPTED copy of a file encrypted on disk (`encryption` not KEEP and the trailer encryption string in `metadata`, the signal that survives `authenticate()`) or a caller-flagged plaintext copy (`in_memory=True`) is written by MuPDF into an `fz_buffer` instead and never touches disk (`serialize_in_memory` mirrors `Document.save`'s prelude: `resynth_required = 0`, `JM_embedded_clean`, `JM_ensure_identity` unless `no_new_id`; it falls back to `tobytes` if a private name is missing). `encryption` has no default and `incremental` is not accepted. `PDFModel.serialize_document_bytes` (KEEP by default) passes the model's temp dir and forces memory for a secure-latched session (its `garbage=0` snapshots still hold what a destructive edit removed). Always in memory: the controller merge (pages decrypted from encrypted sources), the optimizer (`_document_bytes`: its working documents are decrypted copies), the watermark save clone (it receives those working documents), `text_commit.verify` (may run on a decrypted scratch) and, since w1b, the open-time xref compaction (`xref_compaction.compact_in_memory`: `garbage=2`, `encryption=KEEP`, `in_memory=True`; its bytes are only reopened as the session's memory-backed document, so no temp file is written at open). The controller merge now calls the model instead of `save(io.BytesIO)` itself. `test_live_doc_roundtrips_preserve_encryption` also checks the serializers' calls on the live document. Measured on a copy of the 4M fixture: `_capture_doc_snapshot` 20.9 s -> 0.41 s; one highlight (2 snapshots) ~40 s -> 0.8 s; the scenario above 148.0 s -> 9.1 s, both saves append (3.3 s each, 29.5 KB, signed prefix kept).
**Gotchas:** (1) `tobytes(use_objstms=1)` is not a fix: it MUTATES the handle it serializes (each call adds an `/ObjStm` and an `/XRef` object, `xref_length` 4000002 -> 4000004 -> 4000006, doc left dirty), and a state reopened from those bytes declines the signed append (container rule). (2) A test counting `fitz.Document.tobytes` calls no longer sees model snapshots; count `model.doc_bytes.serialize_doc` too (the preview contract tests count both), and call sites use `doc_bytes.serialize_doc` through the module so such a patch reaches them. (3) With `no_new_id=0` the second `/ID` element is new on every call, through either sink.
**Not switched:** `_repair_doc_xref_in_memory` (the open-time `garbage=1` repair round trip) still uses `doc.tobytes`. Snapshot memory stays O(declared slots) (80 MB at 4M), bounded by `CommandManager.MAX_UNDO_STACK_BYTES`.
**Round 12 (F12-H102-2) - the temp file must never be a precondition of an edit:** `tobytes()` never needed a disk, so once every KEEP snapshot went through `serialize_via_file` a vanished model temp dir (a temp cleaner / Storage Sense on a long session) or a full volume made every snapshot-recorded edit (`_capture_doc_snapshot` before the mutation) raise `FileNotFoundError` / MuPDF `FzErrorSystem`, while Save As to another path still worked. `serialize_doc` now retries the same options through `serialize_in_memory` when the file sink raises `OSError` or `fitz.mupdf.FzErrorBase` (note: a failed `Document.save` to a path raises MuPDF's `FzErrorSystem`, which is NOT an `OSError`), with a logged warning; the bytes are identical and a real document error (zero pages -> `ValueError`) still propagates from the retry. Only KEEP / plaintext-source documents reach the file sink, so the fallback never weakens the encrypted-copy rule. Every snapshot site is behind `serialize_doc` (AST-pinned), so this one chokepoint covers them all. Not changed in Round 12: the user-initiated Save / optimize paths that staged a file in the temp dir (`save_*.pdf`, `optimized_*.pdf`, `recover_*.pdf`); Round 13 (F13-ENV-1, below) fixed them. Tests: `test_doc_bytes.py` (`test_a_failing_file_sink_falls_back_to_the_memory_sink`, `test_a_vanished_scratch_dir_falls_back_to_the_memory_sink`, `test_a_genuine_document_error_still_propagates_through_the_fallback`, `test_edits_are_still_recorded_after_the_model_temp_dir_is_removed`). Not verified: a real ENOSPC (simulated by a failing `Document.save`).
