## Ctrl+S over the open file failed with WinError 5 after a text edit on a page with 2+ annotations: PyMuPDF Page<->Annot cycle garbage still held the file (MBT-1)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`_install_stage_over_open_file`, `_atomic_full_save`, signed append), `utils/path_staging.py` (`replace_file`, `write_via_staging`), `utils/pymupdf_refs.py` (`forget_walked_annot`), `model/text_commit/inspect.py` (`_annotation_entries`), `model/tools/annotation_tool.py` (`_find_annotation`), `model/pdf_optimizer.py`
**Symptom:** (Round 10 MBT-1.) A file-backed session whose page 1 carries two or more annotations and a pending watermark: a Tier 0 text edit on that page, then Ctrl+S. The prepared-clone install `os.replace`d the staged sibling over the open file right after `live.close()` and raised `PermissionError [WinError 5]`; the session was rebound to `recover_*.pdf`, the target was not written, dirty stayed True, and the immediate retry (`write_via_staging`) failed the same way until an unrelated gen-2 collection ran. One annotation, no edit, or a rejected edit saved fine.
**Cause:** `page.first_annot` / `Annot.next` register every walked annotation in a strong `Page._annot_refs` dict, and an annotation reached through `.next` owns a strong reference to that parent page: a Page<->Annot reference cycle (the first annotation uses a weak proxy and is cycle-free, which is why 1 annotation never failed). `Document.close()` does not release it, so the MuPDF file stream stays open until the cyclic GC runs. `page_fingerprint` -> `_annotation_entries` walked the list that way on every Tier 0 edit, and `_find_annotation` on every annotation move/update. The repo already collected before deleting a detached copy (`_remove_detached_copy`, `_sweep_retired_live_copies`) but not before the staging `os.replace` sites. `page.annots()` / `load_annot` use a weak parent and leave nothing, but are O(n^2) (the reason `_annotation_entries` walks the list).
**Fix:** (1) the producers: `utils.pymupdf_refs.forget_walked_annot` drops the page-side registry entry of every `.next` annotation, so `_annotation_entries` and `_find_annotation` leave no cycle (the O(n) walk is kept). (2) the chokepoint, whatever creates the garbage: `utils.path_staging.replace_file` = `os.replace`, and on `PermissionError` one `gc.collect()` plus one retry (a lock that survives the collection is real and re-raised; the happy path never collects). Used by `write_via_staging` (every non-secure save to a user path, headless merge), `_atomic_full_save`'s plain replace, `_install_stage_over_open_file` (before the recovery rebind), the signed-append install and the optimizer's two destination installs. Rule: a close is not a release - anything that replaces or deletes a file a PyMuPDF handle read must tolerate cycle garbage; never walk `first_annot`/`next` without cutting the registry entry.
**File:** `utils/path_staging.py`, `utils/pymupdf_refs.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/pdf_optimizer.py`, `model/text_commit/inspect.py`, `model/tools/annotation_tool.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_persistence.py` (`test_the_fingerprint_annotation_walk_leaves_no_page_annot_cycle`, `test_annotation_lookup_by_xref_leaves_no_page_annot_cycle`, `test_replace_file_*`, `test_write_via_staging_over_a_file_pinned_by_uncollected_cycle_garbage`, `test_ctrl_s_after_a_tier0_edit_on_a_page_with_annotations_installs_over_the_open_file`, `test_install_stage_over_open_file_survives_cycle_garbage_pinning_the_target`)

## A file MuPDF reads as 0 pages was replaced by a blank page, and Ctrl+S then overwrote the real file (H10-3)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`PDFModel.open_pdf`, `_guard_foreign_doc`, `_ZERO_PAGE_MESSAGE`)
**Symptom:** (Round 10 H10-3.) A signed 2-page file plus one incremental revision whose trailer `/Prev` points at its own xref (or an A<-B<->C loop): pikepdf and pypdf read 2 pages, MuPDF 1.27.1 reports `cannot find object in xref (1 0 R)`, `page_count == 0`, `is_repaired == False`. `open_pdf` installed a fresh in-memory blank page (name None, not dirty) with only a log warning; one edit plus Ctrl+S rewrote the original path: 1759 -> 1046 bytes, 1 page, signature and both text pages gone, "save complete" shown. The same 0-page input silently contributed nothing to a merge / insert.
**Cause:** the 0-page "fallback" (meant to avoid crashes) detached the session from the file it was opened from while keeping `original_path`, so the normal save path treated the blank as the user's document.
**Fix:** `open_pdf` closes the handle and raises `RuntimeError` (no session, file untouched; the controller already shows "打開 PDF 失敗"). The message avoids the password-retry keywords. `_guard_foreign_doc` (the chokepoint for merge sources, `insert_pages_from_file`, `headless_merge`, `compose_merged_document`) raises the same error, so a foreign 0-page source can no longer be dropped silently. Rule: never substitute a synthetic document for an unreadable one while keeping the source path; refuse instead.
**Residual:** the file cannot be opened in the editor at all (repair via qpdf/pikepdf first); opening it read-only with a recovery path is an owner/UX decision, not implemented.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`; `test_scripts/test_security_pdf_resource_guards.py` (`test_open_pdf_refuses_a_zero_page_file_instead_of_substituting_a_blank`, `test_open_pdf_zero_page_refusal_keeps_the_already_open_session`, `test_guard_foreign_doc_rejects_a_zero_page_source`, `test_headless_merge_refuses_a_zero_page_input_and_writes_nothing`, `test_insert_pages_from_file_refuses_a_zero_page_source`)

## Save As to a name with a trailing dot or space: the session key matched no later lookup, reopening made a second tab (F10-FS-2)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`_canonicalize_path`, `save_as`, `find_session_by_path`, `_path_to_session_id`), `model/pdf_optimizer.py` (`save_optimized_copy`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (output-path comparisons)
**Symptom:** (Round 10 F10-FS-2.) Save As to `t2.pdf.` (or `t3.pdf `) through a dialog or CLI that does not strip it. Windows creates `t2.pdf`; `find_session_by_path` returned None for both spellings and opening `t2.pdf` from Explorer / recent files made a second tab on the same file. (The "both tabs write" part was not reproduced: the already-open guard still fired from the stale tab because the file existed by then.)
**Cause:** `save_as` computed `canonical_new` BEFORE the file existed, from the typed spelling (`...t2.pdf.`); `Path.resolve()` only normalises names of files that exist. After the write every lookup resolved to `...t2.pdf`, so the stored key was dead.
**Fix:** `_canonicalize_path` strips trailing dots/spaces from the last component on Windows (the key of a not-yet-existing path is already the key the file gets; covers the pre-write Save As guards, the optimizer's new-path check and the controller's output comparison), and `save_as` re-derives the session key after the write (also covers 8.3 forms). `display_name` is the stored name. Inner dots/spaces and dot segments are untouched. Rule: a path key for a file you are about to create must be computed from what the OS will store, and re-derived after the write.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`; `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py` (`test_save_as_to_a_name_with_a_trailing_dot_or_space_keeps_the_session_findable`, `test_canonical_path_of_a_not_yet_existing_name_matches_the_name_windows_will_create`, `test_save_as_onto_another_tabs_file_through_a_trailing_dot_spelling_is_still_refused`)

## Save As that only changes the case of the name (a.pdf -> A.pdf) reported success and renamed the tab, but the file kept the old case (F10-FS-3)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`save_as`, `_save_as_unchecked`, `_install_stage_over_open_file`, `_atomic_full_save`, signed-append install), `utils/path_staging.py` (`write_via_staging`, `resolve_as_requested`)
**Symptom:** (Round 10 F10-FS-3, case-insensitive Windows only.) Open `a.pdf`, edit, Save As `A.pdf`: no error, the directory still lists `a.pdf` (with the edit), while `saved_path`, `display_name` and the tab say `A.pdf` and the next Ctrl+S box shows "...\A.pdf". The data was saved; the name was not changed.
**Cause:** every install target was `Path(x).resolve()`, which returns the ON-DISK spelling of an existing file; `os.replace(stage, <a.pdf>)` keeps that name. `Path` equality is also case-insensitive on Windows, so the request was classified as an ordinary save over the open file (and the incremental append could not rename either).
**Fix:** `utils/path_staging.resolve_as_requested` restores the typed final name when it differs from the resolved one only by `os.path.normcase` (not for symlinks; 8.3 forms and stripped trailing dots keep the resolved name) and is used by every install target (`write_via_staging`, `_atomic_full_save`, `_install_stage_over_open_file`, signed-append install). `_save_as_unchecked` does not take the incremental path for a case-only rename. `os.replace` onto the typed spelling gives the file that spelling (verified on NTFS); a rename of the file while MuPDF holds it fails with WinError 32, so the install (which closes the handle first) is the only place to do it. "Same file" decisions still use plain `resolve()`. Rule: an install target must carry the spelling the user chose, a comparison key must not.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `utils/path_staging.py`; `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py` (`test_save_as_that_only_changes_the_case_renames_the_file_on_disk[incremental|full|secure]`, `test_save_as_onto_an_existing_file_keeps_the_typed_case`, `test_resolve_as_requested_only_restores_a_case_difference`)

## Plain Ctrl+S renamed the file back after another program changed its case (F11-FS-3)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`save_as`, `_without_stale_stored_spelling`), `utils/path_staging.py` (`resolve_as_requested`, `on_disk_spelling`)
**Symptom:** (Round 11 F11-FS-3, case-insensitive Windows, memory-backed session: compacted open, repaired file, or after a snapshot undo; a file-backed handle blocks the rename.) Explorer renames `report.pdf` -> `Report.pdf`, the user edits and presses Ctrl+S: the directory lists `report.pdf` again. Before F10-FS-3 the file kept `Report.pdf`.
**Cause:** the F10-FS-3 rule "an install target keeps the spelling it was called with" assumed every `save_as(path)` carries a typed name. Ctrl+S (`PDFController.save`, `save_session_as` for close-with-save) replays `saved_path or original_path`, whose spelling is stale after an external rename, and `resolve_as_requested` restored it. The model cannot see who called, only the string.
**Fix:** `save_as` first passes the path through `_without_stale_stored_spelling`: a name that is exactly (case-sensitively) the session's stored `saved_path`/`original_path` name, for the file the session already is (`session.canonical_path == canonical_new`), is a replay, so `utils/path_staging.on_disk_spelling` swaps in the on-disk case (case-only differences only) and the install keeps it; `saved_path`/`original_path`/`display_name` heal to the on-disk spelling. Any other spelling of the same file (`REPORT.pdf`), and the stored name typed for a different file, stay typed requests and still win (F10-FS-3). All four install targets are covered because they all sit behind `save_as`. Accepted residual: typing exactly the stale stored name in Save As is indistinguishable from Ctrl+S and keeps the on-disk case. Rule: classify a path as typed or replayed at the one entry point, before the install helpers; the helpers must not guess.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `utils/path_staging.py`; `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py` (`test_ctrl_s_keeps_the_spelling_another_program_gave_the_file`, `test_a_typed_case_change_still_wins_after_an_external_rename`, `test_the_stored_name_typed_for_another_file_keeps_its_case`, `test_on_disk_spelling_only_adopts_a_case_only_difference`)

## A plain edit -> undo -> save session leaves free xref slots that are never reclaimed; the file grows across sessions (LS-3)
**Area:** `model/xref_compaction.py`, `model/pdf_model.py` (`open_pdf`, `_compact_doc_xref_in_memory`, `_note_persisted_baseline`)
**Symptom:** (Round 8 LS-3.) 15 grip-move -> undo -> Ctrl+S cycles on a 1,252-byte copy grew the file by 260 bytes per cycle (`xref_length` 11 -> 206, 197 `null` entries), page text unchanged, one `%%EOF`, zero unreachable objects. No later session reclaimed the slots either, so the table grows without bound.
**Cause:** The numbering rule: every non-secure full save serializes with `garbage=1`, which frees unreachable objects but keeps every slot (20 bytes each) so the live document's numbering, `xref_epoch` and the retained page snapshots survive the save. PyMuPDF never reuses a free slot, and a `garbage>=2` save would renumber the LIVE document and strand the undo history, so no save may compact.
**Fix (owner decision, option B: compact at open):** the one history-free moment is the open. `open_pdf` runs `_compact_doc_xref_in_memory` just before the xref repair step (since OD-FS1-READALL the free-slot count normally comes from the open-time read of every object, see that entry; the census loads objects, so a lazily damaged file can get repaired by MuPDF during the walk: the walk fails, `is_repaired` turns True and the existing repair round trip takes over; a compacted document is already clean and skips it): encrypted files are skipped first (`_doc_is_encrypted`, metadata string; `tobytes` would emit a decrypted document), then `xref_compaction.open_compaction_verdict`: skip above `MAX_FILE_BYTES` (64 MB), skip a table above `MAX_CENSUS_SLOTS` (200,000) or one that declares more slots than the file has bytes (`signed_append_save.xref_slots_are_unbacked`, H10-2 class), then a bounded `xref_object(x) == "null"` census that stops as soon as the thresholds are unreachable (a healthy table is walked for at most half its length; a table under 512 slots is not walked at all) or met; compaction needs free slots >= `MIN_FREE_SLOTS` (512) AND free / (`xref_length` - 1) >= `MIN_FREE_RATIO` (0.5). Only then is the AcroForm walk paid: `document_has_a_signed_signature` (fail-closed) keeps signed files uncompacted. `compact_in_memory` is a `garbage=2` round trip through `doc_bytes.serialize_doc(in_memory=True)` (the bytes `tobytes(garbage=2)` gives; the lowest renumbering level: no object merge, no `deflate`, content streams byte-identical) and the session gets the memory-backed result, the shape the xref repair and a snapshot undo already leave: `doc.name == "pdf"`, `persisted_xref_length` None, incremental saves off for that session, every save the staged `garbage=1` full rewrite (`_full_save_to_path` else branch via `_save_doc_to_user_path`), which is how the compact layout reaches the file; `_detach_live_doc_from_source_file`, the install/recovery paths and the signed-append path are never entered. The file on disk is byte-identical until that save and the session is NOT dirty (`session_has_unsaved_changes` reads only command / tool / transfer state), so a file opened and never saved keeps its slots; growth within a session is accepted (the next open resets it). The `DocumentSession` is created after the compaction with a fresh `xref_epoch`; never run this from `import_session_transfer` or any reopen-after-save (history exists there). Gotcha: `tobytes(garbage>=2)` renumbers the SOURCE handle in place, through either sink (measured with `tobytes`: `xref_length` 5207 -> 7 on the original handle, `can_save_incrementally()` still 1; the in-memory sink renumbers the same way, probed 2026-10-21), so a failure after it must replace a file-backed handle with a fresh `fitz.open(path)`; keeping the renumbered one would let the next incremental save write numbers the file does not have. Numbers (measured 2026-10-10, PyMuPDF 1.27.1): `tobytes(garbage=2)` 163 ms on a 47 MB / 402-page file (~3.5 ms/MB, same as the `garbage=1` repair round trip; `garbage=3` 319 ms, `garbage=4` 270 ms and rewrites streams); census ~1.2 us per free slot and ~4.4 us per in-use slot on a fresh handle, the same on the `use_objstms=1` form of that file (200,000 slots ~1 s worst case); corpus census of the 2,936 PDFs under `test_files`: 222 carry any free slot, the highest ratio of a sound file is 0.368 (20-slot test-suite files; `unreadablemetadata.pdf` 96 of 267), only the broken `corrupted.pdf` (279 of 284) exceeds the ratio and no file has more than 279 free slots, so no sound corpus file trips the gate while the repro trips it after ~40 cycles (~10 KB of waste). Second gotcha: a lazily damaged file (one in-use xref offset off by a few bytes, undetected at open) gets repaired by MuPDF in the middle of the census (`xref_object` raises `bad xref`, `is_repaired` turns True), which is why the compaction runs BEFORE the repair step; and the walk's warning must log `str(exc)`, never the exception object or `exc_info` -- the traceback holds the failing `xref_object` frame whose arguments include the SWIG document, so a handler that keeps records (pytest's caplog) kept the file open past `doc.close()` and the next `os.replace` failed with WinError 5 (pinned by `test_a_damaged_file_with_many_free_slots_opens_clean_and_saves_a_readable_file[last]`). Found on the way: `persisted_xref_length` was recorded for the repaired memory document because `doc.name == "pdf"` counted as a file name (see the `doc.name` entry near the top); the open and `_note_persisted_baseline` now key on `_backing_file`.
**File:** `model/xref_compaction.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`; `test_scripts/test_open_compacts_free_xref_slots.py`

## Detaching an encrypted tab decrypted the session; Ctrl+S in the new window wrote the file back without its password (F11-OPEN-1)
**Area:** `controller/session_transfer.py` (`SessionTransferPayload.from_model`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`capture_session_transfer_bytes`, `import_session_transfer`)
**Symptom:** (Round 11 F11-OPEN-1.) Open an AES-256 file with its user password, drag the tab out into its own window, edit, Ctrl+S: the original path now holds an unencrypted PDF anyone can read, no warning. An owner-password-only file loses its permission restrictions the same way. The same edit + Ctrl+S without detaching keeps the encryption.
**Cause:** the payload's `snapshot_bytes` came from `capture_worker_snapshot_bytes` -> `_decrypted_snapshot_bytes` (`encryption=NONE`), bytes meant only for throwaway worker/print readers. `import_session_transfer` installed that plain stream as the new window's LIVE document, so `_doc_is_encrypted` was False for the rest of the session and every later `encryption=KEEP` save had nothing to keep. The payload's `password`/`auth_level` were stored but unused.
**Fix:** decrypted reader bytes must never become a live session document. The transfer captures `capture_session_transfer_bytes` (`_encryption_keeping_bytes`: `garbage=0`, `encryption=KEEP`, the same serialization `_open_numbering_clone` uses on the live handle), and `import_session_transfer` reads `needs_pass` once on the fresh handle and authenticates with `payload.password` (auth class from the result); a locked snapshot without a working password is refused (handle closed, no session), so the detach fails and the tab stays in the source window. Only the transfer installed reader bytes as a live doc; every other live-doc replacement (`_roundtrip_live_doc`, `_restore_doc_from_snapshot`, save reopen, recovery) already serializes with KEEP and re-authenticates, and the optimizer re-applies encryption through its own descriptor.
**File:** `controller/session_transfer.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`; `test_scripts/test_tab_detach.py` (`test_transfer_payload_of_encrypted_session_stays_encrypted`, `test_detached_user_password_session_saves_back_encrypted`, `test_detached_owner_only_session_keeps_permission_restrictions`, `test_import_transfer_refuses_encrypted_snapshot_without_password`)

## Detaching a tab re-measured the on-disk fingerprint: a foreign rewrite the original window refuses to overwrite was overwritten from the new window (F11-OPEN-2)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`import_session_transfer`, `DocumentSession.disk_fingerprint` / `disk_fingerprint_path`), `controller/session_transfer.py` (`SessionTransferPayload`)
**Symptom:** (Round 11 F11-OPEN-2.) Open a.pdf, edit, Save As b.pdf, then another program rewrites b.pdf in place. Ctrl+S in the same window is refused (`SourceChangedOnDiskError`, F10-FS-1). Drag the tab out and press Ctrl+S in the new window: no refusal, b.pdf holds the session's pages and the other program's content is gone.
**Cause:** `import_session_transfer` called `_record_disk_fingerprint(session, source_path)`, i.e. it measured the file at import time. The sender's baseline was not in the payload, so anything a foreign writer did between the sender's open / last save and the detach became the new window's baseline and the gate compared the file with itself.
**Fix:** `SessionTransferPayload` carries `disk_fingerprint` and `disk_fingerprint_path` (filled by `from_model` from the session) and `import_session_transfer` installs them unchanged; the import never reads the file for a baseline. A payload without a baseline (hand-built, or the sender had none) yields a session with none, which never refuses. Rule: a baseline is only ever taken at open or after the session's own write, never at a handoff.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `controller/session_transfer.py`; `test_scripts/test_tab_detach.py` (`test_detached_save_refuses_a_foreign_rewrite_made_before_the_detach`, `test_import_keeps_the_senders_baseline_when_the_file_changes_after_capture`, `test_payload_carries_the_senders_disk_baseline`, `test_an_untouched_detached_session_still_saves_and_rebaselines`, `test_a_payload_without_a_baseline_imports_without_measuring_the_file`)

## The password-retry check matched keywords in the error text, which contains the file path: a corrupt file under "Unencrypted Exports" looped on password prompts and hid the real error (F11-OPEN-3)
**Area:** `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`open_pdf`, `_open_source_with_password_prompt`, `_resolve_merge_file`, `resolve_insert_source_file`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`open_pdf`, `_guard_foreign_doc`)
**Symptom:** (Round 11 F11-OPEN-3.) Open a corrupt, missing or 0-page PDF whose path contains "encrypted" (`...\Unencrypted Exports\report.pdf`, `*_unencrypted.pdf`): the password dialog appears again and again, and cancelling ends the loop with no error at all. A wrong password for a genuinely encrypted file under such a path skips the "密碼錯誤" notice. Merge and insert-from-file sources behaved the same.
**Cause:** The controller decided "password needed" with `"需要密碼" in err_msg or "encrypted" in err_msg.lower()`. Model messages end with the user's path (MuPDF's `Failed to open file '<path>'`, `原始檔案不存在: <path>`, the H10-3 zero-page refusal), so the path itself matched. The H10-3 wording had been chosen to dodge the keywords, but the path tail defeated it. The wrong-password branch was checked after the keyword branch, so it lost too.
**Fix:** Typed errors: `PdfPasswordError(RuntimeError)` with `PdfPasswordRequiredError` and `PdfPasswordRejectedError`, raised where `needs_pass` / `authenticate()` are evaluated (`PDFModel.open_pdf`, `_guard_foreign_doc`); `open_pdf`'s catch-all re-wrap re-raises the same type with the same message. The controller's `open_pdf` loop and `_open_source_with_password_prompt` (merge and insert-from-file sources) catch the base `PdfPasswordError` and branch on its subtype. Rule: never classify a model error by a substring of its message; any message that embeds a path or user text can match anything. Fakes in tests must raise the typed errors.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`; `test_scripts/test_pdf_merge_workflow.py` (`test_open_pdf_unreadable_file_under_encrypted_named_path_shows_error_not_password_prompt`, `test_open_pdf_wrong_password_under_encrypted_named_path_still_reports_wrong_password`, merge and insert variants), `test_scripts/test_security_pdf_resource_guards.py` (`test_password_failures_are_typed_and_survive_the_open_wrapper`, `test_non_password_failures_are_never_password_errors_even_with_keyword_paths`)

## A failed or cancelled open still finalized the inline editor and cancelled OCR on the tab the user stayed on (F11-OPEN-4)
**Area:** `PDFController.open_pdf`, `PDFModel.open_pdf`, inline editor / OCR lifecycle
**Symptom:** File > Open, drag-and-drop or a forwarded CLI open of an encrypted file whose password prompt is cancelled, a corrupt or zero-page file, a missing file or one over the size or page limit left the user on the same tab, but an unverified inline edit had been discarded with a "not applied" warning and a running OCR job had been aborted without any message.
**Cause:** `open_pdf` ran `_finalize_inline_editor_before_session_change()`, `cancel_ocr()` and `_cancel_search()` before calling `model.open_pdf`, i.e. before knowing whether the session would change. The finalize must precede the session switch (it commits against the still-active document), which is why it was placed first, but the validation (existence, size, password, page count) lives inside `model.open_pdf`.
**Fix:** `PDFModel.open_pdf(..., before_activate=callable)` calls the hook once, after every check has passed and before the session is appended or an existing one activated (old session still active; a hook that raises closes the new document and aborts the open). The controller passes its teardown as that hook. Rule: tear down state that belongs to the current session only at the point the session really changes; an operation that can still fail or be cancelled must not do it up front. Other session-change sites (`_switch_to_session_id`, tab close after its confirm prompt) already change the session unconditionally. `detach_document_session` finalizes before the handoff because the payload snapshot must include the commit; a failed handoff after that keeps the tab but not an unverified edit (accepted).
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`; `test_scripts/test_multi_tab_plan.py` (`test_open_cancelled_password_keeps_inline_editor_and_ocr`, `test_open_rejected_password_then_cancel_keeps_inline_editor_and_ocr`, `test_open_failure_keeps_inline_editor_and_ocr`, `test_open_over_page_limit_keeps_inline_editor_and_ocr`, `test_successful_open_tears_down_against_the_still_active_old_session`, `test_model_open_pdf_before_activate_hook_runs_only_on_a_real_open`)

## A failed `open_pdf(append=False)` closed every open session before the new file was parsed (F11-OPEN-5)
**Area:** `PDFModel.open_pdf` (replace-open), scripts and tests that call the model directly
**Symptom:** `model.open_pdf(bad, append=False)` with a corrupt file, a missing or wrong password, an over-page-limit file, a zero-page file or a raising `before_activate` hook raised as expected but left the model with zero sessions, discarding every open (possibly dirty) document. The same failures also left the freshly parsed `fitz.Document` unclosed (password-required, password-rejected, hook failure).
**Cause:** the `if not append: self.close_all_sessions()` ran right after the size guard, before `fitz.open`, authentication, the page-limit check and the 0-page refusal. The controller always passes `append=True`, so only direct model callers hit it.
**Fix:** the replace-open close now runs as the last step before the session is created, after validation and the `before_activate` hook; every failure between `fitz.open` and that point closes the parsed handle and re-raises with the existing sessions untouched. Rule: any "replace the current state" operation does its destructive step only after the replacement is fully validated (same shape as F11-OPEN-4).
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`; `test_scripts/test_security_pdf_resource_guards.py` (`test_failed_replace_open_keeps_existing_sessions`, `test_failed_replace_open_over_page_limit_keeps_existing_sessions`, `test_replace_open_runs_before_activate_while_old_sessions_are_alive`, `test_replace_open_before_activate_failure_keeps_sessions_and_closes_new_doc`, `test_failed_open_on_encrypted_file_closes_the_parsed_handle`)

## Text rebuild / push-down / textbox move duplicated every overlapping annotation that is not a FreeText (F11-ANN-1)
**Area:** `AnnotationTool._save_overlapping_annots` / `_restore_annots` around `apply_redactions` (legacy rebuild `_apply_redact_insert_body`, `_push_down_overlapping_text`, `_redact_and_restore_textbox_region`)
**Symptom:** a consented rebuild, a same-page text move or a textbox move over an annotated line left two copies of each Square / Circle / Highlight / Underline / StrikeOut on it; the Highlight / Underline copies had the rect (-2147483648 .. 2147483520) and no `/QuadPoints` (only a swallowed `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'set_colors'` warning). Push-down left the original annotation on the old line and added a copy on the pushed line. The duplicates survived redo, Save As and reopen. A re-created StrikeOut came back as a Squiggly.
**Cause:** the restore assumed `apply_redactions` deleted every intersecting annotation and re-added all of them. On PyMuPDF 1.27.1 it deletes only FreeText (and links, which `page.annots()` never returns); Text, Square, Circle, text markup, Line, Ink, Polygon, Stamp, Caret and FileAttachment survive. Text markup was re-added with `quads=annot.vertices` (a flat point list): `Page._add_text_marker` inserts the annotation, THEN raises TypeError in `JM_quad_from_py`, so a half-built marker stayed on the page. `_ANNOT_STRIKEOUT` was a hand-typed 10, which is `PDF_ANNOT_SQUIGGLY`.
**Fix:** `_save_overlapping_annots` records each annotation's `xref`. `_restore_annots` reads the page's `(xref, type)` set after the redaction: a survivor is never re-added; when the entry carries `offset=(dx, dy)` (push-down passes `(0, delta_y)` instead of a pre-shifted rect) it is moved in place by `_translate_annot`, which shifts /Rect, /QuadPoints, /Vertices, /L, /CL and /InkList and does not call `update()` (the appearance stream is mapped onto /Rect, so a foreign AP is kept). Only removed annotations are re-created, once per xref, at `rect + offset`; text markup is rebuilt from `fitz.Quad`s (4 vertices each), info (content/title/subject/dates) is copied, and a re-create that raises deletes whatever it inserted. Type codes are PyMuPDF's named constants. Rule: never assume what `apply_redactions` removed; ask the page afterwards. Links (which `page.annots()` never lists) are covered by F11-ANN-3. Not covered here: the FreeText re-create is lossy (F11-ANN-5).
**File:** `model/tools/annotation_tool.py`, `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_push_down_overlapping_text`); tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_consented_rebuild_keeps_each_overlapping_annotation_once`, `test_push_down_moves_neighbour_annotations_instead_of_copying_them`, `test_restore_recreates_a_deleted_text_marker_from_its_quads`), `test_scripts/test_object_manipulation_model.py` (`test_move_textbox_keeps_overlapping_annotations_once`)
## A Page still loaded across a page-snapshot undo kept MuPDF's old annotation / link lists: "xref N is not an annot of this page" until reopen (F11-ANN-2)
**Area:** `model/page_snapshot.restore_page_graph` (every page-level undo / redo / rollback: `EditTextCommand`, `AddTextboxCommand`, object ops, cross-page move), `utils/pymupdf_refs.sync_open_pages`
**Symptom:** after a consented rebuild of a line carrying a Highlight and a FreeText, then Ctrl+Z, the page's `/Annots` was back to `[9 0 R 11 0 R]` and `annot_xrefs()` listed xref 11, but `page.load_annot(11)` raised `xref 11 is not an annot of this page`. Every later text edit on the page raised out of `EditTextCommand.execute` (`page_fingerprint` -> `_annotation_entries` -> `load_annot`), the annotation panel (`get_all_annotations`) and `toggle_annotations_visibility` raised the same way, until the file was reopened. Render and save were correct. A restored link was also missing from `get_links()`.
**Cause:** MuPDF keeps one loaded page per page number, and that page holds annotation, widget and link lists built when it was loaded. While any `fitz.Page` of the page is alive, every later `doc[n]` wraps that same MuPDF page. `restore_page_graph` writes the page dictionary and its annotations back by xref (`update_object`), which bypasses MuPDF's annotation API, so a page that stayed loaded across the restore kept the pre-restore lists. Here the Page was kept alive by the failing `add_highlight_annot(quads=...)` path of F11-ANN-1. The same happens for anything that keeps a Page alive: Page<->Annot cycle garbage (MBT-1), a traceback a log handler keeps, or a caller's variable. With no Page alive, the next `doc[n]` loads fresh and the bug does not show. That is why only the Highlight + FreeText combination reproduced it.
**Fix:** `restore_page_graph` calls `utils.pymupdf_refs.sync_open_pages(doc)` in a `finally` after any write, on both the success and the put-back path. That function is MuPDF's own post-undo resync, `pdf_sync_open_pages` (reached with `pdf_document_from_fz_document(doc.this)`), which rebuilds the lists of every loaded page from the current objects. It is best effort and logs `str(exc)` without raising, because the write has already happened. It skips a non-PDF document, whose PDF view is a null wrapper that MuPDF would dereference. After the sync, a held `fitz.Annot` whose annotation is no longer listed reads as xref 0 / type -1 instead of pointing at a dead xref. Rule: any write that replaces a page's dictionary, its `/Annots` array or link annotations by xref must resync the loaded pages. Do not rely on "nobody holds a Page". Class audit: `restore_page_graph` is the only writer of page dictionaries and `/Annots`. The other in-place writers change content streams or `/Contents` (`restore_stream_storage`, `ToolManager` rollback, `pdf_object_ops` XObject removal, font compaction), which MuPDF re-reads. Two writers touch annotation dictionaries but not the lists: `restore_annotation_parent_refs` (same values, key order only) and `_translate_annot` (geometry read through the indirect reference; on a Link it is followed by `_reattach_link`, which appends to `/Annots`, and `_restore_annots` resyncs the loaded pages after both, F11-ANN-3). Whole-document restores open a new handle. After F11-ANN-1 the original trigger no longer leaks a Page, so the tests keep a Page alive on purpose.
**File:** `model/page_snapshot.py`, `utils/pymupdf_refs.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_page_snapshot_identity.py` (`test_restore_refreshes_the_annotation_and_link_lists_of_a_page_still_loaded`), `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_undo_of_a_rebuild_keeps_the_annotation_list_of_a_page_still_loaded`)
## Text rebuild / push-down / textbox move silently deleted the links over the redacted rect (F11-ANN-3)
**Area:** `AnnotationTool._save_overlapping_annots` / `_restore_annots` around `apply_redactions` (legacy rebuild `_apply_redact_insert_body`, `_push_down_overlapping_text`, `_redact_and_restore_textbox_region`)
**Symptom:** a URI or GoTo link on a line was gone after a consented rebuild of that line, a same-page drag of it, a textbox move over it, or a push-down of the unedited line below a wrapped edit (link count 1 -> 0). Undo brought the link back, redo removed it again, and Save As persisted the loss. Nothing was logged and nothing told the user.
**Cause:** `_save_overlapping_annots` iterated `page.annots()`, which never returns Link (or Widget) annotations, so no link was ever saved. `apply_redactions` removes every link intersecting the redaction from the page's `/Annots` array. The link object itself stays in the xref table until a garbage-collecting save, but nothing referenced it any more.
**Fix:** `_save_overlapping_annots` also appends Link entries (`_save_overlapping_links`): every `PDF_ANNOT_LINK` in `annot_xrefs()` whose `/Rect` mapped by `page.transformation_matrix` intersects the redact rect. That is the unrotated space of `annot.rect` and of the redact rects; `get_links()["from"]` is in rotated space and must not be used. `_restore_annots` does not re-create a removed link, because that would lose `/BS`, `/H`, `/QuadPoints`, structure keys and the xref. It moves the original object by the entry's `offset` with `_translate_annot` and then appends `N 0 R` back to `/Annots` (`_reattach_link`). An inline or indirect array is extended in place, so its direct entries are kept. MuPDF's redaction itself rewrites an indirect `/Annots` inline. A link that cannot be saved is logged, not silently dropped: a direct `/Annots` link dictionary has no object to put back, and a `/Rect` that is not 4 numbers is skipped. A link the redaction left listed is only moved. When any link entry was handled, it calls `utils.pymupdf_refs.sync_open_pages` in a `finally`, because MuPDF does not refresh a loaded page's link list after a write by xref (F11-ANN-2). Placement follows F11-ANN-1: links under a rebuilt or dragged line stay at their rect, and the push-down moves them with the pushed text. A re-attached link is appended last, so its `/Annots` (tab) order relative to the other annotations can change. Rule: `page.annots()` is not the page's annotation list. Any save/restore around a redaction must cover links, and widgets if MuPDF ever removes them (PyMuPDF 1.27.1 keeps widgets and popups).
**File:** `model/tools/annotation_tool.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_consented_rebuild_keeps_the_links_on_the_rebuilt_line`, `test_same_page_move_keeps_the_links_where_they_were`, `test_push_down_moves_the_links_of_a_pushed_line_with_their_text`, `test_restore_reattaches_links_a_redaction_removed`, `test_restore_reattaches_a_link_to_an_indirect_annots_array`), `test_scripts/test_object_manipulation_model.py` (`test_move_textbox_keeps_links_over_its_old_rect`)

## A FreeText under a rebuilt / pushed / moved line came back with a different appearance: text colour = old background, 10.5 pt, yellow fill, /Rotate = page rotation, no author or dates (F11-ANN-5)
**Area:** `AnnotationTool._save_overlapping_annots` / `_restore_annots` around `apply_redactions` (legacy rebuild `_apply_redact_insert_body`, `_push_down_overlapping_text`, `_redact_and_restore_textbox_region`)
**Symptom:** after a consented rebuild of the line under a 9 pt red-on-light-blue FreeText its `/DA` was `0.8 0.9 1 rg /Helv 10.5 Tf` (light-blue text, 10.5 pt) and `/C` was `[1 1 .8]` (yellow); on a 90-degree page it gained `/Rotate 90`, so its text turned; `/T`, the dates, `/RC` and `/IT` were dropped and the annotation got a new xref. Undo restored it, redo and Save As kept the changed look. Nothing was logged.
**Cause:** `apply_redactions` removes a FreeText from `/Annots` (as it does a link, F11-ANN-3) but leaves the object and its appearance stream in the xref table. The restore re-created it with `add_freetext_annot(fontname="helv", fontsize=10.5, text_color=colors["stroke"], fill_color=colors["fill"] or (1, 1, 0.8), rotate=page.rotation)`. For a FreeText `annot.colors["stroke"]` is `/C`, the background, not the text colour (that lives only in `/DA`), and `colors["fill"]` is `/IC`. The size, fill and rotate were placeholders.
**Fix:** a removed annotation whose object survives is put back as the same object (`_reattach_entry`: `_translate_annot` by the entry's `offset`, then `_reattach_annot` appends `N 0 R` to `/Annots`, and the loaded pages are resynced as in F11-ANN-2). This is generic over the subtype, so a FreeText keeps `/DA`, `/C`, `/Rotate`, author, dates, `/RC`, `/IT`, its appearance and its xref, and a push-down moves `/Rect` and `/CL` with its text. Only an entry whose object cannot be reattached (no xref, object gone, subtype changed) is re-created; `_save_overlapping_annots` now stores `freetext_style` (`/DA` size, font resource, text colour and `/Rotate`, `_freetext_style`) and the fallback uses it, with `/C` as the fill and the info (title, dates) copied. Rule: never regenerate an object a redaction only unlisted; relist it. A regenerated annotation is always a lossy copy.
**File:** `model/tools/annotation_tool.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_consented_rebuild_keeps_a_freetext_exactly_as_it_was`, `test_restore_reattaches_a_freetext_the_redaction_removed_and_moves_it`, `test_recreated_freetext_keeps_its_style_when_the_object_cannot_be_reattached`, `test_restore_recreates_a_deleted_text_marker_from_its_quads`)

## Annotation appearance text was indexed as editable page text and burned into the content (F11-ANN-4)
**Area:** page text extraction for the edit pipeline: `TextBlockManager._build_page_index`, `_extract_plain_text_lines`, `_dynamic_scan`, `pdf_text_edit._push_down_overlapping_text` / `_glyph_keys_in_rect` / `_validate_protected_spans`, the index-aligned reads in `pdf_model` (`_get_chars_in_run_unrotated`, selection lines, the block fallback)
**Symptom:** a FreeText's body ("FT comment") was a clickable, editable text block. A consented rebuild (or same-page move / push-down) of the line next to it replayed that text into the content stream as a "protected span" while `_restore_annots` also re-created the annotation, so it showed twice and survived the annotation's deletion; a consented rebuild of the FreeText "block" itself painted the new text into the content, left the annotation unchanged and shredded the line under its redact rect. A form-field value was indexed the same way, and an annotation glyph that survived a redaction (widgets and popups are not removed by `apply_redactions`) counted as an unerased source glyph and rolled the rebuild back.
**Cause:** `page.get_text(...)` runs the whole page, annotations and widgets included (`fz_run_page`), and every extraction in the edit pipeline used it. The block index, protected spans, push-down candidates and the glyph-survivor probe therefore treated annotation appearance streams as page content. The tiered engine only masked it (its stream matcher rejects the annotation block); the legacy rebuild and the push-down re-insert anything the dict names.
**Fix:** `model/page_content_text.py`: `content_text(page, option, flags=, clip=, textpage=)` builds the text page like `Page.get_textpage` (unrotated) but runs the page with `fz_run_page_contents` (no annotations, no widgets), and is identical to `get_text` on an annotation-free page (rotation, CropBox, clip and a real 50-page document pinned). Do NOT build it from `get_displaylist(annots=False)`: replaying a display list regroups text objects and changes line/space segmentation (three pages of `hvac-dwg.pdf` extracted differently and broke `test_paragraph_table_cells`). The index, `_extract_plain_text_lines`, `_dynamic_scan`, the index-aligned `dict`/`rawdict` reads (their `block_idx` must come from the same extraction as the index), `_validate_protected_spans`, `_glyph_keys_in_rect` and the push-down use it. Rule: any extraction whose result decides what to edit, preserve, replay or move is content-only; an extraction that describes what the user SEES (`text_commit.verify`, search and its hit context, the inserted-text presence check) stays `page.get_text`. Selection copy is content-only: the rectangle reader (`get_text_selection_snapshot`) reads the index and `content_text` and falls back to `page.get_text("text", clip=)` only on a page without runs; the drag reader (`get_text_selection_snapshot_from_run`) reads the index alone. A grep test (`test_edit_pipeline_extracts_structure_only_through_the_content_helper`) fails on a stray `get_text` in the edit modules.
**File:** `model/page_content_text.py`, `model/text_block.py`, `model/text_block_parsing.py`, `model/pdf_text_edit.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_page_content_text.py`, `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_annotation_appearance_text_is_not_indexed_as_page_text`, `test_consented_rebuild_does_not_burn_annotation_text_into_the_content`, `test_push_down_leaves_annotation_text_out_of_the_content`)

## The annotation show/hide toolbar toggle raised AttributeError: `fitz.ANNOT_FLAG_HIDDEN` does not exist (F11-ANN-6)
**Area:** `AnnotationTool.toggle_annotations_visibility` (toolbar "顯示/隱藏註解" -> `PDFController.toggle_annotations_visibility`)
**Symptom:** on any document with a Text or FreeText annotation the toggle raised `AttributeError: module 'fitz' has no attribute 'ANNOT_FLAG_HIDDEN'` before any flag was set, so annotations could never be hidden or re-shown.
**Cause:** the code used a constant name PyMuPDF 1.27 does not define; the only hidden-flag constant is `fitz.PDF_ANNOT_IS_HIDDEN` (2). A missing `fitz.<name>` fails only when its line runs, and no test drove this toggle.
**Fix:** use `fitz.PDF_ANNOT_IS_HIDDEN` (as `pdf_object_ops` already did). `test_every_fitz_attribute_used_in_source_exists` parses model/controller/view/utils and fails on any `fitz.<name>` this PyMuPDF lacks. Rule: constants come from the installed PyMuPDF (`dir(fitz)`), not from memory of other versions; a feature with no test that runs its line can ship broken.
**File:** `model/tools/annotation_tool.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_markup_annotations.py` (`test_toggle_annotations_visibility_sets_and_clears_hidden_flag`, `test_every_fitz_attribute_used_in_source_exists`)

## A hand-off that arrived while a modal dialog was open switched the active tab under it; Save As / merge / optimize then acted on the new tab (F11-1)
**Area:** `PDFController.handle_forwarded_cli` (single-instance / file-association hand-off), `_on_optimize_copy_succeeded`, every dialog-then-act flow that reads the active session after `exec()` returns
**Symptom:** with Save As open for A, double-clicking B.pdf in Explorer opened B behind the dialog; the path the user picked for A received B's bytes, B's tab was renamed to it and A stayed unsaved (an overwrite-confirmed existing file was replaced by the wrong document). The same with the merge dialog (C appended to B, B dirty, A unchanged) and the optimize dialog (`A.optimized.pdf` held B).
**Cause:** the hand-off ran `open_pdf` from `QTimer.singleShot(0)`. A modal's nested `exec()` loop (QDialog, QMessageBox, QMenu, the native file dialog) dispatches timers and queued signals, so the open ran inside the dialog and activated B. The dialog's caller resumes afterwards and reads `model.doc` / `get_active_session_id()` only then. The optimize worker's success handler (`open_pdf(output)`) is the same shape: a queued signal that can land inside any modal once the progress dialog is dismissed.
**Fix:** tab activations started from outside the user's flow go through `_run_when_session_activation_allowed(callback)`: FIFO queue, drained on a later turn only while `_session_activation_blocked()` is false (no popup, no visible modal top-level -- every one, not just the topmost -- other than the background jobs' own `show()`-n optimize / print / OCR progress dialogs, which no caller waits on), re-checked every `DEFERRED_SESSION_ACTIVATION_RETRY_MS`; a reentrancy flag keeps a callback's own password prompt from nesting the next hand-off. Defence in depth where the controller owns the dialog: `start_merge_pdfs` refuses merge-into-current when the active tab differs from the one it opened for, and `_start_optimize_submission(session_id=...)` binds to the dialog's tab. Rule: anything that opens or activates a tab from a timer, a socket or a worker signal must go through the gate; a dialog-then-act flow should capture its session id before `exec()`. Not driven: the real native Windows dialog (Qt marks its hidden `QFileDialog` modal); the View-hosted dialogs (Save As, metadata, export) rely on the gate alone.
**File:** `controller/pdf_controller.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_m3_forwarded_cli_focus.py` (`TestForwardedCliWaitsForModal`), `test_scripts/test_pdf_merge_workflow.py` (`test_merge_into_current_refuses_when_the_active_tab_changed_under_the_dialog`), `test_scripts/test_pdf_optimize_workflow.py` (`test_optimize_copy_stays_bound_to_the_tab_the_dialog_was_opened_for`, `test_optimize_success_during_a_modal_waits_before_opening_the_copy`)

## A second launch while the running instance's GUI thread was busy for more than 2 s silently lost the requested open (F11-2)
**Area:** `utils/single_instance.py` (`send_to_running_instance`), `main.py` secondary-launch path (`return 0 if forwarded else 1`)
**Symptom:** saving a large document (the save joins the thumbnail worker for up to `SAVE_READER_JOIN_TIMEOUT_MS` = 5 s, then writes synchronously) or double-clicking several PDFs in Explorer while the first instance runs its synchronous startup `open_pdf` loop: every launch in that window exited with code 1 and no dialog, and the PDF never opened anywhere.
**Cause:** the sender used the 2 s liveness timeout for the whole hand-off. A live primary accepts the connection instantly but only services the socket from its event loop, and on Windows `waitForBytesWritten` does not complete until the primary reads. So the 2 s write wait (not only the ack wait) expired while the GUI thread was blocked, `finally: socket.abort()` dropped the connection, and an aborted hand-off is never delivered. Probe: 3 clients, 6 s busy primary -> all `forwarded=False` after 2.0 s, primary received `[]`.
**Fix:** split the budgets. `CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` (2 s, `timeout_ms`) only decides alive vs dead; `RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS` (60 s, `response_timeout_ms`) is one deadline shared by the payload write wait and the ack wait, with a `logger.warning` when it expires. A primary that never answers still makes the sender give up (bounded). Never treat "no answer yet" from a connected primary as "gone". Not changed: a failed forward still exits 1 without a dialog (a product choice, see TODOS).
**File:** `utils/single_instance.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_single_instance_forwarding.py` (`test_forward_to_busy_primary_is_not_lost` runs a real subprocess primary that blocks its thread, `test_forward_to_unresponsive_primary_is_bounded`, `test_default_response_budget_outlasts_a_busy_save`)

## On Windows another program could rewrite the open session's file under the live document: the unsaved edits vanished before any save (OD-FS1-LOCK, F10-FS-1 RAM half)
**Area:** `utils/file_share_lock.py` (`acquire`, `suspended`, `FileShareLock`, `path_key`), `utils/path_staging.replace_file`, `model/pdf_model.py` (`open_pdf`, `import_session_transfer`, `save_as`, `_save_as_unchecked` incremental branch, `close_session`, `_sync_session_file_locks`, `_release_session_file_locks`, `DocumentSession.file_locks`)
**Symptom:** (Round 10 F10-FS-1, the half left to the owner.) Open a.pdf, edit, then `copy /y other.pdf a.pdf`, an Explorer copy-overwrite or any `open('r+b')` writer: the write succeeded and the file-backed live document lazily read the foreign bytes - the view showed the other document and the edits were gone before any save. A memory-backed session (compacted open, repaired file, snapshot undo) and the file after a Save As were not held at all, so they could also be renamed or deleted under the session.
**Cause:** MuPDF opens the file with a share mode that allows writers (read + write sharing), and nothing else held the file.
**Fix (owner decision):** on Windows every session holds a second handle on the file it owns, `CreateFileW(GENERIC_READ, FILE_SHARE_READ)`: other processes can still read, but any open for write or delete access (in-place rewrite, `os.replace`/`MoveFileEx` over it, rename, delete) fails with a sharing violation. `open_pdf` takes it BEFORE `fitz.open` (the parsed and fingerprinted bytes are the protected bytes) and releases it in its `finally` unless the new session adopted it; `import_session_transfer` takes it for the source path; `close_session` (and so `close` / replace-open) releases it. One OS handle per file per process (`path_key` = realpath + normcase, `\\?\` stripped), reference counted, so a detached tab and its sender, or two windows on one file, share it. The app's own writes release it only for the write: the incremental append in `_save_as_unchecked` runs inside `file_share_lock.suspended(save_target)`, and `replace_file` suspends `dst` for every staged install in the process (full save, open-file install and its recovery rebind, signed append, secure rewrite, close-with-save via `save_session_as`, Save As onto the same file, optimizer copy, export); suspension is counted and re-opens the handle on whatever file then sits at the path. `save_as` always ends (success or failure) in `_sync_session_file_locks`, which locks `saved_path or original_path` (+ a non-temp backing file if the live handle still reads one), so a Save As moves the lock to the new file and frees the old one, and a degraded claim is retried. Must be `GENERIC_READ`: a handle without data access does not take part in sharing checks and blocks nobody. Never raises and never refuses an open: when the handle cannot be taken (a network share without support, a file another program already holds for writing, a missing source) the claim is degraded with one log line and behaviour is as before; no-op off Windows.
**Rules:** the F10-FS-1 fingerprint gate stays load-bearing (degraded claims, non-Windows, the short window of our own write). A new writer of a session's file must go through `replace_file` or wrap its write in `file_share_lock.suspended(path)`, or it fails with `PermissionError` (fail-safe, not silent). The registry mutex is never held while logging, and a token dropped by the garbage collector (whose finalizer runs in whatever thread triggered the collection) never waits for it: the drop is queued and applied by the next registry call, so it cannot deadlock against a thread that holds a logging / Qt lock. Tests that simulate a foreign writer, rename or delete of an open session's file must request the `share_lock_disabled` fixture (`test_scripts/conftest.py`), or wrap the step in `file_share_lock.suspended`. Same-thread rule (fixed 2026-10-21): the registry mutex is an `RLock`, so a drop that reaches the registry on the thread already inside a registry call (a garbage-collection `weakref.finalize` drop, or an explicit `release()` made by a finalizer or `__del__`, e.g. `PDFModel.__del__` -> `close()` -> `close_session` -> `FileShareLock.release()`) gets the mutex instead of deadlocking on it. It used to apply the drop right there, in the middle of that call: at the exit of `suspended()` and in `ensure()`, which re-open the handle with no holder of their own, a drop of the key's last holder inside the re-open removed the entry, and the handle opened next landed on the removed entry: a deny-write lock nobody could release while `is_locked()` said False. Now every drop is queued (`_finalize_holder` appends first) and only the outermost registry call on the thread (`_registry_call`, `_depth` 1) applies the queue, on entry and again before it lets go, so a drop made mid-operation lands once the operation is complete (the re-opened handle is closed and the entry dropped; `ensure()` reads `held` after that, False for a token released inside it). Every registry operation runs inside `_registry_call` (`_finalize_holder` takes `_mutex` itself first, without blocking for a garbage-collection drop, and enters `_registry_call` only when it is not nested): take `_mutex` nowhere else, and do not swap the `RLock` for a plain `Lock`, which deadlocks an explicit `release()` on the owning thread (the w1b pass-2 simplification tried it). Only drops are deferred: a finalizer or `__del__` that can run inside a registry call may drop claims (`release()`, a finalize) but must not call `acquire()`, `ensure()` or `suspended()`, which would still change the registry mid-operation.
**Behaviour change:** while a tab is open, other programs cannot save over, rename, move or delete the file ("file in use", as with Acrobat); sync clients that rewrite in place get the same error. Readers are unaffected.
**File:** `utils/file_share_lock.py`, `utils/path_staging.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`; `test_scripts/test_session_file_share_lock.py` (29 tests: foreign writers refused while open and allowed after close for file- and memory-backed sessions, an external process cannot rewrite the file and the session keeps its content, Ctrl+S incremental/full/secure, the file stays locked while the document is serialized, Save As moves the lock, Save As over another file, close-with-save, `replace_file` over a locked path, failed save / failed install / refused open release or re-take it, replace-open, two windows, session transfer, read-only file, degraded mode keeps the F10-FS-1 gate, non-Windows no-op, counted tokens and re-entrant suspension, a GC-time release never blocks the collecting thread, and a drop on the registry's own thread inside a re-open: the last claim collected at the `suspended()` exit, the ensured token released inside `ensure()`, another claim dropped inside `ensure()` / `acquire()`, an explicit `release()` inside a registry call that neither deadlocks nor leaks); foreign-writer tests in `test_save_prunes_orphans.py` / `test_tab_detach.py` now run under `share_lock_disabled`

## A lazily damaged file was repaired by MuPDF in the middle of Ctrl+S and the in-memory edits were dropped (OD-FS1-READALL, F10-FS-1 open issue 2)
**Area:** `model/xref_compaction.py` (`read_every_object`, `ObjectWalk`, `MAX_READ_ALL_SLOTS`, `open_compaction_verdict(walk=...)`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`open_pdf`, `_read_every_object_at_open`, `_compact_doc_xref_in_memory`)
**Symptom:** (Round 10 F10-FS-1 probes p12/p13, left to the owner.) A file whose xref entry for an object MuPDF does not need at open is off by a few bytes opens normally (`is_repaired` False) and stays file-backed. Edit (add a text box), Ctrl+S: the first load of that object happens inside the save, MuPDF rebuilds the table there and the document drops every in-memory edit. Incremental save: `PermissionError [WinError 5]` on the hidden `.<hex>.install.pdf` after the "Can't do incremental writes on a repaired file" fallback; full save: success reported, the live document and the file without the edit. Raw PyMuPDF shows the same (`'hello p1\nMY EDIT'` -> `'hello p1'` across `save`, even when the incremental save returns normally).
**Cause:** MuPDF loads objects lazily and repairs the table the first time a load fails, silently (no exception: only `is_repaired` flips False -> True at that object). The open-time repair round trip only ran for damage met during `fitz.open`, and the LS-3 census does not reach a table under 512 slots and stops early on healthy tables.
**Fix (owner decision):** `open_pdf` reads every object once right after the 0-page check and before the compaction / repair steps: `_read_every_object_at_open` -> `xref_compaction.read_every_object` (`xref_object` per slot, slot 0 skipped; goes on past an object that fails to load and logs one warning with a STRING; stops at the repair, after which MuPDF has rebuilt the whole table from a scan). The repair therefore happens at open, before any edit, and the existing `_repair_doc_xref_in_memory` round trip installs a clean memory-backed document (incremental saves off for the session). Encrypted documents are walked too (reading objects never touches `needs_pass`, R9 M9-1); they skip the round trip as before and keep MuPDF's repaired handle (`is_repaired` True right after `open_pdf`), whose saves are full rewrites that keep the edit and the password. The same pass counts the free slots: `open_compaction_verdict(doc, size, walk)` uses them when `walk.census_usable` (complete, not repaired, no failed object, same table length) instead of a second walk; the early-exit census runs only when the walk was skipped or unusable (a repaired table is re-counted). The compaction failure fallback (fresh `fitz.open` of the file) walks the fresh handle again, because it has not met the lazy damage the first walk found.
**Cap (measured, PyMuPDF 1.27.1):** the cost tracks the slot count, not the file size (stream data is not read): 47 MB / 4,028 slots 17 ms, 36.5 MB / 10,679 slots 44 ms, a 15.6 MB file of 200,000 small dictionaries 1.16 s (0.5 s in object-stream form), 500,000 slots 2.2 s. Corpus (2,936 readable PDFs under `test_files`): largest table 40,015 slots (118 ms), slowest 179 ms, 0.74 s for all of them, none repaired by the walk alone. `MAX_READ_ALL_SLOTS` = 200,000 (~1 s, same as `MAX_CENSUS_SLOTS`) plus the H10-2 unbacked-table guard; a byte cap would not bound the cost. Loaded objects stay cached for the document's life (~0.3-0.9 KB per slot; 63 MB at 200,000 slots).
**Rules:** detect a lazy repair by the `is_repaired` flag, never by an exception. Free-slot counts from a walk that repaired or failed objects are not a census. Any new place that re-opens the user's ORIGINAL file as the live document must walk it again (fresh handles have not met the damage); reopening a file the app just wrote needs no walk.
**Residual risk:** tables above 200,000 slots (or declaring more slots than the file has bytes) are not walked and keep the old mid-save behaviour; damage only in stream DATA is not read by the walk (probe: a stream `/Length` off by 50 neither repairs at the walk nor at an incremental/full save; the edit survives). The test fixtures shift a classic-table entry; xref-stream files were not damaged on purpose (the walk is the same call).
**File:** `model/xref_compaction.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`; `test_scripts/test_xref_repair.py` (`test_a_lazily_damaged_file_is_repaired_at_open[last|mid]`, `test_an_edit_on_a_lazily_damaged_file_survives_ctrl_s[last|mid x incremental|full]`, `test_a_lazily_damaged_encrypted_file_is_repaired_at_open_and_keeps_edit_and_password`, `test_a_healthy_file_is_read_once_at_open_and_stays_file_backed`, `test_a_table_above_the_read_all_cap_is_not_walked`, `test_the_read_all_cap_is_pinned`, `test_read_every_object_skips_an_unbacked_declared_table`, `test_read_every_object_reports_the_repair_and_a_complete_census`, `test_objects_that_fail_to_load_do_not_stop_the_walk_or_the_open`), `test_scripts/test_open_compacts_free_xref_slots.py` (`test_a_file_above_the_size_cap_is_not_compacted_and_walked_only_once`, `test_a_compacting_open_walks_the_table_only_once`)

## A consented rebuild with emoji or shaped text commits with a wrong text layer (accepted, OD-UNI1-COMMIT; F10-UNI-1 follow-up)
**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` — `_verify_rebuild_edit`, `_validate_protected_spans`, `_lossy_text_layer_problem`, `_htmlbox_reference`, `_texttrace_glyphs`, `_rebuild_insert_markup`, `_protected_span_markup`  
**Symptom:** After a consented legacy rebuild with emoji, other non-BMP characters or shaped clusters (Devanagari, Gujarati and Tamil conjuncts, Arabic lam-alef, ...) the page LOOKS right, but copy/paste, search and the app's own text index return other characters: U+1F600 comes back as U+1F60, `हिन्दी` as `ह` U+0259 U+010F `दी`, `لا` as U+01BE U+0006. Round 10 refused these edits outright (a `_lost_requested_chars` hit).  
**Cause:** PyMuPDF 1.27 `insert_htmlbox` (MuPDF story -> PDF) draws the right glyphs but writes a wrong ToUnicode: a non-BMP code point is cut to its low 16 bits, and a glyph with no one-to-one cmap entry (a conjunct or a ligature) is mapped to its glyph id read as a code point. Which characters are affected depends on the shaping, not only on the script (Thai, Hebrew, plain Arabic letters and Gurmukhi words in the tests extract fine; one conjunct in the same script does not). `get_texttrace` reports the drawn glyph ids correctly (and U+FFFD for the unmappable ones).  
**Fix (owner decision: commit with the htmlbox rendering, record the limitation):** `_verify_rebuild_edit` renders the SAME markup (`_rebuild_insert_markup`, the one builder the insert also uses) on a scratch page (`_htmlbox_reference`). A requested character missing from the page is forgiven only when (1) the scratch render's text layer lacks it too (htmlbox cannot encode it), (2) the scratch render has no .notdef glyph (glyph id 0: no font draws it -- CJK Ext-B, PUA, unassigned), (3) it is not a placeholder without Unicode identity (U+FFFD, Cc, Co, Cn, Cs; htmlbox draws U+FFFD and control codes as a replacement glyph, which is not the source glyph) -- unless it is untouched and the consent acknowledged it (F11-UNI-1, owner decision C: see that entry), and (4) every glyph the scratch render draws, as `(font, glyph id)` from `get_texttrace`, is drawn on the page around the insert. Anything else keeps the round-10 rule: a character htmlbox CAN encode must be in the page text. The presence gates (exact / similarity / token coverage) then compare the page with the scratch render's text layer instead of the requested text. Protected neighbour spans get the same treatment in `_validate_protected_spans` (`_protected_span_markup` is the one builder for replay and check). The success is logged at WARNING (`rebuild committed with a lossy htmlbox text layer (OD-UNI1-COMMIT)`); the commit outcome is unchanged.  
**Rules:** never accept a lossy text layer on "some glyph is in the rect": insert_text's `·` (U+00B7) is a real glyph too -- compare against the glyphs htmlbox itself draws for the same markup. Never build the verification markup separately from the insert markup. Glyph ids are compared before save, in the same process and PyMuPDF build; do not pin specific glyph ids in tests.  
**Residual:** CJK Ext-B (U+20000+): htmlbox has no font for it (`.notdef`); since EXTB-SUBSET (owner decision C, entry "A consented rebuild with CJK Ext-B characters always rolled back") it is drawn from an in-memory subset of the Windows SimSun-ExtB / MingLiU-ExtB font, and still rolls back where neither is installed. An emoji with a skin-tone modifier rolls back (htmlbox draws the modifier as .notdef); a keycap VS16 does too, but only when the same edit also has a lossy character (alone it never reaches the glyph gate). The wrong text layer itself is not fixed (TODOS.md lists what a real fix needs).  
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_consented_rebuild_never_substitutes_middle_dot_for_non_latin1` "glyphs"/"refused" rows, `test_consented_rebuild_of_a_whole_line_with_a_lossy_text_layer_commits`, `test_consented_cid_rebuild_never_substitutes_middle_dot`, `test_consented_rebuild_rolls_back_when_the_page_does_not_draw_the_lossy_glyphs`, `test_rebuild_verification_refuses_when_requested_chars_are_lost`, `test_protected_span_replay_with_a_lossy_text_layer`, `test_protected_span_validation_fails_when_the_lossy_glyphs_are_not_drawn`)

## A consented rebuild of a line with an untouched U+FFFD / PUA / C1 glyph always refused, and a replayed neighbour U+FFFD was changed silently (F11-UNI-1, owner decision C)
**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` -- `edit_text` (consent branch), `_rebuild_glyph_loss`, `_untouched_glyph_report`, `_unkeepable_glyph_fate`, `_lossy_text_layer_problem`, `_verify_rebuild_edit`, `_validate_protected_spans`; `model/edit_requests.py` (`UnkeepableGlyph`, `RebuildConsent`); `model/pdf_model.py` (`pending_rebuild_glyph_loss`); `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`_confirm_legacy_fallback`, `_fallback_confirmation_message`, `_glyph_loss_line`)  
**Symptom:** "改用重建文字…" on a line such as `Price <glyph> today` whose glyph has no Unicode identity (ToUnicode U+FFFD, an unknown glyph name the index reads as U+FFFD, a Symbol-font bullet U+F0B7, U+E000) always ended in the English modal "requested characters are not on the page after the insert: U+FFFD", although the user never touched that glyph. When the glyph was instead an overlapping NEIGHBOUR run that the rebuild redacts and replays, U+FFFD went the other way: SUCCESS, with the glyph silently redrawn as another one (PUA neighbours were refused).  
**Cause:** the rebuild redacts and re-typesets the text through htmlbox, which cannot reproduce a glyph without a Unicode identity: U+FFFD and control codes come back as a replacement glyph (extracted U+0239 / U+037D), private use as a blank .notdef (extracted NUL). The requested-character check is therefore the only guard against a silent change, so it refused every such line. `_validate_protected_spans` probes neighbours with `_presence_norm`, and `normalize_text` drops U+FFFD, so a U+FFFD neighbour had an empty probe and passed.  
**Fix (owner decision C):** the change is allowed only when the consent dialog said so. Before the ask, `edit_text` computes `_rebuild_glyph_loss`: every unkeepable glyph (`_is_unkeepable_glyph` = identity-less and not whitespace) in the requested text that a character diff (`difflib`, `autojunk=False`) against the target members' text shows as UNTOUCHED (`span_id=None`, index in the requested text), plus every one in the protected neighbour runs (`span_id` = run id). One typed placeholder empties the report, so nothing can be acknowledged. `fate` comes from `_unkeepable_glyph_fate` ("replaced" for U+FFFD / Cc, "removed" for Co / Cs / Cn). The report is exposed as `model.pending_rebuild_glyph_loss` only while the callback runs. The controller adds "注意：此行有 N 個符號無法辨識，重建後無法保留，會變成其他符號或消失（...）" to the dialog (counts only) and, on Yes, returns `RebuildConsent(acknowledged_glyph_loss=report)`. The model accepts the acknowledgement only when it equals the report exactly. `_lossy_text_layer_problem` then forgives an acknowledged placeholder label (the reference render must lack it too) and allows as many reference .notdef glyphs as acknowledged "removed" glyphs. `_validate_protected_spans` refuses a neighbour whose placeholders are not all acknowledged, before the presence probe. A bare `True` consent acknowledges nothing.  
**Rules:** (F16-PASTE-2: the class also holds U+FFFC, the object replacement character, fate "replaced".) A placeholder the user typed is never acknowledgeable. Compare acknowledgements by full equality (index, code point, fate, run), never by label membership. Do not judge a protected span with a `_presence_norm` probe alone, because U+FFFD normalises to nothing. A new consent producer must show the glyph line before it returns a `RebuildConsent`.  
**Residual:** the committed text layer carries the replacement (U+0239 / U+037D) or NUL. The cross-page move asks its consent before the model runs and passes a bare `True`, so a move whose source line carries such a glyph still refuses. The refusal sentence on that path is the move's own (F12-DLG-3, below). Option D (keep the glyph by replaying the original run around the edit) is a TODOS item and needs a plans/ file. The fate mapping is static; `test_unkeepable_glyph_fate_matches_htmlbox` pins it against the pinned PyMuPDF.  
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`, `model/edit_requests.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/edit_commands.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`. Tests: `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_rebuild_reports_untouched_unkeepable_glyphs_before_consent`, `test_acknowledged_untouched_glyph_rebuild_commits`, `test_unacknowledged_untouched_glyph_rebuild_is_still_refused`, `test_a_stale_or_partial_acknowledgement_is_refused`, `test_a_typed_placeholder_is_refused_even_when_acknowledged`, `test_protected_neighbour_glyph_needs_acknowledgement`, `test_unkeepable_glyph_fate_matches_htmlbox`) and `test_scripts/test_text_commit_consent_flow.py` (`test_rebuild_dialog_names_unkeepable_glyphs_and_consent_commits`, `test_declining_the_glyph_loss_dialog_leaves_the_page_untouched`, `test_rebuild_dialog_without_unkeepable_glyphs_has_no_glyph_line`, `test_confirm_returns_an_acknowledgement_of_exactly_the_reported_glyphs`).

## F11-ANN-4 grep guard flagged the htmlbox reference render's own text read (GUARD-DRIFT)
**Area:** `test_scripts/test_page_content_text.py::test_edit_pipeline_extracts_structure_only_through_the_content_helper`, `model/pdf_text_edit.py::_htmlbox_reference`
**Symptom:** the guard failed after OD-UNI1-COMMIT added `_HtmlboxReference(page.get_text("text"), glyphs, notdef)`: a new `page.get_text(` in an edit-pipeline module is an offender unless allowlisted.
**Cause:** the guard bans raw `page.get_text` because it includes annotation/widget appearance text, but `_htmlbox_reference` reads a throwaway `fitz.open()` page that only ever holds one `insert_htmlbox` render, so no annotation or widget can be there and the read IS content text. The guard cannot know that.
**Fix:** exact-line entry in `_VISIBLE_TEXT_ALLOWED` with a comment giving the reason, plus `test_htmlbox_reference_scratch_page_never_carries_annotations`, which spies on the insert and asserts the scratch page has no annotations or widgets even for markup with a link and an input. Rule: allowlist a raw `get_text` only for a page the code itself built; any page that came from the user's document goes through `content_text`.
**File:** `test_scripts/test_page_content_text.py`, `model/pdf_text_edit.py`

## A signed save that could not append silently fell back to a full rewrite and invalidated the signature (SIG-DIALOG)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`SignatureWouldBreakError`, `save_as` / `save_session_as` / `_save_as_unchecked` `allow_signature_loss`, `_save_signed_by_appending`, `_signature_loss_gate`), `model/signed_append_save.py` (`try_append_state_onto_source`, `DECLINE_REASONS`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`_save_with_signature_consent`, `_confirm_signature_loss`, `_signature_loss_texts`), `view/message_boxes.py` (`confirm_signature_loss`)
**Symptom:** (Owner decision, round 10 "Signed-save residual declines".) Ctrl+S / Save As / close-with-save / Save All of a digitally signed PDF wrote a full rewrite whenever the append-only save was not possible (secure latch after a page delete / TOC / metadata edit, incremental saving off, a repaired or spent file-backed handle, a changed or vanished source, a user-password source, another catalog, the growth cap, a failed verification, an exploding replay, a watermark clone, a failed in-place append). The signature stopped verifying with only a log line; the user was never told.
**Cause:** every one of those declines answered `False` and the caller ran `_full_save_to_path` (or the prepared-doc full save, or the `except` fallback of the in-place append) unconditionally: the save path had no way to say "this write breaks the signature" to anyone who could ask the user.
**Fix:** `_save_signed_by_appending` returns `None` (written), `SIGNED_APPEND_UNSIGNED` (no signed signature: the rewrite loses nothing) or a reason code; `try_append_state_onto_source` carries the replay's own code (`append_state_onto_source` stays the bool wrapper). Before each of the three full-rewrite routes of a signed document `_signature_loss_gate` raises `SignatureWouldBreakError(reason_code, path)` unless `allow_signature_loss=True`; it is raised before anything is written (the stage is discarded, the session stays dirty, `save_as` does not re-record the disk fingerprint), except `incremental_failed`, whose failed in-place append is rolled back first and whose fingerprint IS re-recorded (F12-SIG-1, see that entry). The controller wraps every save call site (`save`, `save_as`, `_save_session_with_dialog`, `_save_session_for_close`, so Save All too) in `_save_with_signature_consent`: it asks with a Traditional Chinese dialog (signature will be invalid, one plain line per reason code, suggests Save As to keep the original; default and Esc = 取消) and retries with `allow_signature_loss=True` only on 仍要儲存. A cancel is not a failed save: no error, no "儲存完成", no Save dialog on the close path, and the close / Save All is aborted with the tab and its edits kept. Session transfer has no save of its own: the receiving window saves through the same controller methods. Rule: a save path that would destroy something the user cannot see (a signature) raises a typed refusal from the model; never decide it silently in a fallback. Round 12 (F12-DLG-1): the dialog names the signed document. A Save All / per-tab close asks for tabs in session order while another tab is still the visible, active one, and File > Save As acts on the ACTIVE tab, so an unnamed "cancel, then Save As" advice made the user save the wrong file (the signed tab stayed dirty). `_save_with_signature_consent(save, session_id)` now passes the session being saved; `_confirm_signature_loss(exc, session_id)` resolves its `display_name` (`_signature_document_name`) and `_signature_loss_texts(exc, document_name, other_tab)` writes it into the main text and, when that session is not the active tab, adds "switch to the 「name」 tab" to the Save As advice. The dialog does not switch tabs itself (F11-1: no tab changes under a modal). Rule: any modal raised from the per-session close loop must name its document; the other close-loop modals already do (`SourceChangedOnDiskError` and `SaveRecoveryError` messages carry the file, the Save dialog shows the session's path). Not changed: the generic `儲存失敗: ...` text of a non-signature error in `_save_session_with_dialog` still relies on the exception text.
**Residual risk:** `apply_pending_redactions` (`clean_contents` of pages with queued maintenance) has already run on the live document when the refusal is raised; the content is equivalent and nothing is written. A failed in-place append (`incremental_failed`) whose partial revision cannot be rolled back (the truncate itself fails, or the file's leading bytes no longer match) stays torn until the next save (F12-SIG-1). No real PKCS#7 validator was run; the tests check the byte prefix / `%%EOF` count as before. `document_has_a_signed_signature` is fail-closed (an unreadable form tree or one over the 4096-node cap answers "signed"): that used to cost nothing visible (the save appended), but now an UNSIGNED file with such a form tree plus a secure latch, incremental saving off or a watermark gets a dialog that says the document carries a signature it does not have.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/signed_append_save.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`, `view/message_boxes.py`; `test_scripts/test_signed_save_consent.py` (`test_real_models_save_all_dialog_names_the_signed_background_tab` and the `names the` tests), `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py` (`test_signed_doc_with_the_secure_latch_still_gets_the_sanitising_rewrite`, `test_signed_append_failure_falls_back_to_the_full_save`, `test_encrypted_signed_save_keeps_the_live_session_and_the_file_readable`, `test_signed_save_as_after_a_foreign_in_place_rewrite_does_not_embed_the_foreign_file`, `test_signed_save_as_over_a_source_that_vanished_still_degrades_not_crashes`)

## A consented rebuild with CJK Ext-B characters always rolled back (htmlbox has no font for them; EXTB-SUBSET, owner decision C on OD-UNI1-COMMIT)
**Area:** `utils/cjk_ext_b_font.py` (new); `model/font_stream_compaction.py` -- `insert_htmlbox_tracked`; `model/pdf_text_edit.py` -- `_texttrace_glyphs`, `_lossy_text_layer_problem`
**Symptom:** A consented legacy rebuild whose text contains an Ext-B ideograph (U+20000 and up) rolled back with `no font draws some of the requested characters (.notdef glyph): U+20000`, on every machine.
**Cause:** PyMuPDF 1.27's htmlbox fallback fonts stop at the BMP for Han, so it draws glyph id 0 (no ink). A `@font-face` pointing at the whole Windows Ext-B font renders it but embeds 11.7 MB (SimSun-ExtB) / 17.2 MB (MingLiU-ExtB) in every saved file. Two traps once it renders: (1) htmlbox's 16-bit cut of the code point turns U+20000..U+200AF into U+2000..U+200A (whitespace) and `_texttrace_glyphs` skipped whitespace codes, so the glyph evidence for such characters was silently empty and a page that did not draw them would still have passed; (2) fontTools renumbers glyph ids per subset, so two different subsets of one font on a page would share `(font name, glyph id)` keys.
