**Fix:** The htmlbox chokepoint `insert_htmlbox_tracked` calls `utils.cjk_ext_b_font.ext_b_htmlbox_resources(html)`: Ext-B runs in text nodes (never inside a tag) get their own `<span style="font-family: PdfEditorExtB-...">`, the font is subset in memory with fontTools to exactly those code points (no hinting, no layout features, `meta` dropped) and handed to htmlbox through an in-memory `fitz.Archive` with a matching `@font-face`. Font per character, first that has it: SimSun-ExtB `simsunb.ttf` (single TrueType face, 60,349 code points at U+20000 and up: Ext-B to Ext-F), then MingLiU-ExtB `mingliub.ttc` face 0 (47,095; has 11 compatibility ideographs SimSun-ExtB lacks, and is used when `simsunb.ttf` is missing). Both carry OS/2 fsType 0x8 (editable embedding, subsetting allowed) and draw near-identical Ming shapes. Each subset is named `PdfEditorExtB-<SimSun|MingLiU>-<8 hex of a sha1 of its code points>` (at most 31 characters: MuPDF truncates font names there), so keys never collide across subsets, and `_texttrace_glyphs` exempts that prefix from the whitespace skip. Because the chokepoint does the wrapping, the real insert, protected-span replays, push-down replays and the verification's scratch reference render all draw the same subset. Measured on the maintainer's machine (SimSun-ExtB, PyMuPDF 1.27.1, fontTools 4.66.1): +2,379 bytes saved for 2 Ext-B glyphs, +10,069 bytes for 40 (test bounds 16 KB / 64 KB). Font missing (not Windows, neither file installed, or unreadable): nothing is wrapped, htmlbox draws .notdef and the refusal now ends `CJK Ext-B needs the Windows font SimSun-ExtB (simsunb.ttf) or MingLiU-ExtB (mingliub.ttc), and neither is installed: U+20000` (or names the characters the installed fonts lack, e.g. plane-3 Ext-G U+30000). fontTools is now a core requirement (`requirements.txt` / `pyproject.toml` `fonttools>=4.60.2,<5`; `constraints-ci.txt` pins it per interpreter: fontTools 4.66 requires Python 3.11+, so CI's 3.10 gets 4.65.0 and the .venv 4.66.1 -- a pin that ignores `requires-python` breaks every CI install step).
**Rules:** never embed the whole Ext-B font; never key glyph evidence for these fonts on the texttrace code; do the Ext-B wrapping only through `htmlbox_args_with_ext_b` (the chokepoint and the view's live preview both call it; never hand-roll it per call site) so the reference render, the insert and the preview cannot diverge, and give every new `insert_htmlbox` call in `view/`, `controller/` or `utils/` that call first (AST guard `test_view_and_controller_htmlbox_calls_apply_the_ext_b_subset`); keep the fontTools import lazy and only in `utils/cjk_ext_b_font.py` (AST guard `test_fonttools_is_imported_only_by_the_ext_b_subsetter`).
**Residual:** the text layer stays lossy (U+20B9F extracts as U+20B9, U+20000 as a space; TODOS accepted limitation). Windows only. The view's live CSS preview (`PreviewRenderer.render`, a bare `insert_htmlbox` on a throwaway page) used to draw .notdef (an empty box) for Ext-B while the editor was open, the committed page being right (S12-EXTB-PREVIEW, fixed round 12: the view may not import `model`, so the shared `utils.cjk_ext_b_font.htmlbox_args_with_ext_b` does the wrapping/`@font-face`/archive for both; pinned by `test_live_preview_draws_ext_b_like_the_committed_page`). Under the default tiered engine an existing line previews from the plan raster, so only add-new and the legacy engine ever reached the CSS preview. Subsets are cached per (font file, code points) for the process (LRU of 64).
**Round 12 (F12-DLG-4):** the `ext_b_font_missing` dialog sentence tells the user to install the system Ext-B fonts, which is only true on Windows with neither candidate installed. With `simsunb.ttf` / `mingliub.ttc` installed and a character they lack (U+30000, Ext-G and later) or off Windows (`find_ext_b_fonts()` is always `()`) installing changes nothing. `_lossy_text_layer_problem` now returns `EXT_B_FONT_MISSING` only when `utils.cjk_ext_b_font.ext_b_install_would_help()` (Windows and no candidate font); every other Ext-B case is `NO_FONT_FOR_CHARACTERS` ("use other characters"), and the log detail still names the installed fonts / the characters. Rule: a refusal sentence may advise an action only on the paths where that action can work. Partly installed (only one candidate present) is treated as installed.
**Round 13 (F13-ENV-2):** `find_ext_b_fonts()` looked only in `%WINDIR%\Fonts`, but a font installed the default no-admin way (Windows 10 1809+, double-click > Install) lands in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts`. On a Windows without the system copies the user got the install sentence, installed the font, retried and got the same refusal, and `ext_b_install_would_help()` kept saying True (the F12-DLG-4 rule violated). `_font_dirs()` now returns the system folder and then the per-user folder (`LOCALAPPDATA` unset: system only); each candidate yields one `ExtBFont` from the first folder holding it, so a system copy wins over a per-user copy of the same file and `_subset_name` keys stay unique. `find_ext_b_fonts()` is the only lookup, so `font_for_codepoint`, `ext_b_htmlbox_resources`, `ext_b_refusal_reason` and `ext_b_install_would_help` all follow. Rule: a font lookup must cover every location the OS's documented install paths can put the file, or the advice to install it cannot be satisfied. Not followed: fonts registered under `HKCU\...\Fonts` pointing at another folder; the per-user location is documented Windows behaviour, not reproduced here (tests fake `WINDIR` and `LOCALAPPDATA`). Tests: `test_cjk_ext_b_font.py` (`test_per_user_*`, `test_system_font_wins_over_a_per_user_copy_*`).
**Round 13 (F13-ENV-3):** `_coverage_cached` imported fontTools inside a broad `except Exception`, so an unimportable fontTools (a venv made before it became a runtime dependency, a partial install) logged a per-font "unreadable" WARNING and cached an EMPTY coverage for the process; with the fonts present every Ext-B character then counted as uncovered and the refusal was `NO_FONT_FOR_CHARACTERS` ("installed fonts have no glyph ... use other characters"), blaming the fonts for a broken program. Now `fonttools_import_error()` (importlib on `fontTools.ttLib` and `fontTools.subset`; `from fontTools import subset` would find an already bound attribute and miss a missing submodule) is checked, uncached, before every coverage lookup: while it fails `_coverage` returns an empty set WITHOUT caching it (the cache cannot outlive the cause), one ERROR names the cause (`_log_component_missing`, once per distinct message), `ext_b_htmlbox_resources` degrades like a missing font, `ext_b_refusal_reason` carries `COMPONENT_MISSING_HINT` plus the ImportError, and `_lossy_text_layer_problem` raises the new `TextEditRefusal.EXT_B_COMPONENT_MISSING` (zh-TW: the program lacks a component, reinstall or use common characters) when `ext_b_component_missing()` (a font is installed and fontTools does not import). With no font installed the install-the-fonts sentence still comes first. Rule: an environment failure (import, I/O) must never be folded into the same "empty" answer as a legitimate negative (no glyph) or be cached as one. Not changed: a corrupt font FILE stays fail-closed as "no glyph" (a data problem, logged as unreadable); the lost label in the rebuild log is the NFC-normalised character (U+2F825 -> U+52C7), a log-only quirk. Tests: `test_cjk_ext_b_font.py` (`test_unimportable_fonttools_*`, `test_component_missing_*`, `test_a_failed_fonttools_import_does_not_poison_the_coverage_cache`), `test_text_edit_refusal_messages.py` (`test_ext_b_with_fonttools_unimportable_*`).
**Round 14 (S14-EXTB-PREVIEW-WORKER, owner decision C on F13-EXTB-PERF-1):** the live preview ran the fontTools work for every NEW Ext-B character set on the GUI thread: `PreviewRenderer.render` -> `htmlbox_args_with_ext_b` -> `_coverage_cached` (first set: cmap load) and `_subset_cached` (subset + save), measured 0.14-0.16 s per new set and 0.31 s for the first, once per 150 ms-debounced pause that adds a set (add-new boxes and the legacy engine only; the plan raster goes through the commit chokepoint). Now `render(..., defer_ext_b=True)` -- what the inline editor's `_render_css_frame` passes, pinned by an AST test -- calls `htmlbox_args_with_ext_b(..., cached_only=True)`, which only PEEKS the caches (`_PeekCache`, a thread-safe LRU that replaced `functools.lru_cache` for coverage and subsets and keeps its `cache_clear` / `cache_info`) and raises `ExtBSubsetNotReady` instead of computing. On that miss the frame draws .notdef for the Ext-B characters (accepted transient; text with nothing else in it has no ink, so `_mutated_preview_is_valid` goes False and the editor paints Qt's native text until the glyph arrives), is NOT cached (`PreviewRenderer.pending_ext_b_html` names its markup, and a pending frame must not overwrite the render cache or the next render with the same key would return the .notdef image), and the editor hands the markup to its `ExtBSubsetService` (`view/ext_b_subset_worker.py`: one `QThread` at a time, latest request wins, the thread only calls `utils.cjk_ext_b_font.warm_ext_b_subsets` and emits a signal, no Qt/fitz object crosses threads). The result arrives as a queued signal; `_on_ext_b_subsets_ready` drops it unless the markup is still the editor's pending one (text typed since), else re-renders the CSS frame, now a cache hit. A markup whose subsets are still missing after its worker finished is not requested again (no loop: a font that cannot be subset keeps the .notdef frame). Closing the editor (`TextEditManager._teardown_editor` -> `release_background_work`) closes the service; a running thread is parentless and held in a module registry until finished, so it is never destroyed while running, and `aboutToQuit` waits for it. Measured through the editor: GUI-thread stall 2-3 ms per new set (was 140-310 ms), glyph appears 0.16-0.4 s later. Rule: fontTools / font-file work for a keystroke-driven preview belongs on a worker behind a peek-only cache read; the COMMIT path (`insert_htmlbox_tracked`, once per Apply) still subsets synchronously and is the only other caller. Not covered: driven through a real GUI session with a human typing. Tests: `test_cjk_ext_b_font.py` (`test_live_preview_subset_runs_on_a_worker_then_the_glyph_appears`, `test_a_cached_ext_b_set_renders_at_once_without_a_worker`, `test_a_subset_result_for_older_text_is_dropped`, `test_closing_the_editor_cancels_the_worker_callback`, `test_the_view_calls_the_deferred_preview_render_only`, `test_cached_only_resources_never_run_the_subset`, `test_deferred_render_reports_the_pending_markup_and_does_not_cache_it`).
**File:** `utils/cjk_ext_b_font.py`, `model/font_stream_compaction.py`, `view/text_editing.py` (`PreviewRenderer.render`), `view/ext_b_subset_worker.py`, `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_cjk_ext_b_font.py`, `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` ("ext_b" rows of `test_consented_rebuild_never_substitutes_middle_dot_for_non_latin1` / `test_consented_cid_rebuild_never_substitutes_middle_dot` / `test_protected_span_replay_with_a_lossy_text_layer`, `test_consented_ext_b_rebuild_refuses_with_a_clear_reason_when_no_ext_b_font_is_installed`, `test_consented_ext_b_rebuild_keeps_the_saved_file_small`, `test_protected_ext_b_span_fails_validation_without_an_ext_b_font`), `test_scripts/test_layer_boundaries.py`, `test_scripts/test_environment_pins.py`

## A second launch whose hand-off the running instance rejects dropped the valid files too, with no message (F11-3)
**Area:** `utils/single_instance.py` (`forwarded_token_is_acceptable`, `partition_forwardable_argv`, `_forwarded_argv_is_acceptable`), `main.py` (`_hand_off_to_running_instance`, `_show_rejected_cli_files_dialog`, `_rejected_cli_files_message`)
**Symptom:** `pdf_editor good.pdf moved.pdf` (or a real PDF without a `.pdf` suffix) while an instance runs: the receiver's whole-message fail-closed filter acked `0`, `main.run` returned 1 before any UI, so `good.pdf` was never opened and nothing told the user why. A first launch opens `good.pdf` and shows an error for `moved.pdf`.
**Cause:** the launcher forwarded every token as one message and had no copy of the receiver's rule, so it could neither split the tokens nor explain the rejection.
**Fix (owner decision B):** the per-token rule is ONE function, `forwarded_token_is_acceptable` (resolves the token, requires an existing `.pdf`; OSError/ValueError/RuntimeError from resolve means rejected). The receiver's `_forwarded_argv_is_acceptable` is `all(...)` over it, so the two sides cannot drift; a test spies on it. The launcher (`_hand_off_to_running_instance`) runs `partition_forwardable_argv`, forwards the valid tokens as one message so they open, THEN shows a Traditional Chinese `QMessageBox` naming the rejected tokens (capped at 10; the modal box does not delay the valid files). With no valid token nothing is forwarded and the box is shown; exit code is 1 unless the hand-off was acked. A bare launch (no arguments) still forwards the empty message to raise the window.
**Rules:** do not loosen the receiver (it cannot tell a trusted launcher from a crafted peer; a mixed message sent straight to the socket is still rejected whole); the dialog lives in `main.py` because `utils/` may not import QtWidgets. Extension-less real PDFs are still rejected (option C, a `%PDF-` sniff, was not chosen). A hand-off that fails for a transport reason (primary hung over 60 s, no live server) still exits 1 with no message (F11-2 open item).
**File:** `utils/single_instance.py`, `main.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_single_instance_forwarding.py` (`test_token_predicate_is_the_one_the_receiver_uses`, `test_partition_splits_valid_and_rejected_tokens_in_order`, `test_receiver_still_rejects_a_mixed_message`, `test_launcher_*` incl. `test_launcher_end_to_end_opens_the_valid_file_in_the_running_instance`, `test_rejected_cli_files_message_*`)

## A refused text edit reached the user as the English technical modal (ZH-REFUSALS)
**Area:** `model/text_edit_refusal.py` (`TextEditRefusal`, `TextEditRefused`), `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_RebuildRolledBack`, `_TextLayerProblem`, `_lossy_text_layer_problem`, `_verify_rebuild_edit`, `_protected_glyphs_unacknowledged`, `edit_text` except branches), `controller/text_edit_refusals.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`edit_text`, `move_text_across_pages`, `add_textbox`)
**Symptom:** a refused rebuild (vertical text that redaction could not remove, characters lost after the insert, CJK Ext-B with no installed font, an unidentifiable glyph nobody acknowledged, a replayed neighbour that failed validation, a failed rollback) ended in a modal such as "編輯失敗: overlap edit verification failed: requested characters are not on the page after the insert: U+FFFD" -- English diagnostics, code points, no hint what the user can do. Owner decision (round 11, "Refusal UI"): one plain Traditional Chinese message per refusal reason, technical detail in the log only.
**Cause:** the Model signalled every refusal with a bare `RuntimeError(<technical text>)` and the Controller's catch-all did `show_error(f"編輯失敗: {e}")`; there was no machine-readable reason, so the only way to say anything else was to parse the English message.
**Fix:** `TextEditRefused(reason, detail)` is the one exception for a text edit that did not commit (Qt-free; subclass of `RuntimeError`, so every existing `except RuntimeError` still holds; `str(exc)` is the detail). Every raise site in the edit path carries a `TextEditRefusal` code: the five `_RebuildRolledBack` sites, the two rollback-failed wrappers, the `except Exception` wrapper and now the uncoded-`RuntimeError` branch (`edit_failed`). The verification's text-layer check returns `_TextLayerProblem` (a `str` carrying `.reason`) so each branch of `_lossy_text_layer_problem` has its own code (placeholders only -> `unidentifiable_glyphs_not_acknowledged`, else `characters_lost`; `.notdef` -> `ext_b_font_missing` or `no_font_for_characters`; undrawn glyphs -> `glyphs_not_drawn`); a failed protected-span validation is split by `_protected_glyphs_unacknowledged`. `controller/text_edit_refusals.py` maps code -> sentence (`refusal_message`), falls back to `GENERIC_REFUSAL_MESSAGE` for an unknown code or an uncoded exception (`user_message_for_exception`) and logs `reason=` and `detail=` (`log_edit_failure`). The cross-page move's own aborts use `UserFacingEditError` (message already plain).
**Rules:** a new refusal raise in the text-edit path must use `TextEditRefused` with a `TextEditRefusal` member, and the member needs a sentence in `_MESSAGES` (a test pins that every member has a distinct one with no Latin letters). Never put document content, code points or file names in a sentence (P0-C privacy contract); they stay in `detail`, which only the log sees. Do not map by parsing the detail text. `EditTextResult` values and `CommitOutcome.degraded_reason` codes keep their own mappings (`_edit_result_to_message`, `view/text_edit_reasons.py`).
**Residual:** (undo / redo exception handler: added in round 12, see "A coded refusal from a redo-time re-run escaped the Qt slot"); other `show_error(f"...{e}")` sites outside the text-edit path still show English exception text; the sentences were not driven through the real GUI.
**File:** `model/text_edit_refusal.py`, `model/pdf_text_edit.py`, `controller/text_edit_refusals.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_text_edit_refusal_messages.py` (the map, the dialog per code, uncoded exceptions, cross-page move, add textbox, one real refusal per code, the text-layer branches) and the `refusal_reason` / `.reason` assertions in `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py`

## A coded refusal from a redo-time re-run escaped the Qt slot (S12-REDO-REFUSAL)
**Area:** `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`undo`, `redo`, `_report_history_step_failure`), `controller/text_edit_refusals.py` (`user_message_for_history_failure`), `model/edit_commands.py` (`EditTextCommand.execute` re-run branch, `CommandManager.undo/redo`)
**Symptom:** commit an `engine="legacy"` edit, undo it, then redo it when the re-run is refused (verification rolled back): `TextEditRefused` propagated out of `PDFController.redo()`. No zh-TW sentence, no dialog; under Qt the slot exception only reached the default excepthook.
**Cause:** `redo()`/`undo()` called `CommandManager` with no `try`. A redo of a command with no replay record (the `engine="legacy"` baseline, outcome `None`, and by code reading a tiered Tier-2 legacy commit with chain `("legacy",)`) re-runs the whole `model.edit_text()` in `EditTextCommand.execute`, which can raise any coded refusal. The first-edit path (`edit_text`, `add_textbox`) already had the boundary; the history path never did. Undo never calls `edit_text`, so a coded refusal cannot reach it, but any other exception from a command's own undo/redo (for example `AddTextboxCommand` without an after-snapshot) escaped the same way.
**Fix:** both slots wrap the `CommandManager` call; `_report_history_step_failure` logs the detail (`log_edit_failure`), shows ONE modal `show_error` (modal on purpose: `rollback_failed` tells the user not to save) and refreshes the undo/redo tooltips. A coded refusal / `UserFacingEditError` keeps its own sentence; any other exception gets a neutral Latin-free sentence (`user_message_for_history_failure`), never the text-edit one, because the command may not be a text edit. `CommandManager.undo/redo` move a command between stacks only after the step returns, so a raise leaves both stacks untouched and the command stays retryable (pinned by a second, un-refused redo that succeeds). `False` returns keep the existing toast path.
**Rules:** every Qt slot that runs a command or a model edit needs the `log_edit_failure` + `show_error` boundary; do not let a `CommandManager` call escape. Keep a failing history step from touching the stacks (move after success).
**Residual:** after a raise the page is not re-rendered (same as a refused first edit); for `rollback_failed` the page may already differ from the view. The tiered Tier-2 legacy-chain redo was established by code reading only (the test drives `engine="legacy"`). Not driven through the real GUI.
**File:** `controller/pdf_controller.py`, `controller/text_edit_refusals.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_text_edit_refusal_messages.py` (`test_redo_that_re_runs_a_refused_edit_shows_the_mapped_sentence`, `test_an_uncoded_history_failure_is_reported_not_raised`)

## A signed in-place append that failed half-written locked every later save out as "changed by another program" (F12-SIG-1)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` -- `save_as` (`except SignatureWouldBreakError`), `_save_as_unchecked` (in-place incremental branch), `_roll_back_partial_append`, `_SIGNATURE_REFUSALS_AFTER_A_WRITE`
**Symptom:** Ctrl+S of a signed, file-backed document whose in-place append failed part-way (disk full, a network drop: `OSError` 28 after some bytes were appended) showed the signature dialog (`incremental_failed`); on 仍要儲存 the retry was refused with "已被其他程式修改或取代 ... 請改用「另存新檔」", every later Ctrl+S was refused the same way, and the file kept ending in a torn half revision. With consent given up front (the pre-SIG-DIALOG single call) the same failure saved fine.
**Cause:** `save_as` re-raised `SignatureWouldBreakError` without re-recording the disk fingerprint on the premise "refused before any write". That holds for every refusal except `incremental_failed`: its gate runs after `_save_doc(..., incremental=True)` has already appended to the session's own file, so the session's own bytes looked like a foreign writer's to `_refuse_save_over_foreign_rewrite`. Re-recording alone is not enough: `_signed_append_base_bytes` would then take the torn file as "what the session opened" and a later Save As would copy the torn tail into the new file's history (today the stale fingerprint happened to cut it off).
**Fix:** `_save_as_unchecked` takes `_file_fingerprint(save_target)` right before the in-place append; on failure `_roll_back_partial_append` truncates the file back to that size (inside its own `file_share_lock.suspended`) only when the first `size` bytes still carry the recorded edge digest, never raises, and runs before the signature gate (unsigned documents too; their full save follows anyway). `save_as` re-records the fingerprint for the refusal codes in `_SIGNATURE_REFUSALS_AFTER_A_WRITE` (`incremental_failed` only) when the target is the session's own file, mirroring the generic `BaseException` branch; truncation changes mtime, so the re-record is needed even after a successful rollback. The other codes are genuinely pre-write (`_save_signed_by_appending` discards its stage, `secure_latch` / `incremental_disabled` / `watermark_rewrite` / every append decline gate before any write, `SourceChangedOnDiskError` is raised before `_save_as_unchecked`) and still do not re-record: that would absorb a foreign change. The consented retry appends again from the same handle (MuPDF writes at the end of file it read at open and truncates after its revision), so the signature survives it too.
**Rules:** a refusal raised after the save may have written the session's own file must undo that write when it can and must re-record the fingerprint; add any new such code to `_SIGNATURE_REFUSALS_AFTER_A_WRITE`. Never truncate without checking that the prefix is still the bytes the append started from.
**Residual:** the tests simulate the torn append with a `_save_doc` stand-in that writes then raises; a real MuPDF writer that fails mid-write was not exercised, so the state of the live handle after such a failure is unverified (it is deliberately NOT marked spent: that would route the signed retry to `in_place_append_unavailable` and a full rewrite). When the rollback fails the re-recorded fingerprint covers the torn file, so a Save As to another name before the next successful Ctrl+S copies the torn tail behind the signed prefix (the signature's `/ByteRange` still covers only the original bytes).
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_signed_save_consent.py` (`test_a_torn_in_place_append_of_a_signed_doc_is_rolled_back_and_the_retry_saves`, `test_save_as_after_a_cancelled_torn_append_does_not_copy_the_torn_bytes`, `test_a_torn_append_that_cannot_be_rolled_back_does_not_lock_the_session_out`, `test_the_rollback_only_ever_cuts_the_failed_revision`)

## Text-commit engine and preview wrote garbage=0 snapshots of a secure-latched session to snap_*.pdf in the system temp root (F12-H102-1)
**Area:** `model/text_commit/engine.py` (`TieredCommitEngine._build_scratch_copy`), `model/text_commit/preview.py` (`_live_keep_round_trip`, `open_preview_session`), `model/doc_bytes.py` (`keep_snapshot_in_memory`, `SnapshotSerializer`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`get_tiered_commit_engine`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (plan-preview request)
**Symptom:** (Round 12.) After a page, object, TOC or metadata delete latched `secure_save_required`, opening the inline editor (1 write) and each true-text edit (3 writes) serialized the live document with `garbage=0` to a `snap_*.pdf` temp file with `scratch_dir=None`, i.e. the system temp root, outside the model temp dir that `close()` sweeps. Each file still held the deleted page's content stream or the deleted image's pixels. The model's own `_capture_doc_snapshot` in the same session made 0 disk writes. A failed unlink (antivirus / indexer handle) or a process killed mid-serialize leaves the file behind.
**Cause:** The secure-latch rule ("a latched session's whole-document snapshots stay in memory") lives in `PDFModel.serialize_document_bytes`. The two text-commit sites called `doc_bytes.serialize_doc` directly with neither `in_memory` nor `scratch_dir`, on the reasoning that KEEP bytes of an encrypted file are ciphertext; for an unencrypted latched document they are plaintext. The sibling `verify.py` sites already passed `in_memory=True`.
**Fix:** The engine and `open_preview_session` take an injected `serialize` callable (`doc_bytes.SnapshotSerializer`); the model passes `serialize_document_bytes` (engine in `get_tiered_commit_engine`, preview from the controller's plan-preview request), so they get the model temp dir and the latch rule from the one funnel. Without one they use `doc_bytes.keep_snapshot_in_memory` (fail-closed: never a temp file); the decrypted-clone serialization in `_session_snapshot_bytes` says `in_memory=True` explicitly. Guard for the class: an AST test allows `serialize_doc` without `in_memory=True` only inside `serialize_document_bytes`.
**Gotchas:** (1) A test that builds a controller around a `MagicMock` model must give it a real `serialize_document_bytes` (a MagicMock return is not bytes); see `_minimal_controller` and `_give_the_mock_model_its_snapshot_funnel`. (2) The delete command's own pre-state undo snapshot is taken before the latch is set and does go through a temp file in the model temp dir; it holds the content the source file still has. (3) A standalone engine (scripts, tests) now serializes in memory instead of a temp file; the native in-memory sink is the same MuPDF writer.
**File:** `model/doc_bytes.py`, `model/text_commit/engine.py`, `model/text_commit/preview.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`; `test_scripts/test_doc_bytes.py` (`test_a_secure_session_text_edit_never_touches_disk`, `test_a_secure_session_engine_scratch_copy_never_touches_disk`, `test_a_secure_session_preview_snapshot_never_touches_disk`, `test_an_ordinary_session_text_commit_snapshots_go_through_the_model_temp_dir`, `test_a_bare_engine_and_preview_keep_their_snapshot_in_memory`, `test_no_production_site_serializes_a_live_doc_to_disk_behind_the_models_back`), `test_scripts/test_text_commit_preview_contract.py`

## The cross-page move told the user to "confirm when prompted" for a glyph acknowledgement its prompt never offers (F12-DLG-3)
**Area:** `controller/text_edit_refusals.py` (`refusal_message`, `user_message_for_exception`, `_CROSS_PAGE_MOVE_MESSAGES`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`move_text_across_pages`, `_move_consent_already_given`)
**Symptom:** moving a run that a neighbouring untouched U+FFFD / private-use glyph run overlaps to another page, then answering Yes to the move's rebuild prompt, ended in "請刪除這些符號，或重新操作並在提示時確認". Redoing the move and answering Yes gave the identical refusal, forever; the prompt never mentioned the glyphs.
**Cause:** one sentence per refusal code, but its advice is only true on a path whose consent can carry the acknowledgement. `edit_text` asks inside the model, while the glyph report is live (`pending_rebuild_glyph_loss`), and returns a `RebuildConsent`. The cross-page move asks BEFORE the model runs (report still empty) and the source deletion replays a bare `True`, so the model always refuses with `unidentifiable_glyphs_not_acknowledged` and no prompt on this path can change that.
**Fix:** the sentence is path-aware: `refusal_message(code, cross_page_move=True)` / `user_message_for_exception(exc, cross_page_move=True)` read `_CROSS_PAGE_MOVE_MESSAGES` (today only the glyph code differs) and the move's `except` uses it. The move sentence says the move's prompt cannot confirm the symbols and points to deleting them or editing the line within one page, whose prompt lists them. Behaviour is unchanged: the move still refuses, the page is untouched.
**Rules:** a refusal sentence may promise a confirmation only on a path that can show it. A new path that replays a bare `True` (or any consent that cannot carry a `RebuildConsent`) needs its own sentence for every code that depends on one. Pinned for every code by `test_no_move_sentence_promises_a_confirmation_the_move_cannot_show`.
**Residual:** making such a move succeed is an owner decision (second glyph-naming ask on the source deletion, or a glyph preflight before the move's single ask; TODOS F11-UNI-1). A glyph the user typed (not untouched) still gets the generic sentence, which also says to confirm; not changed here.
**File:** `controller/text_edit_refusals.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_text_edit_refusal_messages.py` (`test_the_move_sentence_for_unacknowledged_glyphs_does_not_point_at_a_prompt`, `test_no_move_sentence_promises_a_confirmation_the_move_cannot_show`, `test_a_cross_page_move_glyph_refusal_does_not_tell_the_user_to_confirm_again`)

## requires-python >=3.9 passed the interpreter check on a Python that no pinned dependency installs on (F12-1)
**Area:** `pyproject.toml` (`requires-python`, ruff `target-version`), `requirements.txt`, `constraints-ci.txt`, `CLAUDE.md`
**Symptom:** on Python 3.9 `pip install .` passed the `requires-python` check and then died with `No matching distribution found for PyMuPDF<1.28,>=1.27` instead of an "unsupported Python" message. The round-11 fontTools pin `fonttools==4.60.2; python_version < "3.10"` and its "newest release that still installs on 3.9" rationale were dead configuration.
**Cause:** the floor was copied from the project's first dependency set. PyMuPDF 1.27.x (no cp39 wheel; 1.26.5 is the newest for 3.9), Pillow 12.2 and numpy 2.2 all declare `Requires-Python >=3.10`, README, CI (`python-version: "3.10"`) and mypy (`python_version = "3.10"`) already said 3.10, and product code uses 3.10-only runtime expressions (`cast(int | float, ...)` in `model/text_commit/verify.py`, `PdfSource = str | bytes` in `src/printing/pdf_renderer.py`). Nothing asserted that the declared floor agreed with them.
**Fix:** floor raised to 3.10 everywhere (`requires-python`, ruff `target-version = "py310"`, the `requirements.txt` header, `CLAUDE.md`), the sub-3.10 fontTools pin removed. `test_requires_python_floor_is_installable_with_the_pinned_runtime_deps` pins the invariant: the floor is admitted by the installed PyMuPDF / Pillow / numpy `Requires-Python`, equals the mypy and ruff targets and a CI interpreter, and no `constraints-ci.txt` marker targets an interpreter below it.
**Rules:** when a runtime pin is bumped, re-read its `Requires-Python` against `requires-python`; a per-interpreter pin for a version below the floor is dead configuration.
**File:** `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt`, `constraints-ci.txt`; `test_scripts/test_environment_pins.py`.

## A failed edit whose rollback also failed left the session saveable: Ctrl+S wrote the half-rewritten page over the original (S13-DLG5-DAMAGED)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`DocumentSession.damaged`, `mark_session_damaged`, `_refuse_save_over_damaged_session`, `DamagedSessionSaveError`, `_restore_doc_after_failed_mutation`), `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_rollback_failed_refusal`), `model/tools/manager.py` (`_check_hook`, `_abandon`), `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`_restore_delete_transaction`), `controller/session_transfer.py`, `controller/text_edit_refusals.py`
**Symptom:** (Round 13, owner decision A + C of F12-DLG-5.) When a legacy rebuild failed after half-rewriting the page and its rollback failed too, the dialog said "reopen the original file", but `open_pdf` on the same path returns the SAME damaged tab, and the session reported `dirty=False`. `controller.save()` / `model.save_as(original)` then replaced the original file with the half-rewritten page and showed "已儲存至".
**Cause:** the only record of the failure was a `ROLLBACK_FAILED` exception that the Controller turned into a sentence. The Model kept no state, so no save path could know the live document was untrustworthy; every other save-side rollback failure (`ProtectedPageViolation` "do not overwrite", `delete_pages` / `move_page` / batch-delete / insert-pages snapshot restores) had the same hole.
**Fix:** a Qt-free `DocumentSession.damaged` latch, set only through `PDFModel.mark_session_damaged(reason)`. Callers: `pdf_text_edit._rollback_failed_refusal` (the ONE builder of `ROLLBACK_FAILED`, both raise sites), `PDFModel._restore_doc_after_failed_mutation` (the rollback form of `_restore_doc_from_snapshot`, used by `delete_pages`, `move_page`, `insert_pages_from_file`, `_restore_delete_transaction`) and the save-hook protected-page rollback failures in `ToolManager`. `save_as` is the one chokepoint (Ctrl+S, Save, save-on-close, `save_session_as`, a Save dialog pointed at the same file all pass it): `_refuse_save_over_damaged_session` raises `DamagedSessionSaveError` (plain zh-TW, nothing written) when the target is the session's `canonical_path` / `saved_path` / `original_path` or one of the files frozen at the latch (`damaged_protected_paths`, F14-DMG-1 entry below); a Save As to a NEW file works. The controller shows the message as written (`_save_failure_text`), and `_save_session_for_close` shows it before offering the Save dialog. `SessionTransferPayload.damaged` carries the latch across a tab detach. The ROLLBACK_FAILED sentence now says to close the tab (not saving), reopen the file, or use Save As for a new file.
**Rules:** (1) any code that rolls back a mutated document and can fail to must latch the session through `mark_session_damaged` (use `_restore_doc_after_failed_mutation` for a snapshot rollback), never only raise; a user-facing sentence is not a guard. (2) The latch is permanent for the session (undo does not clear it, and a Save As keeps it: the in-memory document is still the damaged one), so Ctrl+S after a Save As is refused too. (3) A damaged session that is otherwise clean is not "dirty": closing the tab does not prompt.
**Residual:** the latch is per session and in memory; a reopened file is a fresh session. A rollback failure inside the tiered engine's own undo/redo paths (`STALE_UNDO` is zero-mutation by design) is not a damage site. Undo/redo restores that raise are history failures (`user_message_for_history_failure`), not latched.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/pdf_text_edit.py`, `model/tools/manager.py`, `model/pdf_object_ops.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`, `controller/session_transfer.py`, `controller/text_edit_refusals.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_text_edit_refusal_messages.py` (`test_damaged_session_*`, `test_both_rollback_failed_raise_sites_latch_the_session_damaged`, `test_the_damage_travels_with_a_detached_tab`, `test_a_failed_structural_rollback_latches_the_session_damaged`), `test_scripts/test_text_commit_maintenance.py` (`test_a_failed_protected_page_rollback_latches_the_session_damaged`).

## A damaged session stopped protecting its original after one Save As: a second Save As (or an export / merge / optimize copy) back onto it overwrote the only good copy (F14-DMG-1)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`DocumentSession.damaged_protected_paths`, `mark_session_damaged`, `damaged_protected_paths`, `_refuse_write_over_damaged_original`, `_refuse_save_over_damaged_session`, `save_external_document`, `copy_lost_session_recovery`, `import_session_transfer`, `DAMAGED_SESSION_WRITE_MESSAGE`), `model/pdf_optimizer.py` (`OptimizeSourceSnapshot.damaged_protected_paths`, `capture_optimize_source`, `save_optimized_copy_from_snapshot`), `controller/session_transfer.py`
**Symptom:** (Round 14.) Open A.pdf, a failed edit latches the session damaged, Save As B.pdf (allowed, latch kept), then Save As and pick A.pdf: not refused, and the half-rewritten document replaced A.pdf, the file the latch exists to protect. An export / merge "save as new" / optimize copy pointed at A.pdf after the first Save As went through the same way, and so did a tab detached after the Save As.
**Cause:** the gate derived "the session's own file" from the CURRENT `saved_path` / `original_path` / `canonical_path`, and the tail of `save_as` rebinds all three to the new file (`_detach_live_doc_from_source_file` also moves the live handle to a private copy). After one Save As nothing named or read A.pdf any more, so neither the damaged gate nor the "open in another tab" checks refused it. Export, merge and optimize copy only refuse a path a live handle reads; the transfer payload's `source_path` is the new file.
**Fix:** `mark_session_damaged` freezes the files the session is bound to at the latch into `DocumentSession.damaged_protected_paths` (legacy: `_legacy_damaged_protected_paths`); `PDFModel.damaged_protected_paths(sid)` = that frozen set plus the current file (empty when undamaged) is the ONE source every gate reads. `_refuse_save_over_damaged_session` (Save As) and `_refuse_write_over_damaged_original` (`save_external_document` for export / merge of the active session, `copy_lost_session_recovery` of a damaged lost session) raise `DamagedSessionSaveError`; `capture_optimize_source` freezes the set into `OptimizeSourceSnapshot.damaged_protected_paths` on the GUI thread and `save_optimized_copy_from_snapshot` refuses before writing (the worker never reads live session state). `SessionTransferPayload.damaged_protected_paths` carries the set to a detached window. `clear_session_damaged` empties it. Non-Save-As writes use `DAMAGED_SESSION_WRITE_MESSAGE` (plain zh-TW, "pick a new name").
**Rules:** never derive a protection from fields a save rebinds: freeze it at the moment the protection starts. A new write route that writes a session's content to a user-chosen path must call `_refuse_write_over_damaged_original` (or carry the frozen set across a thread) before writing.
**Residual:** the protection only binds writes of the damaged session's own content. Another (clean) tab may still Save As over A.pdf once the damaged tab has left it (an ordinary overwrite of a file no tab has open), and a tab that reopened A.pdf saves it normally. Files the session was bound to BEFORE the latch (an earlier, clean Save As) are not protected.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/pdf_optimizer.py`, `controller/session_transfer.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_text_edit_refusal_messages.py` (`test_damaged_session_save_as_back_onto_the_original_after_a_save_as_is_refused`, `test_damaged_session_controller_save_as_back_onto_the_original_is_refused`, `test_damaged_session_export_and_merge_never_target_the_original_after_a_save_as`, `test_damaged_session_optimize_copy_never_targets_the_original_after_a_save_as`, `test_damaged_lost_session_recovery_copy_never_targets_the_original`, `test_damaged_session_keeps_the_original_protected_across_a_tab_detach`).

## The cross-page move told the user to reopen and not save after its own whole-document restore had already repaired the document (F13-MOVE-1a)
**Area:** `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`move_text_across_pages` except branch), `controller/text_edit_refusals.py` (`user_message_for_exception(document_restored=...)`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`clear_session_damaged`)
**Symptom:** (Round 13.) The move's source-deletion `edit_text` raised `ROLLBACK_FAILED` (rewrite failed, the model's page rollback failed), the controller restored the WHOLE document from its `before_snapshot` and that succeeded (page identical, no undo entry, not dirty), yet the dialog still said the page may be partly changed, do not save, reopen the original file. A user obeying it closed the tab without saving and lost every other unsaved edit of a healthy document. With the S13-DLG5-DAMAGED latch the model's flag would also have blocked in-place Save of that healthy document.
**Cause:** the except branch chose the message from the exception alone and ignored the outcome of its own restore; the model latch was set at the raise site, before the controller could repair the document. The inverse hole existed too: when the restore itself failed (any error), the dialog said "page restored" or a generic retry and nothing was latched.
**Fix:** the branch tracks `document_restored` (`None` no restore ran, `True` it succeeded, `False` it failed) and passes it to `user_message_for_exception`: `False` always shows the `ROLLBACK_FAILED` do-not-save sentence and latches the session (`mark_session_damaged`); `True` maps `ROLLBACK_FAILED` to the `EDIT_FAILED` "page restored" sentence and, if the session was not already damaged before the move, lifts the stale latch with `PDFModel.clear_session_damaged` (the one place it is cleared). Every other coded sentence is unchanged.
**Rules:** (1) a caller that restores the whole document itself judges trust by its OWN restore, not by the callee's inner rollback. (2) The latch may be cleared only right after a whole-document restore from a snapshot captured while the session was not damaged. (3) A failed restore latches the session whatever the original error was.
**File:** `controller/pdf_controller.py`, `controller/text_edit_refusals.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_text_edit_refusal_messages.py` (`test_a_move_*`, `test_user_message_follows_the_restore_outcome`).
**Pinned (F13-MOVE-1b):** the exact reproduced state -- source deletion done, destination `add_textbox` raised, whole-document restore raised -- leaves the source text deleted in memory with no undo entry and no dirty mark. That is intended: the do-not-save sentence plus the damaged latch (in-place Save / Ctrl+S / Save All / save-on-close refused, Save As to a new file allowed) are the guard, and the close prompt stays quiet because its Save could not be honoured. Tests `test_a_lost_source_with_a_failed_restore_*`. A RETRY of the same move in that state is a separate bug (positional `target_span_id` fast path of `_resolve_cross_page_move_source_span_id` ignores the text), not covered here.

## Legacy vertical rebuild sized the htmlbox from the BLOCK, so a table-row cell was rebuilt at the row's first cell (F13-VF-1)
**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_apply_redact_insert_body`: vertical `new_rect is None` branch and the `new_rect` clamped-to-nothing fallback)
**Symptom:** (Round 13.) `test_files/hvac-dwg.pdf` p5 (/Rotate 270, run rotation 90), consented rebuild of the cell `空調系統封面` -> `空調系統封面X` (tier0 refused `type0_unicode_unmapped`): SUCCESS, but the new text was drawn ~300 pt away along the row, over the untouched `TWX-AC-0-01` cell, and the edited cell was left empty; it persisted after save/reopen (479 px changed outside the edit bbox). Saved words: `(724, 424)` -> `(723, 134)` unrotated.
**Cause:** PyMuPDF builds one block from a whole quarter-turn table row (`Rect(722.67, 83.58, 731.26, 424.32)`); the edited run is its last 40 pt (`reopen_anchor_rect` `Rect(723.72, 383.82, 731.26, 424.32)`). The horizontal branch used `base_layout` (the run's reopen anchor) but the vertical no-rect branch passed `resolve_result.target.layout_rect` (the block) to `_vertical_html_rect`, and the htmlbox starts the text at that rect's top (bottom when reading up), i.e. at the row's first cell. The drag fallback ("new_rect clamped to nothing -> back in place") also substituted the block. `_verify_rebuild_edit` checks presence inside the shrunk rect, so it passed. ROT90-UP-1's fixture had one run per page (block == run) and could not see it. At HEAD 1f51010 the same misplacement drew a 1.56 pt stroke; the round-4 line-height fix made it full size.
**Fix:** the vertical no-rect branch passes `base_layout` (anchor, else block) to `_vertical_html_rect`; the clamp fallback uses the union of the edited member spans' bboxes (else the block). Rule: a rebuild's position comes from the edited run (its reopen anchor or member spans), never from `TextBlock.layout_rect`; a block can hold several cells' runs. Real repro after the fix: same edit lands at `(723, 434)` (start unchanged, one glyph longer), outside-bbox diff 61 px = the added `X`, reopen identical. Paragraph mode without `new_rect` still uses the block rect (no anchor); not changed here.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_geometry_page_rotation.py::test_legacy_rebuild_of_quarter_turn_run_in_a_multi_run_block_keeps_its_place[90|270 x no_rect|unmoved_rect|off_page_drag]` (red 4/6: `no_rect` and `off_page_drag` landed 199 pt from the run on both quarter turns; `unmoved_rect` is the control).

## The legacy rebuild redacted the overlap cluster's bounding box and erased untouched words outside the cluster (F13-VF-2)
**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_apply_redact_insert_body` redaction, `_push_down_overlapping_text` redaction; helpers `_page_glyphs`, `_glyphs_owned_by_runs`, `_redact_owned_glyphs`, `_glyph_redact_point`, `_owned_redaction_rects`, `_glyphs_still_present`)
**Symptom:** (Round 13.) Consented rebuild of `severe` -> `esvere` on `Awareness.pdf` p1: SUCCESS, but `So-called` (line above) became `So-call` and `health` (same line) became `ealth`, live and after save/reopen (779 px outside the edited box). `GeoTopo.pdf` p2 `einbauen` -> `ienbauen`: `direkt` -> `dire`, `mit` and `zu` gone, `dürfen!` -> `ürfen!` (861 px; the same at HEAD). The overflow push-down did the same to a glyph of another block inside a pushed block's box.
**Cause:** The overlap cluster is one hop (every run touching the TARGET's box), but the redaction rect was the cluster's bounding box (`redact_rect = cluster_union`). With a neighbour above-right of the target (a taller font reaching 0.7 pt into the target's line) that box is L-shaped-empty: it holds glyphs of runs that touch neither the target nor each other. MuPDF erases every glyph whose box touches a redaction, so those were erased, and nothing replayed or validated them (only cluster members are replayed / checked; the survivor check only looked for glyphs that were NOT erased). The push-down redacted each pushed block's box and re-inserted only that block's spans.
**Fix:** Both rewrites erase exactly the glyphs they own. `_page_glyphs` reads the page with the run index's own extraction (`content_textpage(page, 0)`, rawdict), so a run's box is the union of its glyphs' boxes; `_glyphs_owned_by_runs` gives the rebuild the glyphs of each cluster run (same block, inside the run's box +0.5 pt; any block if that finds no inked glyph), the push-down owns every glyph of the blocks it moves. `_redact_owned_glyphs` first removes line art fully covered by the runs'/blocks' own boxes (`text=PDF_REDACT_TEXT_NONE`, the old line-art behaviour minus the union's empty corners), then erases the text (`graphics=PDF_REDACT_LINE_ART_NONE`) through a 0.2 pt redaction at each owned glyph's `_glyph_redact_point` (on the advance midline, 0.15 em above the baseline along the line direction); `_owned_redaction_rects` joins consecutive owned glyphs of one axis-aligned line into one 0.2 pt strip, broken at any non-owned inked glyph of that line (one redaction per glyph cost ~3.5 ms: a 1300-glyph paragraph took 4.5 s, strips 0.03 s). Not the extracted box centre: MuPDF's redaction box is origin/advance x the FONT's ascender/descender, and for MSBM10 (ascender 0.464 em, descender 0) the extracted centre is above it, so the `R` survived. Afterwards an owned glyph still present refuses `REDACTION_LEFT_SOURCE` (as before, e.g. WMode 1), a non-owned glyph that is gone (drawn over an owned glyph's point, e.g. the LaTeX logo's `L` under its `A`) refuses the new `TextEditRefusal.UNTOUCHED_TEXT_WOULD_BE_LOST` (zh-TW sentence in `controller/text_edit_refusals.py`), page rolled back. Presence is "same character within 0.3 pt" (`_glyphs_still_present`): removing glyphs from a show re-emits the later ones one rounding step away (GeoTopo `s` 518.44 -> 518.46), and exact 0.1 pt keys refused 35 clean edits on GeoTopo p1-3. `redact_rect` (still the cluster's box) only bounds the annotation save/restore and the dirty region. The push-down raises `TextEditRefused`; the pre-push probe no longer swallows it, so `edit_text` rolls the page back. The old box helpers `_glyph_keys_in_rect` / `_redaction_left_source_glyphs` are gone.
**Rule:** a rewrite that erases content proves it erased only what it re-draws; a bounding box of several things is never a redaction rect. Line art: a decoration fully inside one cluster run's box is still removed, one spanning two runs (or only inside the union's corner) now stays.
**Corpus sweep (round 13, legacy engine, every run of 3 or more characters, one adjacent-letter swap each; collateral = a word lost that touches no cluster run):** box redaction before -> owned redaction after: `GeoTopo.pdf` p1-3 305 edits, collateral 12 -> 0, one refusal `untouched_text_would_be_lost` (the LaTeX logo: its `A` is drawn over the `L`, so erasing the edited `TEX` run's `A` erases the `L`); `Awareness.pdf` p1 666 edits, collateral 6 -> 0 (`text_does_not_fit` 15 before and after); `google-doc-document.pdf` 139, `test-complexed-layout.pdf` 371 and `hvac-dwg.pdf` p1-2 (every 10th run, 9) 0 -> 0, all SUCCESS. The exact-key version of the check (before `_glyphs_still_present`) refused 29 + 7 of the GeoTopo edits; the extracted-box-centre point (before `_glyph_redact_point`) left MSBM10 glyphs (`REDACTION_LEFT_SOURCE`).
**Same class, fixed in round 16 (F13-VF-2b):** moving, rotating or deleting an app textbox object redacted the textbox rect and erased page text under it; the textbox now empties its own htmlbox Form XObject instead (see the F13-VF-2b entry).
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`, `model/text_edit_refusal.py`, `controller/text_edit_refusals.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_overlap_textbox_edit.py` (`test_rebuild_keeps_untouched_words_inside_the_cluster_bounding_box`, `test_rebuild_refuses_when_the_redaction_would_erase_a_glyph_it_cannot_replay`, `test_push_down_keeps_a_glyph_of_another_block_inside_the_pushed_box`, `test_push_down_refuses_when_the_owned_redaction_reports_a_loss`, `test_owned_glyph_redaction_*`, `test_glyph_redaction_point_sits_above_the_baseline_inside_the_advance`, `test_a_glyph_re_emitted_one_rounding_step_away_still_counts_as_present`, `test_owned_glyphs_of_one_line_share_a_strip_that_stops_at_a_foreign_glyph`), `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py::test_redaction_survivor_check_sees_vertical_survivors_but_not_horizontal_erasure` (ported to the owned-glyph helpers).

## Protected-span replay and push-down redrew untouched neighbours shrunk and moved (F13-VF-3)
**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_replay_protected_spans`, `_replay_protected_span_as_html`, `_place_htmlbox_at_origin`, `_insert_htmlbox_unshrunk`, `_protected_span_drawn_in_place`, `_validate_protected_spans`, `_push_down_overlapping_text`)
**Symptom:** (Round 13.) Consented rebuild `Revit` -> `eRvit` on `test-colored-background.pdf` p1: the untouched `前置作業操作流程` went from 60 pt at baseline 320.7 to 43.03 pt at 313.8 (51,304 px changed outside the edited box; same at HEAD). `severe` -> `esvere` on `Awareness.pdf` p1: the untouched `‘Asian` went from 12.82 pt to 10.57 pt and moved 1.1 pt (779 px); HEAD refused that edit, the working tree (non-Latin-1 neighbours replayed as htmlbox since F10-UNI-1) committed it shrunk. Both persisted after save and reopen. Even a plain 11 pt `Price €5 При` neighbour came back at 9.55 pt.
**Cause:** A neighbour that cannot go through `insert_text` was replayed with `insert_htmlbox(box=its tight bbox, scale_low=0)`. `_build_insert_css` asks for a line box of `max(1.1 em, (ascender - descender) em)`, taller than the bbox of the original font, so MuPDF shrank the text until that line fit and re-anchored its baseline. `_validate_protected_spans` only read the text back, so the shrunk neighbour validated. The overflow push-down re-inserted each pushed block's spans into an estimated 1.55 em box with the default `scale_low=0` (30 pt CJK came back at 22.31 pt). The pdf-text-fidelity rule: an untouched neighbour keeps size and baseline, no shrinking to fit the old bbox.
**Fix:** `_place_htmlbox_at_origin` builds a box far longer and taller than the text (no wrap: `_NO_WRAP_CSS`), draws it once on a scratch page with the live page's size and `/Rotate`, reads where the first glyph lands (`get_texttrace`) and moves the box by the difference to the span's origin (htmlbox's layout is a translation of the box, so this is exact for any rotation). The live insert uses that box with `scale_low=1` (`_insert_htmlbox_unshrunk` raises instead of shrinking; the replay's existing fall-backs then run, and a missing span is refused by the validator). The push-down uses the same helper. `_validate_protected_spans` now also requires a glyph drawn at the neighbour's size (+-0.05 pt) on its origin (+-0.5 pt) (`_protected_span_drawn_in_place`), so a wrong replay is refused (`protected_span_changed`) instead of passing. The lossy-layer reference render and evidence rectangle use the same placement.
**Rule:** an untouched neighbour is replayed at its own size and origin; never hand htmlbox the tight bbox of text it did not author with a shrink allowance, and validate geometry as well as presence.
**Not fixed (T16-5):** the replayed font is still a substitute (Bold CJK -> Droid Sans Fallback Regular, Europa-Bold -> CharisSIL); with size and baseline restored the outside-box difference fell 51,304 -> 36,617 px (colored-background) and 779 -> 554 px (Awareness), the rest is the font face. The edited text's own strategies (`scale_low=0.5` fallback C) are the user's replacement and a disclosed degrade, unchanged. (Round 14, F14-VM-2: its font and size may degrade, but it is now placed on the original first-glyph origin, like the neighbours.) `pdf_object_ops` add-textbox `scale_low=0` fits a user-drawn box on purpose.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_f13vf3_*`: size/origin for CJK 60 pt, curly quote, Euro/Cyrillic, quarter and half turns, rotated pages; validator refusing wrong size/baseline/start; push-down).

## The rebuild re-drew the edited word wider at its old origin and overprinted the next run on the line (F13-VF-4)
**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_right_neighbour_limit`, `_apply_redact_insert_body` fast path, htmlbox rect and strategy B)
**Symptom:** (Round 13.) Consented rebuild of `SCORE` -> `CSORE` on `01_報告書.pdf` p3 (tier-0 `tj_multi_item_array`, then legacy): SUCCESS, live and after save/reopen, but the word grew from x 133.1-168.2 to 133.1-183.0 pt and was drawn over the untouched subscript `EE` (168.3-175.2) and touched the `=` of the next run. Identical at HEAD 1f51010. The probe's outside-the-mask pixel count was 0 because the located new-text rectangle swallowed the neighbour.
**Cause:** The fast `insert_text` path and the horizontal htmlbox rect measured the room available only to the page's right safe margin (`page.x1 - max(60, min(120, 2 * size))`), never to the next run on the line. The substitute font is often wider than the original, so the new word ran over runs that stay where they are. `_validate_protected_spans` checks that a neighbour's text is present, not that nothing is drawn over it.
**Fix:** `_right_neighbour_limit` returns the left edge of the nearest untouched run that shares the edited line band and starts at or past the edited extent's right edge. A non-dragged horizontal edit caps `fast_available_w` at that edge (slack 0.25 pt), so a word that no longer fits leaves the fast path; the htmlbox rect's right edge and strategy B's widening are capped there too, never narrower than the edited extent itself. The existing policy then applies, the same as at the page edge: wrap, else shrink down to 50 % (strategy C), else `TEXT_DOES_NOT_FIT` and a rollback. On the report page `CSORE` is now laid out in the htmlbox font at 13.3 pt, x 134.0-167.3, clear of `EE` at 168.3.
**Rule:** text that stays on its line is bounded by the next run on that line, not only by the page margin. A dragged `new_rect` is where the user put it and is not capped.
**Behaviour change:** runs are word-level, so replacing one word of a line by a much longer one (the next word is the neighbour) is now shrunk or refused instead of silently overprinting the following words; `test_multi_tab_plan.py::test_03_edit_in_a_undo_in_b_isolated` relied on that and now edits a one-word page. Reflowing the rest of the line is the product alternative (not done).
**Not fixed here:** vertical (quarter-turn) edits had the same shape downwards or upwards (their htmlbox grew to the page edge); fixed in round 16, see F13-VF-4b. The neighbour itself is still replayed in a substitute font (T16-5), which now shows as 60 changed pixels outside the edit mask on that page.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_rebuild_never_overprints_untouched_right_neighbour`, `test_rebuild_refuses_when_the_text_cannot_fit_before_the_neighbour`, guards `test_rebuild_keeps_the_fast_path_when_the_neighbour_is_far_enough`, `test_rebuild_ignores_runs_that_are_not_to_the_right_on_the_line`).
**Round 14 (F14-VF4-OVERLAP):** the wall skipped every run that started 0.25 pt or more INSIDE the edited extent (negative kerning or condensed spacing across a style change, a float32 bbox overlap), on the grounds that it is an overlap-cluster member that is replayed. Replay at its own origin does not keep a grown edit from being drawn over it, and with no run further right the limit was `None`: `ab` -> `abc` at gap -0.3 / -0.45 / -1.0 pt drew x 72-94.6 over `NEXT` at x 87.3 / 87.1 / 86.6 and reported SUCCESS (the guard exempts the replayed cluster, trusting this cap). Fix: a non-member run on the line that starts past the edit's own origin (`x0 > extent.x0 + 0.25`) and sticks out of the extent's right edge (`x1 > extent.x1 + 0.25`) is a wall at the extent's old right edge (the old text already reached that far), so the edit may not get wider than it was; it shrinks, wraps or is refused like any other neighbour. A run at or left of the origin, or wholly inside the extent, is still not a right-hand neighbour. Tests: `test_rebuild_never_overprints_a_neighbour_that_starts_inside_the_edited_extent[legacy|tiered]`, guard `test_rebuild_keeps_the_fast_path_for_a_narrower_edit_beside_an_inside_neighbour`.
**Round 14 (F14-VF4-WRAP):** the "wrap" step drew the wrapped lines over the next lines of the same paragraph. See the next entry.

---

## A growing edit wrapped (at the neighbour cap or the page margin) and the wrapped lines were drawn over the next lines of the same paragraph, reported SUCCESS (F14-VF4-WRAP)
**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_apply_redact_insert_body` horizontal htmlbox rect, pre-push probe, strategy A/B/C; `_push_down_can_move`, `_wrap_floor`, `_new_text_overprints`)
**Symptom:** (Round 14.) Synthetic: `ab` (Helvetica 14) + flush red run + the paragraph's next line 17 pt below; `ab` -> `ab cd ef` gave SUCCESS with `cd` / `ef` stacked at x 73-88 over `second line untouched`, live and after save/reopen. Corpus `google-doc-document.pdf` p1 run 29 `better` -> `better-than-ever` (ArialMT 11, TIER2_LEGACY): `than-` / `ever` drawn over `Readability counts.` and `Special cases...`. At HEAD 1f51010 the short edits stayed on one line (over the right-hand neighbour, F13-VF-4); a long edit at the page margin overprinted the next line there too.
**Cause:** Three parts. (1) The horizontal htmlbox rect ran from the edited line to the page foot, but `_push_down_overlapping_text` only moves BLOCKS that start below the edit (`bbox.y0 >= above_y - 1`). The next lines of the same paragraph are the same block, so nothing moved and the wrap was drawn over them. The F13-VF-4 cap made the box as narrow as the edited word, so short edits wrapped too. (2) The pre-push probe measured only strategy A. A text that does not fit at full size returns spare `-1`, which read as "fills the box to the page foot", so the push-down was asked to move the next block about 100 pt. It skips a block that would leave the page, and the shrunk text (strategy C) was then drawn over the block it left behind. (3) `_verify_rebuild_edit` checks presence and similarity only, not that the new text lies clear of untouched text.
**Fix:** (1) `_wrap_floor` finds the top of the nearest untouched span below the edited line, inside the box columns, in a block the push-down never moves. It reads the page after the redaction, so lines that are themselves rewritten (paragraph mode) do not count. The same rule is used in `_push_down_overlapping_text` through the shared `_push_down_can_move`, so the two cannot drift. The rect's bottom is that floor, but never less than one line (`line height + 2.5 pt`). When the box holds fewer than two lines, the markup gets `_NO_WRAP_CSS`, because MuPDF's shrink-to-fit would otherwise stack half-size lines inside the line band. (2) The probe runs the same A -> B -> C chain as the insert (`_strategy_b_rect` is shared). Nothing is pushed when even 50 % does not fit, since the insert then refuses. (3) Chokepoint guard: for every in-place horizontal rebuild (fast path and htmlbox), `_page_glyphs` is read just before and just after the insert. If an added glyph's ink core (middle 70 % of the advance, 0.1-0.6 em above the baseline) overlaps an untouched glyph's core, the page is rolled back and `TEXT_DOES_NOT_FIT` is refused. The overlap cluster's replayed neighbours (`protected_spans`: text the edited run was drawn on top of, overlap textbox edits) are exempt; horizontally the F13-VF-4 cap still bounds them.
**Rule:** the policy is still wrap, else shrink to 50 %, else refuse, but wrapped lines get room only where the push-down can clear it. They never go below the next untouched line of the edited paragraph.
**Behaviour change:** lengthening a word in the middle of a tight paragraph (flush right-hand neighbour, next line one line-height below) now shrinks the word on its line or refuses it. Corpus: `better-than-ever` is refused (`TEXT_DOES_NOT_FIT`, page rolled back), and `better` -> `much better` commits at 5.6 pt (51 %) on its line. When the edited run is the whole first line, the rest of the paragraph becomes its own block once the line is erased, so the push-down moves it straight down (this is the existing wrap path).
**Not fixed:** reflowing the rest of the line or paragraph (the owner alternative from F13-VF-4) is still not done. A wrap at the neighbour breaks a word at its hyphen when the room below is free (`multicolumn.pdf` `Two-Column` -> `Two-Colunm` gives `Two-` / `Colunm`, nothing overprinted); the owner allowed that (D-HYPHEN-WRAP). Dragged `new_rect` edits are not floored or guarded (TODOS F13-VF-4c); quarter-turn in-place edits are capped and guarded since round 16 (F13-VF-4b). A block pushed onto a same-paragraph line further down is not checked by the push-down itself.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_rebuild_wrap_at_the_neighbour_never_draws_over_the_same_block_line_below[legacy|tiered]`, `test_rebuild_wrap_at_the_page_margin_never_draws_over_the_same_block_line_below`, `test_rebuild_refuses_a_wrap_over_a_block_the_push_down_cannot_move`, `test_rebuild_wrap_still_pushes_a_separate_block_below`, guard `test_rebuild_wrap_of_a_whole_first_line_pushes_the_rest_of_the_paragraph`).

## The rebuild clamped text already in the page's right margin to the safe margin, narrower than the word itself (F14-DT-1)
**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_right_safe`, `_right_wall`, `_apply_redact_insert_body` fast-path width and horizontal htmlbox rect)
**Symptom:** (Round 14.) Synthetic kaiu.ttf title at x 480-540 on a 595 pt page: Tier 0 commits `機房配置圖` in place, `engine=legacy` re-wrapped it to `機房配置` / `圖`. Page number `12` at x 550 (10 pt): `12` -> `13` committed in Tier 0/1 but the legacy rebuild raised `TEXT_DOES_NOT_FIT`; `12` -> `123` (Tier 1 commits) was refused by both rebuilds. Corpus `ecc-dwg.pdf` p1 `平面配置圖` -> `平面配置圖二` (Tier 0/1 refuse, so the consented rebuild is the only route): a 6-glyph one-column stack, the untouched `廠商名稱` pushed down 25.2 pt and redrawn in Droid Sans Fallback; survives save/reopen. Pre-existing at HEAD.
**Cause:** The horizontal rect was `x0 .. min(x0 + max(width, right_safe - x0 - 15), right_safe)` with `right_safe = page.x1 - max(60, min(120, 2 * size))`, floored at the edited extent only when a right-hand neighbour existed (F13-VF-4). Text that already reaches past `right_safe` got a box narrower than itself (or inverted when it starts past it), so MuPDF wrapped it character by character. `fast_available_w` used the same margin, so even ASCII edits there left the origin-preserving fast path.
**Fix:** `_right_wall(page_rect, size, extent)` is the one wall for the fast path and the htmlbox. It is the safe margin when the edited runs' extent ends inside it (unchanged); otherwise the page edge less 10 pt for a single line (the bound a dragged box and strategy B already use), or at least the extent's own old right edge for a multi-line extent (paragraph). A wall that replaced the safe margin gets no extra 15 pt slack in `max_w`. The neighbour cap still applies on top of it.
**Rule:** a limit that is meant to keep text off a margin must never lie left of the text it limits.
**Not fixed:** a new text wider than the room that is left on the page still wraps (corpus `平面配置圖二`: `平面配置圖` / `二`, nothing pushed) instead of shrinking; a dragged box is still not capped but is overprint-guarded since S17-DRAG-GUARD (TODOS F13-VF-4c); quarter-turn edits are bounded by F13-VF-4b.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_rebuild_keeps_a_title_past_the_safe_margin_on_one_line`, `test_rebuild_does_not_refuse_a_page_number_that_starts_in_the_right_margin`, `test_right_wall_for_text_that_already_reaches_past_the_safe_margin`, guard `test_rebuild_still_keeps_the_safe_margin_for_a_line_that_ends_before_it`).

## The rebuild drew the edited text by its rect corner, not its first-glyph origin: every in-place edit was off by 1 pt and a baseline, and a drag never came back (F14-VM-2)
**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_apply_redact_insert_body` strategies A/B/C and the vertical insert, `_align_htmlbox_rect`, `_start_glyph_origin`, `_probe_htmlbox_chars`)
**Symptom:** (Round 14, merged with F14-MM-3.) `test-horizontal-texts.pdf` p1 `testrunning` -> `testrunnign` (Aptos 48 pt, consented rebuild, TIER2_LEGACY): the word's origin moved from (497.71, 220.49) to (498.71, 222.98), +1.0 pt x and +2.49 pt y, so it sat visibly below its untouched neighbour at 220.49; the same after save/reopen. The sweep showed +1.0 pt x on every htmlbox commit. A same-page drag (rebuild-only, `new_rect`) added +1.00 pt x and +0.48..+1.85 pt y per move for helv/tiro/Arial at 8..48 pt, and dragging by (dx, dy) and back left the run at (+2.0, +0.6..+3.7) pt: the text could never be returned to its place.
**Cause:** The edited text was handed to `insert_htmlbox` in a rect built from the replaced run's bbox (or the dragged `new_rect`). MuPDF starts the first glyph 1 pt inside the rect's left edge and puts the baseline at the line box's ascent of the substitute font, which is not the original font's ascent. F13-VF-3 placed untouched neighbours by their measured first glyph (`_place_htmlbox_at_origin`) but left the edited text on the rect corner ("the user's replacement, a disclosed degrade"); the consent text names font, letter spacing and neighbour layout, not a shift of the baseline, and a drag has no replacement text at all.
**Fix:** `_align_htmlbox_rect` draws the markup once on a scratch page of the live page's geometry (`_probe_htmlbox_chars`: size and `/Rotate` of the live page, same rect, same `rotate`, same `scale_low`), reads where the first glyph lands (`get_texttrace`) and moves the rect, keeping its size, by the difference to the target origin. `_apply_redact_insert_body` does this for every real insert of the edited text (strategy A, B and C, and the vertical insert with its scale_low=0 retry), through one closure, so fit, wrap and shrink decisions are those of the unmoved rect. Target origin = `_start_glyph_origin(member_spans, rotation, size)` (the run nearest the text start on the first line, for rotation 0 / 90 / 180 / 270; along the writing direction the extreme over all runs, so wrapped lines keep the block edge and are not indented by a first-line indent) plus the drag: `new_rect.tl - source_rect.tl` (the rect the drag started from, passed as `source_rect` from `edit_text`; zero in place, and zero when the page clamp emptied the dragged rect). The returned layout rect and the reopen anchor stay the nominal rect.
**Rule:** an edited run starts on its original text-start origin (the same geometric start on both sides, never the first DRAWN glyph; see F15-VM2-RTL) whatever font renders it; a drag is a pure translation of the run. Never position htmlbox text by the rect's corner.
**Not fixed / scope:** the cross-page move destination is a fresh `add_textbox` into the user's chosen rect (`pdf_object_ops`, `scale_low=0` on purpose) and is still placed by the rect. The returned `new_layout_rect` (the reopen anchor and block frame) is the nominal rect, so a block frame can differ from the glyphs' bbox by the 1 pt / ascent difference. Right-to-left text and a replacement that starts with a blank line were placed wrong by the first-DRAWN-glyph measure; fixed in round 15, see F15-VM2-RTL. The probe is skipped (the nominal rect is used) when it fails or the markup does not fit at that `scale_low`.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_f14vm2_in_place_htmlbox_edit_keeps_the_first_glyph_origin`, `test_f14vm2_a_drag_moves_the_text_by_exactly_the_drag_and_back`, `test_f14vm2_quarter_turn_and_rotated_page_edits_keep_the_first_glyph_origin`, `test_f14vm2_start_glyph_origin_follows_the_writing_direction`, `test_f14vm2_align_htmlbox_rect_keeps_the_box_when_there_is_nothing_to_align`).

## User-initiated saves staged a copy in the model temp dir, so a vanished or too deep temp dir blocked Ctrl+S while the target folder was fine (F13-ENV-1)

**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`private_temp_file`, `_atomic_full_save`, `_full_save_to_path`, `save_as`, `_detach_live_doc_from_source_file`, `_model_temp_file_of`), `model/pdf_optimizer.py`, `utils/path_staging.py`
**Symptom:** (Round 13.) Open a PDF, delete a page (secure latch), Ctrl+S: `FileNotFoundError: [WinError 3]` at `shutil.copy2(stage, recovery)`, shown as "儲存失敗" with no path, so it read as if the user's own folder were missing. A second Ctrl+S failed the same way (the block lasted the session); Save As to a new name worked; the target stayed byte-identical. HEAD did not fail: its secure route never touched the temp dir (the `recover_` copy came with FS-1). The plain full route (`save_*.pdf`, after a rebuild + undo leaves orphans) and the watermark route failed with MuPDF `FzErrorSystem: cannot open file '...	mpXXXX\save_....pdf'`; the `live_` copy of Save As to a new name failed silently (the handle stayed on the source file).
**Cause:** the copies were built as `Path(self.temp_dir.name) / f"<kind>_<uuid>.pdf"` at seven sites (plus the optimizer's `optimized_`). Two conditions broke them: (a) Disk Cleanup / Storage Sense removed the idle `%TEMP%	mpXXXX` mid-session (same premise as F12-H102-2); (b) a deep TEMP: `tmpXXXX\recover_<32hex>.pdf` is the temp dir + 45 characters, so with `LongPathsEnabled=0` (Windows default) it passes 259 from a temp dir of 215 characters (TEMP of about 203), and no extended-length form was applied, unlike the target-side staging sibling.
**Fix:** one chokepoint, `PDFModel.private_temp_file(stem)`, used by every site (and the optimizer through the model): it recreates the temp dir if it vanished (`TemporaryDirectory.cleanup` still removes it) and returns the path in extended-length form when it would not fit (`open`, `shutil`, `os` and MuPDF all accept it). `_model_temp_file_of` strips the prefix on both sides (`utils.path_staging.strip_extended_prefix`) because `Path.resolve()` keeps it only for the long path: without that a long `recover_`/`live_` copy was not recognised as the model's own and never retired or deleted. Names are now `<kind>_<32 hex>.pdf` (the `save_` name had a dashed uuid).
**Not fixed:** a temp dir that cannot be recreated at all (TEMP on a removed drive, a full volume) still ends in the save's own error; the helper logs a warning and lets the caller's write report it. A temp dir whose own path passes the directory limit (248) cannot be created by `tempfile` in the first place.
**Tests:** `test_scripts/test_secure_persistence.py` (`test_secure_ctrl_s_survives_a_missing_or_too_deep_model_temp_dir`, `test_plain_full_ctrl_s_*`, `test_watermark_ctrl_s_*`, `test_save_as_to_a_new_name_detaches_after_the_temp_dir_is_lost`, `test_private_temp_file_recreates_the_vanished_dir_and_uses_extended_form`), `test_scripts/test_pdf_optimize_workflow.py` (`test_save_optimized_copy_survives_a_vanished_model_temp_dir`), `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py` (`test_strip_extended_prefix_inverts_extended_length_path`).
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/pdf_optimizer.py`, `utils/path_staging.py`

## A textbox object move/rotate/delete on a /Rotate page redacted the VISUAL rect: the old copy stayed drawn and unrelated page text was erased (F14-MM-1)
**Area:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`_redact_and_restore_textbox_region`, used by `move_object`, `rotate_object` and `delete_object` for app textboxes)
**Symptom:** (Round 14.) Blank 595x842 page with `VICTIM` at unrotated (310, 320), `/Rotate 90/180/270`; `add_textbox` at visual (300, 300, 460, 330), then move it by (40, 60): the page shows two `Moving box` copies and `VICTIM` is gone, also after Save As and reopen. Delete left an orphan `Moving box` that can no longer be selected and also erased `VICTIM`. `/Rotate 0` was fine.
**Cause:** the textbox marker payload stores the VISUAL rect (the marker's `add_rect_annot` keeps those numbers and `annot.rect` echoes them, which is what the hit test compares against). The helper passed that rect straight to `page.add_redact_annot`, which PyMuPDF 1.27.1 reads in unrotated space (the earlier PITFALLS claim that it is rotation-safe was wrong). The htmlbox glyphs had been inserted at the derotated rect, so the redaction missed them and hit whatever sits at the visual numbers in unrotated space. The annotation/link snapshot (`_save_overlapping_annots`) had the same mix-up: it compares in unrotated space.
**Fix:** the helper maps the visual rect once with `model._visual_rect_to_unrotated_rect` (the helper `_insert_textbox_visual_content` uses for the insert, so redaction and insert agree) and passes that rect to both `_save_overlapping_annots` and `add_redact_annot`. One chokepoint covers move, rotate and delete. The marker's own `add_rect_annot(visual_rect)` is left alone: it is hidden, self-consistent with the hit test, and changing it would change saved files.
**Rule:** every PyMuPDF call that takes a page rect is unrotated-space, writes (`add_*_annot` including `add_redact_annot`, `insert_link`, `insert_image`, `insert_htmlbox`) and reads (`get_text(clip=)`) alike; derotate a displayed rect first. Test with content placed at the unrotated numbers of the displayed rect, and never only at `/Rotate 0`.
**Fixed later (round 16, F13-VF-2b):** the redaction was still geometric, so on every rotation it also erased page text visually under the textbox; the textbox now empties its own htmlbox Form XObject, and the redaction is only a guarded fallback. App image objects on a rotated page had the same space defect; fixed in round 16 (F14-MM-1b).
**File:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_object_manipulation_model.py` (`test_move_textbox_on_rotated_page_leaves_one_copy_and_keeps_unrelated_text`, `test_rotate_textbox_on_rotated_page_leaves_one_copy_and_keeps_unrelated_text`, `test_delete_textbox_on_rotated_page_leaves_no_orphan_and_keeps_unrelated_text`, guard `test_move_textbox_on_rotated_page_keeps_a_link_visually_under_it`)

## An app object's hit bbox was the marker's inflated /Rect: every move grew the box 2 pt and shifted its text (-1,-1) (F14-MM-2)
**Area:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`get_object_info_at_point`, `move_object`), `model/tools/annotation_tool.py` (`_restore_annot_entries`)
**Symptom:** (Round 14.) `add_textbox(1, Rect(100,200,260,230), ...)`, hit-test: bbox `(99,199,261,231)`. Move by (37.5, 61.25) and back leaves `(97,197,263,233)` and the first glyph 2 pt up-left (1438 px changed, also after save/reopen); three round trips grow the box to `(93,193,267,237)`. App rect and image objects grew once on their first move the same way.
**Cause:** `page.add_rect_annot(R)` takes the INNER rect and grows `/Rect` by an `/RD` inset (`[1 1 1 1]`, or border width / 2 when larger); `set_border(width=0)` does not undo it and every `update()` re-applies it (`set_rect(X)` + `update()` gives X inflated). `get_object_info_at_point` returned `annot.rect` as `bbox`, the view starts the drag from that bbox, so `move_object` got `inflated + delta`, re-inserted the text there and created a new, again inflated marker. Same mechanism when `_restore_annot_entries` re-created a Square/Circle from its saved (outer) `annot.rect`.
**Fix:** `_app_object_true_rect(annot, payload)` returns `payload["rect"]` (the rect the user placed; falls back to `annot.rect` only for a payload without a usable rect) and is the one source for the hit bbox and for the rect/image fallback reads. The hit test still uses the outer rect (1 pt pick tolerance). `AnnotationTool._pin_outer_rect` measures the inset a re-created Square/Circle got and shrinks the inner rect by it so the outer rect equals the saved one. Saved marker files are unchanged (the marker is still created with `add_rect_annot(visual_rect)`).
**Rule:** `annot.rect` of a Square/Circle is the OUTER rect (`inner + /RD`). Never use it as an object's geometry or feed it back into `add_*_annot`/`set_rect`; keep the true rect in the payload and read that.
