**File:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py`, `model/tools/annotation_tool.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_object_manipulation_model.py` (`test_textbox_hit_bbox_is_the_true_rect_and_move_round_trips`, `test_rect_object_hit_bbox_is_the_true_rect_and_repeated_moves_do_not_grow`, `test_image_object_hit_bbox_is_the_true_rect_and_repeated_moves_do_not_grow`, `test_recreated_square_or_circle_annot_keeps_its_saved_outer_rect`)

## The lost-session guard read the model's API unconditionally, so controller tests with a model double failed (GATE14-1)
**Area:** `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`_is_lost`, `_live_only`, `save_as`), controller tests that build a `SimpleNamespace` model
**Symptom:** (Round 15 gate.) `test_text_commit_small_defects.py::test_a_save_always_invalidates_the_open_editors_preview_session[*-save_as]` failed with `AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'session_lost'` at `_is_lost`, which `save_as` calls before the code under test. Production was unaffected (`PDFModel` defines it).
**Cause:** S14-SAVEREC-DEAD-TAB put `model.session_lost` / `model.is_session_lost(sid)` behind every guarded slot, save, close, detach and render. A controller test double that predates the API has neither, and the targeted verify runs did not include that module (only the full gate did).
**Fix:** `_is_lost` is the one read of the API and treats a model without it as live (`getattr` default `False`, still `is True` so a truthy double is not a lost tab). The silent default would hide a rename on the real model, so `test_pdf_model_exposes_every_lost_session_name_the_controller_reads_guard` pins the names on `PDFModel`.
**Rule:** a controller guard added in front of many slots reads the model through one tolerant chokepoint, and a test pins the real model's names. Run the full gate (not only the touched modules) after adding a model read to a shared controller path.
**File:** `controller/pdf_controller.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_save_recovery_error_message.py` (`test_is_lost_reads_a_model_without_the_lost_session_api_as_live_guard`, `test_pdf_model_exposes_every_lost_session_name_the_controller_reads_guard`)

## The edited-text and neighbour placement aligned the FIRST DRAWN glyph: a rebuilt Hebrew word moved left by its own width, and a leading blank line was cancelled (F15-VM2-RTL)

**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_align_htmlbox_rect`, `_place_htmlbox_at_origin`, `_probe_htmlbox_chars`, `_start_point`, `_drawn_text_start`, `_push_down_span_start`, `_push_down_overlapping_text`)
**Symptom:** (Round 15.) A consented rebuild of a Hebrew run (`'שלום'`, origins x 301.0..320.2) to one more letter drew the glyphs at 274.9..301.0, and to two words at 250.7..301.0. Both edits returned SUCCESS, and the text moved left by about its own width (27.0 pt and 51.2 pt). A rebuild of `ab` (baseline 300, helv 14) to `\nab` (the user pressed Enter before the text) drew `ab` at y 300.0, so the new line was cancelled. A protected Hebrew neighbour replayed through htmlbox also moved left by its width, onto the other word, and still passed `_protected_span_drawn_in_place`, because its rightmost glyph did sit on the run origin.
**Cause:** The target is geometric. `_start_glyph_origin` and an index run's `origin` give the text start along the writing direction (the leftmost origin at rotation 0). The probe side used `chars[0]`, the first glyph in `get_texttrace` DRAWING order. MuPDF draws right-to-left text rightmost glyph first. A markup that starts with `<br>` has no glyph on its first line, so `chars[0]` is on line 2. The push-down was right only by coincidence: its target is the `dict` span `origin`, which is also the first drawn glyph.
**Fix:** One measure for both sides. `_start_point(points, rotation, size)` is the start rule (first line = the across-extreme within 0.6 em; along = the extreme over all points). `_start_glyph_origin` applies it to run origins, and `_drawn_text_start` applies it to the probe's glyph origins. The writing direction comes from the texttrace span `dir` via `rotation_degrees_from_dir`, the same mapping the index uses. `_probe_htmlbox_chars` returns an `_HtmlboxProbe` (spare, scale, chars, rotation, size). `_align_htmlbox_rect` measures a markup with leading `<br>`s on the same markup without them, in the same box, so the blank first line takes the target and the text lands one htmlbox blank line (14.4 pt here, the body default line, not the css line-height) further on. If the two markups draw at different scales (a `scale_low < 1` shrink), the nominal box is kept. The push-down target is now each span's geometric start, taken from the `rawdict` of the same text page (`_push_down_span_start`).
**Rule:** A placement compares the same geometric point on both sides. Never use drawing order (`chars[0]`) as "the start of the text".
**Not fixed / scope:** RTL LETTER ORDER was a separate gap, fixed in round 16 (F15-RTL-ORDER). The growth direction of an RTL word was changed later by the owner decision D-RTL-GROW: it now keeps its RIGHT edge (`_start_point(rtl=True)`) and grows left; see that entry.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_f15vm2_rtl_rebuild_keeps_the_runs_right_edge_and_baseline`, renamed by D-RTL-GROW, `test_f15vm2_a_leading_blank_line_moves_the_text_down_instead_of_being_cancelled`, `test_f15vm2_align_htmlbox_rect_puts_the_first_line_start_on_the_origin`, `test_f15vm2_align_htmlbox_rect_puts_a_right_to_left_word_by_its_start`, `test_f15vm2_protected_rtl_neighbours_are_replayed_on_their_own_start`, guard `test_f15vm2_push_down_keeps_a_right_to_left_line_on_its_left_edge`)

---

## A diagonal watermark's bbox walled, floored and "overprinted" an edit on a line its ink never touches (F15-VF4OV-DIAGONAL)
**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_is_axis_aligned_dir`, `_right_neighbour_limit`, `_wrap_floor`, `_glyph_ink_core`, `_cores_overlap`, `_page_glyphs` / `_fill_glyph_advances`)
**Symptom:** (Round 15.) A stamped page with a 45-degree "DRAFT" watermark: editing `John` -> `Johnathan Smithers` was refused (`TEXT_DOES_NOT_FIT`, page rolled back) and `Johnny B` was drawn shrunk (CharisSIL 7.58 pt instead of Helvetica 12 pt). Under the round-13 rule both were SUCCESS at full size.
**Cause:** Three F13/F14 geometry rules read the axis-aligned extracted box of a turned run as that run's footprint. A diagonal run's bbox is a large square around a thin diagonal of ink, so (1) `_right_neighbour_limit` saw a "right-hand neighbour" whose bbox starts inside (F14-VF4-OVERLAP) or right of the edited word and shares its line band; (2) `_wrap_floor` took the top of such a bbox as the first untouched line below the edit; (3) the overprint guard's `_glyph_ink_core` projected the 89 pt bbox square of a 60 pt glyph onto its direction and boxed that again, a core that reaches lines the glyph never touches ("'g' over 'D'" rolled the page back).
**Fix:** `_is_axis_aligned_dir(direction)`: only text on a page axis (0/90/180/270 degrees, `max(|dx|, |dy|)` of the unit vector within 1e-3 of 1) has a bbox that is its footprint. `_right_neighbour_limit` and `_wrap_floor` skip runs written off the axes; a 90-degree run keeps its bbox and stays a wall. For off-axis glyphs `_page_glyphs` records the glyph's `advance` (distance to the next origin along the line, `_fill_glyph_advances`), `_glyph_ink_core` returns the glyph's own turned box (four corners) and `_cores_overlap` tests it against a rect with a separating-axis check. The axis-aligned path is unchanged. Real ink under the new word is still caught by the overprint guard, now on the glyph's real footprint.
**Rule:** never treat the bbox of a turned run or glyph as the space it occupies. Use its direction (axis test) and, for ink, its own turned box.
**Not changed (deliberate), since superseded:** the overlap cluster (`find_overlapping_runs`) still included a diagonal run whose bbox meets the edit: MuPDF's redaction removes glyphs by their turned-box bbox, so the run was protected and replayed. The product question whether a diagonal watermark's ink should count as a collision was settled by the owner afterwards: it does not (D-DIAG-INK, below). The owner later decided to protect a watermark under the old word's own box too: such a run is no cluster member any more and is never replayed (S17-WMARK-UNDER, below).
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_rebuild_ignores_a_diagonal_watermark_whose_bbox_covers_the_line`, `test_rebuild_keeps_the_wall_for_an_upright_vertical_run_on_the_line`, `test_wrap_floor_ignores_a_diagonal_run_below_the_line`, `test_ink_core_of_a_diagonal_glyph_is_its_own_turned_box_not_the_bbox_square`).

## The rebuild fast path, the protected-neighbour replay and the push-down drew a turned run in the wrong direction (F15-VM2-FAST180)

**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_classify_insert_path`, `_replay_rotate`, `_protected_span_rotate`, `_replay_protected_spans`, `_push_down_can_move`, `_push_down_overlapping_text`)
**Symptom:** (Round 15.) 'ab' drawn with `rotate=180` at (400, 400); a consented rebuild `ab` -> `abc` (legacy and tiered) returned SUCCESS with the new glyphs at x 407.78 / 415.57 (upright, +x), the word box 400.0..422.6 growing away from the old text. The htmlbox route (`ab€`) drew b at 392.89 and the euro sign at 385.12, correctly upside-down. Same class, found by the sweep: a protected neighbour written UP the page (`rotate=90` in `insert_text`, index rotation 270) was replayed reading DOWN, and the other way round; a pushed-down block written at 180 or 270 degrees was redrawn upright, and a 45-degree block came back horizontal.
**Cause:** (1) `_classify_insert_path` routed only rotation 90/270 to the htmlbox, so a 180 run with Latin-1 text took `page.insert_text(origin, rotate=0)`, which writes upright text along +x from the origin. (2) The protected replay handed `span.rotation` (the writing direction: 90 reads DOWN, 270 reads UP) to `insert_text` / `insert_htmlbox`, whose `rotate` turns the other way, so only 0 and 180 (their own inverse) were right; no test checked the direction, only size and origin. (3) The push-down replay had no `rotate` at all. The 'unrotated' assumption was written down as 'already exact' by the F14-VM-2 sweep, which looked at the origin and not at the direction.
**Fix:** `_classify_insert_path` returns `"htmlbox"` for every `rotation != 0` (the index only yields 0/90/180/270). `_replay_rotate(rotation)` = `(360 - rotation) % 360` is the one run-direction -> PyMuPDF `rotate` mapping (the same one `PDFModel._insert_rotate_for_htmlbox` gives the edited run); `_protected_span_rotate` and the push-down use it, for the htmlbox, the placement probe, the validation reference and the `insert_text` fallbacks. The push-down inserts spans along `line['dir']` in a box built around the span's pushed bbox, and `_push_down_can_move` leaves a block with a line written off the page axes where it is (it cannot be redrawn by a quarter-turn htmlbox; the wrap floor already ignores such a line).
**Rule:** whatever redraws a run must draw it along the run's direction; compare `get_texttrace` `dir`, not only origin and size. Never pass an index `rotation` to a PyMuPDF `rotate` without the mapping.
**Not fixed / scope:** the upside-down display on a `/Rotate 180` page was judged from content-space geometry (direction and glyph order), not rendered to pixels. A pushed block that is NOT moved (diagonal) can now sit under a grown edit; the overprint guard still checks the edit itself. The htmlbox box of a 180-degree rebuild was still the +x one (walls, wrap, push-down): F16-2.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_f15vm2_fast180_classifier_sends_every_turned_run_to_htmlbox`, `test_f15vm2_fast180_a_rebuilt_upside_down_run_stays_upside_down`, `test_f15vm2_fast180_a_replayed_neighbour_keeps_its_writing_direction`, `test_f15vm2_fast180_push_down_keeps_a_turned_block_turned`, `test_f15vm2_fast180_push_down_leaves_a_diagonal_block_where_it_is`).

## Closing the window with Discard all dropped a lost tab without saying where its recovery copy is (F15-DEADTAB-APPCLOSE)

**Area:** `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`handle_app_close`, `_show_lost_discard_notice`, `_lost_sessions_with_errors`, `_confirm_close_lost_session`)
**Symptom:** (Round 15.) After a failed save left a tab lost (S14-SAVEREC-DEAD-TAB, owner decision C), closing the single tab showed the recovery path again on Discard, but closing the WINDOW and choosing the Discard all button showed only the generic "N tabs are unsaved" prompt and closed: the recovery path was never shown. The lost tab was only counted among the unsaved ones. (The report also claimed the copy is deleted by the close; it is not: `handle_app_close` never calls `PDFModel.close()`, the temp dir and the copy go when the interpreter exits, which is the documented decision C.)
**Cause:** the Discard-all branch called `_accept_app_close` directly; only the single-tab path (`_confirm_close_lost_session`) had lost-tab handling. A lost tab that was somehow not dirty would not even have raised the prompt.
**Fix:** one helper, `_show_lost_discard_notice(lost)`, shows the "recovery copy kept until exit" notice for one or several lost tabs and is used by both discard paths. `handle_app_close` adds every lost session to the prompted set, names each lost tab's recovery path in the prompt (and says Save all copies it, Discard all keeps it until exit), and shows the notice before accepting the close on Discard all. Save all still goes through the lost-aware `_save_session_for_close`.
**Rule:** every code path that discards a lost tab must show its recovery path through `_show_lost_discard_notice`; do not call a close/accept for a discarded tab without it.
**File:** `controller/pdf_controller.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_save_recovery_error_message.py` (`test_window_close_discard_all_shows_the_lost_tabs_recovery_path`, `test_window_close_cancel_keeps_the_lost_tab_and_shows_no_discard_notice`, `test_window_close_discard_all_without_a_lost_tab_shows_no_recovery_notice_guard`)

## add_textbox and OCR clamped against raw `page.cropbox`, losing or shifting text on offset or `/UserUnit` pages (F15-G1)

**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`_unrotated_page_rect`, `apply_ocr_spans`), `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`_insert_textbox_visual_content`)
**Symptom:** (Round 15.) At `/Rotate 0`, add_textbox at visual (10,10,200,60) drew no ink on a page with MediaBox [0 0 600 800] and CropBox [30 40 500 700], and an OCR span at (10,10,120,30) became a 1x1 invisible word at (30,100); with MediaBox [50 70 650 870] both were drawn 40 pt right of the request; at `/UserUnit 2` (MediaBox 300x400, `page.rect` 600x800) a textbox in the bottom-right quarter drew nothing. Ordinary text edits on the same pages were fine.
**Cause:** `_unrotated_page_rect` returned `fitz.Rect(page.cropbox)`. PyMuPDF reports `cropbox` as `(cb.x0, mb.y1 - cb.y1, cb.x1, mb.y1 - cb.y0)` in raw PDF units: MediaBox-relative, y-flipped and without `/UserUnit` (measured (30,100,500,760), (50,0,650,800) and (0,0,300,400) where page space is (0,0,470,660), (0,0,600,800) and (0,0,600,800)). The rect clamped against it is page space (from `derotation_matrix`), so the clamp collapsed, shifted or cut it.
**Fix:** `_unrotated_page_rect` delegates to `geometry.unrotated_page_rect(page)` (`page.rect` through `derotation_matrix`), the bound the text-edit path already used; the raw cropbox/mediabox fallback is gone.
**Rule:** never use `page.cropbox` / `page.mediabox` as bounds for page-space geometry; they are raw PDF-unit boxes. Clamp unrotated geometry against `geometry.unrotated_page_rect`, displayed geometry against `page.rect`. Separate defects, not fixed here: PyMuPDF's `insert_text` ignores `/UserUnit` (fixed: F15-G6), `insert_textbox` / `draw_rect` still do (TODOS F15-G1-UU), and `insert_htmlbox` on `/Rotate` pages with an offset CropBox/MediaBox (round-15 finding F15-G4, fixed: see that entry).
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_add_textbox_atomic.py` (`test_add_textbox_ink_lands_at_requested_rect_on_offset_or_scaled_page_boxes`), `test_scripts/test_ocr_model_insert.py` (`test_apply_ocr_spans_word_lands_at_requested_bbox_on_offset_page_boxes`)

## Image bbox discovery and image cm writers flipped y against the MediaBox HEIGHT and ignored `/UserUnit` (F15-G2)

**Area:** `model/pdf_content_ops.py` (`discover_native_image_invocations`, `_bbox_from_stream_cm`, `fitz_rect_to_stream_cm`, `rotated_image_stream_cm`), `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`_rewrite_native_image_matrix`, `_rotate_native_image_absolute`)
**Symptom:** (Round 15.) An image drawn at (100,100,200,200) was discovered at (100,300,200,400) on MediaBox [-100 -200 500 600], at (100,30,200,130) on MediaBox [50 70 650 870] and at (50,50,100,100) on a `/UserUnit 2` page. A click on the image hit nothing, and a click on empty page 200 pt below it selected a phantom. App images (`add_image_object`) could not be moved or rotated (False). Delete returned True but took the orphaned-marker branch: the marker went, the image stayed drawn and nothing could select it again. A move wrote f = 600 where the true value is 400. The free-rotation move/resize also took the destination centre as raw user space, so a rotated image moved on a CropBox [30 40 500 700] page landed (-30,-100) off (the F15-G3 site).
**Cause:** the user-space to page-space map was rebuilt by hand as `y = mediabox.height - f - cropbox.y0` (and the reverse). The correct flip is against the clipped CropBox's y1 (`MediaBox.y1 - cropbox.y0`), so the result was off by `MediaBox.y0`, and `/UserUnit` was never applied. The free-rotation builder took `page_height = mediabox.height` and no CropBox/MediaBox origin at all. Plain pages and a CropBox inside a MediaBox at the origin hide the bug, because there `MediaBox.y0 = 0` and `/UserUnit = 1`.
**Fix:** one chokepoint, `pdf_content_ops.page_user_space_matrix(page)`, returns `PageVisualFrame.base` (the `/UserUnit` scale, the y flip and the clipped CropBox origin) as a float tuple. Discovery maps each cm through it; `fitz_rect_to_stream_cm` builds the placement in page space and maps it back through its inverse; the free-rotation move/resize maps the destination centre and the sizes back through it; the in-place rotate stays in user space (no page geometry needed), and `rotated_image_stream_cm` now takes a user-space centre. When the frame cannot be proven (non-quarter `/Rotate`, empty clipped CropBox, unusable `/UserUnit`) discovery reports MuPDF's own `get_image_rects` placement and the cm writers return None, so the move refuses instead of writing a guessed cm. The arithmetic uses `affine_concat` / `affine_invert` / `affine_point` in Python floats: `fitz.Matrix` products, inverses and `Point * Matrix` round through float32 (114.80241827 becomes 114.80242157), which would have changed every written cm. Old and new cm bytes are identical on plain, cropped and `/Rotate 90` pages with the box at the origin (36,000 random rects measured).
**Rule:** never rebuild the user-space to page-space map from `page.mediabox.height` / `page.cropbox`, and never use `page.transformation_matrix` for it (it drops the CropBox origin and `/UserUnit` on a `/Rotate` page). Use `page_user_space_matrix` (or `transforms.page_visual_frame`) and compose in Python floats. The oracle in tests is `page.get_image_rects`, never a literal rect.
**File:** `model/pdf_content_ops.py`, `model/pdf_object_ops.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_native_pdf_images_model.py` (`test_native_image_discovery_and_hit_match_mupdf_on_offset_box_pages`, `test_native_image_move_and_resize_land_where_requested_on_offset_box_pages`, `test_native_image_on_unprovable_page_frame_reports_mupdf_rect_and_refuses_cm_writes`), `test_scripts/test_image_objects_model.py` (`test_app_image_move_rotate_delete_on_offset_box_pages`), `test_scripts/test_object_free_rotation.py` (`test_free_rotated_image_move_and_resize_on_offset_box_pages`), `test_scripts/test_pdf_content_ops_cm_format.py`

## PyMuPDF page writers (`insert_htmlbox`, Shape, `insert_image`) displaced everything by the dropped CropBox/MediaBox origin on `/Rotate` pages (F15-G4)

**Area:** `model/font_stream_compaction.py` (`insert_htmlbox_tracked`), `model/text_commit/transforms.py` (`pymupdf_writer_shift`, `shift_rect_for_pymupdf_writers`); callers `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`_insert_textbox_visual_content`: add_textbox, textbox move/rotate, the controller's cross-page move) and the legacy rebuild / push-down / protected-neighbour replay in `model/pdf_text_edit.py`
**Symptom:** (Round 15.) A textbox added at visual (200,150,360,200) inked at (202,156) on a plain `/Rotate 90` page but at (162,126) with CropBox [30 40 500 700], (232,116) at `/Rotate 180`, (242,186) at `/Rotate 270`, and (402,256) on MediaBox [-100 -200 500 600] at `/Rotate 90` (200 pt right of its box). The redaction runs in true page space, so moving such a textbox left the old copy drawn: two `MMMM` words. A legacy text rebuild on the same pages drew the replacement 30-41 pt off the run it replaced (or was rolled back by its own verification: "requested characters are not on the page after the insert"). Rotation 0 and plain rotated pages were fine.
**Cause:** these writers convert page space to PDF user space with `~page.transformation_matrix`. Once `/Rotate != 0` PyMuPDF collapses that matrix to `(1, 0, 0, -1, 0, H)` and drops the CropBox/MediaBox origin (and `/UserUnit`), while every rect the model builds is in TRUE unrotated page space (`PageVisualFrame.base`: the origin included). The ink is displaced by `base.e/f - tm.e/f`. `insert_text` / `insert_textbox` do not use that matrix and are not displaced.
**Fix:** `transforms.pymupdf_writer_shift(page)` returns the `(dx, dy)` that cancels it (`tm.e - base.e`, `tm.f - base.f`; zero at `/Rotate 0`, for an unprovable frame and for `/UserUnit != 1`, where the correction is also a scale: superseded by `pymupdf_writer_matrix` in F15-G1-UU-ROT, `pymupdf_writer_shift` is now its translation-only view). `insert_htmlbox_tracked`, the model's one `insert_htmlbox` chokepoint, applies it to the rect (`shift_rect_for_pymupdf_writers`), so every htmlbox site is fixed once and the callers keep speaking true page space (their measure probes run on unrotated scratch pages, where the shift is zero).
**Rule:** a rect handed to a PyMuPDF page writer that goes through `transformation_matrix` (`insert_htmlbox`, `Shape`/`draw_*`, `insert_image`) must pass `shift_rect_for_pymupdf_writers` first; never hand-build the compensation, and never assert placement from `rotation_matrix` arithmetic (use pixmap ink / `get_text("words")`). `add_image_object` (`insert_image`) now derotates, then shifts (round 16, F14-MM-1b / F15-G4-IMG). The `/UserUnit != 1` rotated-page half is fixed (see the F15-G1-UU-ROT entry).
**File:** `model/text_commit/transforms.py`, `model/font_stream_compaction.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_add_textbox_atomic.py` (`test_add_textbox_ink_lands_at_requested_rect_on_rotated_offset_page_boxes`, `test_moving_a_textbox_on_a_rotated_offset_page_leaves_no_old_copy`), `test_scripts/test_font_stream_compaction.py` (`test_insert_htmlbox_tracked_draws_inside_the_box_on_a_rotated_offset_page`), `test_scripts/test_text_commit_visual_frame.py` (`test_pymupdf_writer_shift_*`), `test_scripts/test_text_geometry_page_rotation.py` (`test_legacy_edit_keeps_place_on_a_rotated_page_with_an_offset_cropbox`)

## Watermarks on `/Rotate` pages were off-centre and turned with the page (F15-G5)

**Area:** `model/tools/watermark_rendering.py` (`apply_watermarks_to_page`); callers `WatermarkTool.apply_page_overlay` (live view, thumbnails), `prepare_doc_for_save` -> `apply_watermarks_to_document` (saved file) and the print helper (`src/printing/helper_main.py`, same `apply_watermarks_to_document`)
**Symptom:** (Round 15.) On a 600x800 `/Rotate 90` page (800x600 on screen) an angle-0 watermark was drawn vertical and centred at (533,400) instead of (400,300); an offset CropBox gave the same; `offset_x=+100` moved it 100 pt DOWN, not right as the dialog tooltip says. A document mixing portrait and `/Rotate` landscape pages got different orientations and positions.
**Cause:** `page.insert_text` takes coordinates in, and draws its glyphs in, the UNROTATED page frame (MEASURED at 0/90/180/270 on plain, CropBox and negative-MediaBox pages). The centre came from `page.rect` (the DISPLAYED box) and neither the centre, the offsets nor the glyph angle were mapped through `/Rotate`.
**Fix:** the displayed-frame centre (offsets included, right/down) goes through `model.geometry.visual_to_unrotated_point`, and the morph angle is `angle + page.rotation` (the unrotated frame is turned clockwise by `/Rotate` on screen, so the glyphs are counter-turned). Placement is otherwise the long-standing upright geometry, so a `/Rotate` page now looks exactly like the same watermark on an upright page of the displayed size, and upright pages are pixel-identical to before. Checked with a pixmap ink oracle; `derotation_matrix` was measured to be right for plain, CropBox, negative- and positive-MediaBox pages at all four rotations.
**Rule:** anything drawn with `insert_text` takes UNROTATED-frame coordinates and its glyphs follow that frame: map displayed-space points with `model.geometry.visual_to_unrotated_point` and add `page.rotation` to a counter-clockwise on-screen angle. With `morph=(pivot, mat)` the origin is rotated about the pivot too. Assert placement from rendered ink, not from `rotation_matrix` arithmetic. The upright geometry defect found while measuring (origin turned twice, block half a line high) is fixed, owner decision: see the F15-G5-GEOM entry below. Also open: a CropBox larger than the MediaBox (the unclipped origin displaces `insert_text` at every rotation), `/UserUnit != 1` (TODOS F15-G1-UU), and a non-quarter-turn `/Rotate` literal.
**File:** `model/tools/watermark_rendering.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_watermark_rotated_pages.py`

## Watermark origin was turned twice and the block hung half a line high: ink off-centre at every angle but 0 (F15-G5-GEOM)

**Area:** `model/tools/watermark_rendering.py` (`apply_watermarks_to_page`); every caller (live overlay, thumbnails, `prepare_doc_for_save` save clone, print helper)
**Symptom:** (Round 15, measured; fixed round 16.) The dialog-default 45 degree watermark landed about 80 pt from the page centre, a 90 degree one about a quarter page away, and even an angle-0 "WMARK" was centred about 31 pt high (the block hung from its centre instead of straddling it).
**Cause:** each line's origin was pre-rotated by `angle` about the centre (`dx*cos - dy*sin`) and then handed to `insert_text(morph=(centre, mat))`, whose morph rotates the origin about the pivot AGAIN, so the origin was turned by twice the angle; the lines were also stacked from `-total_height/2 + i*line_height`, i.e. line 0's baseline-less top edge sat on the block centre line rather than the block being centred. Both hid behind the unit tests, which compared a rotated page with an upright twin (the same wrong geometry on both).
**Fix:** the origin is laid out UNROTATED, `centre + (-line_width/2, -total_height/2 + (i + 0.5) * line_height + 0.35 * font_size)`, and the morph alone turns origin and glyphs (`-(angle + page.rotation)`). F15-G5 (rotated pages) and F15-G6 (`/UserUnit`, `insert_text_page_space`) are untouched. Checked with the ink oracle in `test_watermark_rotated_pages.py`: the bounding-box centre of the rendered ink equals the DISPLAYED page centre plus the offsets within 2 pt for angles 0, 45 and 90, single and multi-line text, `/Rotate` 0/90/180/270; the live overlay (`WatermarkTool.apply_page_overlay`), the save clone and the print helper (`_build_snapshot_bytes`) render identical ink.
**Owner-accepted effect (no migration):** a file saved by an older build (any build before F17-COH-2 marked its baked ink) carries the ink baked at the OLD wrong place AND the stored parameters, which a newer build restores as a live overlay at the NEW right place, so such a file shows two copies of the watermark on reopen (measured before the fix: ink area ratio 1.9-2.0). The owner chose to fix the geometry and accept the doubled look instead of versioning the embedded JSON or dropping the overlay of files that already carry baked ink. The user can delete the watermark in the dialog and re-add it; the old baked copy is page content and stays.
**Rule:** when a morph / matrix is applied about a pivot, lay the content out in the unrotated frame and let the transform turn it once; never also pre-turn the coordinates. Assert watermark placement from rendered ink against `page.rect`'s centre, not by comparing two renders of the same renderer. Test texts for a turned line must have square-cornered glyphs (`HEHEH`): round / pointed corners (W, A, K) skew an ink bounding box by 3-4 pt at 45 degrees. Still open (TODOS F15-G5-GEOM): a CropBox larger than the MediaBox displaces `insert_text` at every rotation.
**File:** `model/tools/watermark_rendering.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_watermark_rotated_pages.py` (`test_ink_is_centred_on_the_displayed_page_centre_at_every_angle`, `test_ink_centre_follows_the_requested_offsets_at_every_angle`, `test_dialog_default_angle_45_no_longer_lands_far_from_the_centre`, `test_a_multi_line_block_is_centred_not_hanging_from_its_centre`, `test_overlay_save_and_print_paths_agree_on_the_corrected_geometry`)

## Annotation snapshot and move used `transformation_matrix` / `Annot.rect`: a link under a redaction was missed and a moved annotation shifted 2x on rotated offset-box or `/UserUnit` pages (F15-G2-ANNOT)

**Area:** `model/tools/annotation_tool.py` (`_save_overlapping_links`, `_save_overlapping_annots`, `_translate_annot`); callers `_redact_and_restore_textbox_region`, the legacy rebuild, the push-down in `model/pdf_text_edit.py`
**Symptom:** (Round 16.) On a `/Rotate 90/180/270` page with CropBox `[30 40 500 700]` in MediaBox `[0 0 600 800]`, a link under a 4 pt redaction at its real corner was not saved (`[]`), so `apply_redactions` dropped it and it never came back; the saved rect was displaced by the dropped CropBox origin (30, -40). On `/Rotate 90/270` + `/UserUnit 2` a pushed-down annotation moved by exactly twice the requested vector (rendered ink shift (-20, 40) instead of (-10, 20)), and `Annot.rect` read back with y = -512 for a rect at y 150, so a Square under the redaction was not seen at all; `Annot.vertices` of a highlight had the same y = -510. Unrotated pages and rotated `/UserUnit 1` pages with no box offset were correct, which hid it.
**Cause:** `page.transformation_matrix` collapses to `(1, 0, 0, -1, 0, H)` once `/Rotate != 0` (drops the CropBox/MediaBox origin and `/UserUnit`), and `Annot.rect` is derived from a matrix that drops `/UserUnit` on a rotated page, while the redaction rects and the move vector are in TRUE unrotated page space (`PageVisualFrame.base`). Measured end to end: a redaction at the link's `raw /Rect * base` corner removes the link, one at the `raw * transformation_matrix` corner does not.
**Fix:** `AnnotationTool._user_to_page_matrix(page)` returns `pdf_content_ops.page_user_space_matrix` (the F15-G2 chokepoint), falling back to `page.transformation_matrix` only when the frame cannot be proven. The raw `/Rect` of a link and of every snapshot entry (`_annot_page_rect`, `Annot.rect` only when `/Rect` is unreadable; a text markup's points from its raw `/QuadPoints`, `_annot_page_vertices`) is mapped through it, and `_translate_annot` maps `(dx, dy)` through its inverse; all in Python floats (`affine_*`). Rotation 0 and unrotated-equivalent pages produce the same numbers as before.
**Rule:** raw annotation geometry (`/Rect`, `/QuadPoints`, move vectors) is converted with `page_user_space_matrix`, never `page.transformation_matrix`, `Annot.rect` or `get_links()["from"]` on a page that may be rotated. Oracles in tests: a real `apply_redactions` (removed means overlapped), rendered red ink, `page_visual_frame(page)`. The `add_*_annot` / `Annot.rect` consumers on a rotated `/UserUnit != 1` page are fixed in F15-G1-UU-ANNOT; `model.geometry` itself in F15-G1-UU-ROT.
**File:** `model/tools/annotation_tool.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_link_under_a_redaction_is_saved_on_rotated_offset_pages`, `test_a_square_under_a_redaction_is_saved_with_its_page_space_rect`, `test_a_highlight_under_a_redaction_is_saved_with_page_space_vertices`, `test_translate_annot_moves_the_rendered_ink_by_the_requested_page_vector`, `test_annotation_geometry_falls_back_when_the_page_frame_cannot_be_proven`)

## PyMuPDF `insert_text` takes UNSCALED user units: watermark and OCR text were drawn at 2x on a `/UserUnit 2` page (F15-G6)

**Area:** `model/text_commit/transforms.py` (`insert_text_page_space`, `shape_writer_scale`); callers `model/tools/watermark_rendering.py` (`apply_watermarks_to_page`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`apply_ocr_spans`, `_insert_tiny_plain_text`), `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (three fallbacks)
**Symptom:** (Round 15.) On a MediaBox `[0 0 300 400]` + `/UserUnit 2` page (`page.rect` 600x800) a 48 pt "WMARK" watermark centred at (300,400) was drawn at 96 pt around (600,800): ink (418,702)-(600,772), clipped at the right edge, `get_text` saw only `WMA`. An OCR word requested at (10,10,120,30) landed at (20,27,214,63). The watermark reaches the saved file, the live overlay and the print helper; OCR text is written into the document.
**Cause:** `Page.insert_text` (and `insert_textbox`, `draw_*`) convert the point to PDF user space without the `/UserUnit` scale and size glyphs in user units, while `page.rect`, `get_text` geometry and every model coordinate are multiplied by `/UserUnit` (MEASURED 1.27.1: `insert_text((100, 300), fontsize=12)` draws its baseline at (200, 600) with 24 pt glyphs on a `/UserUnit 2` page, and at (50, 144) with 6 pt glyphs on a `/UserUnit 0.5` page, at every `/Rotate` and with a CropBox or an offset MediaBox). `insert_htmlbox` is not affected. Every unit test used unit-scale pages, where the factor is invisible.
**Fix:** one chokepoint, `transforms.insert_text_page_space(page, point, text, *, fontsize, morph=None, **kw)`: it multiplies the point, the font size and the morph pivot by `shape_writer_scale(page)` (`1 / UserUnit`, exactly 1.0 for a unit page or a `/UserUnit` that is absent, non-numeric, zero or negative) and passes everything else through. All six former `insert_text` sites call it, and an AST test fails on any other `.insert_text(` / `.insert_textbox(` under `model/ controller/ view/ utils/ src/`.
**Rule:** never call `page.insert_text` / `insert_textbox` directly; hand the model's page-space point and font size to `insert_text_page_space`. Assert placement from `get_text` words/spans or rendered ink against a unit-scale twin of the same base-space size, not from matrix arithmetic. Not fixed here: on a ROTATED `/UserUnit` page the displayed-to-unrotated conversion (`geometry.visual_to_unrotated_point`, `page.derotation_matrix`) drops `/UserUnit`, so a watermark/OCR bbox there is still mis-mapped (TODOS `model/geometry.py` item; strict-xfail test); a file saved by an older build keeps its wrong-place watermark ink baked in, so it shows two copies on reopen.
**File:** `model/text_commit/transforms.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_watermark_rotated_pages.py`, `test_scripts/test_ocr_model_insert.py`, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_visual_frame.py`

## An object selection outlived page delete / insert / reorder / rotate, tab switch and undo: Delete removed an image on ANOTHER page (F15-1)

**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`initialize_continuous_placeholders`, `reset_document_view`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`_drop_object_selection`, `undo`, `redo`, `add_image_object`), `view/object_selection.py` (`_delete_selected_object`)
**Symptom:** (Round 15.) 4-page document, images RED on p2, BLUE on p3, GREEN on p4. In objects mode select BLUE, delete p1 from the thumbnail menu, press Delete: GREEN (old p4, now p3) was removed, BLUE stayed, a `delete_object` undo entry was recorded and nothing was reported. An app rect (UUID id) selected on p3 became a silent no-op Delete after the same page delete. Same-page variant: delete image A, select B (now occurrence 0), undo: A is occurrence 0 again and Delete removed A. Move variant (F15-5, same cause): drag a rect/image object, Ctrl+Z (or Ctrl+Y): the frame and its 8 handles stayed at the other position and a BR-handle drag started from the stale selection rect and relocated the object there as a `resize_object` step.
**Cause:** the selection DTO names its object by page number, and a native image by its positional id `native_image:<page>:<occurrence>`; `_find_native_image_invocation` resolves that against whatever page now has the number. The View cleared the selection only on a mode switch and after `add_image_object`. Every scene rebuild (`scene.clear()`) already destroyed the selection overlay and cleared the text selection, but kept the logical object selection: invisible, and live for Delete/move/resize/rotate.
**Fix:** both scene-clear sites (`initialize_continuous_placeholders`, reached by every structural op, structural undo/redo, tab open/switch/close/detach, watermark, merge and zoom; and `reset_document_view`) call `_clear_object_selection()` next to `_clear_text_selection()`. A non-structural undo/redo rebuilds nothing, so `PDFController.undo`/`redo` call `_drop_object_selection()` after a successful step (the one helper `add_image_object` also uses). A refused undo/redo mutates nothing and keeps the selection. A zoom now also drops the selection (its overlay was already gone after the rebuild).
**Rule:** an object reference held by the View (`ObjectHitInfo`, positional native-image id, page number) is valid only for the document state it was read from. Any path that changes page numbering, page geometry, the active document or restores a snapshot must drop it; do not resolve a held id "again" by page number, because a positional id resolves to the wrong object, not to none. The floating note popup keys its edits by annotation xref (stable with garbage=0 snapshots), so it is not in this class; only its `page_idx` history metadata can go stale.
**File:** `view/pdf_view.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_object_manipulation_gui.py` (`test_page_delete_drops_object_selection_so_delete_cannot_hit_shifted_image`, `test_scene_rebuild_drops_object_selection_and_delete_is_a_no_op[...]`, `test_structural_undo_drops_object_selection`, `test_same_page_undo_drops_object_selection_of_renumbered_native_image`, `test_app_object_selection_dropped_after_page_delete`, and for F15-5 the real-mouse `test_history_step_of_object_move_drops_frame_and_handles_so_handle_drag_cannot_relocate[...]`)

## Rotate / Move Object on an edited textbox put the OLD words back (F15-2)
**Area:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`sync_textbox_markers_after_text_edit`, `_textbox_payload_drawn_on_page`, `move_object` / `rotate_object` textbox branch), `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`edit_text` -> `_sync_textbox_objects`, both success exits)
**Symptom:** (Round 15.) `add_textbox` "Hello", edit its words to "Goodbye" in edit_text mode (consented rebuild, or the legacy engine): the page reads "Goodbye". Rotate Object (or Move / resize) and the page reads "Hello" again; "Goodbye" is gone. Save As + reopen keeps the stale marker, so the revert also happens in a later session.
**Cause:** the hidden `pdf_editor_textbox_object` marker payload was written once at `add_textbox` and never again by a text edit. Move / rotate erase the box rect and re-insert `payload["text"]` / font / size / colour, so they wrote the original words back. The marker is a cache of what the page draws, and nothing kept it in step.
**Fix:** every successful `edit_text` (Tier 0 and the legacy rebuild) syncs the markers whose rect holds an edited member run: the members' old text is replaced by the new text in the stored text, matched ignoring whitespace (the index joins wrapped lines differently): exactly once -> replaced, absent -> the box is left alone (page text under the box was edited), more than once -> flagged; a whole-box legacy edit also stores the insert's font/size/colour; an edit that empties the box, or a drag that lands outside it, removes the marker; the ambiguous case flags the payload `content_unsynced`; the box rect grows over the new words the edit drew outside it (page words before vs after the commit, only words of the new text), so a longer text stays inside the object. Move / rotate first check that every stored character (NFKC, letters/digits/punctuation/symbols) is among the words centred in the box (for text whose htmlbox text layer is lossy, every character of that layer: F16-1) and refuse (`False`, nothing touched) otherwise, which also covers markers saved by older builds or changed by another tool. Every page-words read of this path (the pre-commit snapshot, the grow-box diff and the drawn-text check) goes through `model.page_content_text.content_text(page, "words")` (F11-ANN-4 guard): a visible FreeText comment in the box that spells the stale marker text is annotation appearance, not page content, and must not count as the page drawing it (GATE15-2).
**Rule:** an app-object marker that a verb re-creates content from is a cache of the page: every writer that changes what the object draws must update it, and the verb must verify it against the page before it erases and re-inserts. Never re-insert from a payload you have not checked.
**Not fixed:** a partial restyle (one line of a multi-line box) cannot be stored in the one-style payload, so a later move/rotate redraws the whole box in the stored style. A grown box (its words partly loose page glyphs, not one XObject) that covers page text between the old rect and the new words now makes move/rotate/delete refuse instead of erasing that text (round 16, F13-VF-2b).
**File:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py`, `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_object_manipulation_model.py` (`test_textbox_object_op_after_text_edit_keeps_the_edited_text`, `test_textbox_partial_line_edit_syncs_marker_and_survives_save_reopen_rotate`, `test_textbox_edit_to_empty_removes_the_object_marker`, `test_textbox_with_stale_marker_text_refuses_move_and_rotate`, `test_annotation_appearance_text_does_not_prove_the_marker_text_is_drawn`, `test_textbox_text_dragged_out_of_the_box_leaves_no_marker_behind`, `test_textbox_marker_text_replacement_ignores_whitespace_and_refuses_to_guess`, `test_textbox_marker_occurrence_count_ignores_whitespace`, `test_textbox_marker_the_sync_cannot_place_is_flagged_and_refuses_rotate`, `test_textbox_grown_by_a_longer_edit_still_rotates_with_the_new_text`)

## An app image's marker kept the REQUESTED rect: after any free rotation, a letterboxed insert or a near-45-degree resize, Move/Rotate returned False and Delete removed only the marker (F15-4)

**Area:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`add_image_object`, `move_object` / `rotate_object` image branches, `_sync_image_marker_to_drawn`)
**Symptom:** (Round 15.) Add a 150x100 app image, rotate it to 30 degrees with the rotate handle (or to 90 with the context menu "Rotate Object"): the image turns, but afterwards Move and Resize return False (nothing moves; a multi-select batch move still records an undo entry and the frame is rebased), rotating back to 0 returns False, and Delete returns True and records an undo entry while the image stays drawn and the hit test now reports it as `native_image:1:0`. The same happens with no rotation at all when the inserted picture is not 4:3: the UI inserts into a fixed 4:3 default rect and `insert_image` letterboxes the image inside it.
**Cause:** every later verb finds the image through the marker: `_find_app_image_invocation` accepts only a drawn placement within 2 pt of the marker rect and 1 degree of its rotation. Four writers stored the request instead of the drawing: `add_image_object` stored the requested rect (the letterboxed placement is smaller); the absolute-rotation branch re-resolved the rewritten placement with the pre-rotation rect AND the old angle (the payload rotation was updated only afterwards), found nothing and fell back to the old rect with the new angle; the delta-rotation branch never updated the rect (wrong once the start or end angle is not a right angle); `move_object` stored the requested rect, which differs from the drawing when a near-45-degree resize keeps the old size (the AABB-to-size inversion is singular there). An unresolvable marker with no geometric candidate is treated as orphaned, so Delete removed the marker only.
**Fix:** one chokepoint, `_sync_image_marker_to_drawn`, runs after every app-image rewrite (move/resize, absolute and delta rotation). It re-reads the rewritten placement by identity (`stream_xref`, `do_operator_index`, `xref`; an operand rewrite keeps them) and stores its drawn AABB and the new angle in the payload and the marker rect, which is also what the hit test reports (the same AABB-plus-rotation shape native images use). `add_image_object` snapshots the page's placements before `insert_image` and stores the bbox of the one placement it added (by slot, not xref: identical bytes reuse one xref); with no unique new placement it keeps the requested rect and logs a warning.
**Rule:** an app-image marker is the key every later verb resolves by, so it must hold what the page DRAWS (bbox and angle read back from the rewritten placement), never the rect or angle that was requested. Re-read a placement you just rewrote by its content-stream identity, not by the geometry it had before the rewrite.
**Fixed later (round 16 decisions pass, D-OLD-MARKERS):** markers already saved by older builds (pre-rotation rect with the rotated angle, or the 4:3 rect around a letterboxed image) did not resolve: Move/Rotate returned False silently and Delete removed only the marker. They are now repaired when exactly one same-digest, same-angle, same-centre placement exists; otherwise the verb refuses with a message and Delete keeps both (see the D-OLD-MARKERS entry).
**File:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_image_objects_model.py` (`test_app_image_absolute_rotation_keeps_move_rotate_delete_working[...]`, `test_app_image_delta_rotation_from_free_angle_keeps_marker_on_drawing`, `test_app_image_resize_near_45_degrees_records_drawn_bbox`, `test_app_image_letterboxed_insert_records_drawn_bbox`, `test_same_letterboxed_picture_inserted_twice_both_markers_follow_their_drawing`)

## A rect object on a /Rotate page was selectable only where nothing is drawn, and a drag teleported and transposed it (F15-3)
**Area:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`get_object_info_at_point`, `move_object`, `_marker_pick_rect`, `_app_object_true_rect`), `model/tools/annotation_tool.py` (`add_rect`)
**Symptom:** (Round 15.) 600x800 page, `/Rotate 90`, `add_rect` at visual (100, 100, 200, 160) draws correctly; a click at its drawn centre hits nothing, the object is picked at visual (130, 650) where nothing is drawn, and a 20 pt right drag re-draws it at visual (640, 120, 698, 218) with width and height swapped. `/Rotate 0` was fine.
**Cause:** three coordinate spaces on one object. A rect object's annotation is the drawn rectangle, so `add_rect` stores its `/Rect` in UNROTATED space (`derotation_matrix`), while the hit point, `destination_rect` and `payload["rect"]` are VISUAL. The hit test compared the visual point with the raw `annot.rect` and `move_object` wrote the visual destination to `annot.set_rect`. A textbox or image marker is a hidden stand-in built from the visual numbers, so the same raw `annot.rect` read was right for it, which hid the mix at `/Rotate 0` and for the other two kinds.
**Fix:** `_marker_pick_rect(annot, payload)` is the one place that says which space a marker `/Rect` is in (rect kind: mapped with `unrotated_to_visual_rect`; others: as stored); the hit test and the no-payload-rect fallback of `_app_object_true_rect` use it. `move_object` maps the destination with `visual_to_unrotated_rect`, the mapping `add_rect` uses. Delete is unchanged: its `annot.rect` only feeds `mark_page_content_dirty`, which queues by page index.
**Rule:** before reading or writing `annot.rect`, ask whether the annotation is drawn content (unrotated space) or a hidden marker built from visual numbers; convert at the boundary with `model.geometry`. Test the drawn ink (render and find the pixels), not `annot.rect` against the number you passed in.
**Not fixed:** a file saved by an older build after dragging a rect object on a rotated page keeps its mangled `/Rect`. Native images and app image objects on a rotated page had the same space question; fixed in round 16 (F14-MM-1b).
**File:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_object_manipulation_model.py` (`test_rect_object_on_rotated_page_is_selectable_where_drawn_and_moves_there`, `test_delete_rect_object_on_rotated_page_removes_the_drawn_ink`)

## Rotating an app textbox to 90/270 re-flowed its text into the unturned box and shrank the font by half (F15-6)
**Area:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`rotate_object` textbox branch, `_turned_textbox_rect`, `_insert_textbox_visual_content`)
**Symptom:** (Round 15.) Textbox (100, 100, 400, 130) "Quarterly revenue summary" at 14 pt: Rotate Object to 90 drew 3 columns at 6.82 pt crammed against the box's left edge (270: right edge); 180 and 0 kept 14 pt. The marker rect and selection frame stayed the wide unrotated box.
**Cause:** `insert_htmlbox(rect, rotate=...)` takes `rect` as the FINAL (visual) box of the rotated content and lays the text out in its transpose. `rotate_object` re-inserted into the unchanged `old_rect`, so a 300x30 box asked for the text in a 30x300 layout, and the `scale_low=0` insert shrank it until it fit. Pre-existing; PyMuPDF's behaviour was confirmed with a raw `insert_htmlbox` probe over rect x rotate.
**Fix:** `_turned_textbox_rect(old_rect, old_rotation, new_rotation, page_rect)`: when the rotation changes by an odd quarter turn the visual width and height swap about the box centre (the layout box is unchanged, so nothing re-flows and 0 -> 90 -> 0 restores the box); the turned box is slid back inside the page rather than cropped (a crop would re-flow). Half turns and no-ops keep the rect. The new marker rect, hit bbox and frame follow the turned box. Redaction still uses the old rect. Only a turned box larger than the page is cropped by the insert's clamp (text may then shrink, the documented `scale_low=0` backstop).
**Rule:** the rect handed to `insert_htmlbox` with `rotate=90/270` is the box AFTER the turn; change the box with the rotation, never insert rotated content into the old aspect and let the shrink absorb it. Assert font size and line count after a rotate, not only the angle.
**File:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_object_manipulation_model.py` (`test_rotating_a_textbox_keeps_its_font_size_and_line_count`, `test_quarter_turn_swaps_the_box_about_its_centre_and_text_stays_inside`, `test_textbox_quarter_turn_round_trip_restores_the_original_box`, `test_quarter_turn_near_the_page_edge_slides_the_box_in_instead_of_cropping_it`)

## A coordinator that connects a lambda capturing `self` to its own child QThread is freed from inside that thread's destruction: native abort in a later, unrelated `processEvents` (GATE15-3)
**Area:** `controller/page_render_coordinator.py` (`_start_worker`, `_on_thread_finished_signal`), harness `test_scripts/qt_teardown.py` (`dispose_pdf_view`), `test_scripts/test_page_reorder.py`, `test_scripts/test_page_deskew_scope.py`
**Symptom:** (Round 12 3 of 3, round 15 1 of 2, round 16 about 1 run in 8.) `Fatal Python error: Aborted` then `Windows fatal exception: access violation` at `qapp.processEvents()` in the `finally` of `test_page_reorder.py::test_controller_records_structural_move_and_restores_order_with_undo_redo`, only in the 12-file gate batch 10 (it reproduced at HEAD, and was once recorded NOT VALID after 10 clean runs). No Qt message reaches the message handler and no Python frame is running at the crash. The victim test is innocent: the object was leaked by `test_page_render_coordinator.py::test_live_worker_keeps_qt_event_loop_responsive` (bisected by deselecting it: 0 crashes in 70 runs; with it about 1 in 14).
**Cause:** `thread.finished.connect(lambda token=...: self._thread_finished(token))` sits on a `QThread(self)` that is a child of the coordinator. The lambda holds the coordinator's Python wrapper, so dropping the last external reference does not free it; it lives until the thread is destroyed. The thread's own `deleteLater` is then delivered by a later `processEvents`, the thread's connections are released, the wrapper's last reference goes, Python deletes the C++ coordinator, and `~QObject` deletes its child threads, including the one whose destructor is already running. Whether the queued `finished` events are delivered inside the test's own event loop or later is a timing race, which is why it was intermittent and order dependent. A deterministic standalone repro: request one render, quit the loop from the result consumer, `wait_for_done()`, drop the coordinator, `processEvents()`.
**Fix:** `thread.finished` goes to the bound `@Slot() _on_thread_finished_signal`; the token travels on the thread as a dynamic property and is read back with `self.sender()`. A bound slot of a QObject holds no strong reference and is severed with the receiver, so the coordinator is freed at once when dropped. Harness: `dispose_pdf_view` now runs one `processEvents()` after `close()` and before `deleteLater()` (queued `QTimer.singleShot(0, view.method)` callbacks have no receiver context in PySide and raise "Internal C++ object already deleted" if delivered after the delete), and the page-reorder and deskew-scope controller tests use it instead of a bare `close()`.
**Rule:** never connect a lambda that captures `self` to a signal of a child `QThread(self)` (or any child QObject); use a bound slot and carry the key on the object (`setProperty` + `sender()`). A GUI test that drops a coordinator must not rely on a later `processEvents` to retire its threads. Guard: `test_no_coordinator_connects_a_lambda_to_its_own_child_thread`. Same-shape sites checked: thumbnail, text-commit preview, print, OCR, search coordinators have no such lambda (OCR and search use parentless threads in plain-Python coordinators).
**File:** `controller/page_render_coordinator.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_page_render_coordinator.py` (`test_dropped_coordinator_is_not_kept_alive_by_its_own_thread_connections`, `test_finished_thread_releases_slot_and_starts_the_pending_request`, `test_no_coordinator_connects_a_lambda_to_its_own_child_thread`)

## App images on a /Rotate page were drawn elsewhere, and native / app images were hit and moved in unrotated space (F14-MM-1b, F15-G4-IMG)
**Area:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`add_image_object`, `_create_image_object_marker`, `_image_payload_unrotated_rect`, `_app_object_true_rect`, `_marker_pick_rect`, `_sync_image_marker_to_drawn`, `get_object_info_at_point`, the `move_object` / `rotate_object` / `_delete_object_impl` image branches, `_rewrite_native_image_matrix`)
**Symptom:** (Round 16.) On a 595x842 `/Rotate 90` page an app image added at visual (100, 200, 200, 250) was drawn at visual (592, 100, 642, 200) (also wrong at 180 and 270) and turned with the page, while its hidden marker and the hit test stayed at the requested rect, where nothing is drawn. With an offset CropBox or MediaBox the drawing was displaced further (the dropped origin of F15-G4); with a negative-origin box the marker landed at neither place. A native image on a `/Rotate 90` page was selectable only at its unrotated numbers (its drawn centre hit nothing), `ObjectHitInfo.bbox` was unrotated, and a move to a visual destination landed somewhere else.
**Cause:** `insert_image`, the image `cm` writers and `discover_native_image_invocations` speak UNROTATED page space; the request, the hit point, `ObjectHitInfo.bbox` and a move's destination are VISUAL. The visual rect went to `insert_image` raw (no `visual_to_unrotated_rect`, no `shift_rect_for_pymupdf_writers`, no `/Rotate` turn), the native hit test compared the visual point with unrotated bboxes, and the native move handed the visual destination to the `cm` writer. At `/Rotate 0` every mapping is the identity, which hid it.
**Fix:** `pdf_object_ops` is the one boundary. `add_image_object` maps the visual rect with `visual_to_unrotated_rect`, shifts it with `shift_rect_for_pymupdf_writers` and inserts with `rotate=(rotation + page.rotation) % 360`, so the picture is upright on screen and the letterbox is taken in the right frame (measured: `insert_image`'s rotate argument is the discovered raw-cm angle, and upright needs it equal to `/Rotate`). An image payload's `rect` and its marker `/Rect` stay UNROTATED (the discovered placement; PyMuPDF annotation rects are unrotated space too, so the hidden marker sits on the image); `_image_payload_unrotated_rect` reads it for resolution and the `cm` rewrite, and `_app_object_true_rect` / `_marker_pick_rect` map it to visual for the hit test and `ObjectHitInfo.bbox`. The native hit test maps the point with `visual_to_unrotated_point` and reports `unrotated_to_visual_rect(bbox)`; native and app moves map the destination with `visual_to_unrotated_rect`. `ObjectHitInfo.rotation` stays the stored raw-cm angle (an upright image on a `/Rotate 90` page reports 90, as an upright textbox does); rotation deltas are the same in both frames.
**Rule:** anything that reaches a content stream or `discover_native_image_invocations` is unrotated page space; anything that reaches the View is visual. Convert once, in `pdf_object_ops`, with `model.geometry`; a rect for a PyMuPDF writer also goes through `shift_rect_for_pymupdf_writers`. Test the rendered ink (a two-colour strip also shows orientation), never `get_image_rects` or `annot.rect` against the number you passed in.
**Compatibility:** older builds also wrote the image payload `rect` in unrotated space (the numbers they handed to `insert_image`, or since F15-4 the discovered bbox) and their marker `/Rect` sat on those numbers, so their image objects on rotated pages resolve unchanged and are now picked where they are drawn (`test_legacy_image_marker_on_rotated_page_still_resolves`). Nothing is re-inserted: an old image keeps the place and orientation it was drawn with (sideways if it was inserted on a quarter-turned page). Not measured: an old marker on a rotated page with an offset box written before F15-4 (requested numbers, drawing displaced by the dropped origin); it did not resolve before this fix either.
**Not fixed:** form-nested native images keep their axis-aligned-only rewrite.
**File:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_image_objects_model.py` (`test_app_image_on_rotated_page_is_drawn_hit_moved_and_deleted_in_visual_space[...]`, `test_letterboxed_app_image_on_rotated_page_stays_inside_the_requested_visual_rect[...]`, `test_legacy_image_marker_on_rotated_page_still_resolves`), `test_scripts/test_native_pdf_images_model.py` (`test_native_image_on_rotated_page_is_hit_moved_resized_and_deleted_where_drawn[...]`; the offset-box hit/move tests now use a visual oracle)

## Moving, rotating or deleting an app textbox erased the page text under it, and deleting an image erased the text in its `q` block (F13-VF-2b)
**Area:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`_erase_textbox_drawing`, `_empty_textbox_form`, `_textbox_form_candidates`, `_form_drawn_by_another_page_or_form`, `_redact_and_restore_textbox_region`, `_foreign_chars_in_rect`; the textbox branches of `move_object` / `rotate_object` / `_delete_object_impl`; `_remove_native_image_invocation`, `_q_block_paints_only_the_do`)
**Symptom:** (Round 16.) Page text `UNDERLYING PAGE TEXT`, `add_textbox` "Moving box" over it, then Move: the page reads only `Moving box` at `/Rotate 0` (all three words gone) and loses `LYING` at `/Rotate 90`; Delete leaves no text at all; the same after Save As and reopen. A box grown by a longer edit (F15-2) erased the page text between its old rect and the new words on the next move/rotate. Deleting a native image whose `q` block also drew text (`q BT (KEEP) Tj ET cm /Im Do Q`) erased `KEEP`; with no sole-image block (`cm /Im Do BT … ET`) it removed the image `cm` too and moved the text drawn after it.
**Cause:** move / rotate / delete erased the textbox with `add_redact_annot(rect)` + `apply_redactions`, which is geometric: every glyph whose box touches the rect goes, whoever drew it. The textbox's own glyphs are one Form XObject (`insert_htmlbox` appends `q /fzFrmN Do Q`), so identity was available but unused. The native-image remover dropped the whole `q..Q` block whenever it held one `Do`, without looking at what else the block painted, and otherwise removed the `cm` with the `Do`, changing the CTM of later operators in the same scope.
**Fix:** one chokepoint, `_erase_textbox_drawing`, for move, rotate and delete. First `_empty_textbox_form`: the Form XObjects the page content invokes directly and whose placement meets the box are tried best-overlap first; a form is the box's drawing only when emptying its stream takes exactly the stored text's characters (`_compared_chars`, NFKC letters/digits/punctuation/symbols; or, since F16-1, those of the text layer htmlbox writes for it, `_textbox_layer_chars`) off the page content and adds none, and no other page or form invokes it; otherwise its stream is put back. On success the form also loses its `/Resources` (its fonts become unreachable for the save-time garbage pass); the page keeps a `/Name Do` that draws nothing, so no content stream is re-tokenized. No marker field is needed, so boxes saved by older builds and boxes whose form an unrelated redaction renamed (`fzFrm0` -> `Fm1`) resolve the same way. When no form qualifies (a text edit drew some of the words as loose page glyphs, a tiny-canvas insert, a box another tool rewrote) the old rect redaction runs only if the rect holds no page text the box does not own (`_foreign_chars_in_rect`, every glyph box touching the derotated rect); otherwise the op returns `False` and the page is untouched. The image remover drops the `q..Q` block only when every other operator in it is non-painting state (`_NON_PAINTING_OPERATORS`), otherwise the `Do` alone, and never removes a `cm` outside such a block.
**Rule:** deleting or moving an identified object removes that object's drawing, never a rectangle. Prove the identity against the page (characters taken off == the object's characters, nothing added) before keeping the change; when identity cannot be proven, refuse rather than redact over content the object does not own.
**Not fixed:** a box whose drawing is mixed (some words in its form, some loose) over page text it does not own is refused (silently, as F15-2 (a)), not moved; removing loose glyphs by identity needs the text-commit engine's glyph ownership. A textbox whose stored text cannot be read back exactly (emoji, shaped scripts, CJK Ext-B: a lossy text layer) did not qualify for the form path and its fallback saw its own characters as foreign; fixed in round 16 (F16-1): the comparison is against htmlbox's own text layer for the stored text. A box of CJK Ext-B ALONE still takes the guarded fallback (its text layer is spaces, nothing to compare). The emptied form and its `Do` stay in the file (a few bytes per move). Behaviour change: Delete of a stale-marker textbox (stored text no longer what the page draws) whose rect holds the drawn text now refuses too, as move/rotate already did (F15-2); a marker with nothing drawn under it is still removed.
**File:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_object_manipulation_model.py` (`test_textbox_object_op_keeps_the_page_text_under_the_box[...]`, `test_textbox_saved_and_reopened_keeps_the_page_text_under_it[...]`, `test_textbox_drawn_partly_outside_its_xobject_refuses_instead_of_erasing_page_text[...]`), `test_scripts/test_native_pdf_images_model.py` (`test_delete_native_image_keeps_page_text_drawn_in_the_same_scope[...]`)

## Right-to-left runs were indexed in visual (x-sorted) order, so the editor showed Hebrew mirrored and every rebuild drew it mirrored (F15-RTL-ORDER)

**Area:** `model/text_block_parsing.py` (`_parse_runs_from_raw_line`), `model/rtl_text.py`, `model/pdf_model.py` (`_get_chars_in_run_unrotated`, `_build_multi_style_html`), `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_tier0_target_from_resolve`)
**Symptom:** (Round 16.) The index run of a Hebrew word drawn by MuPDF (rightmost glyph shin first) read the letters reversed (final mem first); the paragraph of a two-word line had both the letters and the word order reversed. The editor showed that string, htmlbox draws its input as logical text, so a consented rebuild that appended one letter drew the word mirrored (original rightmost glyph shin, rebuilt rightmost final mem). A protected Hebrew neighbour replay was mirrored the same way.
**Cause:** The run parser sorts every character of a line by x (to cut runs at gaps) and then concatenated the run's characters in that x order. MuPDF's `rawdict` / `get_text` already return right-to-left text in LOGICAL order (measured: a Hebrew word written left to right into a stream, i.e. a visual-order producer, is still extracted in logical order; a real Arabic PDF, `015-arabic/habibi.pdf`, extracts logical text with zero-width glyph boxes), so the x sort undid MuPDF's own bidi handling. A re-sort by x is also unusable as a bidi oracle on broken-geometry fonts (all glyphs at one x).
**Fix:** x order stays for segmentation, bbox and origin (F15-VM2-RTL needs the geometric left edge). `_finalize` takes a run that holds a strong RTL character (`model/rtl_text.contains_rtl`, bidi class R/AL) in source order `(span, char)`; after the line is parsed its runs are renumbered in source order when any of them is RTL, so `span_idx` order is reading order and every join by it (`_make_paragraph_unit`, selection lines, textbox marker sync) is logical. `_get_chars_in_run_unrotated` keeps rawdict traversal order for RTL glyphs so `get_char_context_at_point` text and rectangles line up with `run.text`; `_build_multi_style_html` orders RTL runs by `span_idx`. `_tier0_target_from_resolve` returns None for a member holding RTL text: Tier 0 matches a stream operand byte for byte, and a visual-order operand (or a palindrome such as alef-bet-alef) cannot prove the typed letters land in the right order. Pure LTR lines are unchanged (the whole branch is gated on `contains_rtl`).
**Rule:** The index contract is: run/paragraph TEXT is logical order, BBOX/ORIGIN are visual page geometry. Never rebuild text from an x sort when the line holds RTL characters; never hand index text to a stream patcher without proving the operand order.
**Not fixed / scope:** see TODOS F16-RTL-RESIDUAL (Tier 0 operand reordering, mirrored brackets; RTL table cells were fixed by F16-RTL-CELLS and selection clipping by F16-COPY-2; the growth direction was settled by D-RTL-GROW). `TextBlock.text` and the dict-span fallback already took MuPDF's order and are unchanged.
**File:** `model/text_block_parsing.py`, `model/rtl_text.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_f16_rtl_order_index_runs_hold_logical_text_and_visual_geometry`, `test_f16_rtl_order_rebuild_draws_the_word_in_the_order_typed`, `test_f16_rtl_order_protected_neighbours_are_replayed_in_logical_order`, `test_f16_rtl_order_char_context_matches_the_run_text`, `test_f16_rtl_order_multi_style_colors_follow_the_logical_text`), `test_scripts/test_tier0_target_resolution.py` (`test_shape_right_to_left_target_is_not_a_tier0_target`)

## A reopen anchor migrated onto the nearest run on the page, so re-clicking an edited heading opened another line (F14-ANCHOR-STALE)

**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_choose_anchor_run`, anchor migration after `rebuild_page`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`_stale_anchor_rebind_run`, `_get_text_info_at_point_unrotated`)
**Symptom:** (Round 16.) After a consented rebuild of the `test-complexed-layout.pdf` p1 heading (re-inserted as two runs, `QFIDANCHOR` + the CJK tail), a click inside the heading's old box returned `p0_b0_l0_s0` (the Stirling text above it) carrying the heading's bbox; reopening would edit the wrong text.
**Cause:** The migration ranked rebuilt runs by `(text equals the new text, distance to the anchor centre)`. When the rebuild splits the text, no run equals it, the text term is 1 for all, and distance alone chose an unrelated run. The hit-test's stale-anchor re-bind had the same shape: nearest run centre on the whole page, no check that it was where the anchored text was.
**Fix:** `_choose_anchor_run`: exact-text run (nearest) > fragment of the new text (grouped shows only, then regrouped; a plain run drops the anchor, live run boxes serve the click) > the single run in the old/new box; a run outside that region is never chosen. The hit-test re-bind (`_stale_anchor_rebind_run`) only accepts a run intersecting the anchor rect, preferring the one under the click, deletes the stale key, and drops an anchor with no run inside.
**Rule:** Never bind persistent per-run state to a run on distance alone; require evidence (text, or lying inside the old region). No evidence means drop the state: a missing anchor degrades to the live run box, a wrong one opens other text.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_real_pdf_rebuild_split_heading_reclick_never_opens_another_run`, `test_choose_anchor_run_ranks_text_evidence_over_distance`, `test_stale_run_anchor_is_not_rebound_to_a_run_outside_its_rect`, `test_stale_run_anchor_rebinds_to_the_run_under_the_click`)

## A heading the app re-inserted as several runs on one baseline reopened fragment by fragment (S17-ANCHOR-JOIN)

**Area:** `model/joined_edit_runs.py`, `model/pdf_model.py` (`joined_edit_runs`, `_joined_edit_group_for`, `_joined_text_hit`, `_get_text_info_at_point_unrotated`), `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_record_joined_edit_run`, `_resolve_edit_text_target` joined group)
**Symptom:** (Round 17.) After a consented rebuild of the `test-complexed-layout.pdf` p1 heading to `QFIDANCHOR` + the CJK tail, the line is two runs (`p0_b72_l0_s0`, `p0_b72_l0_s1`: Latin and CJK fonts). A click on the marker opened `QFIDANCHOR` alone, a click on the CJK opened the tail alone, and a click in the 2.7 pt gap between them fell through to the block fallback (the whole line, a third behaviour).
**Cause:** F14-ANCHOR-STALE correctly stopped planting the old box on one fragment, but nothing said the fragments belong together: the index sees two runs and a run is the edit target. Heuristics from geometry (same line, adjacent) would also join source runs that merely share a baseline (a bold word in a sentence).
**Fix:** Provenance. The legacy rebuild records the text it wrote when the rebuilt page shows exactly that text as two or more runs of one line (`find_joined_fragments`; whitespace-only runs between members ride along, a foreign run breaks the window). Every use re-proves the record against the live runs (`prove_joined_group`), so a stale record is inert and undo revives the older one; records are never pruned except by a per-page cap. The hit-test (run mode) returns one `TextHit` for a click on any member or in the gap (the text as typed, the union, the dominant member's font/size/colour, `member_span_ids`, no `source_ref`); the commit re-derives the group and makes all members the target when `original_text` equals the whole text, so one edit replaces every fragment and the overlap cluster covers the union. A caller naming one fragment keeps the single-run target.
**Rule:** join runs on evidence of one write, never on adjacency; keep the evidence re-provable against the live page instead of binding it to span ids (they are reassigned on every rebuild).
**Not fixed:** records are session-local (a saved and reopened file shows the fragments again, as before); paragraph mode keeps its own paragraph grouping; a multi-line rebuild is not joined.
**File:** `model/joined_edit_runs.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_s17_anchor_join_rebuilt_heading_reopens_as_one_box`, `test_s17_anchor_join_joined_box_commits_back_as_one_edit`, `test_s17_anchor_join_does_not_join_runs_the_app_did_not_write`, `test_find_joined_fragments_requires_one_line_exact_text`, `test_real_pdf_rebuild_split_heading_reclick_never_opens_another_run`)

## A quarter-turn rebuild grew to the page edge and overprinted the next run on its column (F13-VF-4b)
**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_vertical_neighbour_limit`, `_apply_redact_insert_body` vertical branch), `model/pdf_model.py` (`_binary_shrink_height`)
**Symptom:** (Round 16.) Two quarter-turn runs on one column, `ab` (Helvetica 14) followed along the reading direction by an untouched red `NEXT` (10 pt) 4 pt later. A consented rebuild `ab` -> `abcdefghijklmnop` returned SUCCESS on both engines and both quarter turns, and the saved file showed the 111 pt word drawn over `NEXT` (rotate 90: edited y 188.7-300.0 over NEXT y 253.8-280.4; rotate 270: edited y 300.0-411.3 over NEXT y 319.6-346.2). `NEXT` itself had not moved.
**Cause:** F13-VF-4 and F14-VF4-WRAP were written for horizontal text only. The vertical branch built its htmlbox rect from the run's start to the page edge (`page_rect.y1` reading down, `page_rect.y0` reading up), `_binary_shrink_height` searched up to the page edge too, `_right_neighbour_limit` was skipped when `is_vertical`, and `_guard_overprint` was `new_rect is None and not is_vertical`. Nothing bounded the growth along the reading direction and nothing checked the result.
**Fix:** `_vertical_neighbour_limit` is the vertical twin of `_right_neighbour_limit`: the nearest untouched axis-aligned run on the same column (more than half of the narrower width overlaps across the reading direction) that starts at or past the edited extent's far edge is the wall (its top edge reading down, its bottom edge reading up); one that starts inside the extent but sticks out past the far edge walls at the extent's old far edge (F14-VF4-OVERLAP); runs behind the start, on another column, or off the axes never wall. The insert rect ends at that wall (never shorter than the old text), `_binary_shrink_height(far_limit=...)` neither searches nor pads past it, and a text that does not fit at full size is retried at `scale_low` 0.5 (like horizontal strategy C) and then refused with `TEXT_DOES_NOT_FIT` and a rollback instead of the old `scale_low=0` speck. Without a wall the old behaviour (shrink to any size) is unchanged. Every in-place quarter-turn insert is now also checked by `_new_text_overprints`, so a multi-column wrap that lands on untouched text is refused.
**Rule:** an in-place edit is bounded by the next run along its OWN direction of growth, whatever that direction is; a guard written for the horizontal case must be checked against the quarter turns.
**Not fixed:** a dragged `new_rect` is still not capped (the user put it there), but it is overprint-guarded since S17-DRAG-GUARD (TODOS F13-VF-4c). There is no cross-axis wrap floor for quarter-turn paragraphs (the `_wrap_floor` analogue): their extra columns are only protected by the overprint guard, which refuses instead of shrinking.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_f13vf4b_vertical_rebuild_never_overprints_next_run`, `test_f13vf4b_vertical_rebuild_refuses_when_the_word_cannot_fit_before_next_run`, `test_f13vf4b_vertical_rebuild_that_fits_before_next_run_still_succeeds`, `test_f13vf4b_vertical_run_on_another_column_is_not_a_wall`, `test_f13vf4b_vertical_neighbour_limit`)

## On a ROTATED `/UserUnit` page `insert_htmlbox`, `insert_image` and the visual-to-unrotated mapping dropped the scale: textboxes, text rebuilds and images were drawn at the wrong size and place (F15-G1-UU-ROT)

**Area:** `model/text_commit/transforms.py` (`pymupdf_writer_matrix`, `pymupdf_writer_shift`, `shift_rect_for_pymupdf_writers`), `model/font_stream_compaction.py` (`insert_htmlbox_tracked`, `_placement_redirect`), `model/geometry.py` (`_rotation_maps` and the four point/rect converters), `model/pdf_model.py` (`_visual_rect_to_unrotated_rect`), `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`_marker_pick_rect`, `_annot_rect_is_scaled_wrong`, the textbox-growth union)
**Symptom:** (Round 16.) MediaBox [0 0 300 400] + `/UserUnit 2` + `/Rotate 90/180/270`: `add_textbox` at visual (10,10,200,60) inked "MMMM" at (23,31,161,58) instead of (12,16,80,29): about 2x the glyph size and offset from the request; a bottom-right box drew nothing (its x0 630 fell past the 800 pt page). At `/UserUnit 0.5` nothing was drawn at all. A legacy text rebuild and `add_image_object` on the same pages were off the same way, a textbox added there could not be picked (its marker `Annot.rect` read back at y = -250 for a request at y = 150) and moving it left the old copy. The unrotated `/UserUnit` page and rotated unit-scale pages were right.
**Cause:** two independent drops of `/UserUnit` once `/Rotate != 0`. (1) PyMuPDF's page writers read the rect they are given through `~page.transformation_matrix`, which collapses to `(1, 0, 0, -1, 0, H)`: no origin and no scale, while every model rect is in `/UserUnit`-scaled page units. (2) `page.derotation_matrix` / `rotation_matrix` build the quarter turn from the UNSCALED box, so `visual_to_unrotated_rect` mapped the request to a wrong place (the textbox rect was (10,200,60,390) where the true one is (10,600,60,790)). `PDFModel._visual_rect_to_unrotated_rect` repeated that arithmetic by hand.
**Fix:** `transforms.pymupdf_writer_matrix(page)` is the whole correction, `~PageVisualFrame.base x transformation_matrix` (a pure translation at `/UserUnit 1`, a translation plus the scale `1 / UserUnit` otherwise; `None` where `transformation_matrix` is already right). `shift_rect_for_pymupdf_writers` applies it (right for `insert_image`). `insert_htmlbox` lays its text out in the rect it is given AND places it there, so `insert_htmlbox_tracked` gives it the unscaled rect for layout (the glyphs keep their point size, the wrap and `spare_height` / `scale` stay in page units) and redirects its single `show_pdf_page` call to the placed rect (`_placement_redirect`; one `insert_htmlbox` call site, the AST guard still holds). `model.geometry` takes the quarter turn from `page_visual_frame(page).quarter_turn` (provable frames; the page matrices otherwise, and at `/Rotate 0`), which also fixes the unclipped-CropBox offset the TODOS "geometry.py shares the rotated-page defect" item described and the rotated `/UserUnit` watermark centre (its strict xfail is gone). A textbox marker on such a page is picked by its payload rect, because MuPDF's `Annot.rect` does not read back what `add_rect_annot` wrote there.
**Rule:** never build a visual/unrotated mapping from `page.rotation_matrix` / `derotation_matrix` or place a PyMuPDF writer rect without `shift_rect_for_pymupdf_writers`; use `model.geometry` and the chokepoints. A writer that lays out AND places in one rect (`insert_htmlbox`) needs the two rects separated on a scaled page.
