Not fixed here: `insert_htmlbox` re-inserts links at the layout rect's centre, so an `<a>` would land wrong on such a page (no model caller emits one); the `AnnotationTool` consumers (a red rectangle added at (30,50,90,80) on a `/Rotate 90` + `/UserUnit 2` page inked at (428,48,492,82)) are fixed in F15-G1-UU-ANNOT.
**File:** `model/text_commit/transforms.py`, `model/font_stream_compaction.py`, `model/geometry.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/pdf_object_ops.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_add_textbox_atomic.py` (`test_add_textbox_ink_lands_at_requested_rect_on_rotated_user_unit_page`, `test_moving_a_textbox_on_a_rotated_user_unit_page_leaves_no_old_copy`), `test_scripts/test_geometry.py` (`test_visual_unrotated_conversions_follow_the_frame_on_a_rotated_page`), `test_scripts/test_text_commit_visual_frame.py` (`test_shifted_rect_reads_back_through_the_writer_matrix_as_the_true_user_space_rect`), `test_scripts/test_font_stream_compaction.py` (`test_insert_htmlbox_tracked_keeps_size_and_place_on_a_rotated_user_unit_page`), `test_scripts/test_image_objects_model.py` (`test_app_image_on_rotated_user_unit_page_is_drawn_and_picked_at_the_requested_rect`), `test_scripts/test_text_geometry_page_rotation.py` (`test_legacy_edit_keeps_place_on_a_rotated_user_unit_page`), `test_scripts/test_watermark_rotated_pages.py`


## Move / Rotate / Delete Object refused every app textbox with emoji, Devanagari or Arabic right after it was created (F16-1)
**Area:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`_textbox_layer`, `_textbox_layer_chars`, `_htmlbox_layer`, `_texttrace_glyph_keys`, `_textbox_markup`; the comparisons in `_textbox_payload_drawn_on_page`, `_empty_textbox_form`, `_foreign_chars_in_rect` / `_redact_and_restore_textbox_region`)
**Symptom:** (Round 16.) `add_textbox` 'Hi 😀 there', a Devanagari line (`नमस्ते दुनिया`) or an Arabic line (`مرحبا بالعالم`) on a /Rotate 0 or /Rotate 90 page, then Move Object or Rotate Object with no edit in between: `False`, logged `the page no longer draws its stored text (missing ...); refusing move/rotate`. With that guard bypassed the erase step refused too (`its drawing is not one XObject and the box holds other page text (U+1F60)`), and Delete Object refused the same boxes. A CJK Ext-B box (U+20000 U+20001, alone or with Latin) could not be moved or rotated either. Latin, CJK, Hebrew, Thai, ligatures, NBSP and tabs were fine.
**Cause:** PyMuPDF 1.27's htmlbox draws these characters correctly but writes a lossy text layer (U+1F600 reads back as U+1F60, conjuncts and the Arabic lam-lam ligature as glyph ids, Ext-B cut to 16 bits). That loss is accepted (OD-UNI1-COMMIT) and the edit path forgives it against a scratch htmlbox reference (`_lossy_text_layer_problem`). The textbox object ops compared the RAW stored text (`_compared_chars(payload["text"])`) with the page text layer at three sites: the F15-2 drawn-text guard, the F13-VF-2b form identity check (`before - after == expected`) and the fallback's foreign-text check, so the box's own lossy characters read as "missing" and as "foreign".
**Fix:** `_textbox_layer` lays the box's stored text out exactly as the insert does (`_textbox_markup`, the one html/css builder now shared with `_insert_textbox_visual_content`; same font resolution, box size from the derotated payload rect, the payload's rotate, `scale_low=0`) on a scratch page (`_htmlbox_layer`, `insert_htmlbox_tracked(..., scratch=True)`, memoised) and returns the compared characters of the text layer htmlbox writes plus the `(font, glyph id)` it draws (`_texttrace_glyph_keys`, the edit path's `_texttrace_glyphs` rule). Each site keeps its raw comparison first and renders the reference only when that fails (a Latin box never renders it): the guard passes when every reference character is drawn in the box, or, when the reference text layer holds no comparable character at all (Ext-B only: its codes are spaces), when every reference glyph is drawn in the box; a form qualifies when emptying it removes exactly the raw OR the reference characters; the fallback's foreign-text check subtracts the reference characters too. A lossy box over page text it does not own is now removed by its form instead of being refused. A stale marker still refuses (stored 'Hi 😀 there' while the page draws 'Hi 😀 here': the reference has 't', the page does not).
**Rule:** never compare a stored string with a page text layer that htmlbox wrote; compare with what htmlbox writes for that string (a scratch render of the same markup), at every check of the path, not only the first one.
**Not fixed:** apart from the Ext-B-only case the reference is a text-layer comparison, not glyph evidence (font compaction after an old insert makes `(font, glyph id)` comparisons with a fresh scratch render less dependable): two characters that htmlbox writes as the same code point are indistinguishable, so a stale marker that differs only there is not detected. `get_texttrace` also reads annotation appearances, so the Ext-B-only glyph check is not content-only (an annotation would need the same subset font and glyph ids). An Ext-B-only box never qualifies for the form path (emptying its form removes no comparable character, which a non-text form would also do) and takes the guarded rect fallback, so over foreign page text it is refused. The marker sync after a text edit matched the index text and the new words against the raw stored text (fixed in round 17, see F16-1-LOSSY below).
**File:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_object_manipulation_model.py` (`test_textbox_with_a_lossy_text_layer_moves_rotates_and_deletes[...]`, `test_textbox_lossy_text_layer_still_refuses_a_stale_marker[...]`, `test_textbox_with_a_lossy_text_layer_over_page_text_removes_only_its_own_drawing[...]`)

## A text edit of a textbox holding emoji / shaped scripts left its marker stale, so Move refused, and a longer text did not grow the box (F16-1-LOSSY)

**Area:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`sync_textbox_markers_after_text_edit`, `_lossy_span_ignoring_whitespace`, `_lossy_raw_boundary`, `_splice_replacement`, `_textbox_reference_text`, `_TextboxLayer.text`, `_grow_box_over_new_words`)
**Symptom:** (Round 17.) `add_textbox` 'Hi 😀 there', then a paragraph-mode edit to 'Hi X' (or to a three-line longer text): the edit succeeded but the marker kept 'Hi 😀 there' at the old rect, and the next Move Object returned `False` with `TEXTBOX_TEXT_CHANGED`; the longer text's last word on line one ended 16 pt past the marker's right edge. The same edit on a Latin box synced and moved.
**Cause:** the edit's `source_text` is read from the page text index, which carries htmlbox's lossy text layer (U+1F600 reads back as U+1F60). `sync_textbox_markers_after_text_edit` looked for it in the RAW stored text, found it zero times and treated the box as untouched (the F16-1 guard then refused the stale marker, safely but wrongly). The growth step compared the new text's raw words with the page words (an emoji word never matched) and skipped any word whose CENTRE lay inside the box, so a word straddling the edge stayed outside for Latin text as well.
**Fix:** when the raw stored text does not hold `source_text` (and the stored text is not pure ASCII), the sync looks for it in the text layer htmlbox writes for the stored text (`_textbox_reference_text`, the F16-1 scratch render, now carrying `_TextboxLayer.text`), aligns the whitespace-free raw text with that layer (`difflib.SequenceMatcher`) and maps both ends of the single occurrence back to raw positions (`_lossy_span_ignoring_whitespace`; an end inside a lossy stretch, or next to a character the layer dropped, has no unique position). The raw span is replaced like a raw match (`_splice_replacement`); the span covering the whole box counts as a whole-box edit (style stored). A source found more than once in the layer, or one whose ends cannot be mapped, flags the marker `content_unsynced` (move/rotate refuse, as for any ambiguous source); a source in neither text leaves the box alone as before. The growth step reads a non-ASCII new text through the same scratch layer, and a word that is not wholly inside the box now grows it.
**Rule:** a string read back from the page text layer is not the string that was written; before matching it against stored text, bring both to the same side (here: the stored text through htmlbox's own layer, mapped back by alignment). A containment test on a word's centre hides a word that overflows an edge.
**Not fixed:** the alignment is a text diff, not glyph evidence: two emoji in one box, or an edit that ends inside a lossy stretch, flag the marker instead of syncing. Growth for a lossy new text assumes the page's text layer for the words the edit drew equals the scratch render's (same font family for the lossy characters). Editing the emoji run itself raises `TextEditRefused` ('need font file or buffer', font `NotoEmoji` = the htmlbox subset) before any commit; that is the edit path's font resolution, not the sync (TODOS F16-1 follow-up).
**File:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_object_manipulation_model.py` (`test_f17_edit_of_a_lossy_textbox_syncs_the_marker_grows_it_and_moves[...]`, `test_f17_sync_places_a_lossy_index_text_in_the_stored_text[...]`, `test_f17_sync_flags_an_ambiguous_lossy_source_and_leaves_foreign_text_alone[...]`)

## An upside-down rebuild was walled on the side it does not grow into and unwalled on the side it does (F16-2)

**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_horizontal_neighbour_limit` / `_right_neighbour_limit`, `_left_safe`, `_left_wall`, `_wrap_ceiling`, the horizontal branch of `_apply_redact_insert_body`: `grows_left`, `_strategy_b_rect`, the pre-push probe, the returned layout rect)
**Symptom:** (Round 16, after F15-VM2-FAST180 sent every 180-degree run to the htmlbox.) 'Hello World' written upside down (`rotate=180`, 14 pt, 'Hello' at larger x). 'World' -> 'Worldwide wonders' returned SUCCESS but drawn at 8.07 pt on two lines (the upright twin: 14 pt, one line). 'Hello' -> 'Hello there' raised `_RebuildRolledBack` ('t' over 'W' at (364.2, 400.0)); the upright twin succeeds by wrapping 'there' to the next line. Same on /Rotate 0 and 180; the same word alone on the page (no neighbour) was fine at 14 pt.
**Cause:** the horizontal htmlbox box assumed text written toward +x with its extra lines stacked down: `_right_neighbour_limit` walled the run at the next run to the RIGHT, `x1` was capped at it (and in strategy B), the right safe margin was the page wall, `_wrap_floor` bounded the wrap below, and the pre-push probe pushed text DOWN. An upside-down run grows toward -x and stacks its lines UP the page (an `insert_htmlbox(rotate=180)` box starts the text at its right edge and bottom). So the +x neighbour capped the box at the word's own width (shrink, wrap) while nothing walled the -x neighbour it grows into (overprint, rolled back by the guard). The FAST180 tests put the only other run 200 pt away on another line, so no wall ever fired.
**Fix:** `grows_left = rotation == 180 and not is_vertical` mirrors the whole horizontal branch. `_horizontal_neighbour_limit(grows_left=)` returns the right edge of the nearest run on the LEFT (the F14-VF4-OVERLAP rule mirrored; `_right_neighbour_limit` is its +x form); `_left_wall` is `_right_wall` evaluated on the page mirrored about its vertical axis (same F14-DT-1 rules, one implementation), `_left_safe` its margin; the box is pinned on the run's right edge and bottom and grows to the left wall / neighbour (`x0 = max(x1 - max(layout width, room), left_wall)`, never narrower than the edited extent) and up to the page top or `_wrap_ceiling` (the nearest untouched axis-aligned line above the edit, any block: nothing is pushed up), with `_NO_WRAP_CSS` when only one line fits; strategy B widens toward -x; the pre-push probe is skipped (the push-down only moves text down, and the wrapped lines go up); the returned layout rect is measured up from the bottom. The overprint guard is unchanged. Probe: the upright and the mirrored upside-down line give identical sizes, line counts and wraps (13.46 pt x 8 lines past the safe margin, 14 pt x 5 lines near it).
**Rule:** a box built for one writing direction is not a box for the other: when a route learns a new direction (FAST180), every wall, margin, wrap limit, pre-push and returned rect it computes must be re-derived for that direction, and its tests need a neighbour on BOTH sides of the run.
**Not fixed / scope:** a dragged `new_rect` of an upside-down run is where the user put it (no wall, as for upright text; its box is pinned at the drag rect's bottom and runs to the page top). Judged from `get_texttrace` direction, size and origin, not rendered to pixels; not eyeballed in the GUI. The quarter-turn htmlbox has its own caps (F13-VF-4b); the preview renderer's box for turned text was not re-derived.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_f16_2_upside_down_edit_grows_into_the_empty_side_at_full_size`, `test_f16_2_upside_down_edit_wraps_away_from_the_neighbour_it_grows_toward`, `test_f16_2_upside_down_edit_is_refused_not_overprinted_when_no_line_is_free`, `test_f16_2_horizontal_neighbour_limit_follows_the_growth_direction`, `test_f16_2_left_wall_mirrors_the_right_wall`, `test_f16_2_wrap_ceiling_is_the_nearest_untouched_line_above`, and 180 added to `test_f14vm2_quarter_turn_and_rotated_page_edits_keep_the_first_glyph_origin`)

## Page operations and bookmark-panel edits regenerated the whole outline in simple form (F16-NAV-1)

**Area:** `model/outline_ops.py` (new: `outline_items`, `follow_page_targets`, `move_targets_to_page`, `retarget_item`, `apply_outline_rows`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`get_toc_rows`, `set_toc`, `_capture_outline` / `_follow_outline` in `delete_pages`, `move_page`, `insert_blank_page`, `insert_pages_from_file`; `straighten_page`), `view/pdf_view.py` (`populate_toc`, `_toc_entries_from_tree`, `_on_bookmark_activated`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`load_toc`, `update_toc`)
**Symptom:** (Round 16.) Deleting page 114 of GeoTopo.pdf (the last bookmark's page) and saving sent 34 of the 35 bookmarks on untouched pages to the top of their page ('1.4 Zusammenhang' to=(90.1, 264.0) -> (72, 36)). On a synthetic outline every insert/delete/move/import turned a URI bookmark into "go to page 1" and dropped the /XYZ target, red colour and bold of the others, through Save As and reopen. Renaming any bookmark in the panel raised `ValueError: TOC page is out of range` (uncaught in `update_toc`; the tree kept the new title, the document did not) on an outline with a URI bookmark, and on one without it reset every other bookmark's target and style.
**Cause:** `_remap_toc_pages` and the panel round-tripped `get_toc()` simple rows (`[level, title, page]`) into `Document.set_toc`, which rebuilds every outline item as a GoTo to (72, 36) of its page with no `/C`, `/F` or collapse state; page -1 (URI, Launch, ...) was clamped to 1 by `max(1, ...)` in the remap and rejected by `set_toc`'s range check in the panel. The remap rewrote whenever its rows differed from `get_toc()`, which one URI bookmark (-1 -> 1) made always. The full form (`get_toc(simple=False)` into `set_toc`) is no fix either: PyMuPDF 1.27 reports `/Fit`, `/FitH` and `/XYZ null null 0` destinations as kind NAMED (probed), for which `set_toc` writes no action, and it re-derives every coordinate.
**Fix:** the outline is edited in place, never regenerated. Outline items reference page objects, so insert, move and import need no write: `_follow_outline` (after the op, same mappers as before) retargets only items that do not resolve to `mapper(old page)`, i.e. the items PyMuPDF's `delete_pages` stripped (it deletes `/Dest`/`/A` and greys `/C` to 0.8), to the survivor page as `[page /Fit]` (`/A/D` of an inline GoTo action, else `/Dest`, else a new GoTo action) and restores their `/C`; items with page -1 are never touched. `straighten_page` (replaces a page by a same-size raster) moves the bookmarks into the old page to the replacement before deleting it, swapping only the page reference of an explicit destination array (view kept). The panel carries an opaque key (outline xref) per row: `get_toc_rows()` -> view `_TOC_KEY_ROLE` -> `set_toc`; a keyed row writes only a changed `/Title`, or its destination when its page changed; page -1 with a key keeps a non-page item as it is; add/delete/reorder relinks `/First /Last /Next /Prev /Parent /Count` of the existing objects (closed items stay closed). Keyless rows are new items, except that a wholly keyless list with the current length and levels (an edited `get_toc()`) is paired by position. `update_toc` catches `TypeError`/`ValueError`, logs and reloads the tree. The view does not navigate for a page -1 bookmark.
**Rule:** never rebuild an outline (or any PDF structure that holds more than an API's simple form) from that simple form; edit only the objects that must change and leave every other key alone. A page reference already follows its page.
**Not fixed / scope:** a retargeted bookmark (deleted page, user re-page, new bookmark) gets a whole-page `/Fit` view, not a position. An outline whose `get_toc` and `get_outline_xrefs` walks disagree has no item identity: a panel edit rebuilds it (logged), a structural op leaves PyMuPDF's result. Names, named links and `/OpenAction` into a deleted or straightened page are handled by F16-NAV-1a (below); merges, page export and page import now carry the outline (F16-NAV-3). The panel shows -1 in the page column of a URI bookmark. Not driven in the GUI (the view+model rename path is tested with a real `PDFView`).
**File:** `model/outline_ops.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`, `view/pdf_view.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_bookmarks_toc.py` (`test_structural_ops_keep_every_outline_attribute`, `test_deleting_a_bookmarked_page_retargets_only_that_item`, `test_delete_all_and_placeholder_import_keep_outline_style`, `test_panel_rename_keeps_uri_and_other_bookmarks_untouched`, `test_panel_reorder_delete_add_and_repage_keep_attributes`, `test_set_toc_rejects_a_keyless_row_without_a_page`, `test_view_round_trips_outline_keys_and_rename_reaches_the_model`, `test_controller_load_toc_passes_keyed_rows_to_the_view`, `test_set_toc_of_simple_rows_is_a_no_op_on_an_outline_with_a_uri`, `test_straighten_page_keeps_the_bookmarks_into_the_replaced_page`)

## Merge, page export and page import dropped the outline, page labels, named destinations and every non-explicit link (F16-NAV-3)

**Area:** `model/navigation_graft.py` (new: `NavigationGraft`), `model/outline_ops.py` (`ImportedItem`, `append_items`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`compose_merged_document`, `export_pages`, `insert_pages_from_file`), `model/headless_merge.py`
**Symptom:** (Round 16.) Merging a bookmarked document with another file (into the current tab, as a new file, or with the CLI) produced a document with an empty bookmark panel, blank page labels (`i, ii, 1, 2` became `''`), no `/Names /Dests` tree and, on page 1, two links instead of three: the one to a named destination was gone. The same happened to every source, the current document included, and to `Export pages` as PDF. Importing pages from a file lost the same links on the imported pages. Nothing warned the user. Measured on a LaTeX file (GeoTopo.pdf, 117 pages, 35 bookmarks, 1318 names, 480 named links) merged with itself: 0 bookmarks, 0 names, 0 named links before; 70 / 2636 / 960 after.
**Cause:** `fitz.Document.insert_pdf` copies pages and, through `_do_links`, only GOTO/GOTOR/LAUNCH/URI links whose GoTo target lies in the same call's page range. It never copies the catalog `/Outlines`, `/PageLabels`, `/Names /Dests` or `/Dests`. And every link PyMuPDF 1.27 reports as `LINK_NAMED` is dropped, which is not only a link to a named destination: an explicit `[page /Fit]`, `/FitH` or `/XYZ null null 0` destination (what LaTeX and Word write) is reported the same way (see F16-NAV-1), so those links vanished too. A GoTo into a page copied by another `insert_pdf` call (page export copies runs, an import of pages 1, 2, 4) was dropped as well.
**Fix:** one place copies pages and carries their navigation, `NavigationGraft(dst).copy_pages(src, pages)` then `finish()`, used by all four call sites. It reads the source from raw objects (its own small PDF object reader over `xref_object`, because `xref_get_key` and `resolve_names` decode string keys and replace `null` by 0) and writes new objects into the target. Outline: `outline_ops.append_items` builds the item objects from the raw `/Title`, destination array (view kept verbatim, `null` included), URI action, `/C`, `/F` and collapse state, and relinks the tree; never `set_toc`. A bookmark that used a named destination becomes an explicit one. Links: every dropped link (`LINK_NAMED`, and a GoTo across insert runs) is re-created from its raw `/Rect`, `/Border`, `/BS`, `/C`, `/H`, `/F` and destination with the page reference pointed at the copy. Names: one flat sorted `/Names /Dests` leaf; the first source keeps a plain name, a later source's clash is renamed `name.2` (`.3` ...) and its links follow it; a name whose page was not copied is dropped with its links. Page labels: the label of each copied page is re-expressed as `/PageLabels` rules read from the raw number tree (`get_page_labels` returns a UTF-16 hex prefix undecoded), so an unlabelled source after a labelled one counts `1, 2, 3` again; prefixes are written with `fitz.get_pdf_str`. Pages that are not copied lose their bookmarks, names and links (children of a dropped bookmark move up a level). Import into an existing document (`insert_pages_from_file`) uses `into_existing=True` and carries everything too (S17-INSERT-NAV below): the document keeps its own navigation and receives the source's beside it. Navigation is best effort: a malformed outline, label or name tree is logged and skipped; the pages are always copied.
**Rule:** `insert_pdf` is a page copier, not a document merge: anything a viewer needs to navigate (outline, labels, name trees, links) must be carried separately, and a new code path that builds a document from other documents goes through `NavigationGraft`. Do not read a destination through an API that decodes or rewrites it (`resolve_names`, `xref_get_key` string values): compare and copy the raw bytes. Never call `Document.resolve_names()` on a document that is still being composed (it memoizes).
**Not fixed / scope:** the owner-accepted limits: (1) a bookmark with a GoToR / Launch / JavaScript action keeps its title but loses the action (no target); (2) the first source owns a plain name and a clash is renamed, so an external link into the merged file by the second source's name needs the renamed one; (3) `/OpenAction`, `/PageMode`, `/ViewerPreferences`, `/Threads`, structure tree, article beads and the document's own link styles other than `/Border /BS /C /H /F` are not carried; (4) a link whose destination array has no page reference (a remote or integer page) is not re-created; (5) a destination that points at an xref that is not a page of its document is dropped (two veraPDF corpus files); (6) one file in the sweep (`annotated_pdf.pdf`, Movie annotations MuPDF cannot synthesize appearances for) makes a second `insert_pdf` from the SAME `fitz.Document` raise `source object number out of range` once its links were read; other files copy twice fine, and the app opens a separate document per merge source, so nothing designs around it; (7) bookmarks of an inserted file are not imported into the current document (a product choice, TODOS F16-NAV-3 follow-up); (8) merging while the CURRENT document is encrypted raised `ValueError: document closed or encrypted`: fixed in round 17, see S17-ENC-MERGE. A password-protected merge SOURCE FILE works and keeps its navigation (probed). A name tree is written as one flat leaf, which is large but valid for tens of thousands of names. Not driven in the GUI by hand; the controller path (`merge_ordered_sources_into_current`, bookmark panel reload, undo) is covered by a test with a real `PDFView`.
**File:** `model/navigation_graft.py`, `model/outline_ops.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/headless_merge.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_merge_composition.py` (`test_merge_keeps_outline_labels_names_and_links_of_every_source`, `test_merge_keeps_every_source_when_the_file_comes_first`, `test_merge_of_documents_without_navigation_invents_none`, `test_merge_survives_a_broken_name_tree_and_keeps_the_rest`, `test_export_pages_carries_the_navigation_of_the_exported_pages_only`, `test_export_pages_drops_links_and_names_into_pages_that_were_not_exported`, `test_insert_pages_from_file_keeps_links_that_pymupdf_drops`), `test_scripts/test_headless_merge.py`, `test_scripts/test_navigation_graft.py`, `test_scripts/test_bookmarks_toc.py` (`test_append_items_*`), `test_scripts/test_pdf_merge_workflow.py` (`test_merge_into_current_keeps_navigation_shows_bookmarks_and_undoes`); fixtures `test_scripts/navigation_fixtures.py`

## Browse copy over a one-show line copied only the first word, or nothing (F16-COPY-1)

**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`TextHit.hit_span_id`, `_browse_span_id`, `_browse_run_at_point_unrotated`, `get_text_selection_lines`, `get_text_selection_snapshot_from_run`, `get_char_context_at_point`), `view/text_selection.py` (`_start_text_selection`)
**Symptom:** a line drawn as one text show (`insert_text` of 'Invoice number 4711 due today', the most common PDF line shape), shipped `text_target_mode` 'run'. A whole-line drag + Ctrl+C copied only the first word; a drag from 'number' to 'today' copied nothing (no highlight, the clipboard kept its old text, no message); a three-line drag cut the last line to its first word; a numeric-token double-click on '4711' did nothing.
**Cause:** run-mode click-time grouping returns a whole proven show for a click on any of its words, with `target_span_id` = the show's FIRST word (the edit target). The browse selection used that same id for the drag start (view) and for the drag end and the char context (model), so every point inside the show became its first word; the same-run character clip then kept nothing or only that word.
**Fix:** `TextHit.hit_span_id` carries the run geometrically under the point (all three run/paragraph branches, also when a reopen anchor won the edit target: after an edit the show's group anchor resolves to its first member, which broke selection and char context on the edited line the same way; None on the block fallback). Browse code reads a hit only through `PDFModel._browse_span_id` / `_browse_run_at_point_unrotated`: drag end in `get_text_selection_lines` and `get_text_selection_snapshot_from_run`, the run in `get_char_context_at_point`; the view stores `hit_span_id` as the drag start; `get_text_selection_lines` also re-maps a start id that is the press point's edit target (or one of its members) to the word under `start_point`. Edit paths (`_create_text_editor`, `_hit_matches_open_editor`, hover outline) keep `target_span_id` and the show union.
**Rule:** an edit-target id is not a location. Code that asks "which glyphs are under this point" must read `hit_span_id`, never `target_span_id`, and its tests must press on a LATER word of a multi-word show (assert `len(member_span_ids) > 1`), also after an edit of it (reopen anchor present), not pass `runs[i].span_id` directly.
**Not fixed / scope:** copied text has no spaces between words (also for one-word-per-show lines; the char-level clip only keeps glyph boxes the index assigns to runs), tracked separately in TODOS. Paragraph mode was already per-run.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `view/text_selection.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_text_selection.py` (`test_grouped_show_*`, incl. `..._after_an_edit_...`), `test_scripts/test_browse_selection_gui_regressions.py` (`test_start_text_selection_stores_word_under_press_not_show_first_word`)


## A pasted control character in a new text box lost the text after it, or drew a replacement glyph (F16-PASTE-1)

**Area:** `model/text_normalization.py` (`strip_unrenderable_controls`), `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`_insert_textbox_visual_content`, `_textbox_markup`), `model/tools/watermark_tool.py` (`_coerce_wm`, `add_watermark`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`add_textbox`)
**Symptom:** in add-text mode, pasting 'Ab', NUL (U+0000), SOH (U+0001), 'Cd' committed a text box (undo depth 1, no notice) whose page and saved text layer read only 'Ab': 'Cd' was gone, while the marker payload still held the full string, so a later move or rotate re-inserted it with the same loss. Pasting 'Ab', VT (U+000B), FF (U+000C), 'Cd' drew a visible replacement glyph (U+0239 in the text layer) between the words. The edit-existing path was already safe (its rebuild verification refuses NUL); add-textbox had no check at all.
**Cause:** `_textbox_markup` put the raw string into the htmlbox HTML (`html.escape` only). MuPDF's HTML engine stops at an embedded NUL and draws every other C0/C1 control code, DEL and noncharacter as a replacement glyph (measured for U+0001..U+001F except tab, LF and CR, U+007F, U+0080..U+009F, U+FFFE, U+FFFF; FF reads back as a space). Nothing compared the inserted text with the request.
**Fix:** one Qt-free helper, `strip_unrenderable_controls`, removes C0/C1 controls, DEL and noncharacters and folds CR LF / lone CR to LF; tab and LF stay. It runs at the text-box chokepoint `_insert_textbox_visual_content` (add, move and rotate all enter there; the function returns the cleaned `text` and the three marker writers store THAT, not the raw string), inside `_textbox_markup` (so the insert and the text-layer reference of the object ops lay out the same story, also for a marker an older build stored with controls), in `PDFController.add_textbox` (a paste of only controls is a silent no-op like blank text) and in the watermark text chokepoint `_coerce_wm` + `add_watermark` (a watermark of only controls is refused). Owner-visible behaviour: silent removal at the model chokepoints (the characters have no visible form); since S17-PASTE-NOTICE the inline editor also reports a paste's removals in the status bar.
**Rule:** text a user types or pastes into anything that DRAWS (htmlbox, `insert_text`) enters through one sanitizer, and the marker/payload stores the sanitized string; a draw path with no read-back check must not trust the clipboard. The edit-existing rebuild keeps its own refusal (it must not silently change text that is already on the page).
**Not fixed / scope:** private-use characters (U+E000) in a new text box are drawn blank and read back as NUL in the text layer; U+2028/U+2029 are kept (drawn as a break-less mark, text layer keeps them); lone surrogates cannot come from Qt. The repro injects QMimeData directly; the Windows clipboard NUL-terminates CF_UNICODETEXT, so a NUL may never reach the app from a real copy (VT/FF and the other controls do).
**File:** `model/text_normalization.py`, `model/pdf_object_ops.py`, `model/tools/watermark_tool.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_text_normalization.py` (`test_strip_controls_*`), `test_scripts/test_add_textbox_atomic.py` (`..._pasted_control_characters`, `..._only_control_characters_...`, `test_textbox_markup_strips_controls_...`, `test_move_of_a_legacy_marker_with_control_characters_redraws_clean`), `test_scripts/test_security_watermark_coercion.py`, `test_scripts/test_text_edit_refusal_messages.py` (`test_add_textbox_*control*`)

## An image in pasted HTML became U+FFFC and was committed as a dashed "OBJ" box (F16-PASTE-2)

**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`InlineTextEditor.insertFromMimeData`), `model/text_normalization.py` (`strip_unrenderable_controls`), `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_is_identityless_placeholder`, `_PLACEHOLDER_CHARS`, `_unkeepable_glyph_fate`, `_verify_rebuild_edit`)
**Symptom:** pasting browser or Word HTML that contains an `<img>` into the inline editor put an image object in the `QTextEdit`; `toPlainText()` read it as U+FFFC (OBJECT REPLACEMENT CHARACTER). Edit-existing: the preview refused ("the original font lacks this character"), the user accepted the rebuild consent (which named only the missing-font reason) and the rebuild committed `Hi U+FFFC X` with a dashed "OBJ" box; U+FFFC stayed in the saved text layer. Add-textbox: the same paste committed `Logo U+FFFC X` and the box with no prompt, toast or refusal. The pasted image itself was dropped silently in both cases.
**Cause:** (1) the editor kept QTextEdit's default rich-text paste. (2) U+FFFC is category So and has a name, so `_is_identityless_placeholder` (Cc/Co/Cs/Cn and U+FFFD) did not flag it. (3) htmlbox draws U+FFFC as a dashed "OBJ" box AND writes it back as itself, so the lossy-layer comparison in `_verify_rebuild_edit` never saw it as lost (every other placeholder is refused through exactly that comparison). (4) The add-textbox sanitizer (F16-PASTE-1) listed only controls and noncharacters.
**Fix:** U+FFFC is an inline-object anchor, never a character a text layer means. `InlineTextEditor.insertFromMimeData` pastes PLAIN text only (the clipboard's text, else the HTML flattened with `QTextDocumentFragment`) and drops U+FFFC, so the image never enters the editor (formatting of a paste never reached the commit anyway). `strip_unrenderable_controls` also removes U+FFFC (text-box chokepoint, `PDFController.add_textbox`, watermark chokepoint; the marker stores the cleaned string; a paste of only anchors is a silent no-op like blank text). `_is_identityless_placeholder` now includes U+FFFC (fate "replaced": the OBJ box), so an UNTOUCHED U+FFFC in the source text is reported in the consent dialog like U+FFFD, and one the user TYPED is never acknowledgeable. `_verify_rebuild_edit` refuses any placeholder that is not in the acknowledged own-glyph report BEFORE the lossy-layer comparison (reason `unidentifiable_glyphs_not_acknowledged`, page rolled back), so a placeholder that round-trips through the text layer cannot slip through.
**Rule:** a character class that must never be committed needs an explicit refusal, not only the "requested text missing from the page" comparison: a glyph that htmlbox draws AND reads back passes that comparison. Text that arrives through the clipboard enters the editor as plain text.
**Not fixed / scope:** the edit-existing consent dialog still names only the missing-font reason when a placeholder was typed (the rebuild is then refused after the consent, the same as a typed U+FFFD; the editor-side strip is what prevents it in practice). A pasted image is dropped (a status-bar notice since S17-PASTE-NOTICE) and leaves its surrounding spaces ("Logo  X"); pasting an image as a PDF image object is not offered. The explicit check is generic over `_is_unkeepable_glyph`, so any other placeholder that round-trips would be covered too (none known).
**File:** `view/text_editing.py`, `model/text_normalization.py`, `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_inline_editor_paste.py`, `test_scripts/test_text_normalization.py` (`test_strip_controls_removes_the_object_replacement_character`), `test_scripts/test_add_textbox_atomic.py` (`..._pasted_image_anchor_...`), `test_scripts/test_security_watermark_coercion.py`, `test_scripts/test_text_edit_refusal_messages.py` (`test_add_textbox_*image_anchor*`), `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`fffc` cases of the F11 tests, `object_replacement_char` cases of the F10 test, `test_a_typed_placeholder_is_refused_even_when_acknowledged[fffc]`)

## A paste into the inline editor removed images and control characters without telling the user (S17-PASTE-NOTICE)

**Area:** `view/text_editing.py` (`InlineTextEditor.insertFromMimeData`, `paste_cleaned`, `paste_cleaned_notice`, `TextEditManager._on_editor_paste_cleaned`), `utils/text_chars.py`, `model/text_normalization.py`
**Symptom:** after F16-PASTE-1/2 a paste with an `<img>` or with control characters (BEL, NUL, VT ...) produced no word at all: the image vanished, and the control characters were only dropped later, at commit, inside the model. The owner (2026-10-12) asked for a short zh-TW status-bar notice saying what was removed, nothing for a clean paste.
**Cause:** the editor only removed U+FFFC; control characters stayed in the editor text until the model's `strip_unrenderable_controls` ran at commit, so at paste time nothing "had been removed" to report, and the View may not call the model's helper (view-no-model).
**Fix:** the unrenderable character set moved to the Qt-free, layer-neutral `utils/text_chars.py` (`split_unrenderable`, `count_unrenderable`); the model's `strip_unrenderable_controls` is now a thin wrapper over it (one definition). `insertFromMimeData` flattens to plain text, strips with `split_unrenderable` (CR LF folded, not counted) and emits `paste_cleaned(controls, images)` only when something was removed; the images count is the larger of the U+FFFC in the text and in the HTML flattened with `QTextDocumentFragment` (a browser copy carries text/plain without the image next to text/html with it; the HTML is only parsed when there is no plain text or it contains `<img`). `TextEditManager` connects the signal (guarded with `getattr`: test fakes have no such signal) and shows `paste_cleaned_notice(...)` through `status_bar.showMessage(..., 4000)`, the same channel as the browse copy message. The View reports through the signal; it never calls the model.
**Rule:** a "we cleaned your input" notice has to be raised at the layer that does the cleaning, at the moment it happens; when two layers must agree on what is unrenderable, share one definition in `utils/` instead of copying it. Keep the model's strip as the backstop for text that arrives some other way.
**Not fixed / scope:** the watermark dialog's own `QTextEdit` still accepts a rich paste and relies on the model strip with no notice; the status message can be replaced by the next `_update_status_bar` refresh before its 4 s end; pasting an image as an image object is a TODOS item.
**File:** `view/text_editing.py`, `utils/text_chars.py`, `model/text_normalization.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_inline_editor_paste.py` (S17 cases), `test_scripts/test_text_commit_editor_mouse_gestures.py` (`test_pasting_controls_and_an_image_into_the_open_editor_shows_a_zh_tw_status_notice`)

## Browse copy dropped every inter-word space, and a right-to-left line copied nothing (F16-COPY-2)

**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`get_text_selection_lines`), `model/selection_text.py`
**Symptom:** a whole-line drag + Ctrl+C copied 'Kernedgapwords' for a pdfTeX line `[(Kerned) -350 (gap) -350 (words)] TJ`, '10kgitem' for '10 kg item' (no-break space), 'cafénaïve' for 'café naïve', 'Total:42' + Hebrew for 'Total: 42 Hebrew'; a pure Hebrew/Arabic line copied the empty string (a left-to-right or right-to-left drag alike); a cross-run drag on a bottom-to-top (run rotation 270) line copied the wrong glyphs ('ABClmnop' for 'CDEFGH ijkl').
**Cause:** (1) the run index splits a line at whitespace and owns no space glyph, and `get_text_selection_lines` joined only the glyphs of the selected runs with '', so the gap (a plain space, a no-break space, a TJ kerning gap that MuPDF reports as a space) never reached the copy. (2) The boundary clip kept 'coord >= first pointer' / 'coord <= last pointer', i.e. assumed every run reads towards larger coordinates; right-to-left runs (logical order since F15-RTL-ORDER) and the 270-degree quarter turn read the other way, so the kept set was empty or the wrong half.
**Fix:** `model/selection_text.py` (Qt-free): `whitespace_chars(rawdict)` collects the page's whitespace glyphs once per call, `whitespace_between_runs(chars, left, right)` returns those lying strictly between two consecutive selected runs of a line (outside the 0.5 pt run-edge tolerance, so a glyph a run already owns is not copied twice), `clip_directions(slice_runs)` gives the first / last boundary run its clip direction from the physical order of the slice's runs (alone on the slice: its own reading direction: right-to-left, 270 degrees = -1). `get_text_selection_lines` inserts the gap glyphs between runs that kept glyphs and clips with those directions. The copied text now equals `page.get_text` for the line, in logical order for Hebrew.
**Rule:** text assembled from the index's runs is NOT the page's text: anything the index excludes (whitespace, kerning gaps) must be taken from the page extraction, and any 'from here onward' comparison on a coordinate must take the run's reading direction (script AND rotation: right-to-left, both quarter turns and the half turn; see F17-COPY-180) into account. Verify copy with a real drag and `page.get_text` as the oracle on kerned, no-break-space, combining and Hebrew lines.
**Not fixed / scope:** two runs far apart on one visual line with no whitespace glyph between them (table columns) join without a separator; a mixed-direction line with a selection ending inside an embedded opposite-direction word is a logical (not visual) selection; the numeric double-click and `get_text_selection_snapshot_from_run` already joined runs with ' '.
**File:** `model/selection_text.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_text_selection.py` (`test_whole_line_drag_copies_the_page_text_including_gaps`, `test_rtl_partial_drag_selects_a_logical_substring_in_both_directions`, `test_vertical_run_cross_run_drag_follows_the_reading_direction`, `test_selection_text_helpers_edges`, and the exact-text `test_grouped_show_*`)

## Browse copy and the char context read every word of a /Rotate 180 page backwards, and right-to-left text on a quarter turn the same way (F17-COPY-180)

**Area:** `model/selection_text.py` (`reading_sign`, `order_run_glyphs`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`_get_chars_in_run_unrotated`, `get_text_selection_lines`, `get_char_context_at_point`)
**Symptom:** (Round 17.) On a `/Rotate 180` page whose text reads upright (`insert_htmlbox(..., rotate=180)`, Helvetica 14 pt) a whole-line drag + Ctrl+C copied `olleH evarb wen dlrow`; mid-second-word to mid-third-word copied `ev en` (`/Rotate 0`: `ve ne`); a two-line drag from the middle of `bravo` to the middle of `charlie` copied `arb\neilr` (`vo\ncha`); `get_char_context_at_point` on the first letter returned `('olleH', 4)` (`('Hello', 0)`), so a numeric double-click selected a number backwards. Hebrew on a `/Rotate 90` or `/Rotate 270` page (run rotation 270 / 90) copied every word letter-reversed and the char-context index was mirrored; Hebrew at `/Rotate 180` was right for a one-line drag and wrong for a two-line drag. The coarse paths (`get_text_selection_snapshot`, `..._from_run`, the highlight rects) were right everywhere.
**Cause:** one reading-direction model, two halves, both incomplete. (1) `reading_sign` returned -1 only for rotation 270 and right-to-left text; upright text on a `/Rotate 180` page is written towards -x (run rotation 180), so a one-run slice (the boundary row of a multi-row drag) was clipped the wrong way, and RTL on a quarter turn was never flipped. (2) `_get_chars_in_run_unrotated` ordered a horizontal non-RTL run by ascending x (reversed reading order at 180) and tested the quarter-turn branch BEFORE the right-to-left one, so a Hebrew run on a quarter turn got a position (y) order instead of MuPDF's traversal (= logical) order that F15-RTL-ORDER fixed for rotation 0. The kept glyph SET was already right whenever two or more runs shared the slice (physical order, `_direction_towards`) or the drag stayed in one run (`lo`/`hi`); only the glyph ORDER was wrong there, and `reading_sign` is reached only by one-run slices.
**Fix:** `reading_sign` is the rotation's base sign (+1 at 0 and 90, -1 at 180 and 270) negated for a run holding right-to-left letters: 0 -> +1 / -1, 90 -> +1 / -1, 180 -> -1 / +1, 270 -> -1 / +1 (Latin / RTL). New `order_run_glyphs(glyphs, rotation)` in the same Qt-free module is the glyph-order twin: right-to-left letters keep the traversal order at EVERY rotation; anything else is sorted along the reading axis (ascending x at 0, ascending y at 90, descending x with rows stacking upwards at 180, descending y at 270). `_get_chars_in_run_unrotated` ends in that call; its `inside` tolerance test was already rotation-correct and is unchanged.
**Rule:** a run's glyph list must line up with `run.text` index by index at every rotation and script, and every "from the pointer onward" comparison reads `reading_sign`; never assume +x or +y. A reading-direction rule is tested over the whole matrix: page `/Rotate` 0/90/180/270 x Latin/Hebrew, each drag described by its ON-SCREEN position (rects mapped with `page.rotation_matrix`), against the `/Rotate 0` result, with a two-line drag so the one-run slice path is hit.
**Not fixed / scope:** Tier 0 target derivation (`_tier0_target_from_resolve`) still orders a multi-run line by `origin.x`, so its `run_join` candidate text reads `world new brave Hello` on the same `/Rotate 180` line (probed; its dict-line proof refuses 180 by design (P6) and the source-show path is unaffected; the downstream effect was not probed). `_split_line_into_cells` keeps its `rotation != 180` guard. Text that is not axis-aligned snaps to the nearest of the four rotations, as before. Not eyeballed in the GUI.
**File:** `model/selection_text.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_text_selection.py` (`test_upright_line_copies_the_same_text_on_every_page_rotation`, `test_upright_two_line_drag_clips_each_boundary_word_on_every_page_rotation`, `test_run_glyphs_follow_the_run_text_on_every_page_rotation`, `test_upright_line_run_level_snapshots_read_the_same_on_every_page_rotation`, `test_reading_sign_covers_every_rotation_and_script`, `test_selection_text_helpers_edges`), `test_scripts/test_numeric_token_selection.py` (`test_model_character_context_reads_a_number_in_order_on_every_page_rotation`)

## Upright text on a /Rotate 180 page got char/word/search boxes 0.64 em off its ink, so a click on the text missed (GATE16-1)

**Area:** `model/page_content_text.py` (`upright_glyph_boxes`, `content_text`, `visible_text`, `visible_search`), `model/text_commit/interpretation.py` (`PageInterpretation.rawdict`), `model/text_commit/verify.py` (rawdict reads), `model/tools/search_tool.py`; PyMuPDF 1.27.1 `JM_char_quad`
**Symptom:** on a `/Rotate 180` page whose text reads upright on screen (Helvetica 20 pt, text matrix `-1 0 0 -1`), the index run box, `content_text(page, "words")`, the text-commit engine's rawdict glyph boxes and `page.search_for` rects all sat 11.3 pt (0.64 em) BELOW the ink on screen: run box (visual) y 195.65-215.65 against ink y 185-200. `get_text_info_at_point` at the ink centre and at the ink top returned `None` (only the bottom 3 pt of the glyphs hit), so the line could hardly be clicked for editing; search highlights and the neighbour-wall / overprint / growth-zone glyph boxes were off by the same amount. Identical on plain, CropBox-offset and negative-MediaBox pages; `/Rotate 0/90/270` and text drawn the normal way on a 180 page were right. The same effect made `test_font_stream_compaction.py::...rotated_offset_page[*-180]` fail only after another test had built a `PDFModel` (word box 15.35 pt below the box top, ink at 6.00 pt for every rotation).
**Cause:** upright text on a 180 page is drawn upside down in unrotated space, so its stext line direction is exactly (-1, 0). PyMuPDF's `JM_char_quad` (used by every dict/rawdict/words/search extraction) re-computes a char quad whenever `small_glyph_heights` is on (the app's production flag, `PDFModel.__init__`) or the font's ascender-descender is below 1; for `dir.x == -1` it sets `trm.d = 1`, i.e. treats the line as a LEFT-RIGHT MIRROR (`-1 0 0 1`), and puts the ascender above the baseline. For a 180-degree glyph that is the reflection of the right box about the char's baseline: right `[oy + dsc, oy + asc]`, reported `[oy - asc, oy - dsc]`. With the flag off and a sane font PyMuPDF keeps MuPDF's own quad, which is right, which is why the effect looked like test-order pollution.
**Fix:** `model/page_content_text.upright_glyph_boxes` walks the text page once (cached on it), and for each char on a (-1, 0) line whose MuPDF quad is upside down but whose PyMuPDF quad (`fitz.JM_char_quad`) is not, reflects the char, span, line and block boxes (dict/rawdict, matched by char origin) and the words (matched by block/line number) about the baseline; a true mirror (upright glyphs) is left alone, and a page without a (-1, 0) line returns before the walk. `content_text` applies it to dict/rawdict/words; `visible_text(page, option)` is the corrected `page.get_text` for the verifier (all four rawdict reads in `verify.py`); `PageInterpretation.rawdict` corrects its own text page; `visible_search` replaces `page.search_for` in the search tool. The compaction test now judges placement by rendered ink, and `test_scripts/conftest.py` pins the production flags around every test (see the small_glyph_heights entry above).
**Rule:** never key a box correction on the page rotation or on the flag: key it on what the extractor reported versus what MuPDF measured. Judge placement tests by rendered ink, not by an extraction box that a process-global flag can move.
**Not fixed / scope:** the `"blocks"` option (block tuples have no line identity) and `clip=` plain-text selection (a char counts when its box merely overlaps the clip, which the mirrored box still does) are not corrected; vertical writing mode is untouched (PyMuPDF never re-computes it).
**File:** `model/page_content_text.py`, `model/text_commit/interpretation.py`, `model/text_commit/verify.py`, `model/tools/search_tool.py`, `test_scripts/conftest.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_text_geometry_page_rotation.py` (`test_upright_180_*`, `test_mirrored_text_box_stays_on_its_ink_guard`, `test_text_commit_verify_reads_glyph_boxes_through_the_upright_helper`), `test_scripts/test_font_stream_compaction.py`, `test_scripts/test_pymupdf_flag_hygiene.py`, `test_scripts/test_environment_pins.py`

## A longer right-to-left word kept its LEFT edge and grew right; the owner rule is its RIGHT edge (D-RTL-GROW)

**Area:** `model/rtl_text.py` (`grows_right_to_left`), `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_start_point`, `_start_glyph_origin`, `_drawn_text_start`, `_align_htmlbox_rect`, `_place_htmlbox_at_origin`, `_rebuild_insert_markup`, `_apply_redact_insert_body`, `_classify_insert_path`, `_replay_protected_span_as_html`, `_protected_span_markup`, `_protected_span_drawn_in_place`, `_push_down_span_start`, `_push_down_overlapping_text`)
**Symptom:** (Round 16 decisions pass; owner decision after round 15: a longer RTL word keeps its right edge and grows left.) A consented rebuild of the Hebrew word 'שלום' (right edge x 399.0) to one more letter drew it at x 369.9..403.5, and to two words at 369.9..428.7: the left edge stayed and the word grew right. On a /Rotate 90 or /Rotate 180 page it grew the same way on the displayed page. A shorter word shrank toward its left edge. The neighbour wall was on the wrong side: a Hebrew word with text on its right was wrapped to two lines (height 27.3 pt instead of 13.6 pt), while text on its left was never a wall. A protected or pushed-down Hebrew neighbour drawn tighter than its font's advances was replayed on its left edge, so its right edge moved by about 4.5 pt.
**Cause:** Every placement used the left-to-right start (`_start_point`: the smallest origin along the writing direction at rotation 0). The htmlbox markup was a left-to-right paragraph, left-aligned in its box. The in-place box was pinned on its left edge, with the wall and the neighbour check on the right. Only the upside-down case (F16-2) mirrored the box.
**Fix:** There is one direction rule, `grows_right_to_left(text, paragraph)`. A run with no RTL letter is left-to-right (unchanged). A run with RTL letters and no LTR letter is right-to-left. A run with both follows the paragraph's base direction: the first strong character of the index block (UAX#9 P2), or the run's own first strong character when the block has none. `_spans_grow_right_to_left` applies the rule to an edit's members (in reading order) and to each replayed neighbour; the push-down applies it with the dict block's text. `_start_point(rtl=True)` takes the FAR advance edge of the glyph or run boxes along the writing direction (largest x1 upright, smallest x0 at 180, largest y1 reading down, smallest y0 reading up) on the first line's baseline. The target side (`_start_glyph_origin`, `_span_anchor`, `_push_down_span_start`) and the probe side (`_drawn_text_start`) both use it. An RTL markup gets `_RTL_BASE_CSS` (`body { direction: rtl; }`: lines right-aligned, neutral punctuation on the RTL side). It is added in the ONE builder of each markup, so the rebuild and its verification reference, the protected replay and its validation reference, and the push-down all match. In `_apply_redact_insert_body`, `grows_left` (box pinned on its right edge, the left wall `_left_wall`, the neighbour on the left) is `(rotation == 180) XOR rtl`. The line-stacking half is `stacks_up` (rotation 180 only: wrap ceiling, no push-down). A quarter turn uses `grows_up = reads_up XOR rtl` for the column growth, the neighbour and the binary shrink, while `reads_up` still names the first-line side. A dragged RTL edit is translated by its start edge. `_classify_insert_path(rtl=True)` always returns htmlbox. `_protected_span_drawn_in_place` matches the replay on the same right edge (`_glyph_start`).
**Rule:** The growth direction comes from the text's direction, not from the page rotation. The start edge is where reading starts (the right edge for RTL), and the pinned box edge, the wall, the neighbour side and the placement measure all follow it. Line stacking follows the rotation. Measure an RTL start by an advance EDGE, never by an origin.
**Not fixed / scope:** Tier 0 never targets RTL text (the F15-RTL-ORDER gate), so it places no RTL run. A probe of an LTR word in a CID TrueType font retyped as Hebrew was refused `no_source_match`. If Tier 0 gains a CID leg, an RTL replacement over an LTR operand needs a gate in the target derivation that preview and commit share. A run without RTL letters (digits or punctuation only) inside a Hebrew paragraph stays left-to-right, as Tier 0 treats it. (The legacy htmlbox live preview used to lay RTL text out left-aligned in the editor frame; fixed, see D-RTL-PREVIEW.) A Hebrew word with a final full stop inside an English paragraph now draws the stop on its left (RTL side). Not checked in the real GUI.
**File:** `model/rtl_text.py`, `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_rtl_edit_growth.py` (`test_rtl_rebuild_keeps_the_right_edge_and_grows_left[0|90|180 x grow_letter|grow_word|shrink]`, `test_rtl_growth_is_walled_by_the_neighbour_on_its_left`, `test_rtl_growth_is_not_walled_by_text_on_its_right`, `test_rtl_growth_stops_at_the_left_page_edge`, guard `test_ltr_rebuild_still_keeps_its_left_edge`, `test_grows_right_to_left_rule`, `test_align_htmlbox_rect_puts_the_right_to_left_end_on_the_anchor[0|90|180|270]`, `test_protected_rtl_neighbour_replay_keeps_its_right_edge`, `test_push_down_keeps_a_right_to_left_line_on_its_right_edge`, `test_rtl_drag_translates_the_right_edge[-30|200]`), `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_f15vm2_rtl_rebuild_keeps_the_runs_right_edge_and_baseline`)

## The legacy live preview laid a Hebrew run out left-aligned while the commit keeps its right edge (D-RTL-PREVIEW)

**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`preview_insert_css`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`build_preview_insert_css`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`build_insert_preview_html`), `view/text_editing.py` (`PreviewRenderer.render`, its `model=` shim and frame cache key)
**Symptom:** (Round 17.) With `engine="legacy"` (so `preview="legacy"`) the htmlbox interim frame of an edited Hebrew run drew the word at the LEFT of the editor frame: in a 200 x 30 pt box the preview ink of 'שלום' was x 201.0..230.9 while the committed rebuild kept its right edge (x 369.1..399.0), a 168 pt gap; for 'שלום עולם' the gap was 137.6 pt. The word jumped to the other side of the box on commit. The shipped tiered + plan default never paints this frame for an edited run, and add_new commits left-to-right too, so neither was affected.
**Cause:** D-RTL-GROW added `_RTL_BASE_CSS` to every COMMIT-side markup builder, but the preview markup is built by a separate path (`build_insert_preview_html` and the view's model shim) that only knew `_build_insert_css`, so the two layouts diverged. The preview call also carried no information about WHICH run was being edited, and the renderer's frame cache key had no direction in it.
**Fix:** One CSS builder, `pdf_text_edit.preview_insert_css(model, size, color, font_hint, line_height, member_spans)` (`PDFModel.build_preview_insert_css`): `_build_insert_css` plus `_RTL_BASE_CSS` when `_spans_grow_right_to_left` holds for the edited runs, the commit's own rule over the run being edited (since F17-RTL-LATIN also over the typed text, see that entry). The controller's public builder takes the edited runs as an opaque `member_spans` argument (the view already holds them and passes them through, it imports no model code); `PreviewRenderer.render` forwards them, its `model=` compatibility shim goes through the same model method, and its frame cache key now includes the runs' span ids so a cached right-to-left frame is never shown for another box. `member_spans` empty or `None` (add_new) keeps the unchanged left-to-right markup.
**Rule:** Every builder of htmlbox markup that stands for a commit takes its base direction from `preview_insert_css` / `_RTL_BASE_CSS` keyed by the EDITED run AND the typed text (F17-RTL-LATIN: an RTL run retyped as Latin text is left-to-right in both). A new route that draws the interim frame must go through the controller's builder.
**Not fixed / scope:** The no-builder, no-model fallback inside `PreviewRenderer` (unit isolation only, never wired in the app) stays left-to-right. The editor frame's minimum-width floor pads the frame on its visual right at 0/180, so for a run narrower than the floor the right-aligned preview sits at the padded edge, not at the run's own right edge. Not checked in the real GUI.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`, `view/text_editing.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_rtl_edit_growth.py` (`test_preview_of_an_rtl_edit_ends_on_the_edge_the_commit_keeps[2 texts]`, `test_preview_markup_direction_follows_the_edited_run`, `test_preview_renderer_model_shim_lays_out_rtl_too`, `test_preview_frame_cache_does_not_cross_directions`)

## A Hebrew word retyped as Latin text was laid out right-to-left: the full stop moved and brackets were refused (F17-RTL-LATIN)

**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_spans_grow_right_to_left`, `_rebuild_insert_markup`, `preview_insert_css`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`build_preview_insert_css`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`build_insert_preview_html`), `view/text_editing.py` (`PreviewRenderer` model shim)
**Symptom:** (Round 17.) A consented legacy rebuild of the Hebrew word 'שלום' (`dir=rtl`) typed as 'Hello world.' committed the visual line '.Hello world' (the full stop on the left, the text layer reading 'Hello world' without it); 'v1.2-beta!' committed as '!v1.2-beta'; 'Price (USD)' was refused `the glyphs for U+0029 are not drawn on the page after the insert (2 missing)` and rolled back (the bidi mirroring of the brackets). The same edits on an LTR word, or with the direction forced LTR, commit exactly as typed.
**Cause:** D-RTL-GROW decided the layout direction of an edit from the OLD runs only (`_spans_grow_right_to_left(model, member_spans)`), so any edit of a Hebrew run got `_RTL_BASE_CSS` (`body { direction: rtl; }`) whatever it was retyped as. `grows_right_to_left`'s own first rule says text with no RTL letter is left-to-right. The live preview builder had the same shape (and a test pinned it: "the direction is the run's, not the typed text's").
**Fix:** `_spans_grow_right_to_left(model, spans, new_text=None)`: the old runs still say WHICH EDGE the box is pinned on (an RTL run keeps its right edge), and the answer is yes only when the text that will be DRAWN is right-to-left too (`grows_right_to_left(new_text, paragraph)`, the paragraph being the one that holds the edited run). `_rebuild_insert_markup` (the ONE builder of the rebuild markup, shared by the insert and its verification reference) passes `new_text`; `preview_insert_css` / `PDFModel.build_preview_insert_css` / `PDFController.build_insert_preview_html` / the `PreviewRenderer` model shim pass the typed text, so the preview frame and the commit still share one rule (the frame cache key already holds the text). A replayed neighbour (protected span, push-down) redraws its own old text, so it keeps `new_text=None`.
**Rule:** The layout direction of markup comes from the text being drawn; the old run only decides the anchor edge. Any new builder of edit markup passes the new text to `_spans_grow_right_to_left`; a replay of existing text passes none.
**Not fixed / scope:** The opposite direction is unchanged: a Latin run retyped as Hebrew (old run not RTL) stays left-to-right, as before D-RTL-GROW, because the old run's left edge is where that text started; a trailing full stop of such Hebrew text is then drawn on its right (LTR paragraph). A mixed new text (Hebrew and Latin letters) follows the base direction of the paragraph being edited, so 'Hello שלום' typed into a Hebrew paragraph stays right-to-left. An edit to the empty string is left-to-right (nothing is drawn). Not checked in the real GUI.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`, `view/text_editing.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_rtl_edit_growth.py` (`test_rtl_run_retyped_as_latin_is_laid_out_left_to_right[4 texts]`, `test_edit_direction_is_the_old_run_and_the_new_text[13 cases]`, `test_preview_direction_follows_the_typed_text`, `test_preview_markup_direction_follows_the_edited_run`)

## The overprint guard refused an edit that printed over a diagonal watermark's ink (D-DIAG-INK)

**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_new_text_overprints`, `_glyph_ink_core`, `_cores_overlap`, `_is_axis_aligned_dir`)
**Symptom:** (Round 16, owner decision after round 15.) On a page with a 45-degree grey `DRAFT COPY` watermark whose ink crosses the edited line, `John` -> `Johnathan Smithers` and `John` -> `Johnny B` were rolled back with `TEXT_DOES_NOT_FIT` ("'h' over 'D'"), because the new word's ink lay on the watermark's ink. The owner decided that edited text may print over off-axis runs.
**Cause:** after F15-VF4OV-DIAGONAL the guard measured a diagonal glyph's ink on its real turned box, so real overlap with the new text was (correctly, by the F14-VF4-WRAP rule) a collision. The rule itself, not the geometry, was what the owner changed.
**Fix:** `_new_text_overprints` takes its `untouched` set only from glyphs whose writing direction is on a page axis (`_is_axis_aligned_dir`, the test the neighbour wall and the wrap floor already use). Off-axis runs are never a collision; horizontal and vertical runs (0/90/180/270) still block, as does the neighbour wall. The watermark run is not touched by the edit: it is erased only if the redaction reaches it (a different refusal, `UNTOUCHED_TEXT_WOULD_BE_LOST`) and is otherwise replayed or left as is; the tests compare its glyphs, origins, directions and every pixel outside the edited line before and after. The turned-core branch of `_glyph_ink_core` stays for an added off-axis glyph.
**Rule:** whether a thing blocks an edit is decided by one predicate (`_is_axis_aligned_dir`) at every site: wall, floor and ink guard. Do not special-case a site.
**Not changed here, settled afterwards:** a watermark glyph that lies under the OLD word's own box was still removed by the redaction, and the edit was refused as `UNTOUCHED_TEXT_WOULD_BE_LOST` (e.g. pivot (120, 350) of the fixture). The owner decided to protect it (S17-WMARK-UNDER, below).
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_edit_may_print_over_a_diagonal_watermark_and_leaves_it_intact[legacy|tiered x 2 texts]`, `test_new_text_overprints_skips_off_axis_untouched_glyphs_only`, guards `test_a_horizontal_neighbour_still_blocks_next_to_a_diagonal_watermark`, `test_a_vertical_run_still_blocks_next_to_a_diagonal_watermark`)

## Old object markers that no longer matched the page made Move / Rotate / Delete fail silently, and Delete removed only the hidden marker (D-OLD-MARKERS)

**Area:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`_resolve_marker_image_invocation`, `_repair_image_marker`, `_image_drawing_may_remain`, `_image_slots_claimed_by_other_markers`, `_resolve_textbox_marker`, `_repair_textbox_marker`, `_single_form_drawing`, `_page_form_placements`, `_form_matrix_angle`, `_refuse`, `_record_outcome`, `move_object`, `rotate_object`, `delete_objects_atomic`), `model/object_op_refusal.py`, `controller/object_op_refusals.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`move_object`, `resize_object`, `rotate_object`, `delete_object`)
**Symptom:** (Round 16 decisions pass; owner decision after round 15: repair + message.) An app image saved by a build before F15-4 (marker with the pre-rotation rect and the rotated angle, or with the 4:3 insert rect around a letterboxed picture) could not be moved, resized or rotated: the verb returned `False` and nothing was said. Delete returned `True` but removed only the hidden marker; the picture stayed drawn and was then hit as a native image. A textbox whose marker text was stale (edited by a build without the marker sync) was refused silently, as were the F13-VF-2b refusal (the box holds page text it does not own) and a lossy-text marker after an edit (F16-1 follow-up).
**Cause:** resolution matched the marker's rect within 2 pt; an old marker's rect never does. Delete treated "no candidate within 2 pt" as an orphaned marker and cleaned it up. Every object verb returned a bare `bool` and `PDFController` returned on `False` without a word.
**Fix:** (1) Repair. An unresolved image marker is re-resolved when exactly ONE drawn placement has its digest (the recorded one, else the recorded xref's), its angle (1 degree) and its centre (1.5 pt per axis; rotation about the centre and letterboxing keep it) and no other marker on the page resolves to it; the marker then records that drawing (`_sync_image_marker_to_drawn`). A textbox marker the page no longer matches is re-resolved when exactly ONE Form XObject the page invokes directly, drawn by nothing else and not at the box of another textbox marker that resolves, shares its centre and its `/Matrix` angle and is ALL the content drawn in its box (emptying it removes exactly the characters of the words centred there, adds none); the marker takes that drawing's box and text (the stored text when it reproduces the drawing, else the drawing's lines joined with `\n`), accepted only when htmlbox, given it, writes the same characters, the same inked glyphs and the same line count, so a lossy text layer is never written back. A `content_unsynced` marker (this build's own flag) is not repaired. The move/rotate `if not xref` guards are gone: a marker without an xref resolves by digest and geometry. (2) Message. Every refusal goes through `_refuse(model, ObjectOpRefusal.X)`; the public verbs (`_record_outcome`) store an `ObjectOpRefused(reason, kind, id)` on `PDFModel.last_object_op_refusal` (`OPERATION_FAILED` when no site named one, `None` after a success). The Controller reads it right after the call and shows ONE zh-TW sentence through `show_error` (`object_refusal_message`); a batch move that partly refuses says how many of how many did not move (`batch_refusal_message`), and a refused batch delete says none of the N was deleted (`atomic_delete_refusal_message`). (3) Delete keeps both: an unresolved image marker is cleaned up alone only when no unclaimed placement of its picture touches its rect or shares its centre (`_image_drawing_may_remain`), else it refuses `IMAGE_NOT_LOCATED`.
**Rule:** an object verb never returns `False` without a reason code, and the Controller never drops one. Repair only on exactly one clear candidate; two equally good candidates, or one claimed by another marker, stay unresolved. Delete removes a marker alone only when nothing of its drawing can still be on the page.
**Behaviour change:** a stale-text textbox whose one htmlbox drawing holds everything in its box now moves/rotates/deletes with the text the page draws (it was refused); `test_textbox_with_stale_marker_text_is_repaired_from_its_one_drawing` replaces the refusal test. Delete of an old image marker whose picture is still drawn near it with no single candidate now refuses (it removed the marker alone).
**Behaviour change (w1b pass 2, owner decision 2026-10-21):** moving a textbox whose marker stores a rotation that `float()` accepts but `int()` rejects (for example the string `"90.5"`) now raises `ValueError` before the drawing is erased or the marker deleted: `_move_object_impl` evaluates `int(payload.get("rotation", 0))` as the last argument of `_reinsert_textbox`, before `_erase_textbox_drawing` runs (a `null` rotation raises `TypeError` at the same place; a JSON number such as `90.5` is truncated by `int()` and moves normally). Before, the move erased the drawing and deleted the marker and then raised, or, when the erase refused, returned `False` with the `TEXTBOX_OVER_PAGE_TEXT` refusal (the zh-TW sentence that the box holds page text that is not its own); that refusal is no longer shown for such a marker. What the user sees: the selection frame jumps to the drop position while the box stays drawn where it was, with no message, no undo step and no page refresh (the exception leaves `PDFController.move_object`, which has no handler, into the Qt slot call and reaches `sys.excepthook`, which the app does not replace, and the view, told of no refusal, rebases the frame).
**Not fixed / scope:** a textbox repair needs the box to be one htmlbox Form XObject: a box partly drawn as loose glyphs (a legacy edit), a tiny-canvas insert or a box on an offset-CropBox page whose form placement is shifted is refused with the message, not repaired. An Ext-B-only stale box has no comparable characters and is refused. The repair rewrites the marker inside the verb, so a verb that then fails for another reason leaves the corrected marker without an undo step (it is invisible). The View rebased the selection frame of a refused move; fixed in round 17, see the D-OBJ-FRAME entry.
**File:** `model/pdf_object_ops.py`, `model/object_op_refusal.py`, `controller/object_op_refusals.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_image_objects_model.py` (`test_old_image_marker_is_repaired_and_the_verb_changes_the_drawing[pre_rotation_rect|letterbox_4_3|letterbox_no_xref x move|resize|rotate|delete]`, `test_old_image_marker_without_one_clear_candidate_refuses_and_keeps_marker_and_drawing[twins|angle_mismatch x move|rotate|delete]`, `test_old_image_marker_saved_and_reopened_is_repaired[pre_rotation_rect|letterbox_4_3]`), `test_scripts/test_object_manipulation_model.py` (`test_textbox_with_stale_marker_text_is_repaired_from_its_one_drawing[rotate|move|delete x live|saved_and_reopened|page_rotate_90]`, `test_textbox_stale_marker_without_one_clear_drawing_refuses_with_a_reason[loose_glyphs_in_box|two_same_centre_drawings|drawing_of_another_box x rotate|move|delete]`, `test_textbox_marker_with_the_pre_rotation_rect_is_repaired_to_its_drawing[rotate|move]`, reason codes added to the F15-2, F13-VF-2b and F16-1 refusal tests), `test_scripts/test_object_controller_flow.py` (`test_refused_object_op_shows_one_plain_zh_tw_message[...]`, `test_batch_move_that_partly_refuses_says_how_many_objects_did_not_move`, `test_batch_move_that_fully_refuses_reports_every_object`, `test_batch_delete_refusal_says_no_object_was_deleted`, `test_every_object_refusal_code_has_a_plain_zh_tw_sentence`, `test_real_stale_textbox_refusal_reaches_the_message_box[move|rotate|delete]`, `test_real_ambiguous_old_image_marker_delete_reaches_the_message_box`)

## A wrap at the right-hand neighbour may break a word at its hyphen; a hyphen that opens the word left a line of just "-" (D-HYPHEN-WRAP)

**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`_latin_word_html`, `_convert_text_to_html`, `_build_multi_style_html`), `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_apply_redact_insert_body` strategy A/B/C, `_wrap_floor`, `_NO_WRAP_CSS`: unchanged)
**Symptom:** (Round 16 decisions pass; owner decision after round 15, TODOS F14-VF4-WRAP-REFLOW hyphen part.) F14-VF4-WRAP left open whether a wrap at the neighbour should break a word at its hyphen or keep the word on one line. `multicolumn.pdf` p1 `Two-Column` -> `Two-Colunm` (CMR17 17.2, the substitute font is wider than the 5 pt gap to `Document`) already gave `Two-` / `Colunm` in both engines, saved and reopened: the hyphen ends line 1, line 2 starts at the same x, `Document` does not move. The one bad case: a word that OPENS with a hyphen (`ab` -> `-abcdefghij` before a neighbour) came out as a line of just `-` followed by `abcdefghij` (shrunk, two lines).
**Cause:** the wrap is not code of ours: MuPDF's HTML line breaker (UAX #14) breaks after U+002D and U+2010, not after U+2011, and keeps a hyphen with a following digit (`-5`). It also breaks after `/`, U+2013 and U+2014, and at a soft hyphen it DRAWS a hyphen. A word-initial hyphen followed by a letter is a break opportunity for it, so the first line got only the `-`.
**Fix:** the decision is the behaviour that was already there, now pinned by tests: a wrap may break after an existing U+002D / U+2010 (hyphen stays at the end of line 1); U+2011 never breaks; a word without a hyphen keeps shrinking (floor 50 %) or being refused; with no room for a second line (`_wrap_floor` / `_NO_WRAP_CSS`) the hyphenated word is not broken either (shrink / refuse); no hyphen is inserted. The only code change is `_latin_word_html`: a word (one `_RE_HTML_TEXT_PARTS` token) that opens with U+002D / U+2010 run(s) followed by a non-digit puts that run in a `white-space: nowrap` span, which MuPDF does not break after, so `-abcdefghij` stays whole (one shrunk line, or `TEXT_DOES_NOT_FIT`) while `-ab-cdefghij` still breaks at its second hyphen. The legacy commit, the live preview (`PDFController` builds it with the same `_convert_text_to_html`) and the paragraph-mode builder share the helper; every other token (inner hyphens, `-5`, a bullet `- `, `--`) is byte-identical markup.
**Rule:** one rule for where a wrapped edit may break a word: after an existing hyphen that has a word character before it. Paragraph reflow is separate (`plans/paragraph-reflow.md`, not built).
**Not changed:** MuPDF's other break opportunities (`/`, en and em dash) keep wrapping as before; they are not hyphens and the decision did not cover them. A soft hyphen typed into the text is refused (`TARGET_NOT_PRESENT`, it is not on the page) rather than drawn as a hyphen. The Tier 0/1 engine never wraps (it falls to the legacy rebuild for a growing word), so both engines give the same result. Vertical (quarter-turn) edits wrap along the reading direction and are walled by `_vertical_neighbour_limit`; the hyphen rule is the same markup, not checked on rotated pages in the GUI.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_hyphen_wrap.py` (`test_multicolumn_title_wraps_at_its_hyphen`, `test_hyphenated_word_wraps_after_its_hyphen_against_a_neighbour[- | U+2010 x legacy|tiered]`, `test_every_hyphen_may_break_but_none_is_added`, `test_a_non_breaking_hyphen_never_breaks`, `test_a_word_without_a_hyphen_keeps_shrinking_or_refusing`, `test_no_room_below_means_no_break_even_at_a_hyphen`, `test_a_soft_hyphen_is_not_turned_into_a_drawn_hyphen`, red then green `test_a_hyphen_that_opens_the_word_is_not_a_break`, `test_markup_of_a_leading_hyphen_word_cannot_break_after_the_hyphen`, `test_markup_of_numbers_and_bullets_is_unchanged`, `test_multi_style_markup_has_the_same_rule`)

## Merging while the CURRENT document is encrypted failed with "document closed or encrypted" (S17-ENC-MERGE)

**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`compose_merged_document`, `active_document_is_encrypted`, `_open_emptied_encrypted_container`, `_prune_encrypted_container`, `_open_authenticated`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`merge_ordered_sources_into_current`, `save_ordered_sources_as_new`, `_choose_merge_encryption`), `view/pdf_view.py` (`ask_merge_encryption_choice`)
**Symptom:** (Round 17; F16-NAV-3 item 8, same at HEAD.) With an AES-256 user-password document open and authenticated, Merge PDFs (into the current tab or as a new file) raised `ValueError: document closed or encrypted` from `NavigationGraft.copy_pages` -> `insert_pdf`, before anything changed; MuPDF printed `aes padding out of range`.
**Cause:** `compose_merged_document` took the current document from `_capture_doc_snapshot()`, which is `encryption=KEEP` bytes, and reopened it with a bare `fitz.open("pdf", bytes)`: a locked handle, never authenticated. The merge container is a fresh plaintext `fitz.open()`, so even with the read fixed the result would have been written decrypted.
**Fix:** the owner chose ASK EACH TIME. The controller asks (`PDFView.ask_merge_encryption_choice`, zh-TW: keep encryption and permissions / save unencrypted / cancel) when the active document is encrypted (`PDFModel.active_document_is_encrypted`, the trailer `metadata['encryption']`, so owner-only encryption counts) and, for Save as new file, only when the list holds the current entry; cancel returns before any state change. The model reads an encrypted current document through `_open_numbering_clone` (authenticated, any password state) and builds the container by `keep_encryption`: unencrypted = the plain `fitz.open()` as before; keep = `_open_emptied_encrypted_container`, an authenticated clone of the live document emptied of its pages, catalog keys, page-tree attributes and metadata, so its `/Encrypt` dictionary survives and every `encryption=KEEP` save keeps the method, user AND owner passwords and permissions exactly (a re-encryption with new credentials could not know the owner password). After the graft `_prune_encrypted_container` round-trips it at `garbage=4` so the emptied pages' objects are not saved along. `_open_authenticated` is the one place a KEEP serialization is reopened and unlocked (`_open_numbering_clone` uses it too). Undo restores the pre-merge encrypted bytes and re-authenticates with the session password, which the unencrypted choice leaves in place on purpose; Save / Save As / secure save then follow the live handle's encryption.
**Rule:** never reopen a KEEP serialization of an encrypted document with a bare `fitz.open`; go through `_open_authenticated` / `_open_numbering_clone`. A container that must keep an encrypted document's encryption is a clone of that document, not a new document plus passwords. Read `needs_pass` only on a fresh handle (guard test `test_needs_pass_is_only_read_where_the_handle_is_known_unauthenticated` audits the function names).
**Not fixed / scope:** the unencrypted result keeps `session.password` / `auth_level` (undo needs them); a later optimize copy therefore skips its file-backed fast path (conservative, harmless). The kept container does not carry the old document's Info / XMP metadata, matching the plain merge. The dialog was driven with simulated button clicks, not by hand.
