**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`, `view/pdf_view.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_pdf_merge_workflow.py` (`test_compose_merged_document_*`, `test_merge_into_encrypted_current_*`, `test_merge_into_unencrypted_current_never_asks_about_encryption`, `test_save_merged_copy_with_encrypted_current_follows_the_choice`, `test_save_merged_copy_without_the_current_entry_does_not_ask`, `test_kept_encryption_container_carries_no_orphans_of_the_emptied_document`, `test_save_in_place_after_merge_into_encrypted_current_follows_the_choice`, `test_view_merge_encryption_question_maps_the_three_buttons`), `test_scripts/test_save_prunes_orphans.py` (needs_pass audit)

## Insert pages from file brought only the links: no source bookmarks, names or labels, and the document's own labels slid off their pages (S17-INSERT-NAV)

**Area:** `model/navigation_graft.py` (`NavigationGraft(into_existing=True)`, `_read_name_entries`, `_snapshot_existing`, `_label_rows`, `_write_labels`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`insert_pages_from_file`)
**Symptom:** (Round 17.) Inserting a 4 page source (3-level outline, `/Names /Dests` with a clashing `chap3` and `srcname`, `/PageLabels` prefix `S-`) at page 3 of a 6 page document with its own outline, names and labels left the bookmark panel without the source's rows, `srcname` unresolvable, and the labels `i, ii, iii, iv, v, vi, 1, 2, 3, ...`: the source's `S-1..S-4` were lost and the document's own `1, 2, 3` (and any page of its own, e.g. `ii`) read a different label than before because `/PageLabels` is indexed by page position and nothing re-expressed it after the pages moved.
**Cause:** `insert_pages_from_file` ran the graft as `NavigationGraft(doc, keep_names=False, outline=False, labels=False)` (F16-NAV-3 kept the document's navigation untouched). Page labels are the one navigation structure that is positional, not object-based, so "untouched" meant "moved off its pages". The graft's writers also assumed a fresh container: `_write_names` replaced `/Names /Dests` (dropping the document's own names) and `_rename_maps` started with no taken names.
**Fix:** owner decision (2026-10-12): import the source's bookmarks, import its named destinations (rename on a clash, links follow) and rebuild the page labels of the whole document. `NavigationGraft(dst, into_existing=True)` reads the document's navigation BEFORE the first `insert_pdf` (`_snapshot_existing`): the raw entries of its `/Names /Dests` tree plus the legacy catalog `/Dests` keys (`_read_name_entries`; the keys seed the taken set so the document's name wins and the source's becomes `name.2`) and the label row of every page keyed by page object. `finish()` then writes the bookmarks through `outline_ops.append_items` (appended after the document's own; its items follow their pages by object and are untouched), one flat sorted `/Names /Dests` leaf holding the document's entries verbatim plus the source's (other `/Names` sub-trees such as `/EmbeddedFiles` stay), and `/PageLabels` rebuilt from a row for every page of the final document (inserted page = the source's row, else the row it had before the insert, else its physical number). The rebuild runs whenever the document or the source has labels, so a label-less source into a labelled document also keeps `ii` on its page (the inserted pages count 1, 2, ... like a merge). A document or source with no labels at all gets none invented. A name the source does not define, but links to, is dropped instead of binding to the document's own same-named destination. Undo/redo are the existing whole-document snapshots, so outline, names and labels come back exactly.
**Rule:** page labels are positional: any code that adds, removes or moves pages in a document that has `/PageLabels` must re-express them (this fix covers the page-copy path only). A writer that merges into a document must read what is there first and never replace a tree it did not read completely.
**Not fixed / scope:** (1) a document whose `/Names /Dests` tree cannot be read completely (missing kid, odd key) or whose `/Names` is not a plain dictionary is left alone: its names stay, the source's names are not imported and the source's named links become explicit ones; its labels are left unchanged only when reading them raises, a partly readable label tree is rebuilt from the rules that can be read, and an unreadable tree that raises nothing counts as no labels. (2) The document's pages that had no labels keep the physical number they showed (`1, 2, S-1.., 3, 4`), they are not renumbered after the insert. (3) The source's bookmarks go at the END of the outline, not next to the insert position. (4) The existing name tree is flattened to one leaf (as in a merge). (5) `insert_blank_page`, `delete_pages` and `move_page` still leave `/PageLabels` indexed by position (no page copy, no owner decision); tracked in TODOS. (6) Not driven in the GUI by hand.
**File:** `model/navigation_graft.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_merge_composition.py` (`test_insert_imports_*`, `test_insert_rebuilds_labels_*`, `test_insert_at_the_front_and_the_end_*`, `test_insert_of_a_label_less_source_*`, `test_insert_into_a_document_without_navigation_*`, `test_insert_of_a_page_range_*`, `test_insert_keeps_legacy_catalog_dests_*`, `test_insert_leaves_an_unreadable_name_tree_alone_*`, `test_insert_into_a_blank_placeholder_*`, `test_undo_of_an_insert_*`, `test_insert_pages_from_file_keeps_links_that_pymupdf_drops`)

## A dragged edit was accepted as SUCCESS over untouched text: the overprint guard was off for every dragged `new_rect` (S17-DRAG-GUARD)

**Area:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_apply_redact_insert_body`: `_guard_overprint`, `_overprint_exempt`, `_refuse_if_overprinted`; `edit_text(place_anyway=)`), `model/text_edit_refusal.py` (`DRAGGED_BOX_OVERPRINTS`), `model/edit_requests.py` (`EditTextRequest.place_anyway`), `model/edit_commands.py` (`EditTextCommand`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`edit_text`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`edit_text` -> `_commit_text_edit`, `_offer_place_anyway`, `_remembered_consent`), `controller/text_edit_refusals.py`, `view/message_boxes.py` (`confirm_place_anyway`)
**Symptom:** (Round 17; TODOS F13-VF-4c.) `ab` (Helvetica 14) at x=72 with the untouched red run `NEXT` (10 pt) starting at x=87.57. Drag-editing `ab` / `abc` 20 pt to the right (a consented rebuild; a drag is rebuild-only) returned SUCCESS on both engines and the saved file showed the edited word at x 92.0-106.9 / 113.4 over `NEXT` (87.6-114.2): about 149 pt2 of overprint, `NEXT` unmoved.
**Cause:** `_guard_overprint = new_rect is None` turned the guard off for every dragged box ("dragged boxes are where the user put them"), and the neighbour cap and wrap floor were off for the same reason. A second thing hid the problem in the touching case: the run that abuts the edited one is in its overlap cluster, so it is a protected span and `_overprint_exempt` (text the edited run was drawn over in the source, which the rewrite may cover again) excused every glyph of it, even after the text had been dragged away from that spot.
**Fix:** owner decision (DRAGGED-BOX): a dragged box gets the overprint guard but no neighbour cap and no wrap floor (the user's placement wins on size, not over other text). `_guard_overprint = new_rect is None or not place_anyway`; a drop that moved the text by more than `_DRAG_MOVED_TOL_PT` (0.5 pt) clears `_overprint_exempt`, so the cluster's neighbours are no longer its domain. The guard's refusal for a dragged box carries its own code, `DRAGGED_BOX_OVERPRINTS` (an in-place edit keeps `TEXT_DOES_NOT_FIT`), with its own zh-TW sentence (the "fewer characters" advice of the other one is wrong for a drag). The Controller, on that code for a request with a `new_rect`, asks `confirm_place_anyway` (zh-TW, "仍要放在這裡" / "取消", default and Esc cancel) and, on yes, re-sends the request with `EditTextRequest.place_anyway=True` (neither cap nor guard, this edit only; no global setting). The first attempt's rebuild consent is replayed (`_remembered_consent`), so the user is not asked twice. On cancel nothing is shown as an error and `_last_edit_result` stays `None`, so the View keeps the editor and the typed text. Headless (no view) the plain refusal sentence is shown. `place_anyway` is ignored for an edit with no `new_rect`.
**Rule:** a guard that exists to stop the app drawing over the user's page must not be keyed on "the user chose the position": the choice is theirs to override per edit, not the guard's to skip. An exemption that says "this was already covered in the source" is only true where the text still is.
**Not fixed / scope:** (1) the cross-page move's destination is a fresh `add_textbox` and is not overprint-guarded (TODOS F13-VF-4d). (2) A drop that moved less than 0.5 pt is judged like an in-place edit (exemption kept). (3) The place-anyway dialog is not driven in the real GUI by hand; the Controller test monkeypatches the dialog. (4) The dialog wording is the same for horizontal and quarter-turn dragged boxes.
**File:** `model/pdf_text_edit.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`, `view/message_boxes.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_s17_dragged_box_onto_untouched_text_is_refused_and_rolled_back`, `test_s17_dragged_box_in_free_space_still_succeeds_uncapped`, `test_s17_place_anyway_writes_the_drop_over_the_neighbour`, `test_s17_place_anyway_does_not_lift_the_guard_of_an_in_place_edit`, `test_s17_a_sub_tolerance_drag_keeps_the_in_place_cluster_domain`, `test_s17_dragged_quarter_turn_box_onto_untouched_text_is_refused`), `test_scripts/test_text_edit_refusal_messages.py` (`test_dragged_refusal_*`, `test_an_in_place_edit_is_never_offered_place_anyway`)

## A diagonal watermark under the edited word's OLD box was erased with the word and the edit refused (S17-WMARK-UNDER)

**Area:** `model/off_axis_shows.py` (new: `restore_turned_shows`, `read_streams`), `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_redact_owned_glyphs`, `_resolve_edit_target`)
**Symptom:** (Round 17, owner decision 2026-10-12.) With the D-DIAG-INK fixture's 60 pt 45-degree `DRAFT COPY` placed so its glyph boxes hold the word (pivot (120, 350) or (135, 345)), `John` -> `Johnny B` was rolled back for both engines with `UNTOUCHED_TEXT_WOULD_BE_LOST` ("erasing the edited runs also erased 1 glyph(s) of untouched text"); the tiered engine fell to the legacy rebuild (`growth_region_not_blank`) and met the same refusal. At pivot (170, 330) the edit worked.
**Cause:** two things. (1) `find_overlapping_runs` put the watermark's runs (bbox = a large square around a thin diagonal) in the overlap cluster, so they were erased with the word and replayed by `_replay_protected_spans`, which can only turn text by quarter turns. (2) MuPDF's text redaction removes every glyph whose box touches a redaction point, and the box of a turned 60 pt glyph is a 60 x 60 pt square: the point inside a 12 pt letter is "inside" glyphs of the watermark (`D`, `R`) that the edit never owned. The redaction itself is not steerable (any point inside the word is inside that square).
**Fix:** (1) `_resolve_edit_target` drops runs written off the page axes from `overlap_cluster` when the edited run is axis-aligned (target members always stay), the same predicate (`_is_axis_aligned_dir`) as the wall, the floor and the ink guard. (2) `_redact_owned_glyphs` (the chokepoint of the rebuild AND the push-down) keeps the page's decoded streams before it redacts when the page has turned text and the edit's own glyphs are upright; when only turned glyphs came out lost it calls `restore_turned_shows`. The redaction rewrites the streams but keeps every operator in order and only drops the erased glyphs (with a kern), so the repair is exact: a top-level `q ... Q` block whose shows are all turned is written back whole (this also brings back a block the redaction emptied to `q Q`, e.g. a watermark drawn one glyph per show), and any other changed turned `Tj`/`TJ` show is written back as its original operator bytes, paired by trm, font, size and text state. Nothing is replayed: text, origins, direction, colour, opacity and drawing order are the source's. The glyphs are re-read afterwards and the inked-glyph count must equal "before minus the word", else the loss is still reported.
**Rule:** protect untouched text by keeping or restoring its ORIGINAL operators, not by redrawing it. Never replay a turned run through a quarter-turn writer. Horizontal and vertical untouched text keep the existing protection: a lost glyph of it still refuses.
**Not fixed / scope:** a turned run inside a Form XObject (an Acrobat-style watermark) is still erased by the redaction and the edit is still refused `UNTOUCHED_TEXT_WOULD_BE_LOST`: the repair reads the page's own content streams only, and a form's local matrix cannot say whether its text is turned (TODOS S17-WMARK-UNDER). No repair when the edited glyphs are themselves turned, when a turned show was dropped or split in a way that cannot be paired, or when the show is `'` / `"`. Not checked in the real GUI.
**File:** `model/off_axis_shows.py`, `model/pdf_text_edit.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_edit_text_helpers.py` (`test_editing_a_word_over_a_diagonal_watermark_keeps_the_watermark[legacy|tiered x 2 pivots x opaque|50 % opacity]`, `test_owned_redaction_leaves_an_off_axis_run_under_the_word_untouched[2 pivots x /Rotate 0|90|180]`, `test_push_down_keeps_a_diagonal_watermark_whose_box_holds_the_pushed_text`), `test_scripts/test_off_axis_shows.py`

## Named destinations and the links using them dangled after their page was deleted, and kept the deleted page in the saved file (F16-NAV-1a)

**Area:** `model/page_refs.py` (new: `repoint_page_references`, `RepointResult`), `model/outline_ops.py` (`named_target`, `follow_dropped_names`), `model/pdf_model.py` (`delete_pages`, `straighten_page`)
**Symptom:** (Round 17.) A 4-page file with `/Names /Dests` `chap3` on page 3 and a page-1 GoTo link `/D (chap3)`: after `delete_pages([3])`, Save As and reopen, `chap3` resolved to page -1 and the link jumped nowhere. The same for a link written `/Dest (chap3)`, a legacy catalog `/Dests` name, `/OpenAction`, and a bookmark whose `/Dest` is the name (it showed page 0 and kept the dead name). Worse, the saved file still contained the deleted page object with its `/Contents`: the dead `[page /XYZ ...]` arrays kept it reachable, so a `garbage` save wrote the deleted page's content into the file (`/Type/Page` objects outside `/Kids`). `straighten_page` had the same hole: the page object is replaced, so names into the old page dangled and PyMuPDF dropped the explicit links into it.
**Cause:** `Document.delete_page` -> `_remove_dest_range` deletes only the link annotations whose destination it can resolve to a page: explicit arrays, and a string `/D` only through `fz_resolve_link`, which expects a URI, so a bare name never resolves (pno -1, `continue`). Nothing edits the name trees, the legacy `/Dests` dictionary, `/OpenAction`, a non-Link annotation's GoTo action, or a bookmark that uses a name (`get_toc` gives such an item page 0/-1, so `_remove_toc_item` and `follow_page_targets` skip it).
**Fix:** one Qt-free chokepoint, `page_refs.repoint_page_references(doc, {old_page_xref: None | new_page_xref})`, reading raw objects through the `navigation_graft` reader (never `resolve_names`) and editing only what must change. `None` (delete) removes the entries of `/Names /Dests` (leaf `/Names` arrays rewritten in place, `/Limits` recomputed, a kid that became empty leaves `/Kids`, nodes without a dead name are not written) and of the legacy `/Dests` dictionary (entries kept verbatim), removes the Link annotations whose `/A /D` or `/Dest` is a removed name or an explicit array to the removed page (as PyMuPDF already does for explicit ones; a name that the other name source still defines keeps its links), nulls the `/A` of a non-Link annotation with such a jump, and drops a matching `/OpenAction`. A page object number (straighten) swaps only the page reference, so the `/XYZ` view, the name and the links stay. `delete_pages` calls it right after the delete loop (before the delete-all placeholder is created) and then `outline_ops.follow_dropped_names` points a bookmark that used a removed name at the nearest surviving page, like every other bookmark; `straighten_page` calls it before deleting the old page. The decision follows two existing rules: PyMuPDF removes an explicit link into a deleted page, and `NavigationGraft` drops a name whose page was not copied together with its links.
**Rule:** a page that stops existing must lose every reference to it, not only the ones PyMuPDF knows: a destination reachable by NAME is a separate reference class from an explicit array, and a dead reference is not harmless, it keeps the page object (and its content) in the saved file. Any new code that deletes or replaces a page goes through `repoint_page_references`.
**Not fixed / scope:** (1) A retargeted bookmark gets a whole-page `/Fit` view (F16-NAV-1 limit); a link or name is dropped rather than retargeted to a neighbouring page (retargeting like bookmarks would silently send a reader to the wrong page; the owner can switch). (2) A `/Names /Dests` tree written inline in the catalog (no object to edit) is reported in `RepointResult.unsupported`, logged and left alone, as is an unreadable node. (3) A tagged PDF's structure tree (`/StructTreeRoot` `/Pg`, `MCR /Pg`) still references the deleted page and keeps its object and content in the saved file (probed: 3 of 15 sample files); so do `/Threads` beads and page-level `/AA`. (4) Only GoTo actions of annotations are repointed; Named, GoToR and JavaScript actions are not touched. (5) A bookmark whose name key is not plain text is not matched (`xref_get_key` decodes it). (6) Measured on a 1500-page file with 30000 named links: one delete 1.05 s. Not driven in the GUI.
**File:** `model/page_refs.py`, `model/outline_ops.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_bookmarks_toc.py` (`test_deleting_a_page_drops_its_names_the_links_using_them_and_the_open_action`, `test_name_tree_limits_and_emptied_kids_follow_the_deleted_names`, `test_deleting_every_page_leaves_no_dead_navigation`, `test_a_name_defined_twice_keeps_its_links_while_one_definition_lives`, `test_names_of_surviving_pages_and_the_legacy_dictionary_are_not_rewritten`, `test_bookmark_that_names_a_deleted_destination_moves_to_the_survivor`, `test_straighten_keeps_names_links_and_open_action_on_the_replacement_page`)

## On a ROTATED `/UserUnit` page `AnnotationTool` mapped requests with `page.derotation_matrix`, so rects, markups and notes were drawn, restored and picked at the wrong place (F15-G1-UU-ANNOT)

**Area:** `model/tools/annotation_tool.py` (`_derotate_rect`, `_derotate_point`, `_displayed_rect_to_quad`, `_pin_outer_rect`), `model/annot_geometry.py` (new), `model/pdf_object_ops.py` (`_marker_pick_rect`, `_image_payload_unrotated_rect`, the rect-object move and delete, `_sync_image_marker_to_drawn`)
**Symptom:** (Round 17.) MediaBox [0 0 300 400] + `/UserUnit 2` + `/Rotate 90/180/270`: `AnnotationTool.add_rect(30,50,90,80)` (red, 2 pt) inked at (428,48,492,82), (328,448,392,482) and (28,348,92,382) instead of (28,48,92,82); highlight, underline, strikeout and note were off the same way, at `/UserUnit 0.5` nothing was drawn. A rect object added there could not be picked where it is drawn, a move placed it nowhere, and a re-created Square under a redaction was inflated by the wrong inset. The unrotated `/UserUnit` page and rotated unit-scale pages (also with an offset CropBox) were right.
**Cause:** MEASURED (1.27.1): three PyMuPDF behaviours that look alike are not. `add_*_annot(rect / point / quad)` reads TRUE unrotated page space (`/UserUnit`-scaled, `model.geometry`'s space); `page.derotation_matrix` drops `/UserUnit` on a rotated page, so every request was mapped by the wrong page size. `Annot.rect` / `Annot.set_rect` live in PyMuPDF's own `/UserUnit`-less derotated space, which is why `Annot.rect * page.rotation_matrix` is the exact displayed rect and `set_rect(point * derotation_matrix)` is the exact move, but `set_rect(true-space rect)` draws nothing. The raw `/Rect` array is exact user space. The round-16 TODO claimed "`Annot.rect` does not read back what `add_rect_annot` wrote": only the write was wrong.
**Fix:** the three write helpers go through `model.geometry` (`visual_to_unrotated_rect` / `_point`). `model/annot_geometry.py` is the one raw-`/Rect` chokepoint (`annot_page_rect` reads it through `page_user_space_matrix`, `set_annot_page_rect` writes it back for a rotated page with a provable frame and uses `set_rect` otherwise), used by the redaction snapshot/restore, `_pin_outer_rect` (the inset is measured in true space and applied with the raw write), the rect object's pick, move and delete and the image marker. The Text/Note read (`get_all_annotations`) and move (`move_annotation`) keep `Annot.rect` with `rotation_matrix` / `derotation_matrix`, because MuPDF keeps a note icon upright (NoRotate) and its raw `/Rect` is not the drawn rect.
**Rule:** never hand `add_*_annot` a rect built with `page.derotation_matrix`; never mix `Annot.rect` / `set_rect` (derotated, `/UserUnit`-less) with `model.geometry` or the raw `/Rect` (true space) in one computation. A new annotation consumer picks ONE of the two pairs and says which. The oracle is rendered ink against the unrotated page of the same `/UserUnit` and displayed size, never `Annot.rect` read back after an `add_*_annot` write.
**Not fixed:** the app textbox marker is created from VISUAL numbers (`add_rect_annot`) and resized by `set_rect`, two spaces on such a page; it is hidden and picked by its payload there (F15-G1-UU-ROT), so nothing is visible. `insert_textbox` / `draw_rect` still ignore `/UserUnit` (TODOS F15-G1-UU); no product code calls them.
**File:** `model/tools/annotation_tool.py`, `model/annot_geometry.py`, `model/pdf_object_ops.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_annotation_rotation.py` (`test_tool_ink_on_a_rotated_user_unit_page_matches_the_unrotated_twin`, `test_note_read_back_and_move_on_a_rotated_user_unit_page`, `test_redaction_restore_recreates_an_annotation_in_place_on_a_rotated_user_unit_page`), `test_scripts/test_object_manipulation_model.py` (`test_rect_object_on_rotated_user_unit_page_is_drawn_picked_moved_and_deleted_in_place`)

## A right-to-left table row was not cut into cells, so a paragraph edit of one cell rebuilt the whole row and moved its neighbours (F16-RTL-CELLS)

**Area:** `model/text_block_parsing.py` (`_split_line_into_cells`, `_split_bidi_line_into_cells`, `_block_text_is_rtl`, `_group_units_into_columns`, `_build_paragraphs`), `model/rtl_text.py` (`first_strong_is_rtl`)
**Symptom:** (Round 17, found by the F16-RTL-RESIDUAL review.) One htmlbox line holding two Hebrew cells with a wide column gap indexed as ONE paragraph. A paragraph-mode edit of the right cell (`שלום עולמות`) rebuilt the whole row and moved the other cell from x 243.9..296.7 to 390.3..443.1 (about +146 pt), closing the column gap; the left-to-right twin left the other cell alone. A split right-to-left line (one cell per PyMuPDF line) composed its text left cell first.
**Cause:** Rule (a) walked the line's runs in `span_idx` order and measured `run.x0 - previous.x1`. A right-to-left line numbers its runs in LOGICAL order (F15-RTL-ORDER), so consecutive runs step left and every gap was negative: the row never cut. The (a2) merge, the column-group order (`min(x0)`) and the unit order all assumed left to right; the flag they take was only ever set for upside-down blocks.
**Fix:** (1) A line holding a right-to-left letter is cut by `_split_bidi_line_into_cells`, which measures the gap between VISUAL neighbours (inked runs sorted by x) and returns each cell with its runs in `span_idx` order and the cells in reading order. Measuring between logical neighbours would also cut a sentence with an embedded English phrase (the next logical run sits on the far side of the phrase). Upside-down (180) lines keep the old walk. (2) A block's reading direction is `upside-down XOR right-to-left script`; script direction is the first strong character in `(line_idx, span_idx)` order (`first_strong_is_rtl`, the D-RTL-GROW rule, now public), so a mostly-English row with one Hebrew cell stays left to right, and upside-down Hebrew reads towards +x. (3) `_group_units_into_columns` orders the groups of one row by that direction, so the right-hand cell is paragraph 0 in a Hebrew row (upside-down Latin keeps its ascending-x group order).
**Rule:** any code that orders or measures gaps between runs must key on `span_idx` (reading order) or on VISUAL neighbours, never on `x0 - previous.x1` along `span_idx` order. A gap sign only means something when the walk direction is known.
**Not fixed / scope:** the run `עולם` is still indexed as `עול` + `ם` on that fixture (a trailing-space glyph box that overlaps the final letter sorts between them in `_parse_runs_from_raw_line`), so the paragraph text reads `עול ם`; TODOS F16-RTL-RESIDUAL item 6. A right-to-left line with no gap wider than the cell ratio is still one cell, as for left-to-right text.
**File:** `model/text_block_parsing.py`, `model/rtl_text.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_paragraph_table_cells.py` (`test_rtl_single_line_row_is_cut_into_cells_in_reading_order`, `test_rtl_line_with_an_embedded_ltr_phrase_is_not_cut`, `test_mostly_ltr_row_with_one_hebrew_cell_keeps_left_to_right_order`, `test_rtl_same_baseline_merge_reads_right_to_left_whatever_the_line_order`, `test_single_line_row_with_a_column_gap_is_cut_into_two_cells[ltr-control|rtl]`, `test_paragraph_edit_of_one_cell_leaves_the_other_cell_in_place[ltr-control|rtl]`)

## `QTimer.singleShot(ms, view.method)` has no receiver context: a view destroyed before the first loop turn ran the callback against deleted children (F16-VIEW-TIMER)
**Area:** `view/pdf_view.py` (`_setup_left_sidebar`, `_show_toast`, `showEvent`, `exit_fullscreen_ui`, `_schedule_finalize_on_focus_change`, the viewport `Resize` branch, the search-highlight removal), `view/text_editing.py` (focus-restore timers), `utils/qt_deferred.py`
**Symptom:** `PDFView()` then `deleteLater()` + `DeferredDelete` before the first event-loop turn, then `processEvents()` raised `RuntimeError: Internal C++ object (_ReorderableThumbnailList) already deleted` from `_update_thumbnail_layout_metrics`. Harness-only in practice (the shipped view lives for the whole session), which is why GATE15-3 only patched `dispose_pdf_view`.
**Cause:** PySide gives `QTimer.singleShot(ms, callable)` no receiver context, so a callable bound to a widget still runs after that widget's C++ object is gone; the Python wrapper survives and its first Qt call raises.
**Fix:** `utils/qt_deferred.call_later(owner, delay_ms, callback)` starts a one-shot `QTimer` that is a child of `owner` (and deletes itself after firing); destroying the owner destroys the pending timer, so the callback is never delivered. Every `QTimer.singleShot` in `view/` now goes through it (owner = the view, or the toast for its own dismissal). Not converted on purpose: `controller/` sites (`PDFController` is a plain Python object whose callbacks run Python state methods) and `ThumbnailCoordinator` lambdas (only touch Python attributes of a live coordinator).
**Rule:** in `view/`, never call `QTimer.singleShot` with a callable; use `call_later(owner, ms, cb)`. Guard: `test_view_modules_have_no_context_free_single_shot`.
**File:** `utils/qt_deferred.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_shell_tab_ux.py` (`test_view_deleted_before_first_event_loop_turn_runs_no_startup_callback`, `test_view_deleted_with_pending_toast_and_focus_timers_is_silent`, `test_toast_still_auto_dismisses_on_a_live_view`, `test_call_later_runs_once_on_a_live_owner_and_never_on_a_deleted_one`, `test_view_modules_have_no_context_free_single_shot`)

## Five script-style test modules disabled logging for the whole pytest process, so `caplog` saw nothing (GATE16-1a)

**Area:** `test_scripts/conftest.py` (`_logging_enabled`), `test_scripts/test_50_rounds.py`, `test_all_pdfs.py`, `test_deep.py`, `test_feature_conflict.py`, `test_overlap_corpus_recursive.py`; `test_scripts/test_pymupdf_flag_hygiene.py`
**Symptom:** `test_cjk_ext_b_font.py::test_unimportable_fonttools_is_a_broken_install_not_missing_glyphs[blocked0|blocked1]` failed (`caplog.text` empty) in any process that also collected one of the five script modules, and passed alone. A feature-conflict test run with `-k` deselecting every test of that module still failed, because the leak happened at collection.
**Cause:** `logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)` is process-global. Each script called it at module level (to cut log I/O for a batch run), which pytest executes when it imports the module for collection; nothing restored it. This is the same class as the PyMuPDF `TOOLS` flags (GATE16-1): a process-global switch set at import and never reset. `test_font_stream_compaction.py` had already worked around it with a spy.
**Fix:** the five scripts call `logging.disable` only under `if __name__ == "__main__":` (script runs unchanged, imports are inert). `conftest.py` has an autouse fixture that clears `logging.disable` (NOTSET) before and after every test, so a future leak, or a test that disables logging and forgets to restore it, cannot reach the next test. `test_pymupdf_flag_hygiene.py` pins both (ordered leak/next-test pair) and has an AST source guard: no `test_scripts/*.py` may call `logging.disable(<non-NOTSET>)` outside a `__main__` guard.
**Rule:** a process-global switch (`logging.disable`, `fitz.TOOLS` flags, `os.environ`) must not be set at import time in a module pytest collects; set it in a fixture that restores it, or in the `__main__` block.
**File:** `test_scripts/conftest.py`, the five script modules above; tests `test_scripts/test_pymupdf_flag_hygiene.py` (`test_a_test_may_disable_logging_without_restoring_it`, `test_the_next_test_still_starts_with_logging_enabled`, `test_no_test_module_disables_logging_outside_a_main_guard`, `test_the_source_guard_sees_unguarded_calls_and_allows_main_guarded_ones`)

## A fixture teardown's `view.close()` was vetoed by the test's own simulated running job, and the window that survived took every hover of a later test file (GATE16-1b)

**Area:** `test_scripts/qt_teardown.py` (`dispose_pdf_view`, `snapshot_visible_gui`, `leaked_gui_since`), the `mvc` / `mvc_legacy` fixtures (now one `_mvc_session` generator) and the autouse `_no_stray_gui_state` of `test_scripts/test_multi_tab_plan.py`; the victim was `test_scripts/test_text_commit_editor_mouse_gestures.py`
**Symptom:** `test_hover_inside_open_editor_shows_ibeam[0]`, `test_the_ibeam_does_not_outlive_the_editor[0]` and `test_the_ibeam_does_not_survive_a_mode_switch[0]` failed (the viewport cursor stayed OpenHand) in any process where `test_multi_tab_plan.py` ran first; bisected to `test_mt1b_close_deferred_by_a_running_job_keeps_the_plan_preview_alive[print|optimize]`. Each passed alone. The product was not at fault: no override cursor (the repo has no `setOverrideCursor`), no job (the tests only patch the `_has_active_*_submission` predicates), and the controller's close-pending flags die with the controller.
**Cause:** `mt1b` simulates a running print or optimize job with `monkeypatch`, which pytest undoes only AFTER the fixture teardown. The `mvc` teardown's `view.close()` reaches `handle_app_close` through `PDFView.closeEvent`, which correctly ignores a close while a job runs, so the test's shown `PDFView` (100,100,1280,800) stayed visible for the rest of the process. `QTest.mouseMove(widget, pos)` is `QCursor.setPos` plus the platform delivering the move, and the offscreen platform hands it to the FIRST exposed top-level window (creation order, not stacking order) whose geometry holds the point. The stray, older window therefore received every move meant for the next test's view, whose `_sync_editor_hover_cursor` never ran. Probe: two overlapping plain `QWidget`s, `QTest.mouseMove(newer)` reaches the older one (older 1 move, newer 0). The guard found two more leakers of the same class: both `test_mt2_*` held-grip-drag close tests (the cancel-answered unsaved prompt vetoes the teardown close).
**Fix:** `mvc` and `mvc_legacy` tear down with `dispose_pdf_view(view, controller, model)`, which also hides the view before `deleteLater()`, so removing the window no longer depends on the close being carried out. Converting a `view.close()` teardown to `dispose_pdf_view` exposed a second hazard, now handled inside the helper: `test_13` .. `test_16` of the same module errored at teardown with `RuntimeError: Internal C++ object (PySide6.QtCore.QThread) already deleted` from `controller/thumbnail_coordinator.py` `_thread_finished`. The close joins the coordinator thread, its `_worker_finished` slot is still queued and posts `QTimer.singleShot(0, lambda: self._thread_finished(token))`; the single `processEvents()` after `close()` delivered the signal only, so the timer fired after `deleteLater()` + `flush_deferred_deletes()` had destroyed the child `QThread` and `thread.wait()` hit a dead object. `dispose_pdf_view` now pumps the event loop for 50 ms (`_settle_zero_delay_callbacks`) between `close()` and `deleteLater()`. Guard: the autouse `_no_stray_gui_state` fixture fails the test that leaves a NEW visible top-level `PDFView` / inline editor or an application override cursor (`snapshot_visible_gui()` / `leaked_gui_since()`; it also hides the stray, so one leaker is one error, reported at the test that caused it). Product behaviour (a close deferred behind a running job) is unchanged and still pinned by mt1b.
**Rule:** a GUI-test teardown must not rely on `view.close()` to remove a window: it is a request the controller may refuse, and a test that simulates a close blocker keeps the blocker active through the teardown. Use `dispose_pdf_view`. A new module that simulates a close blocker (print/optimize job, join timeout, answered prompt) gets the same autouse guard from `qt_teardown`.
**Not fixed (product code, open in TODOS):** `ThumbnailCoordinator._worker_finished` posts a context-free `QTimer.singleShot(0, lambda ...)` whose `_thread_finished` calls `thread.wait(1000)` on a child `QThread`; destroying the view (and with it the coordinator and its thread) before that timer fires raises from the slot. This is the GATE15-3 hazard class through a timer instead of a signal, and it contradicts the `QTimer.singleShot` pitfall in `utils/qt_deferred.py` ('Not converted on purpose') that the `ThumbnailCoordinator` lambdas "only touch Python attributes of a live coordinator". The app only destroys its view at exit, so no user-visible effect is known.
**Not covered:** the guard is per module. A global autouse would hide the shown view of any module-scoped fixture; a read-only audit found no other module that patches a close blocker while its view is shown (`test_print_controller_flow.py` runs a real job and closes after it has finished).
**File:** `test_scripts/qt_teardown.py`, `test_scripts/test_multi_tab_plan.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_multi_tab_plan.py` (`test_mvc_teardown_destroys_a_view_whose_close_is_vetoed[print|optimize|render_join_timeout|thumbnail_join_timeout]`, `test_gui_leak_guard_names_a_stray_view_and_an_override_cursor`, and the autouse guard on every test of the module, red on mt1b[print|optimize] and both mt2 close tests)

## After a refused move, resize or rotate the View still moved or turned the selection frame, so it sat away from the object that stayed (D-OBJ-FRAME)

**Area:** `view/object_selection.py` (`ObjectSelectionManager._emit_object_op`, `_emit_object_op_and_rebase`, `note_object_op_refused`, `_commit_free_rotation`, `_rotate_selected_object`, `_rotate_selected_object_absolute`), `view/pdf_view.py` (`_mouse_release` objects/browse branches, the three delegating wrappers), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`_tell_view_object_op_refused`, `_report_object_refusal`, `move_object`)
**Symptom:** (Round 17; TODOS F15-4 (b), restated by the D-OLD-MARKERS fixer.) After a refused single move (the stale-marker twins fixture, `IMAGE_NOT_LOCATED`, one zh-TW message) the frame was at the requested rect while the object stayed; the next press hit-tested the wrong area. The same held for a refused resize, a refused rotate (the frame and the stored angle turned, the object did not) and, in a batch move, for the objects that refused.
**Cause:** the View emitted `sig_move_object` / `sig_resize_object` / `sig_rotate_object` and then updated its own selection (`_rebase_object_selection_to_bboxes`, the `replace(info, rotation=...)` of the rotate verbs) unconditionally. `Signal.emit` returns nothing and the Controller refuses with a dialog only, so the View could not tell a refusal from success.
**Fix:** a refusal channel Controller -> View. Every View site that follows a request goes through `ObjectSelectionManager._emit_object_op(signal, request)`, which marks one operation in flight, emits (a direct connection: the slot runs inside `emit`) and returns the ids the Controller named through `PDFView.note_object_op_refused(ids)`. `PDFController._report_object_refusal` (single move / resize / rotate / delete) and the refused branch of a batch move call it through `_tell_view_object_op_refused` (guarded: a view without the method, or one that raises, never breaks the refusal report). `_emit_object_op_and_rebase` rebases only the ids that were accepted; with every id refused it still runs the rebase with nothing, which resets the drag start/preview rects and redraws the frame at the object. The rotate verbs return `False` and keep the old angle and frame when refused; a refused free rotation resets the live preview transform and redraws.
**Rule:** a View that follows its own request must learn the outcome from the Controller, never assume success. A refusal reported with no operation in flight (a direct Controller call) is ignored, so a stale id cannot suppress a later accepted op. Any new emit of a move / resize / rotate request goes through `_emit_object_op`.
**Behaviour change:** in a batch move that partly refuses, the moved objects are still one undo step (pinned by `test_batch_move_that_partly_refuses_says_how_many_objects_did_not_move`) and now the frame of only those follows; the refused ones stay selected at their real bbox.
**Not fixed / scope:** Delete still emits and then clears the selection whatever the outcome (`_delete_selected_object`): a refused delete drops the frame while the object stays, and a click selects it again at its true place, so nothing sits in the wrong place. `_report_object_refusal` already names the object to the View on a delete refusal (ignored, no op in flight); routing delete through `_emit_object_op` is the one-line follow-up if the owner wants the selection kept. A queued (cross-thread) connection of the request signals would deliver the refusal after `emit` returns and defeat the channel; the three signals are direct connections today. A lost session (`_live_only` ignores the slot) and an exception inside the slot are not refusals and are not reported to the View.
**File:** `view/object_selection.py`, `view/pdf_view.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_object_manipulation_gui.py` (`test_real_refused_mouse_move_leaves_frame_on_the_object` real model + controller + view + mouse drag, `test_refused_single_move_keeps_frame_at_object`, `test_successful_single_move_still_rebases_frame`, `test_partly_refused_batch_move_rebases_only_the_moved_objects`, `test_resize_release_follows_only_an_accepted_resize`, `test_absolute_and_stepped_rotation_follow_only_an_accepted_rotate`, `test_free_rotation_commit_follows_only_an_accepted_rotate`, `test_a_refusal_outside_an_emit_does_not_poison_the_next_successful_move`), `test_scripts/test_object_controller_flow.py` (`test_refused_object_op_names_the_object_to_the_view`, `test_accepted_object_op_does_not_notify_the_view`, `test_partly_refused_batch_move_names_only_the_refused_objects_to_the_view`, `test_a_view_that_cannot_take_the_notice_does_not_break_the_refusal_report`), `test_scripts/test_object_selection_extraction.py`

## Undoing a page rotation kept the rotated page size: the restored page overlapped the next one and clicks low on it hit the next page (F17-COH-1)
**Area:** `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`undo`, `redo`, `_command_changes_page_layout`, `_refresh_after_command`, `_session_page_sizes`), `model/edit_commands.py` (`SnapshotCommand.changes_page_geometry`, `_PAGE_GEOMETRY_TYPES`)
**Symptom:** (Round 17.) On a 3-page 612x792 document: rotate page 1 by 90 degrees, Ctrl+Z. The page is 612x792 again, but the controller's page-size cache, the view's `_page_base_sizes` and `page_heights` still said 792x612. The 792 pt pixmap sat in a 612 pt slot (page 1 bottom 792, page 2 top 622), and a click 700 pt down page 1 mapped to page 2 at y 78 (`_scene_pos_to_page_and_doc_point`). A zoom rebuilt the scene from the same stale cache (bottom 990 vs top 775 at 125 %). Redo only looked right because the stale sizes matched the rotated page again.
**Cause:** Two halves. (1) `undo()` / `redo()` dropped the page-size cache only for `is_structural` commands (page count or order changed). `rotate_pages` keeps both, and `_session_page_sizes` validates its cache by page count alone, so a same-count size change was never noticed. (2) `_refresh_after_command` sent every non-structural command to `show_page`, which in continuous mode only scrolls and re-renders: the new pixmap went into the old slot. Clearing the cache alone would have left the overlap until the next rebuild.
**Fix:** `SnapshotCommand.changes_page_geometry` (`_PAGE_GEOMETRY_TYPES` = the structural types + `rotate_pages` + `straighten_pages`). `is_structural` keeps its meaning (thumbnail placeholder reset, annotation reload, stale-index drain). One controller helper, `_command_changes_page_layout(cmd)` (`is_structural or changes_page_geometry`, read with `getattr`, so command fakes without the attribute still work), decides `clear_page_sizes` in `undo()` / `redo()` and sends the command to the rebuild branch of `_refresh_after_command` (`_invalidate_thumbnails(affected)` + `_rebuild_continuous_scene(current_page)`, as the forward op does).
**Rule:** an op whose forward path calls `_invalidate_active_render_state(clear_page_sizes=True)` must be in `SnapshotCommand._PAGE_GEOMETRY_TYPES`, or its undo/redo keeps stale sizes. `test_04j_every_page_size_changing_op_is_a_page_geometry_command` (AST scan of `controller/pdf_controller.py`) enforces it, per method: an op that dropped the cache in one method and built its `SnapshotCommand` in a helper would slip past the scan (all seven sites are single-method today). `_session_page_sizes` stays count-keyed on purpose: it runs on every zoom, and re-reading every page rect would load every page. The cache must be dropped at the mutation.
**Not fixed / scope:** `straighten_pages` is in the set defensively. Its replacement page is built at the displayed size, so straighten, undo and redo did not change any size (measured: a /Rotate 90 612x792 page stays 792x612 through all three). Undo/redo of a rotation now rebuilds the scene like the forward rotate and a structural undo do. So a toolbar Undo pressed while an inline editor is open settles that editor (`SCENE_REBUILD`: a verified edit commits, otherwise it is discarded with a notice). `undo()` / `redo()` have no editor gate before they mutate, unlike zoom (`_release_inline_editor_for_rescale` refuses first). The settle runs inside `_refresh_after_command`, after the step: a verified edit committed there records a new command, which clears the redo stack, so the step just undone cannot be redone. That follows from the code; it was not probed. Every structural undo already had this, and this fix extends it to rotate and straighten. Adding the gate is an owner decision.
**File:** `controller/pdf_controller.py`, `model/edit_commands.py`; `test_scripts/test_multi_tab_plan.py` (`test_04h_rotate_undo_redo_relayouts_continuous_scene`, `test_04i_snapshot_command_flags_page_geometry_changes`, `test_04j_every_page_size_changing_op_is_a_page_geometry_command`)

## A watermark this build saved came back on reopen on top of its own baked copy: two copies in view and print, one more in the file per save (F17-COH-2)
**Area:** `model/tools/watermark_rendering.py` (`apply_watermarks_to_page` / `_mark_written_stream`, `strip_marked_watermarks`), `model/tools/watermark_tool.py` (`on_session_open` / `_take_back_saved_copies`), `model/pdf_optimizer.py` (`build_working_doc_for_optimized_copy`)
**Symptom:** (Round 17, measured in the real app.) Add a watermark, Ctrl+S, close the tab and open the file again: view and print drew two copies (page darkness 13.22 against 12.39, the print bytes held the word twice) while the file and its thumbnail held one. Ctrl+S after an unrelated edit wrote the second copy into the file; the next reopen printed three. Removing or changing the watermark in the list could not take away the copy an earlier save had baked. An optimized copy of a reopened session with an unsaved change held two copies, and so did the optimize working copy of a clean reopened session.
**Cause:** the save bakes the list into the file (for other readers) AND stores it in the `__pdf_editor_watermarks` attachment (so it stays editable). On reopen `on_session_open` restored the list as the live overlay, the print stamp and the next save's bake, on top of the baked ink that was still page content of the live document. M9-2 fixed only the same-session variant (the live handle no longer reads the baked target). `build_working_doc_for_optimized_copy` ran the save hooks over a clean session's file, which already is the saved output.
**Fix:** the renderer marks every stream it writes for a watermark that has an `id`: `q /Artifact <</Type /Pagination /Subtype /Watermark /PdfEditorWatermark <hex id>>> BDC ... EMC Q`. At open, `_take_back_saved_copies` calls `strip_marked_watermarks(doc, list)`, which removes from the live document exactly the blocks the restored list draws again (mark id X on a page that X's `pages` name). The reopened session is then the unbaked session M9-2 keeps after its own Ctrl+S: one copy in view, print, thumbnail and file; remove / change take the saved copy away at the next save; the session is not dirty and the file is untouched until a save. Blocks are found with the lossless `pdf_lexer` (strings, hex strings, inline images). A stream that held only the block leaves `/Contents`; a merged stream (`clean_contents`, the optimizer's content cleanup) is spliced and keeps every other byte. A block holding anything but text-and-state operators, unbalanced `q`/`Q` or `BT`/`ET`, or nested marked content is left alone. The optimize working copy of a clean session now opens the file as the prepared output, as `capture_optimize_source` already did.
**Rule:** content the app bakes AND restores as editable state must be marked, so the restore can take the baked copy back; the stored parameters are the one source of truth. Put marked content inside a `q ... Q` of its own: MuPDF's balance count (`Page.wrap_contents`, which every `insert_text` calls) reports top-level marked content as an open `q` plus a stray `Q`, and the next `insert_text` wraps the page in one more `q`/`Q` pair (measured: two more streams per extra line per save and reopen). Do not mark on the stream dictionary: `clean_contents` merges the page's streams and drops their keys (it keeps marked content).
**Not fixed / scope:** (1) Ink baked before the mark existed (older builds, and this build before F17-COH-2) cannot be told apart from page text, so such files still show two copies on reopen (owner-accepted, F15-G5-GEOM, no migration). (2) Only the pages the stored list names are searched: a page another tool moved keeps its copy. (3) A page inserted from the same file (same watermark id) onto a page the list covers draws twice until the session is saved and reopened. (4) The replaced ink and attachment leave free xref slots, about 20 bytes per object per save, as every full save of a changed object does (LS-3's compaction at open bounds them). (5) The strip trusts the attachment to say which marked blocks are the app's: a crafted file can mark real page text with an id its attachment lists, and this app then hides that text at open and drops it at the next save while other readers show it. The operator check bounds it to text and state operators (no images, paths, forms or inline images); same trust level as the `_coerce_wm` (CWE-20) attachment parsing. Not driven by a human in the GUI; the round-17 probe (`coh_wm_reopen`) shows view = file = print = thumbnail (12.39, one text copy) over three sessions.
**File:** `model/tools/watermark_rendering.py`, `model/tools/watermark_tool.py`, `model/pdf_optimizer.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_watermark_save_noop.py` (`test_reopened_watermark_is_drawn_once_in_view_print_and_every_save`, `test_save_reopen_cycles_leave_the_saved_page_contents_unchanged`, `test_removing_a_reopened_watermark_removes_its_saved_copy`, `test_changing_a_reopened_watermark_replaces_its_saved_copy`, `test_optimized_copy_of_a_reopened_watermark_holds_one_copy[clean_session|dirty_session]`, `test_optimize_working_copy_of_a_reopened_watermark_holds_one_copy`, `test_reopen_finds_the_saved_watermark_in_other_content_layouts[indirect_contents_array|merged_by_clean_contents]`; guards `test_unmarked_ink_of_an_older_build_is_left_as_page_content`, `test_saved_watermark_without_its_stored_parameters_stays_page_content`), `test_scripts/test_text_commit_persistence.py` (`test_a_reopened_watermark_stays_one_copy_through_edit_save_and_undo[incremental|full|secure]`)

## A watermark stayed on its page NUMBER: after a reorder, delete, insert or merge it sat on whatever page now held the number, in view, print and the saved file (F17-COH-3)
**Area:** `model/tools/watermark_tool.py` (page identity, `on_pages_restructured`, `capture_page_state` / `restore_page_state`), `model/tools/base.py` / `model/tools/manager.py` (new page-structure hooks), `model/pdf_model.py` (`_pages_restructured`, `_remap_page_bookkeeping`, `capture_page_state`, `replace_active_document_from_snapshot(page_origins=)`, `compose_merged_document_with_origins`), `model/edit_commands.py` (`DocSnapshot.page_state`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`merge_ordered_sources_into_current`, `_invalidate_active_render_state`), `view/pdf_view.py` (`populate_watermarks_list`)
**Symptom:** (Round 17.) Watermark on page 2 of 3, move that page to the front: the original page 1 now carried it (view, print, saved file) and the moved page had none. Delete page 1: the watermark jumped to the page that had been page 3. Delete the page it was on: the list kept a number that named no page (or, at the end of the document, another page), and the panel kept listing it. Insert a page before it: the watermark stayed on the number, now a different page. Undo of the op restored the pages but left the numbers wherever the op had put them. A merge that put another document first did the same.
**Cause:** the dialog and the file store page NUMBERS (`pages: list[int]`) and `_get_watermarks_for_page` matched `page_num in wm["pages"]`; `ToolExtension` had no page-structure hook and no structural op told any tool. The same holds for the model's own page-indexed bookkeeping (`pending_edits`, `fidelity_protected_pages`; TODOS "`delete_pages` never remaps ...").
**Fix:** one chokepoint, `PDFModel._pages_restructured(origins, old_count=)`, called by `delete_pages`, `move_page`, `insert_blank_page`, `insert_pages_from_file` and (through `replace_active_document_from_snapshot(page_origins=...)`) the merge into the current document. `origins[j]` is the 1-based page of the previous list that new page `j + 1` is (`None` = a new page; a page may repeat in a merge or be missing). It moves the page-indexed bookkeeping and calls `ToolManager.on_pages_restructured`. The watermark tool keeps an id per live page (never reused) and, per watermark, the ids it covers; the stored `pages` list is DERIVED from them whenever the page list changes. A watermark whose pages are all gone is hidden (not shown, drawn, saved, editable) but kept, so undo brings the same entry back; it is not marked modified (the structural command owns dirtiness). Undo / redo / rollback: `PDFModel._capture_doc_snapshot` stores `ToolManager.capture_page_state` (the id tuple, immutable and shared between snapshots) in `DocSnapshot.page_state`, and `_restore_doc_from_snapshot` puts it back with the bytes and the maintenance book. A watermark ADDED after the op covers ids, not numbers, so it lands on the right page after undo and redo; one removed after the op is not brought back. The merge's bare `after` bytes are stamped with the live state in `_stamp_live_epoch`. The panel is refreshed from `_invalidate_active_render_state(clear_page_sizes=True)`, which every structural forward op, undo and redo calls (a rotation passes the same flag); `PDFView.populate_watermarks_list` returns early when no row would change, so a rotation does not drop the user's selection.
**Rule:** state keyed by page number must follow its page through ONE chokepoint and ride in the document snapshot. `test_04l_every_model_method_that_changes_the_live_page_list_reports_it_to_the_tools` (AST scan of `PDFModel`: a method that applies `delete_page` / `move_page` / `new_page` / `insert_pdf` / `NavigationGraft` to `self.doc` must call `_pages_restructured`; `straighten_page` replaces a page in place and is exempt) and `test_04m_...` (every controller method recording a structural `SnapshotCommand` reaches it) enforce it. Behind the scan, `WatermarkTool._reconcile` detects a page count that does not fit the stored ids, logs "changed without notifying the tools" and falls back to the numbers (the old behaviour) instead of crashing.
**Not fixed / scope:** (1) The dialog's "all pages" stores explicit numbers, so a page inserted or merged in later is NOT covered; whether a new page should inherit an all-pages watermark is an owner question (pinned by `test_an_all_pages_watermark_does_not_grow_onto_new_pages`). (2) Watermark add / remove / update still have no undo entry; undo of a structural op restores the page identity only, never the list, so an add or remove made after the op is kept. (3) Tab detach carries the document but not the watermark list (TODOS F17-COH-2 found in passing). (4) The hidden entries live until the session closes; they are not written to the file. (5) A source scan that reads `model/pdf_model.py` must open it with `utf-8-sig` (the file starts with a BOM; both new scans failed on `U+FEFF` once).
**File:** `model/tools/watermark_tool.py`, `model/tools/base.py`, `model/tools/manager.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/edit_commands.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`, `model/pdf_optimizer.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_tool_extensions.py` (`test_watermark_stays_on_its_page_through_a_structural_op[...]`, `test_undo_and_redo_of_a_structural_op_restore_the_exact_lists`, ...), `test_scripts/test_multi_tab_plan.py` (`test_04k` .. `test_04o`), `test_scripts/test_pdf_merge_workflow.py`, `test_scripts/test_text_commit_maintenance.py`, `test_scripts/test_watermark_save_noop.py`

## Export pages as PDF and merge into a new file left out the pending watermark that view, print, image export and Save all show (F17-COH-4)
**Area:** `model/pdf_model.py` (`export_pages` PDF branch, `compose_merged_document` / `compose_merged_document_with_origins`, `_prepare_derived_document`), `model/tools/watermark_tool.py` (`prepare_derived_document`, `_bake`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`save_ordered_sources_as_new`, `merge_ordered_sources_into_current`)
**Symptom:** (Round 17.) With a pending watermark on every page, "export pages as image", print, the view and Save showed it (page darkness 12.39); the exported PDF measured 11.08, held no watermark text and no attachment, and the merged copy of the current document had none either.
**Cause:** both writers copy pages out of the UNBAKED live document (the watermark is an overlay on the live document, M9-2) and hand the copy to `save_external_document`, which does not run the save hooks.
**Fix:** `ToolExtension.prepare_derived_document(session_id, doc, origins)` (`ToolManager` fans it out; `PDFModel._prepare_derived_document` is the single call). The watermark tool remaps each watermark to the output's page numbers (`origins[j]` = live page that output page `j + 1` was copied from; `None` for pages of another file), then runs the same `_bake` as the save clone: the ink (marked, F17-COH-2) and the `__pdf_editor_watermarks` attachment with the OUTPUT's numbering, so reopening the export draws one copy. An output that holds none of a watermark's pages gets neither. `export_pages` passes the exported order (duplicates and reordering work); `compose_merged_document` bakes by default and tracks the origins of each source page; `compose_merged_document(bake_watermarks=False)` is for the merge INTO the current document, whose result becomes the live unbaked document (baking there would draw the watermark twice, F17-COH-2) and whose watermark list follows its pages through F17-COH-3.
**Rule:** a function that writes a PDF built from the session's pages must run the bake. `test_every_caller_of_save_external_document_runs_the_session_bake` (AST scan of `pdf_model.py` and `pdf_controller.py`: exactly `export_pages` and `save_ordered_sources_as_new`, each reaching `_prepare_derived_document` or `compose_merged_document` without `bake_watermarks=False`) fails a new writer that skips it. The tab-detach transfer is live session state, not a user file, and is not baked (TODOS F17-COH-2 found in passing).
**Not fixed / scope:** (1) `export_pages` as image was already right. (2) A merge of FILES that carry their own baked watermark copies keeps those as page content (no attachment is copied), the same as before. (3) The exported / merged file is not signed or encrypted by the bake itself: encryption follows `save_external_document` and `keep_encryption`, as before.
**File:** `model/pdf_model.py`, `model/tools/watermark_tool.py`, `model/tools/base.py`, `model/tools/manager.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`; tests `test_scripts/test_merge_composition.py` (`test_export_pages_as_pdf_*`, `test_compose_*`, `test_every_caller_of_save_external_document_runs_the_session_bake`), `test_scripts/test_pdf_merge_workflow.py` (`test_save_ordered_sources_as_new_bakes_the_pending_watermark`), `test_scripts/test_watermark_save_noop.py` (`test_a_pdf_exported_with_a_pending_watermark_reopens_with_one_copy`, `test_a_merged_new_file_with_a_pending_watermark_reopens_with_one_copy`)

## The consented rebuild and the same-page drag drew the text they wrote as plain RGB fill: invisible OCR text became visible, layers, CMYK / spot colour, alpha, blend and outline were lost (F17-COL-1..4)
**Area:** `model/text_paint_state.py` (`PageTextStates`, `style_for_run(s)`, `refusal_for`, `paint_state_applied`), `model/pdf_text_edit.py` (`_rebuild_paint`, `_replay_protected_spans`, `_apply_redact_insert_body`, `_push_down_overlapping_text`, `_refuse_moving_styled_text`, `edit_text(moving_off_page=)`), `controller/pdf_controller.py` (`move_text_across_pages`), `model/text_edit_refusal.py` / `controller/text_edit_refusals.py` (`TEXT_STATE_NOT_REPRODUCIBLE`)
**Symptom:** (Round 17, measured.) After a consented rebuild ("改用重建文字…", `legacy_redact_reinsert`) or a same-page drag, live and after save + reopen: invisible OCR text (`3 Tr`, the app's own `apply_ocr_spans` layer) was drawn as black text over the scan (2487 changed pixels, the replayed neighbour line too); on `test-large-file.pdf` the untouched invisible `<T»>` became large black glyphs over a logo; an edited room label of `ecc-dwg.pdf` left its layer and stayed visible with the layer off; CMYK, K-only black, gray, Separation and Indexed colour became RGB; `/ca` alpha and blend modes were dropped; outline text (`1 Tr` / `2 Tr`) became solid fill. Tier 0/1 kept all of it.
**Cause:** every writer of the rebuild (`insert_htmlbox` through `insert_htmlbox_tracked`, `insert_text` through `insert_text_page_space`) draws DeviceRGB fill text with no render mode, ExtGState or marked content, and the rebuild handed them only (text, size, RGB colour, font): the edited runs, the overlapping neighbours it replays (`_protected_span_replay_style`) and the blocks the overflow push-down moves. Nothing captured the source paint state before the redaction erased it.
**Fix:** one capture and one re-apply. `PageTextStates(page)` walks the page's content streams and the form XObjects they invoke (lossless `pdf_lexer`) and records, per text show, the render mode, the fill (and, for stroking modes, the stroke) colour space and components, the ExtGState entries that change how the text looks (alpha, blend, soft mask, overprint, transfer, pen for stroking modes) and the enclosing `/OC` marked content (and a form's `/OC`). Plain text (DeviceRGB fill, `0 Tr`, nothing else) needs nothing; a page whose shows all share one state needs no mapping; otherwise a scratch copy of the page draws every show in a unique fill colour and MuPDF's own rawdict extraction says which show drew which glyph (no geometry matching). `_rebuild_paint` takes it in `edit_text` BEFORE the consent prompt (and `_apply_redact_insert_body` for direct callers), the push-down takes its own before its redaction. Every live-page write of the rebuild runs inside `with paint_state_applied(page, style)`: the writer's own colour / `Tr` / pen / `gs` operators are removed from the stream and the form XObjects it created, the stream is wrapped in `q [/OC /n BDC] <colour> [<stroke colour, pen>] [/GSn gs] ... [EMC] Q` with the resources registered in the page (by value), and `n Tr` goes right after every `BT` the writer drew (inside the htmlbox form), and the result is read back with the same walker (a mismatch takes the write back and refuses). A user-chosen colour keeps the writer's RGB fill (everything else still applied); several edited runs with different fills are mapped back per drawn colour.
**Rule:** text a rewrite draws again must be painted in the state it was captured in, or refused. Text state (`Tr`) belongs INSIDE the text objects: the save's content cleaning drops a `Tr` set outside `BT` in a stream that draws no text itself, so a page-level `3 Tr` before htmlbox's `q /fzFrmN Do Q` survived live and came back visible after save + reopen (measured during the fix); colour, `gs`, pen and `/OC` marked content around the `Do` survive. A state a page-level wrapper cannot reproduce refuses with `TEXT_STATE_NOT_REPRODUCIBLE` (one zh-TW sentence) before anything is written: a clipping render mode (4-7), a Pattern colour, stroked text under a scaled CTM, a soft mask set under a non-identity CTM or carried by text that moves (drag, push-down), edited runs that differ in anything but their fill, two edited runs drawn in one RGB colour from different colour spaces, or a page the capture cannot read (over 64 MB of stream, a show without operands, form recursion, a scratch copy that does not line up). `test_every_rebuild_write_goes_through_the_paint_state_chokepoint` (AST scan of `pdf_text_edit.py`) fails a new live-page writer call outside `paint_state_applied`. A cross-page move re-creates the text as a plain RGB text box: source text that is invisible, outline, translucent / blended or layered refuses before any change (`moving_off_page=True` on the source deletion).
**Not fixed / scope:** (1) Non-OC marked content (`/MCID` structure, `/Artifact`, `/ActualText`) is not paint and is still dropped by a rebuild, as before. (2) A cross-page move still turns a gray / CMYK / spot colour into the text box's RGB colour (owner question, TODOS). (3) DeviceGray black is non-plain, so most Office text now goes through the wrapper (and through the scratch tagging when the page mixes gray and RGB text); the visual result is the same, the operators are the source's. (4) An invisible (`3 Tr`) edit commits invisibly: after the consent nothing visible changes. (5) The OCR replayed neighbour is still written as one string where the source had one show per word (the text layer merges, as before; F13-VF-3 geometry). (6) Not driven by a human in the GUI.
**File:** `model/text_paint_state.py`, `model/pdf_text_edit.py`, `model/pdf_model.py`, `controller/pdf_controller.py`, `model/text_edit_refusal.py`, `controller/text_edit_refusals.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_editing_fidelity_suite.py`, `test_scripts/test_overlap_textbox_edit.py`, `test_scripts/test_ocr_model_insert.py`, `test_scripts/test_cross_page_text_move.py`, `test_scripts/test_text_edit_refusal_messages.py`

## Object text from `xref_object` and `xref_set_key` is not the object: written back, it renamed names that hold a literal `\uXXXX` (W1B-DICT-RT, fixed)
**Area:** `utils/pdf_object_source.py` (`xref_object_exact`, the reader, and `xref_set_key_exact` / `exact_set_key`, the key setters `model/` and `utils/` now use); `model/text_commit/inspect.py` (`capture_stream_storage`, `restore_stream_storage`, `StreamStorage`; `capture_annotation_parent_refs`, `restore_annotation_parent_refs`) and the code that calls `restore_stream_storage(`: `model/text_commit/patch.py` (`AppliedPatch.revert`, reached from `TieredCommitEngine.commit` in `model/text_commit/engine.py` when the live verification of a just-applied tiered text commit fails or raises, and from `PlanPreviewRenderer.render` in `model/text_commit/preview.py`, the per-keystroke live preview of an inline text edit, which reverts its patch on the scratch copy after every render), `model/edit_commands.py` (`EditTextCommand._apply_retained_patchset`, `_redo_tier0` and `undo`: Undo and Redo of a committed tiered text edit, and the put-back of a replay that failed half way) and `model/tools/manager.py` (`_ProtectedPageGuard._restore_record`, reached through `roll_back` when a save hook rewrote a fidelity-protected page during `ToolManager.prepare_doc_for_save`, that is in a Save, a Save As or an optimized copy); `model/page_snapshot.py` (`capture_page_graph`, `restore_page_graph`, `_write_record`: the page-graph snapshot behind page-level undo and redo); `model/tools/manager.py` (`_storage_key`, `_StreamRecord.decoded`, `_restore_record` and its fallback, `roll_back`); `model/signed_append_save.py` (`_source`, the replay in `try_append_state_onto_source`: a Save of a signed PDF); `model/navigation_graft.py` (`_load` and everything it feeds: links, name trees, the `/Annots` appender `_append_annots`, the outline import) with `model/page_refs.py` (`repoint_page_references`: destinations and the legacy `/Dests` after a page delete or move); `model/text_paint_state.py` (`_ensure_resources`: a styled text edit on a page that inherits an indirect `/Resources`); `model/font_stream_compaction.py` (`_dict_signature`, the new-font-stream dedupe); `model/tools/annotation_tool.py` (`_reattach_annot`); and, as hardening, the object reads of `model/text_commit/` (`cid_fonts`, `fonts`, `inspect`, `marked_content`, `plan`, `transforms`) and `model/text_paint_state.py`; and every key set in `model/`: the 33 `xref_set_key` calls of `annot_geometry`, `font_stream_compaction`, `navigation_graft`, `outline_ops`, `page_refs`, `pdf_model`, `pdf_object_ops`, `text_paint_state`, `tools/annotation_tool`, `tools/manager` and `tools/watermark_rendering`, and the 14 calls of PyMuPDF methods that set keys (`Annot.set_colors`, `Document.set_metadata`, `subset_fonts`, `Page.replace_image`, `embfile_add`)
**Symptom:** (Found in the w1b /simplify review; its follow-up review found the other paths.) A stream whose dictionary holds a name with a literal backslash-u escape, for example `/F\u0031` (the bytes `F`, backslash, `u`, `0`, `0`, `3`, `1`: a backslash is a regular character in a PDF name), comes back from the exact restore as `/F1`: the content stream still selects `/F\u0031`, the font reference no longer resolves, the page renders differently and nothing is logged (`restore_stream_storage` returns True). A name with `\udc80` decodes to a lone surrogate and makes `update_object` raise `UnicodeEncodeError`, so the exact restore logs one WARNING and falls back to a compressed decoded-bytes restore: the dictionary keeps its name, but an unfiltered stream longer than 30 bytes that compresses smaller comes back `/FlateDecode` (decoded content equal). The page-graph snapshot did the same to every object reachable from the page, the page dictionary and its inline `/Resources` included: a restore renamed a page font `/F\u0031` to `/F1` (the text then rendered without its font) and a `\udc80` name failed the restore ("page snapshot restore failed; page put back"). The fallback of `_ProtectedPageGuard._restore_record` (the original content cannot be re-decoded) wrote the raw bytes with `update_stream(raw, compress=False)`, which drops `/Filter`, then raised on a `\udc80` dictionary: a filtered stream was left as encoded bytes with no filter, the page content lost; and `roll_back` always set the page's `/Contents` again with `xref_set_key`, which renamed the page's own names. The signed append save replayed each changed object of the live document onto the signed source from `xref_object` text: adding a highlight to a page whose inline `/Resources` call `/F\u0031` saved a signed file whose page font is `/F1`, with no warning (the post-save check compares decoded text on both sides), and a `\udc80` name ended in `append_error`, the full rewrite that drops the signature. Deleting a page rebuilt the catalog's legacy `/Dests` from `navigation_graft._load`'s parse of `xref_object` text: a destination `/sec\u0031` came back as `/sec1` and the link that selects it stopped resolving (with `\udc80` the step failed and the deleted page's entry stayed). A styled text edit on a page that inherits an indirect `/Resources` copied that dictionary onto the page from `xref_object` text (`_ensure_resources`), and the page's other text lost its font. Two new font streams whose dictionaries differ only by such a name were deduplicated into one (`_dict_signature`). `xref_set_key` did the same to the object it edited: a styled text edit registering its graphics state in a page's inline `/Resources`, a link appended to a page's `/Annots`, the protected-page rollback of a replaced `/Contents`, a baked watermark stripped on open and an image deleted renamed the page's font `/F\u0031` to `/F1`; dropping the `/OpenAction` of a deleted page renamed the form's default font in the catalog; retitling a bookmark renamed the named destination its action jumps to; editing the metadata renamed a custom Info key. A `\udc80` name raised `UnicodeEncodeError` after the placeholder was in the live object, so the edited key was left as the string `(fitz: replace me!)` (a page's `/Contents` or `/Annots`, the catalog's `/OpenAction`, `/PageLabels` or `/Outlines`, a bookmark's `/Title`), and a refused paint state raised that error from its rollback in place of the refusal; an edited key itself named with such an escape was not found in the decoded text, so its placeholder stayed even with no other such name (deleting the image `/Im\u0031`). PyMuPDF's own `Annot.set_colors`, `Document.set_metadata` and `Page.replace_image` (through `xref_copy`) call `xref_set_key`.
**Cause:** `capture_stream_storage` stores `doc.xref_object(xref)` as `StreamStorage.obj`. `xref_object` returns the object text decoded with `raw_unicode_escape` (PyMuPDF 1.27.1: `JM_EscapeStrFromBuffer`; observed on the compiled path this environment uses: `xref_object` shows `/F1` where `xref_get_key` shows `F\u0031`), so the escape `\u0031` reads as the character `1` and `\udc80` as the lone surrogate U+DC80. `restore_stream_storage` writes that decoded text back with `update_object(xref, storage.obj)`, which encodes it as UTF-8 and parses it (`JM_pdf_obj_from_str`). Its self-check compares `xref_object` text with `xref_object` text, both decoded alike, so it passes. `StreamStorage.raw` is exact; only the dictionary round trip is lossy. Every other path above read `xref_object` text the same way and wrote it back (`update_object`, the value of `xref_set_key`, `page_snapshot._write_record`) or used it to prove two objects the same. `xref_set_key` decodes inside: PyMuPDF's `JM_set_object_value` puts a placeholder at the key, prints the whole object, decodes that text with the same `JM_EscapeStrFromBuffer`, looks for `/<key>(fitz: replace me!)` in it, swaps the value in and parses the text again.
**Fix:** `utils/pdf_object_source.xref_object_exact(doc, xref, *, compressed=False)` prints the object with the same MuPDF printer (`pdf_load_object` -> `JM_object_to_buffer`; `-1` prints the trailer) and keeps the bytes undecoded. The printer escapes every byte outside printable ASCII (`#xx` in a name, octal in a string), so the text is ASCII (decoded strictly; a byte outside ASCII, or a PyMuPDF without the private printer, falls back to `xref_object` with one WARNING per process), and `update_object`, which encodes UTF-8 and parses, writes back exactly the object that was read. It raises what `xref_object` raises (`ValueError` for a closed document; `RuntimeError` for a non-PDF document, an xref out of range or a slot without an object, MuPDF's error re-raised without a chained traceback), so the callers' `except` clauses are unchanged. `model/` and `utils/` read objects with it: every capture, comparison and write-back of the paths above (`StreamStorage.obj` and both checks of `restore_stream_storage`, the annotation backup, the `capture_page_graph` records and the live reads of `restore_page_graph` / `_write_record`, the guard's `_storage_key`, `_load`, `_ensure_resources`, `_dict_signature`, the `/Annots` array read of the two appenders) and, as hardening, the object reads of `model/text_commit/` and `text_paint_state` (probed: the text engine already binds the right font for `/F\u0031 Tf` with a `/F1` beside it, because its font lookup does not parse that text). The signed append save's replay reads exact text (`_source(..., exact=True)`); its comparisons (`_differing_xrefs`, `_identical`) keep `xref_object`: about three times cheaper per object on whole-table walks, and decoded text can miss only a change between names that decode alike (`/F\u0031` and `/F1`, two escapes that decode to the same replacement character, or in `_same_object_text` two that decode outside Latin-1), which nothing in the app produces except that decode. `roll_back` sets `/Contents` again only when a hook replaced it. For an object without such a name the text is the one `xref_object` returns (161,568 objects of the 2,936 readable PDFs under `test_files`, two password-protected ones skipped: none differ), so captured text, fingerprints and comparisons are unchanged for every ordinary file. Cost: about 7.5 us per object against 2.2 us for `xref_object` (a 1,000-object page snapshot: +5 ms; the page fingerprints of three pages of each of 38 corpus files: 70 -> 74 ms). Keys: `xref_set_key_exact(doc, xref, key, value)` is PyMuPDF 1.27.1's `xref_set_key` with `JM_set_object_value` inlined and the printed object decoded as ASCII; the checks, the exceptions (types and arguments), the MuPDF calls and their order and PyMuPDF's quirks are kept (`null` stored as null, `-1` the trailer, the placeholder left when the value does not parse or when the key exists behind an indirect dictionary of the path), so an object without such a name comes out the same (24 cases pinned slot by slot; 147,692 dictionary objects of the 2,936 readable PDFs under `test_files`, a key added and then nulled on each: none differ, and none fell back to PyMuPDF's decode). (Superseded 2026-10-22 by W1B-SETKEY-PH: the setter parses the value alone and puts it at the key, so nothing of the object is printed or decoded.) Its error is raised outside the MuPDF frames and without their traceback, so a kept error no longer keeps a closed file open (PyMuPDF's does, LS-3); the exception its caller is handling (a rollback after a failure) keeps its own traceback. `exact_set_key(doc)` shadows `doc.xref_set_key` on that instance for a `with` block, so PyMuPDF's own methods, which call `doc.xref_set_key`, set keys exactly; it is removed on the way out and a block inside another changes nothing. Without the private PyMuPDF functions, or on a printed byte outside ASCII, it does what PyMuPDF does (one WARNING per process).
**Rules:** text from `xref_object` is not the object: read with `xref_object_exact`. `test_xref_object_is_read_only_where_it_is_still_called` fails on any `.xref_object(` call in `model/` or `utils/` outside its reviewed list: the whole-document walks that use a slot's references, size or null-ness (`xref_compaction.read_every_object` / `open_compaction_verdict`, `save_compaction._object_text`, `pdf_optimizer.xref_size_bytes`, `pdf_validator.check_pdf_conformance`), the signed append comparisons (`signed_append_save._source`) and the helper's own fallback; a stale entry fails too. `test_xref_set_key_is_called_only_by_the_exact_helper` fails on any `.xref_set_key` (or `"xref_set_key"`) in `model/` or `utils/` outside the helper; `test_pymupdf_methods_that_set_keys_run_inside_exact_set_key` on a call of a PyMuPDF method that sets keys (`_PYMUPDF_SET_KEY_CALLERS`) outside a `with exact_set_key(...)` block of its function (calls only: an alias or `getattr` escapes it, and `options.subset_fonts` is a setting), and `test_the_guarded_methods_are_every_pymupdf_caller_of_xref_set_key` checks that list against the installed PyMuPDF's source (a version that adds a caller fails). Not looked for by name: `Link.set_flags` (`Annot.set_flags` shares the name and sets no key; the model sets flags on annotations only) and `Widget.update` (the model never updates a widget).
**Probe:** (before the fix) a one-page PDF assembled by hand: the page draws `q /Fm0 Do Q`; Form XObject 5 has `/Resources << /Font << /F\u0031 4 0 R >> >>`, an unfiltered 41-byte stream `BT /F\u0031 24 Tf 72 700 Td (Hello) Tj ET` and no `/Filter`; object 4 is Helvetica. The form's stream was swapped for a blank (`update_stream(xref, b" ")`) and put back, once with the main textbox pair (`update_stream` of the saved decoded bytes) and once with `capture_stream_storage` / `restore_stream_storage`; `xref_object`, `xref_get_key(5, "Resources/Font")`, the rawdict span fonts, the MuPDF warnings and a 36 dpi render hash were read before, after the restore, and after `save` and reopen. Main pair: `Resources/Font` stays `<</F\u0031 4 0 R>>`, the span font stays `Helvetica` and the render hash stays `6d92785b` in all three states, for `F\u0031` and for `F\udc80`. Helper with `F\u0031`: `Resources/Font` became `<</F1 4 0 R>>`, the span font went from `Helvetica` to an empty string, the render hash changed (`6d92785b` -> `a2639302`), no WARNING was logged, and the same held after save and reopen. Helper with `F\udc80`: one WARNING (`UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode character '\udc80'`), the dictionary and the render hash unchanged (the 41-byte stream stayed unfiltered; `JM_update_stream` compresses a stream only when it is longer than 30 bytes and the result is smaller).
**Not fixed / scope:** (1) Fixed 2026-10-22, see W1B-SETKEY-PH (next entry): the setter kept PyMuPDF's placeholder quirk at first (a key that exists behind an indirect dictionary of the path got `(fitz: replace me!)` in that object; the image prune and page straighten set such keys); it no longer prints the object at all, so the "Keys" part of the Fix above describes the first version.
