(2) The signed append comparisons and the whole-document walks of the reviewed list still read decoded text (see Fix). (3) The textbox form swap / restore (`_swap_form_stream`, `_restore_form_stream` in `model/pdf_object_ops.py`) restore with `update_stream` alone and never write dictionary text (unchanged since the w1b pass-2 revert). (4) `Document.subset_fonts` also writes `xref_object` text back with `update_object`, but only to the font objects `_insert_font` just built, whose names come from the font program.
**Gotchas:** (1) A test of such a name must not use `xref_object` as its oracle (it decodes both sides alike): compare `xref_get_key` (it prints a name undecoded), the raw bytes or the render. (2) `xref_get_key` of a `string` value is decoded text, not source. (3) The fixtures build objects with `update_object` of ASCII text holding the literal backslash, which is byte-exact. (4) A `RuntimeError` raised in a frame that holds a MuPDF object (the SWIG document wrapper) keeps the file open after `doc.close()` for as long as the error is kept (probed: `os.replace` over the file fails), and `raise ... from None` still keeps `__context__`: the helper prints in `_print_object`, which returns the error message, and raises outside any handler; `_set_object_value` returns its error without frames for the same reason. (5) `fitz` re-exports `pymupdf`: a private PyMuPDF function patched on `fitz` is not what PyMuPDF's own code calls (patch `pymupdf` too). (6) A fixture that holds such a name must not be edited with PyMuPDF's `xref_set_key` (it renames the fixture itself); build it with `update_object` of exact text.
**File:** `utils/pdf_object_source.py`, `model/text_commit/inspect.py`, `model/page_snapshot.py`, `model/tools/manager.py`, `model/signed_append_save.py`, `model/navigation_graft.py`, `model/text_paint_state.py`, `model/font_stream_compaction.py`, `model/tools/annotation_tool.py`, `model/text_commit/cid_fonts.py`, `fonts.py`, `marked_content.py`, `plan.py`, `transforms.py`, and for the keys `model/annot_geometry.py`, `outline_ops.py`, `page_refs.py`, `pdf_model.py`, `pdf_object_ops.py`, `pdf_optimizer.py`, `tools/watermark_rendering.py`, `tools/watermark_tool.py`; `test_scripts/test_exact_object_text.py` (140 tests at the time; W1B-SETKEY-PH below changed the setter's cases and added its own: the reader keeps the escape, equals `xref_object` elsewhere and on the storage fixtures, and raises what it raises; for `F\u0031`, `F\udc80`, `F\U00000031` and a truncated `F\u00` each: the stream-storage restore of a Form XObject dictionary with save and reopen, the patch revert of a content-stream key, the annotation dictionary restore, the page-snapshot restore of the page's inline font name, the protected-page rollback of a content-stream key, its fallback without the decoded original and its rollback of a page with such a font name, the signed append save of a page with such a font name, the legacy `/Dests` rebuild after a page delete, the inherited `/Resources` copy, the two `/Annots` appenders on an array object of its own; the new-font-stream dedupe; the reader's two fallbacks; a kept read error does not keep the closed file open; the guard; for the keys: the setter does what `xref_set_key` does to objects without such a name (24 cases then, 34 now, no fallback warning) and raises what it raises, leaves the traceback of the error its caller handles, routes over an attribute it did not install and puts it back, keeps such a name elsewhere in the object, routes `Annot.set_colors`, `Document.set_metadata` and `Page.replace_image` inside `exact_set_key` and only there, does not keep a closed file open with a kept error, falls back with one warning; for each name: the paint-state registration, the two `/Annots` appenders on the page dictionary, the protected-page rollback of a replaced `/Contents`, an image deleted, a refused paint state's rollback, a baked watermark stripped, the `/OpenAction` of a deleted page, a retitled bookmark, the metadata edit; the two guards and the pin of PyMuPDF's callers)

## `xref_set_key` left the string `(fitz: replace me!)` in place of the value: a key behind an indirect dictionary, a key printed otherwise, a value that is not one object (W1B-SETKEY-PH, fixed)
**Area:** `utils/pdf_object_source.py` (`xref_set_key_exact` with `_object_at`, `_one_object`, `_walk`; `xref_key_holder`), so every key `model/` sets and every PyMuPDF method run inside `exact_set_key`; the two user actions that hit it: page straighten (`model/outline_ops.py` `move_targets_to_page` and `retarget_item`, `A/D` of a bookmark whose GoTo action is an object of its own) and deleting an image (`model/pdf_object_ops.py` `_remove_native_image_invocation` with `_streams_resolving_the_entry`, `Resources/XObject/<name>` of a page or form whose `/Resources` or `/XObject` is an object of its own)
**Symptom:** (Found 2026-10-21 in the review of the exact set_key, W1B-DICT-RT; TODOS.) Page straighten on a bookmark whose GoTo action is an object of its own wrote `(fitz: replace me!)` into the action's `/D`: the bookmark lost its page (TOC page 0) while the move was counted. Deleting an image on a page whose `/Resources` is an object of its own (every page PyMuPDF makes) wrote that string in place of the image's name instead of `null`; when other pages shared that object and drew the image, their image went too (two pages, one `<</XObject<</Im0 7 0 R>>>>`, both drawing `/Im0`: after the delete on page 1, page 2 drew nothing), and so did a form those pages draw that resolves its names there. Beyond the two actions (differential probe): a key printed otherwise (`F#20G`, `Fé`) or with a trailing slash (`Trail/`) kept the placeholder; a value that is not one PDF object raised after the placeholder was in the live object (`[1 2`, `1 2`, `(a`), added a key of its own (`1 0 R/X 2` set `/X 2` too) or stored null (`R`, `]`); creating a key behind an indirect dictionary raised `path to '...' has indirects`.
**Cause:** PyMuPDF 1.27.1's `JM_set_object_value` puts the placeholder at the key with MuPDF's `pdf_dict_putp`, which follows an indirect dictionary of the path and writes into it; then it prints the object it was given (a reference prints as `N 0 R`), swaps `/<key> <value>` in for `/<key>(fitz: replace me!)` as text and parses the text again for `pdf_update_object`. Where the swap finds nothing (the placeholder sits in another object; the key is printed as `#xx`; Python's `split` names the key `""` for a trailing slash) the reparsed object still holds the placeholder; where the value does not parse, it is already in the live object; and the swap as text lets a value of several objects add keys. The image prune's "still drawn" scan took only pages whose effective resource owner had the same xref (`_effective_page_xobject_binding`), and every page that holds `/Resources` is its own owner, so pages sharing that object were never scanned.
**Fix:** `xref_set_key_exact` no longer prints the object: the first intentional deviation from PyMuPDF's method (owner decision 2026-10-22: fix it once in the exact set_key), and the W1B-DICT-RT decode goes with it. Order: PyMuPDF's checks with its exceptions (closed document, key, value, xref; MuPDF's own errors for a key path of 256 bytes or more and for an object that is no dictionary), then `_one_object` parses the value alone (inside `[...]`: exactly one element and nothing after it, else `ValueError("bad 'value'")`; MuPDF's syntax error passes through; a bare word reads as null, as in a dictionary), then `_walk` goes down the levels above the last as `pdf_dict_putp` does (MuPDF's split: a trailing slash ends the path) and `pdf_dict_puts` puts the value at the last key (null stored as null, in place). A level that is an indirect dictionary (a stream's dictionary included, and through a chain of references to the object at its end, as MuPDF resolves it) is followed, so the key is set where `xref_get_key` reads it and created there when missing; a level that is an indirect object of another kind (array, number, reference to no object) raises PyMuPDF's `Exception("path to '%s' has indirects", <last key>)`; a missing or direct non-dictionary level becomes a new direct dictionary, as before. Every refusal comes before the first write, so a call that raises changes nothing. `xref_key_holder(doc, xref, key)` names the object that holds the last level (the last indirect dictionary the path goes through, else `xref`, `-1` the trailer; for a reference, or a chain of them, the object at its end), with the same walk. The image prune nulls the name only when no stream that resolves it to the same entry still draws it (`_streams_resolving_the_entry`): the invocation's stream, the contents of every page whose effective binding is held by the same object, and, when that object is not the owner itself, every stream whose own `/Resources` lead there (form XObjects, tiling patterns, appearance streams); it keeps the entry when the holder cannot be told or an object of another kind resolves the name there (a Type3 font: its glyph procedures are not read). Page straighten counts a bookmark whose action is shared with one moved before as moved: it already targets the new page (`retarget_item` gave it a whole-page action of its own, detaching it from the shared one). Same as PyMuPDF's method wherever that leaves no placeholder: 34 cases pinned slot by slot (objects and exception type and arguments), and the 147,692 dictionary objects of the 2,936 readable PDFs under `test_files`, a new key set to a name, an array with a reference, a dictionary, a string and null on each (738,460 edits): none differ from PyMuPDF's result, so its print and reparse of the rest of the object changed nothing there either. Cost of the prune's walk over every object (only when the holder is not the owner): about 12 to 30 ms on the corpus files of 4,000 to 11,000 objects, 120 ms (180 ms cold) on the largest (40,016 objects), per deleted image. MuPDF marks the object it writes into, so a full and an incremental save carry the change, also for an object kept in an object stream.
**Rules:** set keys only with `xref_set_key_exact` (W1B-DICT-RT's guards). A write through an indirect dictionary changes it for every object that refers to it: when that matters (a shared `/Resources`, an action used by a bookmark and a link), ask `xref_key_holder` where the key lives and decide there (the image prune compares holders; page straighten moves every target into the replaced page, so a shared action moving for all is the intent). `test_exact_set_key_never_leaves_a_placeholder_and_changes_only_the_holder` runs 5 target kinds × 19 key paths × 12 values: no object holds the placeholder afterwards, a call that raises changes no object, one that returns changes only the holder and reads back through the path.
**Probe:** (before the fix) three pages, a bookmark `<</Title(Two)/A 9 0 R>>`, object 9 `<</S/GoTo/D[<page 2> 0 R/XYZ 0 100 0]>>`: `move_targets_to_page(doc, 1, 2)` returned 1, object 9 then read `<</S/GoTo/D(fitz: replace me!)>>` and `get_toc()` gave page 0. Two pages sharing `/Resources` object 8 `<</XObject<</Im0 7 0 R>>>>`, both drawing `/Im0`: after the delete on page 1, object 8 held `/Im0(fitz: replace me!)` and page 2 rendered 0 dark pixels at 36 dpi (1600 before). Differential of PyMuPDF's method and a placeholder-free prototype over 5 target kinds × 18 key paths × up to 35 values (825 cases): every difference was a placeholder left, a key added by the value, null stored for `R` or `]`, a refused create behind an indirect dictionary, or an exception message; MuPDF's `pdf_dict_putp` with null deleted the key (Gotcha 1).
**Not fixed / scope:** (1) PyMuPDF's own method keeps the quirk (tests use it as the counter-example); without `_as_pdf_document` the helper calls it (one WARNING) and `xref_key_holder` raises, so the image prune keeps the entry. (2) The image prune does not see a form or pattern without `/Resources` of its own (it takes the page's) that draws the name; a stream that nothing draws, or a Type3 font, whose resources hold the entry keeps it (and so the image stays in the saved file). (3) A caller that needs a private copy of a shared dictionary must make it before setting the key; nothing in `model/` does yet. (4) `outline_ops.retarget_item` (an item whose destination is not an array of the moved page, and the repair after a page delete) still sets `A/D` only in an inline action: a bookmark whose GoTo action is an object of its own gets a new inline whole-page action, so its view and the action's other keys (`/Next`) are dropped and it no longer shares the action (unchanged, found in the review; `move_targets_to_page` swaps the page inside the action and is not affected). Likewise an indirect `/Dest` array is replaced, not edited.
**Gotchas:** (1) `pdf_dict_putp(obj, key, null)` deletes the key, and the dictionary moves its last entry into the hole (MuPDF's `PDF_NULL` is the C NULL, its "delete" signal): put the last level with `pdf_dict_puts`, which stores null. (2) `pdf_parse_stm_obj` reads a top-level `1 0 R` as the number 1 (a reference is recognized inside an array or a dictionary only): parse the value inside `[...]` and check that the lexer is at the end. (3) A bare word (`abc`, `obj`) parses as null in an array and in a dictionary alike. (4) MuPDF splits a key path like Python's `split("/")` except that a trailing slash ends it; its buffer takes 255 bytes. (5) Code written against PyMuPDF's refusal to create behind an indirect dictionary would now write into that object; none in `model/` (`text_paint_state` resolves the holder itself with `_dict_holder`, `navigation_graft` sets `Names/Dests` only in a direct `/Names`, `page_refs` sets `/D` of an inline action only). (6) A `fitz.Page` loaded before the set sees the new value (in-place write; PyMuPDF's `pdf_update_object` showed it too). (7) An object can be just a reference (`6 0 obj 5 0 R endobj`); MuPDF resolves such a chain (up to 9 hops) wherever it reads or writes, so the holder is the object at the end of the chain, not the first number (review finding: two pages whose `/Resources` were `6 0 R` and `5 0 R` for the same dictionary got different holders, and the prune took the image from the other page).
**File:** `utils/pdf_object_source.py`, `model/pdf_object_ops.py`; `test_scripts/test_exact_object_text.py` (the parity cases now include a bare word, direct non-dictionary levels, MuPDF's empty levels, the indirect resources dictionary edited itself, the refused paths through an indirect array, number and missing object, the array and number objects as targets and a 300-byte key; the key behind an indirect dictionary set and created in it, with an incremental and a full save, plain and in object streams; null stored there as null; a level that is a stream followed into its dictionary; a chain of references, as a level and as the object itself; `xref_key_holder` raises what the setter raises; ten values that are not one object refused with no object changed; three keys printed otherwise; the class guard, which also pins which cases must raise; the setter does not print the object; the fallback; a kept error of a refused path and of MuPDF's parse does not keep the closed file open), `test_scripts/test_bookmarks_toc.py` (`test_straighten_page_keeps_a_bookmark_whose_goto_action_is_an_object_of_its_own`, `test_straighten_page_moves_bookmarks_that_share_one_action_object_together`), `test_scripts/test_native_pdf_images_model.py` (`test_delete_native_image_prunes_the_entry_of_a_resources_object`; `test_delete_native_image_on_a_shared_resources_object_prunes_only_when_nothing_else_draws_it`: page 2, a form on page 2 or a pattern on page 2 draws it, a Type3 font uses those resources, nothing else draws it and the save drops the image; a form-nested delete keeps the name a page sharing the form's resources draws; the name is kept when its holder cannot be told)

## page.annots() raises AttributeError on an inline /Annots dictionary, and xref-keyed annotation proofs collide on xref 0 (T16-4X S10)
**Area:** `model/text_commit/inspect.py` (`require_indirect_annotations`, `annotation_entries`, `_annotation_entries`, `InlineAnnotationError`), `plan.py`, `engine.py`, `preview.py`, `verify.py`.
**Symptom:** On a page whose /Annots array holds an inline annotation dictionary (for example `[<< /Type /Annot /Subtype /Text /Rect [...] >>]`), `TieredCommitEngine.prepare`, `commit` and the plan preview raised `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'm_internal'` instead of returning a refusal. Separately, the fingerprint's annotation entries gave two inline annotations the same rect (last-wins on `rects[0]`), so they were indistinguishable by xref or by rect.
**Cause:** PyMuPDF 1.27.1 `page.annot_xrefs()` reports an inline dictionary as `(0, kind, '')`, and `page.annots()` loads each entry by xref (`load_annot(0)` finds nothing). An xref-keyed proof (V0b "annotations untouched", the fingerprint's rect map) cannot identify an annotation that has no xref. Inline Link/Popup/Widget give xref 0 too but `annots()` filters those kinds out and does not raise.
**Fix:** one kind-filtered detector (`require_indirect_annotations`, shared predicate `_is_listed_inline`), one strict reader (`annotation_entries`) used by the V0b captures, an `ANNOTATIONS_NOT_INDIRECT` gate in `prepare_plan` plus backstops in `engine.prepare`, `engine.commit` (FAILED, before any splice) and the preview render. `page_fingerprint` uses a tolerant twin that takes each xref-0 rect in walk order and never raises. The typed error subclasses `Exception`, not `ValueError`/`RuntimeError`, so the existing "unreadable" handlers do not swallow it under another code. Neither reader calls `page.load_annot`: it walks the same list as `first_annot`, so it cannot find an xref the walk missed and raises a bare `Exception` that no handler names (a page handle held across an `/Annots` write lists the new xref in `annot_xrefs()` but not in MuPDF's list); an unreachable xref raises the typed error in the strict reader and takes a `(0, 0, 0, 0)` rect in the fingerprint. The View hides the rebuild button for this code (its annotation safeguard fails the same way); the model does not gate it, so a consented rebuild or move still reaches the legacy path (annotation loss from `apply_redactions` was not shown).
**Fix round 2:** `page.widgets()` has the same disagreement: it loads each `annot_xrefs()` widget row by xref and raises a bare `Exception` ("xref N is not a widget of this page") for an inline widget (xref 0) or a widget written by xref under a held handle, out of `prepare`, `page_fingerprint` and `PDFModel.edit_text`. `page_has_widgets_or_signatures` now reads the `annot_xrefs()` kinds (no widget loaded) and the fingerprint folds `_widget_entries` (tolerant `first_widget`/`next` walk). An unloadable INDIRECT annotation raises `AnnotationListOutOfSync` (subclass of `InlineAnnotationError`), mapped to `verification_failed` (prepare, preview) and `STALE_PLAN` (commit), never to `annotations_not_indirect`.
**Fix round 3:** two totality guards. `require_indirect_annotations` wraps its `annot_xrefs()` read in `except (RuntimeError, ValueError, fitz.mupdf.FzErrorBase)` and raises `InlineAnnotationError("/Annots unreadable")`, so a read failure is refused (`annotations_not_indirect`) without relying on `page_has_widgets_or_signatures` running first (PyMuPDF 1.27.1 tolerates every malformed /Annots shape probed, so the test injects the failure). `_widget_entries` wraps its `first_widget`/`next` walk in the same `except` (a widget /Parent cycle makes MuPDF raise `FzErrorFormat` "cycle in resources"; fixture-proven) and falls back to a `(0, 0, 0, 0)` rect per widget row, so `page_fingerprint` and `open_preview_session` stay total.
**Rules:** read annotations through `annotation_entries` in text-commit code, not `page.annots()`. Prove zero mutation on the object table (`xref_object_exact` plus raw streams), not on `doc.tobytes()` (its trailer `/ID` differs between calls).
**Not fixed / scope:** `model/tools/annotation_tool.py` `get_all_annotations` and `toggle_annotations_visibility` still raise on this shape (TODOS.md, T16-4).
**File:** `model/text_commit/dto.py`, `inspect.py`, `plan.py`, `engine.py`, `preview.py`, `verify.py`, `view/text_edit_reasons.py`; `test_scripts/test_text_commit_direct_annots.py`.


## A bundle's status words and numbers are claims: recompute them, and resolve a source by sha, never by the bundle's own before.pdf (I0c)
**Area:** evidence ingestion: `scripts/evidence_bundle.py`, `scripts/evidence_schemas/`, `scripts/evidence_rederive.py`, `test_scripts/fixtures/public_corpus_sha256.json`; `plans/true-text-frontier-loop.md`.
**Symptom:** A Grok bundle can satisfy its own schema and still be false: phases that self-report `pass` while the numbers say `fail`; a `K_written` that is not the NUMBER token written; a new operand holding `re f` after the string; `trm_scale` 0.0849 instead of 0.060 (the four-component norm, so `growth_pt` 2.983 instead of 2.1095); a PNG not named `render-*` (the only PNGs git ignores); a client string hiding in a hex operand; a `before.pdf` swapped for a doctored copy that "re-measures" true.
**Cause:** the schema only types the record. Every status word (`status`, `phases.*.result`, `calibration.*.ok`, `redaction.scan.*`) is a self-report, and the file the bundle ships is not the file the product sees.
**Fix:** `evidence_bundle.validate_batch` recomputes the nine phase results, the brief 5.3 status, the parent summary, the calibration controls and canaries, the pre-registration and the redaction scan from the recorded numbers, and reports every violation at once (exit 1). Whatever needs the original file is listed under `unverifiable`, which never counts as a pass. The original is resolved by `source.sha256` from tracked lists only (`public_corpus_sha256.json`, `acc.CORPORA`, the allowlisted synthetic builder; `evidence_rederive.resolve_source`), a `before.pdf` is hashed, never opened, a status never means success, experiment bytes are re-applied and both advances recomputed with the product's own functions (H1), and a machine-path test sample is built at run time.
**Rules:** (1) add a reject shape to `test_evidence_bundle_contract.py` and watch it fail before the rule exists; each forged `pass` needs an honest `fail` twin that validates. (2) Hash file bytes: a test that writes the plan with `Path.write_text` on Windows gets CRLF line ends and a digest that no longer equals `sha256(text.encode())`. (3) Lex a hex operand with `pdf_lexer.lex_content_stream` and read only STRING/HEXSTRING payloads: decoding the token text as UTF-16BE invents CJK code points. (4) Pointers and details are printed into reports that may be committed: no matched text, no unknown JSON key, no unknown file name, no bundle-supplied word outside the status/reason enums (the chokepoint is `validate_batch`; `test_planted_text_never_reaches_the_report_or_stderr` plants a sentinel in status, class_id, reason, exception_type and a file name). (5) `trm_scale` is `hypot(linear[0], linear[1])`, never `hypot(*linear)`. (6) A Tier 0 `PreparedEdit` leaves `source_advance` and `replacement_advance` at 0.0 (only Tier 1 sets them): never compare a Tier 0 record's advances to the prepared ones; the validator's `product_advance_mismatch` is Tier 1 only and rederive recomputes Tier 0's from the font tables. (7) Scratch copies that will be `saveIncr`-ed must be opened BY PATH (`ValueError: incremental needs original file` on a bytes-opened document), and `get_texttrace()` dirties the page it runs on, so locate on a `tobytes()` measurement copy. (8) A `relative_path` such as `test_files/../<batch>/candidates/<id>/before.pdf` passes the schema pattern: resolve it and require it under `<root>/test_files/` and outside the bundle directory before opening anything. (9) Open verified bytes (`fitz.open("pdf", data)`), not the path you hashed a moment ago. (10) A re-derivation report echoes nothing from the bundle or the document: route every string through `_safe_value`/`_templated`, take the case id through `_show_id`, and take the slug from the registry (`test_report_and_stderr_never_carry_bundle_words`). (11) `verify._growth_zone_rect(...)` returns a strip whose longer side is the CROSS axis when growth is smaller than the glyph height: compare the dominant-edge amount (`evidence_bundle._extent`), never `max(width, height)`. (12) Mark an `unverifiable` code closed only inside the branch that compared it. (13) Fix round 1, forger findings: a K token must carry all four K components (`k_null_rule`), the validator only sees them, so rederive recomputes `K_sum` from the fixture and `K_disp_engine` / `abs_diff_written_vs_sum_engine` from the product, but never forces `K_written == K_sum + K_disp_engine` (CANARY_KSIGN is an honest wrong sign). (14) A canary operand may carry operator operands (`0.25 Tc`, `/C2_0 97.023 Tf`): only numbers inside a TJ array are K tokens, a NAME is a resource name or scanned like text, and comment, dictionary, brace, inline-image and unknown-operator tokens are rejected. (15) The validator prints a case id outside the `r2-...` shape as a digest, in `case_id` and in `cases/<digest>/`: every consumer that matches violations to cases must match both spellings (`_cmd_rederive`), and a violation that belongs to no case taints the whole batch. (16) `emit_rows` trusts the validator's RECOMPUTED status, never a row's own kind or phases: a failed experiment would otherwise become a candidate positive. (17) An experiment row waits for the same six oracles a committed product row waits for; until they exist it is `deferred`, not `rederived`. (18) One sha256 is one document: group lineage by sha as well as by the brief 3.7 slug groups, or two labels for one file count as two lineages.
**Fix round 2 gotchas:** (a) `controls[class_id] = row` keeps the LAST row, so a failed R0 control hidden by an honest twin passed or failed depending on the order of `cases.json`: aggregate per class and reject the duplicate (`control_duplicate`). (b) `adv * hscale / 100` and `adv * (hscale / 100)` differ in the last bit for a share of Tz values; the product multiplies by `th = hscale / 100`, so an exact comparison must use the same association (the first form false-failed an honest Tz 110 Tier 1 row as `oracle_assert_growth_zone_was_blank`). (c) A PDF array parser that skips tokens it does not know (`null`, names, strings, dictionaries) shifts every later index: one token, one slot. (d) A self-reported flag the validator can recompute from boxes it already holds (`halo_shadowed`, `ink_checked`, a target record's `is_space`, the target run size) is a free pass if it is trusted. (e) `unverifiable` is not `ok`: the report says `pending_rederive`, and rederive refuses a validation file that is not for this batch name and this `cases.json` digest. (f) A list or dict in a field a check uses as a dict key raises `TypeError` and drops the whole report: coerce for the batch-level checks and guard every check (`check_error`). (g) A detail printed verbatim because the BUNDLE says `public` leaks a proprietary fixture's font names: trust the registry's provenance, not the claim.
**Probe:** the 2026-09-24 batch `_evidence_pilot/20260924_1431` (read-only) exits 1: `schema_required` for `schema_version`, `schema_additional` for `seq`, 17 `file_missing`, `done_missing`.
**Not fixed / scope:** the advance values, token alignment, frame conversion, `region_dict`, the background quad, ParentTree walk and F3 prefix/suffix of non-public rows are re-measured by `evidence_rederive.py`, not here. R0 completeness (every control and canary present) is a violation `calibration_incomplete` whenever a counted row exists (it stays `unverifiable` only in a calibration-fail batch with no frontier row); a batch with frontier rows and no R0 rows used to validate with calibration `pass` (fix round 1). Until I0a (manifest `corpora`) every `local_unrecorded` row quarantines as `provenance_unverified` and every proprietary row except hvac/ecc as `before_pdf_mismatch`; until I0b (`true_text_acceptance_helpers`) only `assert_growth_zone_was_blank` exists, so a committed row and every replayed experiment or canary row is `deferred: oracles_incomplete` and `emit_rows` writes no `engine_active` row. The 2x/6x renders, the ink-landed leg, neighbour pairing and glyph-identity gids are not re-measured yet.
**File:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py`, `scripts/evidence_bundle.py`, `scripts/evidence_schemas/true_text_{case,plan,parent}.v2.schema.json`, `test_scripts/fixtures/public_corpus_sha256.json`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_bundle_contract.py`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_rederive.py`.

## The redaction scan failed open: a non-UTF-8 file, a duplicate JSON key, an absent denylist and a free-text wrapper tag all passed it (V1/V6/R7-2)
**Area:** `scripts/evidence_bundle.py` (`_scan_texts`, `scan_redaction`, `validate_batch`, `_is_ascii_name`), `scripts/evidence_rederive.py`.
**Symptom:** A bundle file saved as UTF-16/UTF-32 or with NUL bytes, or a JSON object with a duplicate key, skipped the machine-path and denylist scan; a batch with proprietary rows validated `ok` on a machine with no denylist file; a CJK or spaced string in a wrapper `tag` was scanned as tokens and accepted.
**Cause:** The scan decoded only what it could parse as UTF-8 JSON and treated "nothing to scan" as "nothing found". A missing denylist was the same as an empty one. The wrapper tag was allowlisted by words, not by shape.
**Fix:** every .json/.md/.py file is read as bytes; one that is not strict UTF-8 (or has NULs) is `file_not_utf8` and still raw-scanned under every plausible decoding (BOM, utf-16 le/be, utf-8 replace), line by line, also with JSON escapes unescaped. JSON loads with an object-pairs hook (duplicate key is unparseable). `denylist_missing` is raised when any row is not provably public/synthetic and no denylist was loaded (`denylist_required` makes an explicit missing `--denylist` path fatal); the report carries `denylist_present` and `denylist_entries`. A wrapper tag must fully match `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,127}`.
**Rules:** a scan that finds nothing must prove it looked: fail closed on unreadable, undecodable or absent inputs; a missing provenance is non-public; shape-check a name instead of allowlisting words. Validating a batch with proprietary rows needs the denylist file present (rederive refuses `denylist_missing`).
**Not fixed / scope:** an existing but empty denylist file still counts as present (entries=0).
**File:** `scripts/evidence_bundle.py`, `scripts/evidence_rederive.py`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_bundle_contract.py`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_rederive.py`.


## An integer-valued JSON float (12.0) or a bool bypassed `isinstance(x, int)` gates in the validator (V5)
**Area:** `scripts/evidence_bundle.py` (`_as_int`, `_int_pair`, `_int_sum`, `_check_fragment`, `check_pairing`, `_check_target_run`, parent sums).
**Symptom:** `char_count_old: 12.0`, a bool `gid`, or a float in a by_status count skipped the rule that guards the field (the check read `isinstance(v, int)` and moved on), so a dependent rule was silently not run, or a count was dropped from a sum.
**Cause:** Python's `json` returns 12.0 as float and `bool` is an `int` subclass; an `isinstance` gate that falls through on mismatch is fail-open.
**Fix:** one helper `_as_int(value, acc, pointer)`: null returns None (nullable fields), bool/str/non-integer float emit `integer_expected` and return None, an integer-valued float emits `integer_expected` once per (file, pointer) and is coerced so dependent rules still run.
**Rules:** never gate a rule on `isinstance(..., int)` without a violation on the else branch; reject bool explicitly.
**Not fixed / scope:** `consistency.gid == gid` is still plain equality (a bool compares equal to 1).
**File:** `scripts/evidence_bundle.py`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_bundle_contract.py`.


## A null `consistency` left glyph_identity not_run, so CTRL_SYN_T0 could never pass and the calibration failure cascaded over the batch (V9)
**Area:** `scripts/evidence_bundle.py` (`check_glyph_identity`, `check_cross_field`), brief v3 §5.2 glyph_identity.
**Symptom:** `20261024_1803_r2`: CTRL_SYN_T0 recorded glyph_identity `not_run` (`no_consistency_occurrence`), its calibration control was not ok, `calibration_status == "fail"`, and §5.3 rule 4 turned every control and positive row of the batch into `insufficient_evidence`.
**Cause:** brief §5.2 made the consistency check (b) mandatory for every replacement character (the lead-in 「每個替換字…都要滿足」), while §2.1 pins the CTRL_SYN_T0 fixture (`你好世界` plus tail `後綴`, one show) and the replacement `再見世界`, so a non-target occurrence of 再/見 cannot exist on that page: the control was structurally unable to pass nine phases. The validator implemented (b) literally, as undecided for a schema-legal `null`. The brief itself says (b) is not independent evidence and that glyph correctness is proven by the leg (c). Dropping the optional cross-check also exposed that the only remaining in-phase wrong-character check, `independent_leg.equals_char`, was an unrecomputed producer self-note (and `char` was free text): the real 1803 CANARY_WRONGGLYPH keyed its consistency occurrence on the written CID, not on the character, so (b) passed it and only Grok's honest `equals_char=false` caught it.
**Fix:** `consistency: null` (key present) means (b) does not apply; (a) and the leg decide, in both brief revisions (brief change (m): the relaxation resolves a conflict inside the brief that v2 shares, so it is ungated). A non-null non-dict or a missing key is undecided `consistency_malformed`; `no_consistency_occurrence` is retired. Three tightenings gated on `brief_revision == 3`: `equals_char` is recomputed as `isinstance(leg.value, str) and leg.value == char` (a differing note is `glyph_note_mismatch` at `/independent_leg/equals_char`; `leg_char_differs` is decided on the recomputed value), `char` must equal `replacement[index]` for non-space glyphs (`glyph_identity_char`, cross-field), and a null consistency needs a null `gid_equals_consistency` (`glyph_note_mismatch`). Reference bundles 1114 (rev 2) and 1713 (rev 3) keep zero violations with identical phases and statuses.
**Rules:** never turn an optional cross-check into a not_run trigger; check that each control's own pinned fixture can satisfy every rule it must pass; a self-note is never evidence: recompute it or do not read it.
**Not fixed / scope:** a false `null` (a producer hiding a differing occurrence) cannot be refuted by the fitz-free validator; the I1 oracle must select the consistency occurrence by character, not by written CID, and search the font xref itself to refute a false null; the validator also does not check that `consistency.show_seq`/`char_index` point away from the target. `20261024_1803_r2` stays non-green after V9 (its recorded `not_run` rows become `phase_result_mismatch`; the halo_shadowed/ink_checked flag and CANARY_UNSAVED violations are unrelated) and needs a fresh Grok run under (m), never a re-ingest. Rederive needs no change: it has no consistency rule and defers every committed or replayed row until `assert_glyph_identity` exists.
**File:** `scripts/evidence_bundle.py`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_bundle_contract.py`, `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v3.md`.


## A non-applicable growth row that spilled was a bundle violation with a recomputed pass, so an honest CANARY_FONT rejected every full rev-3 R0 run (V10)
**Area:** `scripts/evidence_bundle.py` (`check_growth_zone` non-applicable branch and the two applicable spill checks), `scripts/evidence_rederive.py` (`_after_bound`), brief v3 §5.1 cross-field rules, §5.2 growth_zone, §2.2 CANARY_FONT.
**Symptom:** `20261024_1803_r2`: CANARY_FONT on hvac p4 s11 recorded growth_zone `fail` ("after bbox grew 6.09808 pt on the main edge"); the validator emitted `growth_after_exceeds_target`, recomputed the phase `pass`, then `phase_result_mismatch` and `calibration_mismatch` (`failed_phases` differs). R0 completeness requires CANARY_FONT, so every full rev-3 run on hvac was rejected by construction.
**Cause:** the non-applicable branch of `check_growth_zone` only emitted a violation when `_extent(T, A) > OWN_CHAR_TOL_PT` and never `acc.fail`, treating the spill as a record defect ("declared equal width, after box wider"). The record was honest: the advance measured with the target font's /W is equal (`displacement_ink` 0), nothing contradicts itself, but the texttrace after box under the swapped font is wider. The spill is a fidelity fact, ink in a strip never proven blank (with no growth the product's verify box IS the target box, `model/text_commit/plan.py:2393-2394` `_grown_verify_bbox`), so it belongs to the phase verdict, not to the bundle shape.
**Fix:** gated on `brief_revision == 3`, all three geometry spill checks are growth_zone phase fails with reason words and no violation: `after_exceeds_target` (non-applicable), `after_not_grown` and `after_exceeds_verify` (applicable). Rev 2 keeps the old shapes byte for byte. Reach conditions, the 0.5 pt strict predicate (None strip counts 0), `growth_fields_not_null` and the early returns are unchanged; `_canary_row`, `check_calibration` and `recompute_status` pick the fail up (rules 5/6 blocked, rule 7 or 8, never a pass status). Rederive's `_after_bound` (H1 mirror, applicable rows) records the remeasured extents under rev 3 instead of quarantining; a lying `after_bbox_raw` stays the `after_bbox_raw` comparison. Brief: CANARY_FONT's spill is REQUIRED (§2.2), the default `no ink growth` pass applies only at <= 0.5 pt (§5.2), a product_commit row reaching the fail is a product finding (§5.2, §5.3 rule 8), change (n).
**Rules:** a check that compares two honestly measured numbers decides a phase, never the bundle's admissibility; before calling a shape "a lie", find the mechanism that lets an honest producer write it; every must-have canary is run through the validator's recomputation on its real geometry before a brief is pasted.
**Not fixed / scope:** (r1) a simple-font target ending in byte 32 under nonzero Tw, replaced at equal or shrinking advance by text without a trailing space, gives an after box `Tw*Th*scale` wider than T with no fault (the texttrace box is `adv - Tc - Tw*[last char is space]` while `plan._advance` counts every Tw): such a row fails growth_zone under V10; triage it, do not "fix" the record. (r2) UNVERIFIED: the equal-box argument assumes MuPDF `fz_advance_glyph` uses the PDF /W or /Widths table as the product's advance functions do; if it used hmtx where that differs, a subset font could spill with no fault. The boxes being PyMuPDF texttrace ADVANCE boxes (x1 = origin + advance) is what makes side bearings, italic overhang and stroke outset unable to trip the rule.
**File:** `scripts/evidence_bundle.py`, `scripts/evidence_rederive.py`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_bundle_contract.py`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_rederive.py`, `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v3.md`.


## A malformed frontier plan row (dotted slug, invented variant) had no owning case, so rederive refused the whole 2116 batch and dropped 56 measurements (V11)
**Area:** `scripts/evidence_bundle.py` (`check_pre_registration`, `_scope_plan_violations`, `_plan_row_key`, `_case_reg_key`); `scripts/evidence_rederive.py` owner lookup (unchanged); brief v3 §1 file types, §3.4, §5.1 slug/variant, §6 item 1, change (o).
**Symptom:** `20261024_2116_r2` (calibration pass, 64 cases = 14 R0 + 50 frontier): 8 plan-block rows failed the plan schema, 5 with a `slug` copied from veraPDF PDF/UA file names containing `.` (`/cases/28`, `/cases/34`–`37`) and 3 E_F3S rows with the invented variant `split` (`/cases/52`–`54`). `validate_instance` on the plan emitted them with `case_id: null`; rederive's rule "a violation that belongs to no case taints the whole batch" refused with `8 batch-level violation(s): ['schema_enum', 'schema_pattern']`, and the other 56 cases (14 R0 controls/canaries + 42 frontier rows, this loop's first frontier measurements) were never measured. The 8 citing cases carried the same defects case-level (`/source/slug`, `/join_key`, `/case_id`, `case_id_mismatch`) and were already rejected on their own, so the refusal protected nothing.
**Cause:** the plan file is a batch file, so every schema violation inside it was batch-level by construction, although brief §6.1 (v2 line 750 = v3 line 776) defines the consequence of registration per case. Same class, latent: a list or dict in a key field of a row raised `TypeError` while building the `registered` dict from raw `.get()` tuples; `_guarded` turned that into a case-less `check_error` and every prereg flag became False, so the batch stayed blocked.
**Fix:** `_scope_plan_violations`: a plan violation whose pointer matches `/cases/<i>(/|$)`, on a row whose `class_id` is a frontier class (`F_CLASSES | {"OUT"}`), is copied once per case whose registration key `(class_id, slug, page_index, show_seq, variant)` equals the row's (raw cid, so `_scrub_entry` digests it like every other entry; code, file and pointer unchanged; `_dedupe` keys on case_id, so twins eq1/eq2 both keep theirs). The row still registers (no artificial `pre_registered_mismatch`; statuses unchanged). A frontier row that no case cites becomes an unverifiable `plan_row_invalid` whose detail names the row index and the original code; rederive never closes it, it stays in `unverifiable_closure.open`, and the exit code is unaffected. Everything else stays batch-level: pointers outside `/cases/<i>`, rows that are not objects or whose class cannot be read as a frontier class, and any row with an R0 class (`CTRL_*`, `CANARY_*`) or cited by a case whose `kind` is outside `COUNTED_KINDS`: R0 is the batch's premise (brief §2.3), and a merely rejected R0 case would leave `check_calibration` at "pass" with every frontier row measured against it. `_plan_row_key` returns None for a non-object row or a non-scalar key field, so the `TypeError` path is gone. Ungated (v2 and v3 share the §6.1 sentence): 1114 and 1713 reports are identical before and after (0 violations, 18 unverifiable, same statuses and calibration; rederive 1713 identical apart from head/date/validation sha). Rederive needed no change: it resolves the owner by `case_id` first and `schema_*` is not in `BATCH_LEVEL_CODES`. On 2116 the report diff is exactly the 8 `case_id` fields; rederive then runs: 8 `validator_rejected`, 12 rederived, 15 deferred (`oracles_incomplete`), 28 quarantined (reasons: remeasure 18, provenance_unverified 9, before_pdf_mismatch 4, reason_order 2), 1 skipped, closure 252 closed / 0 open.
**Rules:** a defect confined to an identifiable row belongs to the cases that cite the row, never to the batch, unless the row is part of the batch's premise (R0); never build a dict key from untrusted JSON with raw `.get()` tuples, guard every part to a scalar first; `validate` can now print `ok: true` while `unverifiable` lists `plan_row_invalid`, so read `pending_rederive` and rederive's `open` list, not `ok` alone; a case-less violation refuses the batch, so every new violation site decides whether it has an owner.
**Not fixed / scope:** (1) the same class pre-exists for case-level violations on R0 rows: an R0 control or canary rejected by its own violation still feeds `check_calibration` "pass" (it ignores violations) and rederive only skips that case; the class fix is a rederive refusal when any `validator_rejected` case has kind control or canary (a tightening, gate it on `brief_revision == 3`). (2) there is no registered-but-unrun check: 2116 row 21 (F30W isartor-6-5-3-t01-fail-a) vanished silently after a runner `AttributeError`; a `plan_row_unrun` unverifiable gated on rev 3 is the candidate. (3) the brief's new §5.1 rules (`slug` = rederive `_slugify` of the file stem; closed variant vocabulary; `grow` = advance changed, wider or narrower) are not cross-checked by the validator against the measured advance. (4) the slug rule turns 2116's `isartor-manual` into `isartor-test-suite-manual`, so `join_key` continuity across batches breaks once; record it in the loop plan, do not tolerate it in code. (5) every `local_unrecorded` row and every public file outside `public_corpus_sha256.json` (ua1-*, ua2-*, vera-*, several isartor-*) quarantines `provenance_unverified` until I0a registers them; those quarantines in the 2116 rederive are not V11 regressions.
**File:** `scripts/evidence_bundle.py`, `scripts/evidence_rederive.py` (comment only), `test_scripts/test_evidence_bundle_contract.py`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_rederive.py`, `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v3.md`.


## F2/F3 rows named a slice of the show but rederive measured the whole show, and `item_range` meant indices to Grok and byte offsets to rederive (V12)
**Area:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py` (`_derive_target`, `_locate_trace(sub=)`, `frame_prepare`, `_check_changes`, `_old_new_codes`, `_whole_show_view`, `emit_rows`); `scripts/evidence_bundle.py` (`_check_target_granularity`, `_rev`, `check_revision_schema`); `scripts/evidence_schemas/true_text_case.v2.schema.json`; `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v4.md`.
**Symptom:** `20261024_2116_r2` rederive quarantined 12 of the 28 rows `remeasure` (F2I, F2R, F2G, F3 and the F3 negative): `original`, `original_sha256`, `target_bbox_raw`, `expected_origin_visual` (and the cascaded advances, `displacement_ink`, `verify_bbox_visual`, `fragment_item_range`) differed. The record's box was the item or run, the recomputed box was the whole 15-item show; the F3 negative was probed as a mixed edit (whole show as target, fragment replacement) and the product PREPARED a Tier 1 edit instead of recording `no_source_match`.
**Cause:** the brief was silent or self-contradicting. Sections 3.3 / 3.4 and the validator's target-run sizing say the target is one item, a run or a byte slice; M0 / M1 and the neighbour pairing rule decode, locate and probe the WHOLE show. `target.item_range` was defined nowhere except the schema: Grok wrote a half-open index pair (`[0, 1]`), rederive read stream byte offsets (`token_kinds[(item_range[0], item_range[1])]`) and sliced the stream with them, which produced the advance cascade. rederive also took `original` from the record's own show text and used the show text as the probe target.
**Fix:** brief revision 4 defines it: `original` = the target slice, `show_text_sha256` = the whole show, `item_range` = indices of the string items of the TJ array, locate = the whole-show run pinned by the replay origin plus the slice's glyph sub-range, probe target = the slice with the whole show as a second view. rederive derives the slice from the PDF (the record is compared, never trusted) and checks the change against it; the validator checks bounds, old-operand item count and the hash binding. The new reading applies to rederive from brief revision 3 (owner Q1 A) so 2116 is the regression fixture: 28 quarantined became 16, rows #1-11 `deferred` (`oracles_incomplete`), the F3 negative `rederived`; the 1114 and 1713 validate and rederive reports are unchanged.
**Rules:** a field that locates or sizes a target needs a definition in the brief that says whole show or slice, not only a schema line; never read a record's own text to decide what the record is about (derive it from the file and compare); an index range and a byte range must not share a name across the two readers; a release that lets F2R / F2G rows pass as measurements must hold them off the manifest in the same change (`measurement_only`), because clearing their quarantine makes them emit-eligible. Not fixed here: the validator does not require `probe.whole_show_max_tier_1` on a slice row (rederive records and compares it when present); `reason_order` (the F2 negative twins), canary operand selection, LocateError scoring, `font_kind` and the provenance rows are V13-V16.
**File:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py`, `scripts/evidence_bundle.py`, `scripts/evidence_schemas/true_text_case.v2.schema.json`, `scripts/evidence_schemas/true_text_parent.v2.schema.json`, `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v4.md`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_rederive.py`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_bundle_contract.py`.


## rederive scored its own LocateError as a product exception and located untracked-origin shows on someone else's glyphs (V13)
**Area:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py` (`_locate_target`, `_locate_positional`, `_Scene.locate_info`, `frame_prepare`, `_run_probe`, `_fallback_probe_ok`, `_probe_view`, `_compare_probe`, `_recompute`, `emit_rows`); `scripts/evidence_bundle.py` (`_check_geometry_nullability`, `check_revision_schema`); `scripts/evidence_schemas/true_text_case.v2.schema.json`; `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v4.md`.
**Symptom:** three `20261024_2116_r2` rows were quarantined `remeasure` with ten divergences each: `r2-F17-1017c455-p0-s1-cen1` (`result`, `reason`, `exception_type`, `locate` x3, `font_kind`), `r2-F30B-644ac66a-p0-s0-eq1` (Wingdings TrueType without ToUnicode) and `r2-F5-69f6b7f4-p0-s830-cen1` (Type3, texttrace unicode in a private-use plane). In all three the recorded probe was the product's honest verdict (`untracked_advance`, `encoding_failed`, `mc_wrapper_not_pure_layer`) and rederive reported it as `result: exception`, `exception_type: LocateError`.
**Cause:** (1) `_run_probe` returned the `LocateError` it raised itself and `_probe_view` labelled it a product exception, so every miss of rederive's own text locate (texttrace unicode U+FFFD or private-use never equals the decoded text) became nine divergences against a correct record. (2) The brief had no positional branch (Grok located by position and said so in `limits`) and `_locate_trace` needs the text. (3) For an untracked origin (`origin_reliable` false: an earlier show's advance was not tracked) `show.origin_user` is the earlier show's origin; M1 anchors on it and forbids a retry, so Grok recorded the earlier show's glyph box, and a text locate on that origin happily hits the earlier show's glyphs when the text repeats. (4) `font_kind` was derived from whether a CID codec parsed (`cap.cid`), so a Type0 font whose ToUnicode did not parse read as `simple` while the record, correctly, said `type0`.
**Fix:** a locate miss is quarantine `target_unlocatable`, the probe view is `unlocatable` and `_compare_probe` compares nothing against it; one function (`_locate_target`) serves both the recompute and the probe: untracked origin -> not located, else text locate, else positional (anchor within 0.02 pt and unique, the show's own glyph count, one contiguous run, anchor U+FFFD or private-use; `remeasured.locate_method = positional`, absent for text so the control reports stay byte-identical); recorded geometry on an untracked origin is a `geometry_on_untracked_origin` divergence (every revision); census and negative rows with null geometry get a reason-only probe (`expected_origin=None`) when exactly one replayed show spells the target and it is the record's (`remeasured.probe_fallback`, never an `emit_rows` row; Q13, 2026-10-25: a shared spelling is also probed and accepted only as `ambiguous_source_match`, `probe_fallback = reason_only_shared`); `font_kind` is `/Subtype`. Brief v4 + schema: the three geometry fields are nullable exactly when `origin_reliable` is false, validator `geometry_on_untracked_origin` / `geometry_null_on_tracked_origin` / `geometry_partly_null` / `geometry_null_without_limit` (rev 4), the probe on such a row passes no origin (the one exception to "no origin retry"). Effect on 2116: #18 `rederived`, #17 keeps only `provenance_unverified`, #16 stays quarantined with `target_unlocatable` + `geometry_on_untracked_origin` (a rev-3 record cannot satisfy the new null rule; only a fresh run under brief v4 can). 1114 / 1713 validate and rederive reports unchanged (rederive differs in `date_utc` only).
**Rules:** a failure of the checker's own measurement is never a fact about the product: give it its own outcome and never compare it with the record; a locate anchored on a replayed origin must check the origin is tracked before it trusts a hit, or it will confirm a record against the wrong object; when a fallback exists, make it narrow (unique target, null geometry, kinds that carry no mutation) and keep its rows off the manifest; derive the font kind from the font dictionary, not from a capability that can fail to parse. **Not fixed / scope:** the positional anchor requires only the first glyph to be undecodable (a Wingdings show decodes some glyphs, e.g. U+2327, so requiring all of them would refuse the real row), which accepts a decodable-looking tail on an undecodable head; two glyphs within 0.02 pt of the anchor (zero-advance marks) make the positional locate refuse; a codec-less Type0 slice (F2/F3) still decodes latin-1 with a 1-byte glyph unit in `_derive_target`; the validator does not cross-check `limits[]` for the `locate_method: positional` words.
**File:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py`, `scripts/evidence_bundle.py`, `scripts/evidence_schemas/true_text_case.v2.schema.json`, `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v4.md`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_rederive.py`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_bundle_contract.py`.

## A multi-change canary was remeasured from its first change, and its after box was the nearest copy of the replacement text on the page (V14)
**Area:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py` (`_operand_index`, `_operand_change`, `_old_new_codes`, `_first_change_old`, `_check_changes`, `_judge_experiment`, `_locate_after`, `_span_at`, `_glyph_union`); `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v4.md`.
**Symptom:** `20261024_2116_r2` rederive quarantined three canaries `remeasure`: `CANARY_TC` and `CANARY_FONT` (`adv_old_text_space` 0.0 against 1419.94, `displacement_ink`, `verify_bbox_visual`, `K_written` 0.25 / 140.644 where the record says null) and `CANARY_FONT` / `CANARY_WRONGGLYPH` (`after_bbox_raw` 76.56 pt away from the record's, on a second occurrence of the replacement string).
**Cause:** (1) rederive read `changes[0]` as the string operand everywhere. A canary records its `Tc` / `Tf` insertions as separate changes, and `changes[0]` is the zero-width insertion, so the old operand was empty and every advance, displacement, verify box and K token was computed from the wrong bytes. (2) The after glyph box was found by searching the reopened page for the replacement TEXT and taking the nearest hit with no distance gate (whole-show rows) or anchored on the record's own `after_bbox_raw` (slice rows). A canary whose glyphs are wrong (WRONGGLYPH) or drawn by another font (FONT) does not spell the replacement at the target, so the search landed on a pre-existing copy elsewhere. (3) `fitz.Rect.__or__` drops an empty box, so even the right glyphs under-measured when a fallback font drew nothing for some of them (CANARY_FONT: ArialMT for CJK, three zero-height boxes).
**Fix:** one operand selector (a multi-change canary needs exactly one STRING/HEXSTRING change inside the show's operator span, the others zero-width operator-only insertions; else `canary_changes_shape`), used by the three readers; the after box is anchored on the before-origin rederive located (0.02 pt gate), falling back to the glyph span that starts at the anchor, with the plain min/max union the validator uses; `after_text_identity` is recorded separately (divergence except on CANARY_FONT / CANARY_WRONGGLYPH, which exist to show it). The brief gets a clarifying row (r), no new rule: Grok's records were right. 2116: quarantined 15 -> 12, 1114 / 1713 byte-identical (only `date_utc` differs in their rederive reports).
**Rules:** never index a list of edits by position when a record can legitimately carry several; a locate that anchors on the text it is checking confirms whatever else spells that text, so anchor on the position the object is known to start and compare the text afterwards as its own observation; a union of boxes must keep empty boxes if the contract's union does. **Not fixed / scope:** the selector is limited to the experiment and canary path by design (`_check_prepared` and the controls keep `changes[0]`); a positional after-locate has no ink check, so a canary that draws nothing at the anchor is only caught by `after_text_identity` (divergence on non-fault canaries).
**File:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py`, `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v4.md`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_rederive.py`.

## The reason_order quarantine fired on every F2I/F2R row that claimed tj_multi_item_array, including the whole-show negative twin the brief orders (V15)
**Area:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py` (`_rederive_inner`, `_is_whole_show_negative`); `plans/true-text-frontier-design.md` (rederive paragraph, rejection list, R3-1 row).
**Symptom:** `20261024_2116_r2` rederive quarantined `r2-F2I-f17a0919-p0-s0-neg1` and `r2-F2R-f723638d-p0-s1-neg1` as `reason_order` although record and recompute agreed on both tiers: they are the whole-show negative twins brief L237 orders, so every compliant F2I/F2R twin was lost.
**Cause:** the check was a static predicate on two record fields (`class_id` in `F2_CLASSES`, `corpus_case.expected_reason == "tj_multi_item_array"`), evaluated before the source was even resolved. The design doc (R3-1) wrote the same record-only predicate, so the code matched the doc and the doc conflicted with the brief.
**Fix:** the decision moved after `_Scene` is built and uses recomputed facts only: `sha256(scene.text) == original_sha256`, `mutation` null, `kind` negative, `byte_range_in_item` null. Anything else, and any row that never reaches a scene (unresolved source, scene error), keeps the quarantine (fail closed). The design doc lines (rederive paragraph, rejection list, R3-1 row) were amended in the same change.
**Rules:** a quarantine whose exemption exists must derive the exemption from recomputed state, never from the record field the Grok side controls (`item_range` alone is not proof of a whole-show target); when a doc and the brief disagree on a shape the brief orders, amend the doc with the predicate, do not widen the brief. Rows #19-20 now rederive (2116: quarantined 12 -> 10); they stay subject to the X5 measurement-only hold in `emit_rows`.
**File:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py`, `plans/true-text-frontier-design.md`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_rederive.py`.

## Nine 2116 rows were quarantined for provenance because the registry knew four public files too few, the manifest did not exist, and a null path made an unresolvable source look like a hash mismatch (V16)
**Area:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py` (`load_registry`, `_manifest_entries`, `CorpusRegistry.by_sha`, `_slugify`, the `--manifest` CLI option); `scripts/evidence_bundle.py` (`check_cross_field`: `relative_path_required`, `slug_not_derived`, `_slugify`); `test_scripts/fixtures/public_corpus_sha256.json`; `test_scripts/fixtures/true_text_corpus/manifest.json`; `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v4.md`.
**Symptom:** `20261024_2116_r2` rederive quarantined nine rows for provenance although the files were intact and hash-verified on disk: rows #17 and #21-24 (`provenance_unverified`: isartor 6.3.7 t03-fail-a, isartor 6.3.2 t01-fail-a x2, veraPDF test suite 6-8-3-3-t01-fail-a, isartor 6.3.4 t01-fail-d) and rows #25-28 (`provenance_unverified` AND `before_pdf_mismatch`: test-colored-background and test-complexed-layout, `relative_path` null). `before_pdf_mismatch` on #25-28 looked like a tampered file; nothing mismatched. Row #23's slug (`vera-6-8-3-3-t01-fail-a`) was not what `_slugify(stem)` gives, and no validator rule noticed.
**Cause:** (1) `public_corpus_sha256.json` listed 15 files and the four others were simply not registered (brief section 3.0 says that is the expected quarantine until the owner adds them). (2) The brief said the four `local_unrecorded` files live in the manifest `corpora`, but the manifest did not exist at HEAD (the design's I0a had not landed), and `load_registry` had no manifest leg. (3) Brief 5.4 grouped `local_unrecorded` with proprietary under 'always null' and narrowed only `relative_path` for proprietary, so Grok wrote null; with no registry entry and no path rederive had nothing to read and reported the generic `before_pdf_mismatch`, whose meaning is 'bundle before.pdf sha differs OR the source is unresolvable'. (4) The slug rule ('mechanically derived, the same as rederive') was stated in the brief but never enforced.
**Fix:** the four public files went into the public list and the four `local_unrecorded` files into a new minimal manifest (`true-text-corpus/1`, `corpora` only), every sha recomputed from the owner's bytes on disk (they equal the memo's and the brief's prefixes, but none was copied). `load_registry` gained the manifest leg (`_manifest_entries`; a missing file registers nothing and is logged, a present one must be exact and raises `ValueError` otherwise, a sha already registered is refused so the manifest cannot re-label a public file; `--manifest` / `manifest=` override the default path). `CorpusRegistry.by_sha` keeps its provenance filter, so a `local_unrecorded` registration vouches for nobody who declares another provenance. The validator got `relative_path_required` and `slug_not_derived`, gated on `_rev(case) >= 4` (the memo wrote rev >= 3; at rev 3 rows #23 and #25-28 would turn into validator rejections instead of the resolved rows I0a is for), sharing one `_slugify` with rederive. `before_pdf_mismatch` keeps its name; its double meaning is documented in ARCHITECTURE (rename deferred: it touches the `QUARANTINE` pin, the design doc and the brief). Effect on the 2116 rederive: quarantined 10 -> 4 (rederived 16 -> 20, deferred 29 -> 31): #17 and #21, #22 now `rederived`, #23 and #24 `deferred` (`oracles_incomplete`), #25 `rederived`, and #26-28 (test-complexed-layout) are measured for the first time and stay quarantined for the V13 reasons (`target_unlocatable`, `geometry_on_untracked_origin`). The 1114 and 1713 reports are unchanged.
**Rules:** a registry the brief promises must exist before the brief is sent, and a recompute that cannot find its source should say 'unresolvable' in its own code rather than reuse a code that means 'tampered'; a contract line that sounds like a rule ('slug is derived mechanically') needs a validator check, or the next run proves it is only a hope; a manifest leg that fails open on a malformed file would be a way to register anything, so a missing file registers nothing and a bad one raises; register by hashing the bytes on the owner's disk, never by copying a sha out of the bundle that is being judged; gate every new validator rule on the brief revision that introduced it so earlier batches keep their verdicts.
**File:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py`, `scripts/evidence_bundle.py`, `test_scripts/fixtures/public_corpus_sha256.json`, `test_scripts/fixtures/true_text_corpus/manifest.json`, `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v4.md`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_rederive.py`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_bundle_contract.py`.

## The measurement-only hold lived in the plan entry, a slice row could omit its second view, and a codec-less Type0 counted one-byte glyphs (V12-V16 review)

**Area:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py` (`emit_rows`, `default_plan`, `_check_planned`, `_run_probe`, `_glyph_unit`, `_derive_target`, `_whole_show_replacement`); `scripts/evidence_bundle.py` (`_check_target_granularity`: `whole_show_view_required`); `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v4.md`.
**Symptom:** (1) `emit_rows(..., DEFAULT_PLANNED)` (a tuple) or a `--planned` JSON with `"F2R": {}` emitted F2R/F2G rows although owner decision 2 defers X5; once I0b lands the V15 whole-show negative twins would have become manifest rows. (2) A rev-4 slice row with no `probe.whole_show_max_tier_1` validated and rederived clean although brief v4 M1 says the second view is part of a slice row. (3) For a Type0 font without a CID codec, `_derive_target` returned `glyph_count = len(bytes)` (twice the glyphs) while `_Scene.glyph_total` said `len(bytes) / 2`. (4) Round 2: a `--planned` JSON with `"measurement_only": null`, `0`, `1`, `"true"` or `"false"` emitted F2G rows. (5) Round 2: a rev-4 slice negative whose slice probe was unlocatable and refused the reason-only fallback came out `rederived` with `probe_fallback: reason_only` and no `target_unlocatable`.
**Cause:** (1) the hold was `plan.get("measurement_only") is True`, so it existed only when whoever built the plan wrote it; `_planned_entry` gives `{}` for a list plan. (2) rederive compared the view only when present and the validator never asked for it. (3) three places computed the glyph unit as `2 if cap.cid is not None else 1` (the codec) and one as `cap.subtype == "Type0"` (the font), the same split V13 fixed for `font_kind`. (4) `plan.get("measurement_only", <class default>) is True`: a present non-bool value replaced the class default and then failed `is True`, so the hold was lifted by anything that was not exactly `True`. (5) `_run_probe` set the one `scene.fallback_used` flag for the whole-show second view too (its spelling is unique even when the slice occurs in two shows), and `rederive_case` reads that flag to drop `target_unlocatable`.
**Fix:** (1) the default is the class: `plan.get("measurement_only", class_id in MEASUREMENT_ONLY_CLASSES) is True`, so only an explicit `false` lifts it. (2) validator rule `whole_show_view_required` (rev >= 4, slice target, probe present, view null or absent). (3) one `_glyph_unit(cap)` keyed on `/Subtype`, used by all four sites. (4) `flag = plan.get("measurement_only")`; held when `flag is True` or (class in `MEASUREMENT_ONLY_CLASSES` and `flag is not False`); `_check_planned` makes `--planned` refuse a non-bool flag (exit 2, names the class). (5) the flag is set only when `not whole`: the primary probe alone decides `target_unlocatable`. Regression: 1114 and 1713 validate byte-identical, rederive identical but for `date_utc`.
**Rules:** a deferral the owner decided belongs to the thing deferred, not to the config that happens to name it; a field the brief makes mandatory needs a validator rule, "compared when present" is not mandatory; when one concept (code unit, font kind) has a definition in one place, grep every other spelling of it in the same change; a hold that a value lifts must test for that exact value (`is False`), never `get(key, default) is True`, because a present wrong-typed value evicts the default; a flag shared by a primary and a secondary probe must be set by the primary only.
**File:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py`, `scripts/evidence_bundle.py`, `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v4.md`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_rederive.py`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_bundle_contract.py`

## A slice target's font-metric background quad started at the show origin and ignored its inner kerns (Q10, Q11)

**Area:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py` (`_check_growth_geometry`, `_growth_checks`, `OracleContext`, `_slice_terms`, `_quad_terms`, `_text_advance`); `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v4.md` (§5.1 slice `advance`, §5.2 `growth_zone.background_bbox_visual`, change list (t)).
**Symptom:** a row whose target is a SLICE of its show (F2I/F2R/F2G/F3, `target.item_range` / `byte_range_in_item`) recorded `growth_zone.background_bbox_visual` at the show origin with the slice's width. The strip covered the glyphs before the slice, not the slice, and the raster proof (`raster_proof`, `probe_regions_px_96dpi`) was computed on that wrong strip. Brief and rederive both stated `(0.0, -0.35*Tfs, adv_old*Th, Tfs)`, so they agreed and nothing flagged it. Batch 2116 DID exercise it: two F2G `tj_run` rows (`f17a0919-p0-s4-grow1`, `f723638d-p0-s0-grow1`, `item_range` [19,21] of 21 and [13,15] of 15) carried the origin-based quad about 393 pt left of the target. Q11: a third row, F2R `bdb495e9-p0-s2-eq1` (`item_range` [0,2], x_pre 0, one inner kern 27), had its recorded x1 0.32 pt past the target's box because the width summed the string advances and ignored the kern between its items.
**Cause:** the formula is the product's `_build_tier1` quad (`plan.py`), which only ever has a WHOLE-SHOW target, so `x0 = 0` is right there. V12 made slice targets legal and made `adv_old` the slice advance (brief 5.1), but nobody moved the quad's origin; the oracle feed in `_growth_checks` rebuilt the same quad from `ctx.adv_old` as well. Two copies of one formula, and the check used the same formula as the record.
**Fix:** one helper (`_slice_x_pre`, renamed `_slice_terms` by Q11 below) = text-space advance (before Th) of everything the show draws before the target: string items before `i0` (same advance function as `_measure_advances`' `adv_old`), `-K/1000*Tfs` for every kern number before the slice, plus the bytes before `b0` of item `i0` for an F3; `0.0` for a whole-show target without a leading kern (so every whole-show row without inter-item or leading kerns (every Tj show, every product tier-1 row) is bit-identical). The quad is `(x_pre*Th, -0.35*Tfs, (x_pre + adv_old)*Th, Tfs)` in `_check_growth_geometry` and in the oracle (`OracleContext.x_pre`, default 0.0; a tier 1 plan passes 0.0 because the product quad is whole-show and compared exactly). An unprovable prefix gives a null expectation (`background_bbox_visual` divergence), the oracle refuses (`ValueError`, reported as "oracle raised"); neither raises. The validator does not recompute this quad. 2116 rederive moved from 20 rederived / 31 deferred / 8 validator_rejected / 1 skipped / 4 quarantined to 20 / 29 / 8 / 1 / 6: the two rows above flipped deferred -> quarantined(`remeasure`) on `background_bbox_visual`, and the new quad's x0 matches `target_bbox_visual` x0 to about 0.03 pt; 1713 is identical. Q11 adds the width term: `_slice_terms(scene) -> tuple[float, float] | None` returns `(x_pre, k_inner)` from one lex of the operand, `k_inner` being the sum of the kern numbers BETWEEN the target's own string items (`items[i0].end <= pos < items[i1-1].start`; 0 for a single item, an F3 and a Tj; the inter-item kerns of all items for a whole-show TJ), and the quad is `(x_pre*Th, -0.35*Tfs, (x_pre + adv_old - k_inner/1000*Tfs)*Th, Tfs)` at every site; `OracleContext.k_inner` mirrors `x_pre` (same default and None semantics), and a tier 1 plan passes 0.0 for both. 2116 then moved to 20 / 28 / 8 / 1 / 7: the two F2G rows keep their quarantine with x1 shifted by `k_inner/1000*Tfs`, and the F2R row joined them (deferred -> quarantined(`remeasure`), new x1 within 0.002 pt of `target_bbox_visual`); 1114 and 1713 are identical. The leading-kern follow-up drops the `whole -> 0.0` short-circuit, so a leading kern counts into `x_pre` for a whole-show TJ too (`[30 <..> 30 <..> 20 <..>] TJ`: whole-show `x_pre = -30/1000*Tfs`); regression: 1114, 1713 and 2116 unchanged, no whole-show leading-kern row reached a growth gate.
**Rules:** when a formula is copied from the product, copy its precondition too (here: whole-show target) and re-check it each time the contract widens what the formula is fed; a check that uses the same formula as the record cannot see a wrong formula, so compare the result against an independent quantity (the target's own box) at least once on real data; fix the class (every site that builds the quad, one shared helper), not the one site; keep the kern terms in any prefix advance, because the strings-only prefix is wrong by `K/1000*Tfs` per kern; the width has the same shape as the origin (a quad over a TJ spans the string advances MINUS the kerns between its items), so test a kern before, inside and after the target (the fixture's 30 and 20) and a mutant that counts the prefix kern, drops Tfs or adds instead of subtracts; `x_pre` means 'the advance before the FIRST target item' for every target, whole show included, because a special case for 'whole' hides a leading kern (the product rejects one, `TJ_LEADING_KERN_UNPROVEN`, so only the evidence path ever sees it; a mutant restoring `whole -> 0.0` must die).
**File:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py`, `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v4.md`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_rederive.py`.

## MuPDF keeps `/Widths` as integers: a kern computed from fractional widths leaves a sub-0.01 pt successor residual

**Area:** `scripts/evidence_bundle.py` (`check_pairing`, `_inshow_successor_bound`, neighbours phase), brief v4 section 5.2 neighbours; `scripts/evidence_rederive.py` (does not measure neighbours yet).
**Symptom:** `20261025_1824_r2` rows `r2-F3-f723638d-p0-s7-grow1` (inshow successor off by 0.00109 pt) and `r2-F3-bdb495e9-p0-s49-grow1` (0.00296 pt) were `probe_rejected` by the neighbours phase alone: the 1e-6 pt limit for `role=inshow_successor` could not be met. Equal-advance permutations (the F2R rows on the same fonts) measured 0.0, which is why T16-4X P-B saw 0.0.
**Cause:** MuPDF stores simple-font `/Widths` as integers (rounded to the nearest unit): on `minimal-document.pdf` the texttrace advance of `e` is 444 where `/Widths` says 444.4 and `m` is 833 for 833.3. The product computes the compensating kern K from the exact widths (K agrees to 1e-6), so after an edit that changes the glyph multiset the glyphs after the edit point inside the same show sit off by (sum_new(round(w) - w) - sum_old(round(w) - w)) * Tfs * Th * trm_scale / 1000, where round(w) - w is within [-0.5, +0.5] unit per glyph (the residual is the difference of rounding errors, not of fractional parts: `/Widths [600.7 600.4 600.5]` at 10 pt, `[(A) 0 (C)] TJ` -> `[(B) -0.3 (C)] TJ` moves C by 0.7 unit). The observed rows are -0.1 unit (444.4 -> 444 is -0.4, 833.3 -> 833 is -0.3) on `f723638d`, i.e. 0.1 * 10.9091 / 1000 = 0.00109, and +0.3 unit (500.0 and 833.3) on `bdb495e9`, i.e. 0.3 * 9.9626 / 1000 = 0.00296. Each glyph contributes at most half a unit, so the one-unit-per-glyph bound keeps a 2x margin.
**Fix:** for `brief_revision >= 4` the validator's neighbours phase fails `inshow_moved` only above `(char_count_old + char_count_new) * Tfs * Th * trm_scale / 1000 + 1e-6`, read from the first advance object and `target.trm_scale` (1 when absent); a missing or invalid count, Tfs or Th falls back to the plain 1e-6 (fail closed); rev 2 and 3 keep 1e-6. The exact residual recomputed from `/Widths` in rederive (compared at 1e-3) waits for I0b. The integerisation is pinned in CI so the premise cannot drift with PyMuPDF. The two 1824 rows validate with `phase_result_mismatch` (recorded fail, recomputed pass) until a fresh run.
**File:** `scripts/evidence_bundle.py` (`_inshow_successor_bound`), `test_scripts/test_evidence_bundle_contract.py` (`test_q12_*`, `test_q12_mupdf_integerises_fractional_widths`), `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v4.md`.

## A runner edited between two `--phase` runs is invisible to a DONE-time hash; only the last RUNS.json entry plus a per-row runner sha catches a composite batch (brief v5 (w))

**Area:** `scripts/evidence_bundle.py` (`check_code_revision`, `_check_runs_json`), brief v5 section 6 items 2/4/8, both `*.v2.schema.json` (`code_revision.runner_sha256`).
**Symptom:** `20261026_0032_r2` mixed R0 rows from `--phase all` with frontier rows from a `--phase cases` re-run made after Grok edited `run_pilot.py`; validate reported 0 violations because v4 has no single-run rule, and a sha of `run_pilot.py` taken at DONE time would have matched the file on disk by construction.
**Cause:** PARENT_SUMMARY is regenerated at the end of the batch, so any "DONE-time" runner hash equals the final runner text; the composite is only visible per row (which runner produced it) and per run (what the last `--phase` was).
**Fix:** rev >= 5 rows and the parent carry `code_revision.runner_sha256`; `run_pilot.py` appends `{phase, runner_sha256, started_utc}` to `RUNS.json` at the START of every run; the validator checks rows == parent == sha256 of the file on disk (`runner_sha_missing`, `runner_sha_mixed`, `runner_sha_disk_mismatch`; the reference is PARENT_SUMMARY's value, else the first row's), requires every RUNS entry to be well-formed (`runs_missing` / `runs_malformed`) and rule-checks only the LAST entry (phase `all`, same sha as the reference: `runner_partial_rerun`); all six are batch-level in rederive; a rev <= 4 row or parent carrying `runner_sha256` is `schema_additional`; batch `.py` files are `-text` in `.gitattributes` so the runner bytes survive a git round trip. Earlier RUNS entries are attempt history, so a section 6.8 self-check fix followed by a full rerun stays legal. Rev 2-4 batches are untouched (1114/1713/2116/0015/0032 validate byte-identical).
**File:** `scripts/evidence_bundle.py`, `scripts/evidence_rederive.py` (`BATCH_LEVEL_CODES`), `test_scripts/test_evidence_bundle_contract.py` (`test_v5_*`), `plans/grok-briefs/brief-v5.md`.

## `single_family` counted negative and census rows' producer families, so a negative sibling from a second family lifted a class to `method_reproducible` (brief v5 (w2))

**Area:** `scripts/evidence_bundle.py` (`recompute_parent_summary`, `class_state_overclaim`), brief section 3.0 and 6 item 4.
**Symptom:** `20261026_0032_r2` F30B and F2I: Grok wrote `method_reproducible_single_family`, the validator recomputed `method_reproducible`, and nothing fired because `_diff` skips `class_state_proposal`; `distinct_producer_families` differed only because the second family came from a negative (F30B) or an unresolvable proprietary census row (F2I).
**Cause:** brief 3.0 keys single_family on the POSITIVES' producer family; the recompute added every counted row to the family set.
**Fix:** for a rev >= 5 batch (one flag per batch: parent or any row at rev >= 5), `distinct_lineages`, `distinct_producer_families` and the proposal count the save_reopen_pass positives only (the brief 3.0 bar is "positives from two lineages", so a negative on a second lineage must not clear it either); the overclaim guard reads the same fields. Rev <= 4 keeps the all-row counts so older reports stay byte-identical.
**File:** `scripts/evidence_bundle.py`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_bundle_contract.py` (`test_v5_single_family_*`, `test_v5_rev4_rows_keep_the_all_row_family_count`).

## A census row claiming `tj_multi_item_array` on a whole-show target stays `reason_order` after its source resolves (V15 predicate requires kind=negative)

**Area:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py` (`_is_whole_show_negative`, `reason_order`), `test_scripts/fixtures/true_text_corpus/manifest.json` (office-report-23p row, decision 7).
**Symptom:** after registering office-report-23p (`test_files/office-report-23p.pdf`, proprietary manifest row, 2026-10-26) the 0032 F1 census row rederives, but F2I `r2-F2I-880a637f-p0-s6-cen1` (whole three-item Type0 TJ, `expected_reason` tj_multi_item_array, mutation null) is still quarantined `reason_order` although the recomputed show text hashes to `original_sha256`.
**Cause:** `_is_whole_show_negative` accepts only `kind == "negative"`; a census row with the same shape can never satisfy it, so the R3-1 twin exemption never applies to census.
**Fix:** none yet (owner question D22): either accept kind in {negative, census} with a red test on the 0032 F2I shape, or document that census rows never claim `tj_multi_item_array`. Until then the row is a known false quarantine, not a Grok defect. The manifest leg accepts `proprietary` rows under `test_files/`; the owner renamed the local file to the slug so the tracked manifest row carries no document name (the pre-rename name survives in older tracked notes such as TODOS and the 20260924 FONT_INVENTORY; scrubbing them is a separate owner call).
**File:** `scripts/evidence_rederive.py`, `test_scripts/test_evidence_rederive.py` (`test_v5_office_report_23p_is_registered_as_proprietary`).

## Registering hvac/ecc in the manifest `corpora` made `load_registry` raise on the acc leg
